term_table.lsj_entry_text: νᾶπυ, τό, Att. , = σίναπι (cf. Phryn. 255 , Plin. HN 19.171 ; on the accent v. Hdn.Gr. 1.354 ), mustard, ν. Κύπριον Eub. 19 ; ν. βλέπειν Ar. Eq. 631 : gen. νάπυος Thphr. HP 1.12.1 : dat. νάπυϊ IG 42(1).126.17 , 21 (Epid., ii A.D.), Luc. Asin. 47 .
term_table.greek_sentence: καθάπερ γε πάλιν εἰ νᾶπυ τρίψας ἐν ἀέρι ψυχρῷ, μεθ’ ὕδατος ψυχροτάτου χειμῶνος ὥρᾳ, προσενέγκῃς ἐξαίφνης ἀραιῷ τε καὶ ἀσθενεῖ σώματι, φρίξει οὐδὲν ἧττον ἢ εἰ χιὼν ἢ κρύσταλλος ἔψαυσεν αὐτοῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Just as, again, if you grind mustard in cold air, with very cold water, in the season of winter, and apply it suddenly to a loose-textured and weak body, it will shiver no less than if snow or ice had touched it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So too, conversely, if you grind mustard in cold air, with very cold water in the winter season, and apply it suddenly to a rare and weak body, the body will shiver no less than if snow or ice had touched it.

term_table.english_sentence_A: But if it remains in contact with the body of an animal for a longer time, it will first produce a sensation of slight heat, then of more, then of so much that one seems to be burned by fire.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if it stays in contact with the body of an animal for a longer time, it will first produce a sensation of slight heat, then of more, and then of so much that the body seems to be burned by fire.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμπειρος, ον, (πεῖρα) experienced or practised in a thing, acquainted with it, c. gen., τῆς θυσίης Hdt. 2.49 ; τῶν χώρων Id. 8.132 ; Βοιωτῶν Id. 9.46 ; τῆς ἐκείνου διανοίης Id. 8.97 ; κακῶν A. Pers. 598 ; γάμων S. OC 752 ; θαλάσσης Th. 1.80 ( Sup. ); τοῦ ἀγωνίζεσθαι Antipho 5.7 ; ὁ περὶ τῶν νόμων ἔ. Pl. Lg. 632d ; οἱ μάλιστα περὶ ταῦτα τῶν ἱερέων ἔ. Id. Ti. 22a : abs., οἱ ἔ. the experienced, S. OT 44 , OC 1135 ; experts, Pl. Lg. 765b ; ναυσὶν ἐμπείροις for ships skilfully handled, Th. 2.89 ; τὸ ἐμπειρότερον αὐτῶν their greater experience, ib. 87 . Adv. -ρως, τινὸς ἔχειν to know a person or thing by experience, by its issue, X. An. 2.6.1 , Antiph. 3 , etc.; παιδεῦσαι D. 59.18 ; διώκειν Aen.Tact. 2.6 ; πόλεμον διενεγκεῖν Jul. Or. 2.95a : Comp. -οτέρως Aeschin. 1.82 .
term_table.lsj_first_sense_gloss: experienced or practised in a thing
term_table.greek_sentence: διωρισμένων οὖν ἡμῖν τῶν τοιούτων ἁπάντων ἐν τοῖς περὶ τῆς τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων δυνάμεως ὑπομνήμασιν, ἕνδεκα τὸν ἀριθμὸν οὖσιν, ἐπ’ αὐτὴν ἤδη τρέψομαι τὴν χρήσιμον διδασκαλίαν, ἐν ᾗ γυμνασάμενός τις, ἐὰν καὶ μηδ’ ὅλως ἐπιφέρηται τὰς γραφὰς τῶν πολυφαρμάκων δυνάμεων, οὐκ ἀπορήσει τῶν ἐπιτηδείων πρὸς ἕκαστον [366] πάθος, ἐὰν οὗτος, ὡς ἔφην, ἔμπειρος ᾖ τῆς ὕλης τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Since, then, all such matters have been defined by us in the commentaries On the Power of Simple Drugs, which are eleven in number, I shall now turn to the useful teaching itself, in which, once someone has exercised himself, even if he carries about with him no written formulae at all of the many-ingredient preparations, he will not be at a loss for the remedies suitable for each [366] affection, provided that he, as I said, is experienced in the material of simple drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Since, then, all such matters have been determined by us in the commentaries On the Power of Simple Drugs, which are eleven in number, I shall now turn to the useful instruction itself. Whoever has trained himself in it, even if he does not carry with him at all the written formulas of the many-ingredient preparations, will not be at a loss for the remedies suitable to each [366] affection, provided that he, as I said, is experienced in the material of simple drugs.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πάρεργος, ον, (ἔργον) beside the main subject, subordinate, incidental, ὁ λόγος π. ὤν Pl. Ti. 38d ; παρέργῳ τῇ ποιήσει καταχρήσασθαι treat it as a mere accessory, ib. 21c ; ὅ τι μὴ π. Id. Phdr. 274a , etc. ; πάντα π. ποιησάμενος PHib. 1.44.5 (iii B. C.). Adv. -γως by the way, cursorily, opp. ἀκριβῶς, Pl. Lg. 793e ; opp. ἐξεταστικῶς, D. 17.13 ; π. ἔχειν πρός τι Din. 3.14 ; οὐ π. ἔμαθον Hegesipp.Com. 1.6 , cf. Men. 462.6 ; φέροντα μὴ π. Id. Sam. 293 , cf. Porph. Abst. 2.61 , PMag.Par. 1.2640 ; transiently, Phld. Mus. P. 39 K. as Subst. πάρεργον, τό, subordinate or secondary business, πόνων E. Or. 610 ; ππάρεργ' ὁδοῦ a secondary purpose of my journey, Id. El. 509 ; π. τῆς τύχης a trifling set-off to my for tune, Id. Hel. 925 ; πάρεργα ἐμῶν κακῶν baubles in comparison with my ills, Id. HF 1340 ; πάρεργα δόμων, = νόθοι , Id. El. 63 ; π. γίγνεσθαι to be slain among the rest, Paus. 10.27.2 ; ἐν παρέργῳ as a by-work, as subordinate or secondary, Th. 6.69 , etc. ; ἐν π. θοῦ με treat in such a way, S. Ph. 473 : ὡς ἐν π. τῆς ἐμῆς δυσπραξίας feeling it no great addition to . . , E. IT 514 , cf. Pl. Smp. 222c ; ἐν παρέργου μέρει Id. R. 37o c ; ἐκ παρέργου πόλεμον ποιεῖσθαι Th. 7.27 ; ἐκ π. μελετᾶταί τι Id. 1.142 ; εἴ τις ἐν π. σκέψεται Pl. Tht. 184a ; τἄλλα πάρεργα πρός τι νομίζειν D. 51.17 ; π. ἐᾶν τι γίγνεσθαι Pl. Lg. 766a , cf. Euthd. 273d ; πρὸς τὸ κέρδος . . πάντα τἄλλα . . π. γίγνεται Alex. 98.2 ; ὅπως μὴ τὰ π. τῶν ἔργων πλείω γίνηται Arist. EN 1098a32 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν παρέργῳ δὲ ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐπιδείκνυσι καὶ τὴν τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν ἰατρῶν φιλονεικίαν εἰς ὀνείρατά τε καὶ τύχην καὶ περίπτωσιν ἀναγόντων τὰ σύνθετα φάρμακα σχεδὸν ἅπαντα, πλὴν ὀλιγίστων τινῶν, ἃ κατὰ τὸν κοινὸν ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπων λόγον, ὃν ἐπιλογισμὸν αὐτοὶ καλοῦσιν, εὑρηκέναι φασί.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Incidentally, this discourse also demonstrates the contentiousness of the Empiricist physicians, who refer nearly all compound drugs to dreams and chance and accidental encounter, except for some very few, which they say they have discovered according to the reasoning common to all human beings, which they themselves call epilogismos.
term_table.english_sentence_B: As a by-product, this account also exposes the contentiousness of the Empirical physicians, who trace back nearly all compound drugs, except for a very few, to dreams, chance and accidental encounter (periptōsis). These few they say they discovered by the reasoning common to all human beings, which they themselves call epilogismos.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔνιοι, αι, α, some; never in Ep. , Lyr., or Att. Poets before Men. , exc. Ar. Pl. 867 (cf. however ἐνίοτε); first used in Ion. Prose, as Hdt. 1.120 , 8.56 , Hp. Praec. 6 ; πολλοὶ μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Lys. 25.19 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Pl. Tht. 151a , X. Mem. 4.2.38 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . οἱ δὲ . . Pl. Mx. 238e ; ἔνιοί τινες Isoc. 15.258 : later in sg., οὐ πᾶσα κίνησις θερμαίνει, ἀλλ' ἐνία ψύχει Arist. Pr. 884b13 , cf. Thphr. Vert. 1 ; περὶ ψυχῆς ἐνίας θεωρῆσαι Arist. Metaph. 1026a5 : neut. pl. as Adv., συμμανῆναι ἔνια δεῖ Men. 421 ; ἔστι καὶ ταὐτόματον ἔνια χρήσιμον Id. 486 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ ὅταν ἀλλήλοις μίξωμιν φάρμακα τὴν αὐτὴν ἐπιδεδειγμένα διὰ τῆς πείρας ἐνέργειαν, ἄλλο δ’ ἐπ’ ἄλλου σώματος ἄμεινον ἢ χεῖρον ἐνηργηκὸς, εὔλογον μὲν ἡμῖν ἔδοξε, φασὶν ἔνιοι τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν, οὐ γὰρ δὴ πάντες γε, συνθεῖναι πλείω τοιαῦτα χάριν τοῦ κᾂν ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν εὑρεθῆναι τῇ φύσει τοῦ θεραπευομένου σώματος οἰκεῖον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: As when we mix with one another (μίξωμιν, read μίξωμεν) drugs that have displayed through experience the same action, but one having acted better or worse on one body and another on another: "it seemed reasonable to us," say some of the Empiricists—for certainly not all of them—"to compound several such drugs together, so that at least one of them might be found to be appropriate to the nature of the body being treated." This, they say, is what happened in the case of this very novel drug called the "cephalic", all those ingredients having been mixed in it which are known, even singly, to produce flesh in wounds.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For instance, they say, when we mix together drugs that have shown the same action through experience, but one acted better or worse on one body and another on another, it seemed reasonable to us (so say some of the Empiricists, though certainly not all) to combine several such drugs, so that at least one of them might be found appropriate to the nature of the body under treatment.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σαρκ-ωτικός, ή, όν, making flesh grow, Id. 1.261 , 11.799 ; πληγῶν ς. interpol. in Dsc. 1.126 ; κόλπων ς. Id. 1.1.2 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλὰ κατὰ τίνα γε λόγον ἰὸς μιχθεὶς ἁπλῇ κηρωτῇ σαρκωτικὸν ἐργάζεται φάρμακον, οὐδετέρου τῶν μιχθέντων σαρκοῦντος, οὐκέτι λέγουσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But by what rationale verdigris, when mixed with a simple cerate, produces a flesh-producing drug, though neither of the ingredients mixed produces flesh, they no longer say.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But by what reasoning verdigris mixed with simple cerate produces a flesh-producing drug, when neither of the ingredients mixed produces flesh, this they do not go on to say.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: οὐδέτερ-ος, α, ον, not either, neither of the two, Hdt. 1.51 , Ar. Ra. 1412 , Pl. Phlb. 21e : in pl., when each party is pl., first in Hes. Th. 638 , Sc. 171 , cf. Hdt. 1.76 , etc.: divisim, v. ἕτερος 1 . Adv. οὐδετέρως in neither of two ways, Pl. Lg. 902c : also neut. pl. as Adv., = οὐδετέρως , Id. Plt. 258a , Tht. 184a , etc. neutral, τῶν μὲν αἱρετῶν οὐσῶν, τῶν δὲ φευκτῶν, τῶν δ' οὐ. Arist. EN 1175b26 : so in Medic., of a state which is neither illness nor health, διάθεσις Herophil. ap. Gal. 6.388 ; σῶμα Gal. 1.307 , 311 . in Gramm., neuter, ἀρσενικῶν καὶ θηλυκῶν καὶ οὐ. D.H. Amm. 2.10 ; τὸ οὐ. (sc. γένος) the neuter gender, A.D. Pron. 6.19 . Adv. -ρως in the neuter, Id. term_table.lsj_entry_text: κηρωτή, ἡ , ʽκηρόὠ = κήρωμα 1 , cerate or salve, used medically, Hp. Off. 12 , Art. 14 , Ar. Ach. 1176 , Ph. Bel. 96.18 ; κ. οἰνανθίνη, ῥοδίνη, Dsc. 1.109 , 2.110 ; κ. ὑγρά Gal. 11.391 ; used as a cosmetic, Ar. Fr. 320.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ κηρωτὴ δὲ πρᾷον μέν ἐστι καὶ ἄδηκτον, ἀντὶ δὲ σαρκὸς νέας ῥύπον ἐπιτρέφει τοῖς ἕλκεσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For verdigris eats away the [367] ulcerated flesh, being a hot and pungent drug; whereas the cerate is mild and non-biting, but instead of new flesh it breeds filth upon the ulcers.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For verdigris eats away the [367] ulcerated flesh, being a hot and acrid drug, whereas cerate is mild and non-biting, but instead of new flesh it breeds filth upon the ulcers.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πρᾶος, ον, also πραΰς, Ion. πρηΰς, εῖα , ΰ:—πρᾶος supplies sg. in Att. , Trag., and Com., exc. that the fem. is always πραεια (πρᾶος as fem. only in Plu. 2.168d ); but sg. πραΰς, Ion. πρηΰς, is used in Ep. and Lyr. (also in X. and usu. in LXX , Plb. , etc.):—pl., nom. πρηέες Hp. Epid. 1.10 , πρηεῖς AP 5.208 ( Posidipp. or Asclep. ), πρᾶοι Pl. R. 562d , etc.; fem. πρηεῖαι AP 6.244 ( Crin. ); neut. πραέα X. Oec. 15.4 , Eq. 9.10 , etc., πρᾶα Arist. HA 488b22 , f.l. in Ph. 2.351 ; gen. πραέων X. An. 1.4.9 ; dat. πραέσι Pl. Lg. 888a , 930a , fem. πραίαις written for πραείαις IG 7.3101 (Lebad., iii A.D.); acc. πραεῖς Plb. 18.37.7 , πράους Isoc. 3.55 : Comp. πραότερος Lys. 20.21 , πραΰτερος Epich. 153 , Pl. Ti. 85a , etc., Ion. πρηΰτ- Hdt. 2.181 : Sup. πραότατος Pl. Phd. 116c , etc., πραΰτατος Syria 5.337 (Sidon); Ep. and Ion. πρηΰτατος A.R. 2.937 , AP 6.349 ( Phld. ); πράϋστος MAMA 1.237 (Phrygia). (The ι subscr. is freq. written in codd., but Πρᾶος is written in IG 22.1928.20 (pr. n., iv B.C.), IGRom. 4.504 (Pergam.), cf. Phot., Et.Gud. 478.31 ; πραύτερος is found once in codd., Pl. Ti. l.c. (proved wrong by πραΰς Com.Adesp.in Gött. Nachr. 1922.31 , πραέα (neut. pl.) in PCair.Zen. 33.12 (iii B.C.), πραέως UPZ 144.6 (ii B.C.), and by the absence of iota in Ion. πρηΰς)):—mild, soft, gentle (not in Il. or Od. ): of things, πρηῢ σέλας H.Hom. 8.10 ; πραῢς ὄαρος Pi. P. 4.136 ; mild, πυρετοί Hp.l.c.; ἰητρείη πρηεῖα Id. Art. 69 ; of sound, soft, gentle, τὴν φωνὴν πραοτέραν ποιοῦνται X. Smp. 1.10 ; ἀνέμων πρηΰτατε Ζέφυρε AP 6.349 ( Phld. ); ὠδῖνες ib. 244 ( Crin. ); κέντρον ib. 229 (Id.). of persons, mild, gentle, meek, πραῢς ἀστοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 ; πᾶσιν ἵλεώς τε καὶ πρᾶος Pl. R. 566e ; πρὸς τοὺς οἰκείους π. ib. 375c ; π. τὸ ἦθος Id. Phdr. 243c ; π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Id. Euthd. 303d ; esp. after having been angry, Hdt. 2.181 ( Comp. ); ὁ θὴρ ὅδ' ἡμῖν π., of Dionysus, E. Ba. 436 ; of a horse, gentle, ἀλλήλοις πραότεροι X. Cyr. 2.1.29 ; of other animals, tame, ἰχθύων μεγάλων καὶ πραέων Id. An. 1.4.9 , cf. Arist. HA 488b22 ; ζῷα . . πραέα πρὸς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους X. Oec. 15.4 : prov., πραΰτερος μολόχας Epich. 153 ; also, τόπος ἡμερώτερος καὶ πραότερος Isoc. 9.67 . of actions, feelings, etc., mild, τιμωρίαι πραότεραι Pl. Lg. 867b ; πραότεραι ἡδοναί ib. 815e ; λόγοι, ἤθη, φύσις, ib. 888a , 930a , R. 375c ; ὄσσοισι πρηέσιν δέρκευ BMus.Inscr. 921b8 (Branchidae, i/ii A.D.); τὰ πραέα caresses, X. Eq. 9.10 ; πραότερα πάσχειν Pl Cri. 49b . making mild, taming, φάρμακον πραῢ τείνων ἀμφὶ γένυι, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; προκινεῖν αὐτὸν [τὸν ἵππον] ὡς πραοτάτοις σημείοις X. Eq. 9.3 . Adv. πράως, mildly, gently, πράως πείθειν τινά, φέρειν τι, Pl. R. 589c , Cri. 43b ; πράως ἔχειν πρός τι Id. Ly. 211e ; πράως λέγειν τὸ πάθος to speak lightly of it, X. An. 1.5.14 ; πράως διακεῖσθαι, opp. ὀργίζεσθαι, D. 21.183 ; πράως, μὴ πικρῶς Id. 18.265 ; in physical sense, gently, Orib. Fr. 134 : Comp. , πραότερον προδιδάσκειν, κολάζειν, Pl. Grg. 489d , Phd. 94d ; πραοτέρως ( v.l. -υτέρως ) ἔχειν τινί J. AJ 17.6.4 : Sup. , φέρειν . . ὡς πραότωτα Pl. R. 387e : later form πραέως ( πράως [Ἀττικοί], οὐ πραέως Phot. ), UPZ 144.6 (ii B.C.), D.S. 1.36 , Dsc. 1.13 , dub. in Com.Adesp. 336.5 (cf. πρατίας), etc.: Ion. πρηέως cj. in Democr. 46 (πράως and πραέως codd.). (Cogn. with Skt. prīṇā´ti 'love, give pleasure to', Goth.frijon 'love', frijonds 'friend'.)

term_table.english_sentence_A: How this too is mixed together with the other, and likewise all the other drugs that are compounded in the same manner from contraries, has already been stated by me also in the third book of the therapeutic treatise, and now too the exercise in particular cases will be set out with an example for each affection.

term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, among the drugs that draw by means of heat, just as among those called septic, some display their own power as soon as they are applied to the body, while others require two or three or four hours; and some a whole day, or even the night after it, or even several in succession.

term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, among the drugs that draw by means of heat, just as among those called septic, some display their own power as soon as they are applied to the body, while others require two or three or four hours; and some a whole day, or even the night after it, or even several in succession.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Thus among those that ulcerate through heat, as also among those called septic, some display their own power as soon as they are applied to the body, while others need two or three or four hours; some need a whole day, or the following night as well, or even more days and nights in succession.

term_table.greek_sentence: αἱ δὲ ὗλαι τῶν φαρμάκων, αἱ μὲν ἀπὸ φυτῶν εἰσιν, αἱ δὲ ἀπὸ μετάλλων, αἱ δ’ ἀπὸ ζώων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The materials of drugs are some from plants, some from metals, and some from animals; and you have learned all of them, distinguished, in the treatise on simple drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Of the materials of drugs, some come from plants, some from minerals, and some from animals.

term_table.greek_sentence: πρὸς γὰρ τοὺς ἑταίρους ὁ λόγος οὗτός ἐστί μοι μάλιστα, τοὺς ἀξιώσαντάς με δεύτερον νῦν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀπολωλόσι γράφειν ταῦτα· καθάπερ δὲ τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων τὰς δυνάμεις [370] ἁπάντων ὑμᾶς ἀκριβῶς ἐπίστασθαι προσῆκεν, ἵνα ἐν παντὶ χωρίῳ δύνησθε ῥᾳδίως ἐκ τῶν παρόντων συντιθέναι τὰ λυσιτελοῦντα τοῖς θεραπείας δεομένοις σώμασιν, οὕτω καὶ τῶν παρὰ φύσιν πασῶν διαθέσεων τὰς διαφορὰς ὑπόμνημα· δεύτερον δὲ τὸ περὶ τῆς τῶν συμπτωμάτων, καὶ τρίτον ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς, ἐν ᾧ περὶ τῶν τὰς νόσους ἐργαζομένων αἰτίων διέρχομαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For this discourse of mine is addressed above all to my companions, who have asked me now to write these things a second time, after the loss of the earlier ones. And just as it was proper for you to know accurately the powers [370] of all the simple drugs, so that in every place you might easily compound, from what is at hand, the things that are beneficial to the bodies in need of treatment, so too [you should know] the differences of all the conditions contrary to nature, [on which you have] a treatise; a second is the one on the differences of the symptoms, and a third after these, in which I go through the causes that produce diseases; and in addition to these, three others on the causes in the symptoms.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For this discourse of mine is addressed chiefly to my companions, who have asked me now to write these things a second time, after those that were lost. And just as it is fitting that you know precisely the powers [370] of all the simple drugs, so that in every place you may easily compose, from what is at hand, the things that are of benefit to bodies in need of treatment, so too [it is fitting that you know] the differences of all the dispositions contrary to nature … treatise (ὑπόμνημα) [the text appears defective here: probably a first treatise, on the differences of diseases, has dropped out]; second, the one on the [difference] of symptoms, and third after these, the one in which I go through the causes that produce diseases.

term_table.english_sentence_A: You also have my writing On Plethora and that On the Differences of Fevers; and after these, the books of the Therapeutic Method, through which you learned the conditions by which activity is harmed, and that treatment is of these first, just as, conversely, prophylaxis is of the causes that produce them.

Op. 633 : with the Art., τὸν ἐμὸν χόλον Il. 4.42 , etc.: in Poets sts. joined with gen., to strengthen the possessive notion, ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ mine own, 6.446 , Od. 2.45 ; δαὴρ . . ἐμὸς ἔσκε κυνώπιδος Il. 3.180 ; θρῆνον ἐμὸν τὸν αὐτῆς A. Pl. 33 . mine, i.e. favourable to me, τεκμήρια ἐμά, οὐ τούτων Antipho 2.4.10 . objectively, relating to me, against me, ἐμὴ ἀγγελίη Il. 19.336 ; τὸν ἐμὸν γάμον Od. 2.97 ; τὴν ἐμὴν αἰδῶ respect for me, A. Cyr. 8.3.32 ; sts. with another gen. added, τὰς ἐμὰς Λαΐου διαφθοράς murder of L. by me, S. Hel. 364 (anap.). without a Subst., mine, οὐ γὰρ ἐμὸν παλινάγρετον my word, Il. 1.526 ; τὸ μὲν ἐμόν [ἐστι] 'tis my counsel, Pi. I. 8(7).42 : in Trag. and Prose, it is my duty, my business, E. Ion 1020 , Pl. Lg. 664b . ἐμοί my friends, Il. 20.205 ; οἱ ἐμοί X. Cyr. 3.2.28 , etc.; ὁ ἐμὸς Ἡράκλειτος my dear Heraclitus, Arr. Epict. 2.2.17 . τὰ ἐμά my property, Pl. Prt. 310e , etc.; of children, S. El. 538 , OC 922 ; τὸ τύπτειν καὶ ἐμὲ καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ ἀδίκως Pl. Grg. 508e ; of servants. PEdgar 4.6 (iii B.C.), etc.; but also τὰ ἐμά or τὸ ἐμόν, my part, my affairs, my interest, οὕτω τὸ ἐμὸν ἔχει things stand thus with me, Hdt. 4.127 ; τὰ τούτου μᾶλλον ἢ τοὐμόν S. Aj. 124 ; ἔρρει τἀμὰ παντελῶς X. Cyr. 6.1.3 ; τὸ ἐμὸν εὖ πράττει Pl. R. 463e , etc.; in full, τοὐμὸν μέρος S. Tr. 1215 : hence in Trag. and Att. , my conduct (almost periphr. for ἐγώ), Id. El. 1302 , Tr. 1068 , Ar. Th. 105 ; τὸ μὲν οὖν ἐμὸν οὐκ ἐμποδὼν ὑμῖν ἔσται Lys. 8.19 , cf. Pl. Grg. 452c , etc.: abs., τό γε ἐμόν for my part, as far as concerns me, Hdt. 1.108 , Pl. term_table.greek_sentence: ἔχετε δὲ καὶ τὸ περὶ πλήθους ἐμὸν γράμμα καὶ τὸ περὶ τῆς τῶν πυρετῶν διαφορᾶς· ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς τε τὰ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου, δι’ ὧν ἐμάθετε τάς τε διαθέσεις, ὑφ’ ὧν ἐνέργεια βλάπτεται, καὶ ὡς ἡ θεραπεία τούτων πρώτων ἐστὶν, ὥσπερ γε πάλιν ἡ προφυλακὴ τῶν ἐργαζομένων αὐτὰς αἰτιῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: You also have my writing On Plethora and that On the Differences of Fevers; and after these, the books of the Therapeutic Method, through which you learned the conditions by which activity is harmed, and that treatment is of these first, just as, conversely, prophylaxis is of the causes that produce them.
term_table.english_sentence_B: You also have my writing on plethos and the one on the difference of fevers; and after these the books of the Therapeutic Method, through which you learned both the dispositions by which a function is damaged, and that the treatment is of these first, just as, in turn, prevention is of the causes that produce them.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐμάθετε δὲ καὶ ὅτι πρῶτος σκοπὸς τῆς θεραπείας ἐκ τῶν νοσωδῶν εὑρίσκεται διαθέσεων, ὅτε τε συνενδείκνυται τούτοις ἡ τοῦ πεπονθότος μορίου φύσις, ἅμα τῇ τοῦ περιέχοντος ἡμᾶς ἀέρος κράσει καὶ κατάστασιν καὶ ἡλικίαν καὶ ὥραν καὶ χώραν, ἐπιτηδεύματά τε καὶ ἔθη συνεπισκέπτονται πολλοὶ τῶν ἀρίστων ἰατρῶν, [371] ὑπὲρ ὧν εἰρήσεταί τινα καὶ νῦν, ἔνθ’ ἂν αὐτῶν γένηται χρεία.
term_table.english_sentence_A: You learned also that the first indication of the treatment is discovered from the morbid conditions, and that the nature of the affected part gives a joint indication together with these, along with the mixture of the air that surrounds us; and many of the best physicians consider in addition the constitution (of the atmosphere), age, season and region, as well as pursuits and habits, [371] about which some things will be said now too, wherever there is need of them.
term_table.english_sentence_B: You have learned, too, that the first goal of treatment is found from the diseased dispositions, and when the nature of the affected part co-indicates along with these. Together with the krasis of the air that surrounds us, many of the best physicians also take into consideration the state [of the weather], the age, the season and the region, as well as pursuits and habits, [371] about which some things will be said now too, wherever there is need of them.

term_table.greek_sentence: ταῦτ’ οὖν ὑμᾶς οὕτως ἅπαντα διὰ μνήμης ἔχειν χρὴ πρόχειρα, βουλομένους ἐν ἅπαντι χωρίῳ φαρμάκων εὐπορεῖν ἁπλῶν τε καὶ συνθέτων, ἔτι τε πρὸς τούτοις, ὡς ἐνίοτε μὲν ἕν τι φάρμακον αὐτοφυὲς ἁπλοῦν, ἱκανόν ἐστι τὴν παρὰ φύσιν ἰάσασθαι διάθεσιν, ἐνίοτε δὲ χρεία γίγνεται συνθέτου καὶ διὰ τί γε πράττομεν τοῦτο λεκτέον ἐφεξῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: All these things, then, you must thus hold in memory ready to hand, if you wish in every place to be well supplied with drugs, both simple and compound; and further, in addition to these, that sometimes one single naturally occurring simple drug is sufficient to cure the condition contrary to nature, while sometimes there is need of a compound one; and why indeed we do this must be stated next.
term_table.english_sentence_B: All these things, then, you must have thus ready at hand in memory, if you wish to be well supplied in every place with drugs both simple and compound. Further, in addition to these, you must bear in mind that sometimes a single natural, simple drug is sufficient to cure the disposition contrary to nature, while sometimes there is need of a compound one; and why indeed we do this must be stated next.

term_table.greek_sentence: ταῦτ’ οὖν ὑμᾶς οὕτως ἅπαντα διὰ μνήμης ἔχειν χρὴ πρόχειρα, βουλομένους ἐν ἅπαντι χωρίῳ φαρμάκων εὐπορεῖν ἁπλῶν τε καὶ συνθέτων, ἔτι τε πρὸς τούτοις, ὡς ἐνίοτε μὲν ἕν τι φάρμακον αὐτοφυὲς ἁπλοῦν, ἱκανόν ἐστι τὴν παρὰ φύσιν ἰάσασθαι διάθεσιν, ἐνίοτε δὲ χρεία γίγνεται συνθέτου καὶ διὰ τί γε πράττομεν τοῦτο λεκτέον ἐφεξῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: All these things, then, you must thus hold in memory ready to hand, if you wish in every place to be well supplied with drugs, both simple and compound; and further, in addition to these, that sometimes one single naturally occurring simple drug is sufficient to cure the condition contrary to nature, while sometimes there is need of a compound one; and why indeed we do this must be stated next.
term_table.english_sentence_B: All these things, then, you must have thus ready at hand in memory, if you wish to be well supplied in every place with drugs both simple and compound. Further, in addition to these, you must bear in mind that sometimes a single natural, simple drug is sufficient to cure the disposition contrary to nature, while sometimes there is need of a compound one; and why indeed we do this must be stated next.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: διάθεσις, εως, ἡ, (διατίθημι) placing in order, arrangement ( ἡ τοῦ ἔχοντος μέρη τάξις Arist. Metaph. 1022b1 ), Antipho Soph. 24a ; πολιτείας Pl. Lg. 710b ; τῶν ξενίων Id. Ti. 27a . disposition or composition in a work of art (opp.εὕρεσις), Id. Phdr. 236a ; opp.ἱστορία, μῦθος, Plb. 34.4.1 , Plu. term_table.greek_sentence: ἀνάλογον γὰρ εἶναι χρὴ τῇ θεραπευομένῃ διαθέσει τὸ θεραπεῦον φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For the drug that treats must be proportionate to the condition being treated.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐὰν οὖν ἡ διάθεσις ᾖ ψυχρὰ, τέτταρσιν ἀριθμοῖς ἀφεστῶσα τῆς κατὰ φύσιν, ὅτι μὲν εἶναι χρὴ τὸ θεραπεῦσον αὐτὴν φάρμακον, ἴσῃ ποσότητι θερμότερον τοῦ συμμέτρου πρόδηλον παντί.
term_table.english_sentence_A: If, then, the condition is cold, standing removed from the natural one by four numbers, it is obvious to everyone that the drug which is to treat it must be hotter than the well-proportioned by an equal quantity.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If, then, the disposition is cold, standing four numbers away from the natural state, it is evident to everyone that the drug which is to treat it must be hotter than the moderate by an equal quantity.

term_table.greek_sentence: τινὰ δὲ τῶν ἁπλῶν οὐδ’ εἰς χρῆσιν ἀχθῆναι δύναται χωρὶς ἑτέρας μίξεως, οἷον ὅταν ἐμπλαστὸν φάρμακον ἐπιτιθέναι τινὶ βουλώμεθα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Some of the simples, moreover, cannot even be brought into use without mixture with something else, as for instance when we wish to apply an emplastic drug to someone; for none of the simples is suitable for such a use.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Some of the simples, moreover, cannot even be brought into use without a further admixture, as when we wish to apply a plaster drug to someone.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὔτ’ οὖν ἄσφαλτος οὔτε κηρὸς οὔτε ῥητίνη, καθάπερ οὐδὲ πίσσα πρόπολίς τε καὶ λάδανον, ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ἰὸς καὶ ψιμύθιον ἢ λιθάργυρος ἢ μολύβδαινα ἢ τῶν ἄλλων τι με ταλλικῶν φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Neither asphalt, then, nor wax nor resin, just as neither pitch nor propolis nor ladanum, and still less verdigris and white lead or litharge or molybdaena or any of the other metallic drugs.

term_table.english_sentence_A: In the same way neither can herbs by themselves make an emplastic drug.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Likewise herbs alone cannot make a plaster drug either.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐμ-πλαστός, ή, όν, daubed on or over: ἔμπλαστον (with or without φάρμακον), τό, plaster, salve, Hp. Hum. 5 :—also ἔμπλαστος, ἡ, Alex.Aphr. de An. 25.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰκότως οὖν ἐπενόησαν οἱ πρώτως συνθέντες ἐμπλαστὰ φάρμακα καὶ δι’ ἐλαίου μίξεως ἕψειν μὲν τὰ μεταλλικὰ, τήκειν δὲ τὰ τηκτὰ, προσεμβάλλειν δ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ βοτάνας ξηρὰς, κεκομμένας τε καὶ διηθημένας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Reasonably, therefore, those who first compounded emplastic drugs devised the plan of boiling the metallic substances with an admixture of oil, of melting the meltable ones, and of adding to them also dry herbs, pounded and sifted.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Reasonably, therefore, those who first compounded plaster drugs devised, through the admixture of oil, to boil the metallic substances and to melt the meltable ones, and to throw in with them also dry herbs, pounded and sifted.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐφ’ ἑτέρων πάλιν διαθέσεων, χρεία ἑνὸς φαρμάκου μόνου τῶν αὐτοφυῶν ἐστιν, ἐπιμίγνυμεν δ’ αὐτῷ τινὰ, ποτὲ μὲν [373] ἀμβλῦναι τὸ σφοδρὸν τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ βουλευόμενοι, ποτὲ δὲ τὴν ἀηδίαν παραμυθήσασθαι, καθάπερ Ἱπποκράτης ἐν τῷ περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων ἔφη κατὰ τήνδε τὴν ῥῆσιν· ἢν δ’ ὑπὸ φρένας ᾖ τὸ ἄλγημα, ἐς δὲ τὴν κληῗδα μὴ σημήνῃ, μαλθάσσειν χρὴ τὴν κοιλίην ἢ μέλανι ἐλλεβόρῳ ἢ πεπλίῳ, μέλανι μὲν δαῦκον ἢ σέσελι ἢ κύμινον ἢ ἄνισον ἢ ἄλλο τι τῶν εὐωδέων μίσγοντα, πεπλίῳ δὲ ὀπὸν σιλφίου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: In other conditions, again, there is need of one single drug from among the naturally occurring ones, but we mix something in with it, sometimes [373] intending to blunt the vehemence of its power, sometimes to mitigate its unpleasantness, just as Hippocrates said in the work On Regimen in Acute Diseases in the following passage: 'If the pain is beneath the diaphragm and gives no sign toward the collarbone, one must soften the belly either with black hellebore or with peplion, mixing with the black (hellebore) daucus or seseli or cumin or anise or some other of the fragrant things, and with peplion the juice of silphium.' In this passage Hippocrates clearly indicated that there is need of the purging drug, but that its unpleasantness in the drinking and in the belly alone requires a sweetening agent.
term_table.english_sentence_B: In other conditions, again, there is need of a single drug only, one of the natural ones, but we mix something in with it, sometimes [373] intending to blunt the vehemence of its power, sometimes to mitigate its unpleasantness, as Hippocrates said in On Regimen in Acute Diseases in the following passage: 'If the pain is below the diaphragm and gives no sign towards the collarbone, one must soften the belly either with black hellebore or with peplion; with the black, mixing in daukos or seseli or cumin or anise or some other of the fragrant things, and with the peplion, juice of silphium.' In this passage Hippocrates clearly indicated that there is need of the purging drug, but that only its unpleasantness, in the drinking and in the belly, requires a seasoning.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐφ’ ἑτέρων πάλιν διαθέσεων, χρεία ἑνὸς φαρμάκου μόνου τῶν αὐτοφυῶν ἐστιν, ἐπιμίγνυμεν δ’ αὐτῷ τινὰ, ποτὲ μὲν [373] ἀμβλῦναι τὸ σφοδρὸν τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ βουλευόμενοι, ποτὲ δὲ τὴν ἀηδίαν παραμυθήσασθαι, καθάπερ Ἱπποκράτης ἐν τῷ περὶ διαίτης ὀξέων ἔφη κατὰ τήνδε τὴν ῥῆσιν· ἢν δ’ ὑπὸ φρένας ᾖ τὸ ἄλγημα, ἐς δὲ τὴν κληῗδα μὴ σημήνῃ, μαλθάσσειν χρὴ τὴν κοιλίην ἢ μέλανι ἐλλεβόρῳ ἢ πεπλίῳ, μέλανι μὲν δαῦκον ἢ σέσελι ἢ κύμινον ἢ ἄνισον ἢ ἄλλο τι τῶν εὐωδέων μίσγοντα, πεπλίῳ δὲ ὀπὸν σιλφίου.

term_table.greek_sentence: πολλὰ γάρ τοι τῶν πινομένων φαρμάκων ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἀηδῆ τοῖς προσφερομένοις ἐστὶν, ὡς ἀνατρέπεσθαι τὸν στόμαχον, ἐμεῖσθαί τε παραχρῆμα, τινὰ δὲ κᾂν ἐπ’ ὀλίγον ἐν τῇ γαστρὶ μεῖναι δυνηθῇ, μετὰ ταῦτα γοῦν ἐμεῖσθαι μοχθηρὰς ἐρυγὰς κινήσαντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For indeed many of the drugs that are drunk are so unpleasant to those who take them that the stomach is upset and they are vomited at once, while some, even if they are able to remain for a short time in the belly, are nonetheless afterwards vomited, having stirred up foul eructations.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For indeed many of the drugs that are drunk are so unpleasant to those who take them that the stomach is upset and they are vomited at once; and some, even if they are able to remain in the belly for a little while, are at any rate vomited afterwards, having provoked noxious belchings.

term_table.greek_sentence: καθάπερ δὲ τῶν καθαιρόντων οἷον ἡδύσματά ἐστι τὰ τοιαῦτα τῶν φαρμάκων, ὧν Ἱπποκράτης ἐμνημόνευσεν, οὕτως τῶν ἀνωδύνων ὀνομαζομένων, ἕτερα τῆς σφοδρότητος ὑπάρχει πραϋντικὰ, καθάπερ ὅταν ὀπὸν μήκωνος [374] ἢ ὑοσκυάμου σπέρμα παραδιδόαμεν ἢ μανδραγόρου ῥίζης φλοιὸν, ὥστε καὶ αὕτη χρεία συνθέσεως φαρμάκων ἐστί.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And just as, for the purgatives, such drugs as those which Hippocrates mentioned are, as it were, sweeteners, so too for the drugs called anodynes there are others that mitigate their vehemence, as when we administer poppy juice [374] or henbane seed or the bark of mandrake root; so that this too is a need for the composition of drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Just as such drugs as Hippocrates mentioned are, as it were, seasonings of the purgatives, so for the drugs called anodyne there are other things that mitigate their violence, as when we give poppy juice [374] or henbane seed or the bark of mandrake root; so this too is a use for the compounding of drugs.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἥδε ἡ χρεία συνθέσεως φαρμάκων ἐστὶν, ὅταν ἕν τι φάρμακον ἔχειν βουλώμεθα πρὸς πολλὰ τῶν ἰοβόλων θηρίων ἢ θανασίμων φαρμάκων ἐπιτήδειον, ἥτις χρεία καὶ τὴν θηριακὴν ὀνομαζομένην ἀντίδοτον ἐσκεύασε καὶ πρὸς αὐτῇ τὴν Μιθριδάτειον ἑτέρας τε πολλάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But there is also this need for the composition of drugs, when we wish to have a single drug suitable against many of the venomous beasts or deadly drugs—a need which produced the antidote called Theriac, and in addition to it the Mithridatium and many others.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But this too is a use for the compounding of drugs, when we wish to have a single drug suitable against many venomous beasts or deadly poisons; it is this use that produced the antidote called theriac, and besides it the Mithridatic and many others.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἥδε ἡ χρεία συνθέσεως φαρμάκων ἐστὶν, ὅταν ἕν τι φάρμακον ἔχειν βουλώμεθα πρὸς πολλὰ τῶν ἰοβόλων θηρίων ἢ θανασίμων φαρμάκων ἐπιτήδειον, ἥτις χρεία καὶ τὴν θηριακὴν ὀνομαζομένην ἀντίδοτον ἐσκεύασε καὶ πρὸς αὐτῇ τὴν Μιθριδάτειον ἑτέρας τε πολλάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But there is also this need for the composition of drugs, when we wish to have a single drug suitable against many of the venomous beasts or deadly drugs—a need which produced the antidote called Theriac, and in addition to it the Mithridatium and many others.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But this too is a use for the compounding of drugs, when we wish to have a single drug suitable against many venomous beasts or deadly poisons; it is this use that produced the antidote called theriac, and besides it the Mithridatic and many others.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χρεία (written χρέα PCair.Zen. 25.2 , 148 (iii B. C.)), Ion. χρείη Call. in PSI 11.1216.43 , ἡ: (χράομαι, κέχρημαι):— need, want, χρείας ὕπο A. Th. 287 ; ἵν' ἕσταμεν χρείας considering in what great need we are, S. OT 1443 ; χρείᾳ πολεμεῖν to war with necessity, Id. OC 191 (anap.): c. gen., want of . . , φαρμάκων χρείᾳ κατεσκέλλοντο A. Pr. 481 ; ἐν χρείᾳ τύχης Id. Th. 506 ; ἐν χρείᾳ δορός in the need or stress of war, S. Aj. 963 ; φορβῆς χρείᾳ Id. Ph. 162 (anap.), cf. 1004 : ἵππων ἡμῖν χρεία μὲν οὔτε τις πολλῶν οὔτε πολλή [ἐστιν] Pl. Lg. 834b ; ἦ μὴν ἔτ' ἐμοῦ χρείαν ἕξει will have need of my help, A. Pr. 170 (anap.), cf. Call.l.c.; ἀφίκοντο εἰς χρείαν τῆς πόλεως came to feel the need of its assistance, Pl. Mx. 244d ; ἰατρῶν ἐν χρείαις ἐσόμεθα, ἐν χρείᾳ ἡγεμόνος εἶναι, Pl. R. 373d , 566e ; ὅτου σε χ. ἔχει S. Ph. 646 ; so τίς χ. σ' ἐμοῦ [ἔχει]; E. Hec. 976 , cf. χρεώ 1.2 : χρείαν ἔχω, c. inf., Ev.Matt. 3.14 (folld. by (ίνα, Ev.Jo. 2.25 ); signfs. 1.1 and 111 in the same sentence, οὐχ οὕτως χ. ἔχομεν τῆς χ. παρὰ τῶν φίλων ὡς . . Epicur. Sent.Vat. 34 : prov., χ. διδάσκει, κἂν βραδύς τις ᾖ, σοφόν 'necessity is the mother of invention', E. Fr. 715 , cf. El. 376 , Men. 263 : pl., αἱ χρεῖαι τολμᾶν βιάζονται Antipho 3.2.1 ; αἱ τοῦ σώματος χ. X. Mem. 3.12.5 ; πρώτη γε καὶ μεγίστη τῶν χ. ἡ τῆς τροφῆς παρασκευή Pl. R. 369d ; αἱ ἀναγκαῖαι χ. D. 23.148 , cf. 45.67 (sg.); πολεμικαὶ χ. Arist. Pol. 1328b11 . want, poverty, S. Ph. 175 (lyr.), E. Hel. 420 , etc.; διὰ τὴν χ. καὶ τὴν πενίαν Ar. Pl. 534 (anap.). a request of necessity, opp. ἀξίωσις (a claim of merit), Th. 1.37 , cf. 33 : generally, request, τὴν πρίν γε χ. ἠνύσασθ' ἐμοῦ πάρα A. Pr. 700 ; κἀγὼ . . τοιάνδε σου χ. ἔχω make such a request of or to thee, Id. Ch. 481 . business, ὡς πρὸς τί χρείας; for what purpose? S. OT 1174 , cf. 1435 ; χρῆσθαί τινι χρείαν ἣν ἂν ἐθέλωσι Pl. Lg. 868b ; δοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν χ. Plb. 8.16.11 . esp. military or naval service, ἡ πολεμικὴ χ. καὶ ἡ εἰρηνική the employments of war and of peace, Arist. Pol. 1254b32 ; αἱ κατὰ θάλατταν [χ.], ἡ ἐν τῇ γῇ χ., Plb. 6.52.1 , 31.21.3 ; οἱ ἐπὶ τῶν χ. Aristeas 110 , LXX 1 Ma. 12.45 ; οἱ πρὸς ταῖς χ. Ju. 12.10 ; οἱ ἐπὶ χρειῶν τεταγμένοι BGU 543.1 (i B. C.); in military sense, action, engagement, αἱ κατὰ μέρος χ. Plb. 1.84.7 , al. generally, business, employment, function, Id. 3.45.2 , etc.; ἡ ἐγκεχειρισμένη χ. the duty assigned, PTeb. 741.11 (ii B. C.); οὓς καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χ. ταύτης Act.Ap. 6.3 ; χ. πολιτικαί Plu. Mar. 32 , etc. a business, affair, matter, like χρέος , Plb. 2.49.9 , al.; τὴν ὑπὲρ τούτων χ. the study of these things, Epicur. Ep. 1p.29U. χ. ἀναγκαία need of nature, D.S. 4.33 ; τροφῆς χ. Ph. 2.472 . use, as a property, use, advantage, service, χρείης εἵνεκα μηδεμιῆς Thgn. 62 ; τῆς χ. τοῦ παιδὸς ἀποστερηθῆναι Antipho 3.3.4 ; ἡ χ. τῆς ῥητορικῆς Pl. Grg. 480a ; πωλοῦντες τὴν τῆς ἰσχύος χ. Id. R. 371e ; χρείαν ἔχειν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις to be of service to mankind, Id. Smp. 204c ; τὰ οὐδὲν εἰς χρείαν things of no use or service, D. Prooem. 56.3 ; χρείαν ἔχει εἴς τι is of service towards . . , Sosip. 1.41 ; for S. OT 725 , v. ἐρευνάω 1 : pl., χρεῖαι . . φίλων ἀνδρῶν services rendered by them, Pi. N. 8.42 ; χρείας παρέχεσθαι render services, Decr. ap. D. 18.84 , IG 22.654.15 , cf. Plb. 1.16.8 (sg.); ἵνα σοι τὰς χ. παρέσχωμαι (sic) PCair.Zen. 498 (iii B. C.); μεγάλην παρεῖχε χ. τοῖς κοινοῖς πράγμασιν Plb. 3.97.4 ; παρέχειν χ. to be serviceable, useful, Aristo Stoic. 1.79 ; ἑξήκοντα καὶ τριακόσια χρειῶν γένη παρέχον δένδρον Plu. 2.724e ; χ. ναυτικαί equipments, Ael. VH 2.10 . as an action, using, use, κτῆσις καὶ χ. X. Mem. 2.4.1 , Pl. R. 451c ; ἐν χρείᾳ εἶναι in use, Id. Phd. 87c ; κατὰ τὴν χ. for use, Id. R. 330c ; πρὸς τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην χ. X. Mem. 4.2.25 ; ἡ χ. τῶν λόγων the employment of words, Pl. Sph. 239d , cf. Plt. 272d : pl., λάμπει γὰρ ἐν χρείαισιν ὥσπερ . . χαλκός is made bright by constant use, S. Fr. 864 . of persons, familiarity, intimacy, τινος with one, Antipho 5.63 : generally, any relation of business or intercourse, ἐν χρείᾳ τινὶ τῇ πρὸς ἀλλήλους Pl. R. 372a ; ἡ πρὸς ἀλλήλους χ. Arist. Rh. 1376b13 ; [ Νικόμαχοσ] συνεβίω Ἀμυντᾳ . . ἰατροῦ καὶ φίλου χρείᾳ in the relationship, capacity, D.L. 5.1 . Rhet., pregnant sentence, maxim, freq. illustrated by an anecdote, Sen. Ep. 33.7 , Hermog. Prog. 3 , Aphthon, Prog. 3 , Theon Prog. 5 , etc.: pl., title of works by Zeno ( D.L. 6.91 ), Aristipp. , etc.; by Macho , a collection of sayings of courtesans, Ath. 13.577d ; ἡ τοῦ Κλεομένους χ. Plu. 2.218a ; χρεῖαι καὶ ἱστορίαι ib. 78f .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰσὶ δὲ καὶ ἄλλαι τινὲς χρεῖαι, μικρότεραι μὲν τῶν εἰρημένων, ὅμως δ’ οὖν ἀναγκάζουσαι πολλάκις ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὴν σύνθεσιν ἀφικνεῖσθαι τῶν φαρμάκων, ἃς ἐν τῇδε τῇ πραγματείᾳ πάσας μαθήσεσθε.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μικρός and σμικρός, ά, όν, Dor. , Ion. μικκός (q.v.): σμικρός is corroborated by metre in Il. 17.757 , Hes. Op. 361 , and might be restored in Il. 5.801 , Od. 3.296 (μικρός codd.); it is prob. the only form in Hdt. ( μικρός Hdt. 2.74 codd.): freq. in Lyr. and prob. always in Trag. (exc. where metre requires μικρός, as S. Aj. 161 (anap., Comp. )); most freq. in Pl. ; but in Th. , also Ar. and other Com., μικρός prevails, σμικρός being found Th. 4.13 , 7.75 , 8.81 , Ar. Ach. 523 , V. 5 ; Att. Inscrr. have σμικρός IG 12.313.111 , al., μικρός ib. 369.10 , al.:—small, little, in Size, μ. ἔην δέμας Il. 5.801 ; μ. λίθος Od. 3.296 ; κίρκον, ὅ τε σμικρῇσι φόνον φέρει ὀρνίθεσσιν Il. 17.757 ; σμ. ἄστεα Hdt. 1.5 ; μεγάθεϊ σμικροί Id. 2.74 : with Dims., μ. πολίχνιον, γῄδιον, παιδάρια, Isoc. 5.145 , X. Cyr. 8.3.38 , Ages. 1.21 : as a Com. exaggeration, δικαστηρίδιον μ. πάνυ Ar. V. 803 ; σκαλαθυρμάτι' ἄττα μ. Id. Nu. 630 , etc.: c. inf., μικροὶ δ' ὁρᾶν Id. Pax 821 : as a term of reproach, Κλειγενὴς ὁ μικρός Id. Ra. 709 , cf. Pl. Prt. 323d , Arist. EN 1123b7 , Alex. 98.7 ; Ἀμύντας ὁ μ. Arist. Pol. 1311b3 ; οἱ ἐν μικρῷ μεγάλοι short but stoutly built, Philostr. Gym. 36 ; ὁ μ. δάκτυλος SIG 1172.4 (Lebena). in Quantity, σμικρὸν ἐπὶ σμικρῷ καταθεῖναι Hes. Op. 361 ; μέλιτος μικρόν Ar. V. 878 ; μ. ὄψον, ἀργυρίδιον, X. Mem. 3.14.1 , Ar. Pl. 240 , cf. Antiph. 44 . in Amount or Importance, petty, trivial, slight, σμ. πρόφασις Thgn. 323 ; ἔπος, ἔγκλημα, ῥοπή, etc., S. OC 443 , Tr. 361 , OT 961 , etc.; ἐκ σμικροῦ λόγου on some slight pretext, Id. OC 620 ; ἐν σμικρῷ λόγῳ παρῆκεν as of small account, ib. 569 ; αἰτίας μικρᾶς πέρι E. Andr. 387 , etc.; οὐδὲ μικρόν, = οὐδὲ γρῦ , D. 19.37 ; of persons, of small account, opp. μέγας, σμ. ἐν σμικροῖς, μέγας ἐν μεγάλοις Pi. P. 3.107 ; ἄριστ' ἂν καὶ μέγας ὀρθοῖθ' ὑπὸ μικροτέρων S. Aj. 161 (anap.), etc.; σμ. τίθησί με Id. OC 958 ; βίος ὁ μ., = μέτριος , E. Fr. 504 ; τίνος σμικροτάτου μεταβαλόντος, σμικρότατος τὴν δύναμιν, Pl. R. 473b ; of the mind, οὐ σμικρὸν φρονεῖ S. Aj. 1120 ; of style, mean, [ Φίλιστοσ] μικρὸς ταῖς ἐκφράσεσιν D.H. Vett.Cens. 3.2 ; of festivals, of lesser importance, Ἁλίεια τὰ μεγάλα καὶ τὰ μ. SIG 1067.14 (Cedreae). of Time, short, Pi. O. 12.12 , Ar. Pl. 126 , etc.; εἰς μ. χρόνον Pl. R. 498d ; ἐν μικρῷ (sc. χρόνῳ) shortly, X. Cyn. 5.32 , Eq. 8.7 ; πρὸ μικροῦ Poll. 1.72 ; ἔτι μικρὸν καὶ καταλιθοβολήσουσί με LXX Ex. 17.4 . of Age, young, Ostr.Bodl. i237 (ii B.C.), etc. Adverbial usages, regul. Adv. σμικρῶς, but little, Pl. Criti. 107d ; μικρῶς by a little, prob. in Archim. Stom. 1 : Sup. σμικρότατα X. Mem. 3.11.12 . σμικροῦ or μικροῦ within a little, almost, Id. Cyr. 1.4.8 , D. 18.151 , etc.; in full, μικροῦ δεῖν, v. δεῖ 11 , δέω (B) 1 ; μικροῦ τινος ἀπελείφθη τοῦ μή . . Ach.Tat. 7.13 ; but μικροῦ πρίασθαι for a little, cheap, X. Mem. 2.10.4 . σμικρῷ by a little, with Comp. , Pl. Plt. 262c , etc.; also σμικρῷ πρόσθεν a little before, Id. Lg. 719b , etc.; μικρῷ ἄνωθεν D. 44.6 . μικρόν a little, σμικρὸν ὑπολείπεσθαι, σμ. τι παρακλίνειν, X. An. 5.4.22 , Pl. Cra. 410a ; of Time, X. An. 3.1.11 , etc.; repeated, μικρὸν μικρόν Antiph. 10 : pl., of Degree, σμικρὰ γεωμετρίας ἔμπειροι Pl. R. 527a , etc.; σμίκρ' ἄττα διατρίψαντες Id. Prt. 316a ; μικρὰ διακινήσω σε περὶ τοῦ πράγματος Sosip. 1.22 ; περιπάτησον μικρὰ μετ' ἐμοῦ Men. Sam. 243 , cf. Plu. Luc. 31 . with Preps., ἐπὶ σμικρόν but a little, S. El. 414 , Antipho 6.18 , Hdt. 4.129 . κατὰ μικρόν into small pieces, X. An. 7.3.22 ; so κατὰ μικρὰ γενομένης τῆς δυνάμεως ib. 5.6.32 ; also, little by little, κατὰ μικρὸν ἀεί Ar. V. 702 , cf. Nu. 741 ; opp. συλλήβδην, Pl. R. 344a ; καὶ κατὰ σμ. or μ. ever so little, Id. Sph. 241c , Isoc. 3.10 , D. 2.22 . παρὰ μικρόν within a little, παρὰ μ. ἐλθεῖν c. inf., to be within an ace of doing, E. Heracl. 295 (anap.), cf. Isoc. 7.6 , etc.; παρὰ μ. ἦλθον ἀποθανεῖν Id. 17.42 ; τὸ παρὰ μ. ὥσπερ οὐδὲν ἀπέχειν δοκεῖ Arist. Ph. 197a30 ; but τὸ παρὰ μ. σῴζεσθαι to be only just saved, Id. Rh. 1371b11 , cf. Simp. in Ph. 344.10 ; gradual, imperceptible change, Arist. Pol. 1303a20 ; οὐδὲ παρὰ μ. ἦν κρεῖττον c. inf., Plb. 12.20.7 ; [ ἡ τύχη] παρὰ μ. εἰς ἑκάτερα ποιεῖ μεγάλας ῥοπάς Id. 15.6.8 , cf. Isoc. 4.59 ; but also παρὰ μ. ποιεῖσθαι, ἡγεῖσθαι, to think little of . . , D. 61.51 , Isoc. 5.79 . μετὰ μικρόν a little after, Ev.Matt. 26.73 . besides regul. Comp. and Sup. μικρότερος, -ότατος ( Ar. Eq. 789 , D. Prooem. 48 , etc.), there are the irreg. ἐλάσσων, ἐλάχιστος, from ἐλαχύς, and μείων, μεῖστος, also μειότερος; v. μείων. [ι by nature; ι only in late Poetry, Epigr. ap. Phleg. Fr. 36.17 J. ] (Perh. cf. Lat. mīca, mīcidus, OHG. smāhi, ONorse smár 'little'.)

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: [375] [Περὶ τοῦ διὰ χαλκίτεως ἐμπλαστοῦ φαρμάκου.] Τίνι λόγῳ συνέθηκα τὴν διὰ χαλκίτεως ἔμπλαστρον, ἣν φοινικίνην ὀνομάζω, κολλητικήν τε καὶ συνουλωτικὴν ἑλκῶν καὶ φλεγμονῶν θεραπευτικὴν, ἐπειδὰν τακεῖσα σύστασιν ὑγρᾶς ἔχῃ κηρωτῆς, τοὺς μὲν ἐμπειρικοὺς ἐάσαντες ὁμολογεῖν τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀμαθίαν, ἀποστάντες δὲ καὶ τῶν περὶ τὸν Θεσσαλὸν, ἀγνοούντων τὰ κάλλιστα τῶν ἡυρημένων τοῖς ἰατροῖς φαρμάκων, ἐξ ἐναντίων δυνάμεων συγκείμενα, τὸν λογισμὸν ἀσκεῖτε πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι συντιθέναι φάρμακα ταῖς αὐταῖς ἐμοὶ χρώμενοι μεθόδοις, ἵν’ ἔργῳ καὶ αὐτοὶ πεισθῆτε καὶ τὰ τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ἡυρημένα λογισμῷ συντίθεσθαι πάντα, ληρώδους τῆς τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν περιπτώσεως οὔσης.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [375] [On the plaster-drug made with chalcitis.] As to the reasoning by which I composed the plaster made with chalcitis, which I call phoinikine (the date-plaster) — agglutinative of wounds and cicatrising them, and curative of inflammations, whenever, once melted, it has the consistency of a liquid cerate — leave the Empiricists to confess their own ignorance, and stand apart also from the followers of Thessalus, who are ignorant of the finest of the drugs discovered by physicians, those composed out of opposite powers; and exercise your reasoning so as to be able to compose drugs, using the same methods as I do, in order that you yourselves may be persuaded by actual practice that the drugs discovered by our predecessors were all composed by reasoning, the 'chance encounter' of the Empiricists being nonsense.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [375] [On the plaster drug made with chalcitis.] By what reasoning did I compound the plaster made with chalcitis, which I call the palm plaster (phoinikinē), an agglutinative and cicatrizing remedy for wounds (helkē), and curative of inflammations whenever, once melted, it has the consistency of a liquid cerate? You, leaving the Empiricists to confess their own ignorance, and standing apart also from the followers of Thessalus, who are ignorant of the finest of the drugs discovered by physicians, which are composed of contrary powers, must train your reasoning so that you are able to compound drugs using the same methods as I do.

term_table.greek_sentence: διαφορητικὴν μὲν ἔχει δύναμιν ἔλαιόν τε παλαιὸν καὶ στέαρ, ἀποκρουστικὴν δὲ καὶ στυπτικὴν ἥ τε χαλκῖτις καὶ ὁ τοῦ φοίνικος χυλός.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Old oil and fat have a discutient power, while chalcitis and the juice of the date have a repellent and astringent power.
term_table.english_sentence_B: I must now, then, set out the reasoning behind the composition of the drug before us. Old olive oil and fat have a discutient power, while chalcitis and the juice of the palm have a repellent and astringent power.

term_table.lsj_first_sense_gloss: of the same species or kind
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐκ τούτων οὖν ἐγὼ συνέθηκα φάρμακον, ᾧ πάνυ πολλοὺς ἤδη χρωμένους [376] ἴστε διὰ τὸ τῶν ὁμοειδῶν ἁπάντων ἄμεινον κεκρίσθαι, δι’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἔργων βασανισθέν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: From these, then, I composed a drug which you know very many people already use, [376] because it has been judged better than all those of the same kind, having been tested by the works themselves.
term_table.english_sentence_B: From these, then, I compounded a drug which you know very many people are already [376] using, because it has been judged better than all others of the same kind, having been tested by the results themselves.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μέθοδ-ος, ἡ, (μετά, ὁδός) following after, pursuit, νύμφης μέθοδον ποιεῖσθαι Anon. ap. Rh. 1358a4 ; joined with τέχνη, Id. EN 1094a1 , cf. Phld. Rh. 1.32 S. ; μ. ἔχειν to have a plan or system, Arist. Top. 101a29 ; ἡ περὶ τὸν πίνακα μ. Plu. Rom. 12 . ἡ τοῦ πάντα κινεῖσθαι μ. the doctrine of motion, Pl. Tht. 183c . 'methodic' medicine, ἰητὴρ μεθόδου . . προστάτα Epigr.Gr. 306 (Smyrna), cf. Julian. ap. Gal. 18(1).256 . Rhet., means, τῆς εὑρέσεως, τοῦ κατορθοῦν, τοῦ ἀνεπαχθῶς ἑαυτὸν ἐπαινεῖν, Hermog. Meth. 2 , 22 , 25 . means of recognizing, τῶν στάσεων Id. Stat. 1 , 2 . mode of treating the subject-matter, Id. Id. 1.1 . trick, ruse, Plu. 2.176a : pl., Vett. Val. 242.11 ; μ. ἐρωτικαί Aristaenet. 1.17 ; stratagem, LXX 2 Ma. 13.18 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὁ μὲν γὰρ λόγος εὑρίσκει τὴν σύνθεσιν, ἡ δὲ πεῖρα κρίνει τὴν τῶν εὑρεθέντων ἀρετὴν, ὥστε καὶ τοῖς ἀπείροις λογικῶν μεθόδων πιστεύεσθαι τὰ τεχνικῶς συντεθέντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For reason discovers the composition, but experience judges the excellence of what has been discovered, so that things composed with art are trusted even by those inexperienced in rational methods.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For reason discovers the composition, but experience judges the excellence of what has been discovered, so that even those inexperienced in logical methods come to trust what has been compounded according to the art.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὗς (A), ὗν, gen. ὑός [υ]; or σῦς, σῦν, gen. συός, ὁ and ἡ: Hom. prefers σῦς, and uses ὗς only metri gr.: in Hdt. and Att. ὗς is the prevailing form, as also at Rhodes, IG 12(1).905 , Myconos, SIG 1024.16 (iii/ii B. C.), etc., and ὑῶν ὄρος is an Argive place-name, ib. 56.25 (V B.C.); ὖς Alc. 99 (s.v.l.); both forms in Pi. , v. infr.; ὗς in PCair.Zen. 462.7 (iii B. C.), LXX Le. 11.7 , al. (σῦς only as v. l. in Ps. 79(80).14 ), and Plb. 8.29.4 , 31.14.3 , 34.8.8 (συναγρειον f.l. in 8.26.10 , B. -W. ii Praef. p.lxxvii); but σῦς (acc. σῦν) in IG 5(1).1390.34 , al. (Andania, i B. C.): pl., nom. ὕες, σύες; acc. ὕας, σύας, Att. ὗς Pl. Tht. 166c , Plb. 12.4.5 , 8 , GDI 5633.9 (Clazomenae) ( σῦς Od. 14.107 ); gen. ὑῶν, συῶν; dat. ὑσί ( συσί Il. 5.783 , 7.257 ), but Ep. also ὕεσσι Od. 13.410 , σύεσσι (v. infr.):—the wild swine, of the boar, σῦν ἄγριον ἀργιόδοντα Il. 9.539 , cf. 8.338 , al.; ἀργοτέρῳ συΐ καπρίῳ 11.293 ; ἀγροτέροισι σύεσσιν ἐοικότε 12.146 ; ἀργιόδοντος ὑός 10.264 ; also called σῦς κάπριος or κάπρος, v. sub vocc.; cf. also χλούνης; of the sow, συὸς ληϊβοτείρης Od. 18.29 ; ὗς ἄγριος Hdt. 4.192 , cf. X. Cyr. 1.6.28 , etc.; ὕες ( v.l. ὗς ) ἄγριαι Arist. HA 578a25 . of the domesticated animal, Od. 14.14 ; the hogs being eaten, ὕες θαλέθοντες ἀλοιφῇ Il. 23.32 ; they were fed on acorns, Od. 10.243 ; also on μῆλα πλατανίστινα, Gal. 6.597 ; τοκὰς ὗς sus foeta, Luc. Lex. 6 , cf. Od. 14.16 ; ὗς ἐπίτεξ Alciphr. 3.73 . provs., Βοιωτία ὗς, of stupidity (cf. συοβοιωτοί), Pi. O. 6.90 , cf. Fr. 83 (σύας); ὗς ποτ' Ἀθαναίαν ἔριν ἤρισεν (or more shortly ἡ ὗς τὴν Ἀθηνᾶν, Lat. sus Minervam, Plu. Dem. 11 ), of dunces setting themselves up against wise men, Theoc. 5.23 ; οὐκ ἂν πᾶσα ὗς γνοίη Pl. La. 196d ; ὗς διὰ ῥόδων 'a bull in a china-shop', Crates Com. 4 ; ὗς ἐκώμασε, of arrogant and insolent behaviour, Theognost. Can. 24 ; ὗς ὑπὸ ῥόπαλον δραμεῖται, of one who runs wilfully into destruction, Dinoloch. 14 ; παχὺς ὗς ἔκειτ' ἐπὶ στόμα (cf. βοῦς VIII) Men. 21 ; λύσω τὴν ἐμαυτῆς ὗν I will give my rage vent ('go the whole hog'), Ar. Lys. 684 . = ὕαινα 11 , Epich. 68 , Archestr. Fr. 22.1 . v. ὕσγη. (Cf. Lat. συς, O E. sú, sw-in: perh. I.- E. sū-s fem. 'mother', cf. Skt. sū-s 'mother', sū-te 'bring forth (young)'; change of meaning as in Polish maciora ( 1 ) 'mother', ( 2 ) 'sow', and in Sardinian mardi 'sow', from mater; Skt. sū-s is also masc., and σῦς is difficult.)
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐμάθετε γάρ πως παραπλησίας μὲν εἶναι ἀλλήλοις δυνάμεως τό τε ἔλαιον καὶ τὸ στέαρ τῶν ὑῶν, μαλακτικώτερον βραχὺ καὶ θερμότερον ὂν τῇ δυνάμει τὸ στέαρ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For you have learned, I think, that oil and the fat of pigs are of a faculty similar to one another, the fat being slightly more emollient and hotter in its faculty.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐμάθετε δὲ καὶ ὡς παλαιούμενα λεπτομερέστερά τε καὶ διαφορητικώτερα γίγνεται καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ταῖς μὲν ὀδυνηραῖς φλεγμοναῖς παρηγορικώτερα ﻿ [377] τὰ νέα, ταῖς δὲ μὴ τοιαύταις ὠφελιμώτερα τὰ παλαιά.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀρχομένων δὲ καὶ αὐξανομένων τῶν φλεγμονῶν ἐπικρατεῖν προσήκει τὴν τῶν στυφόντων τε καὶ ψυχόντων φαρμάκων δύναμιν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τηκόμενον εἰς πάχος κηρωτῆς ὑγρᾶς τὸ ἐμπλαστὸν τοῦτο φάρμακον ἱκανῶς πολύχρηστον γίγνεται ποτὲ μὲν οἴνου προσλαμβάνον ἢ ὄξους ἢ ὕδατος, ἔστι δὲ ὅτε δι’ ὠμοτριβοῦς ἐλαίου τηκόμενον ἤ τινος τῶν στύψιν ἐχόντων, οἷόν ἐστι τὸ Σπανόν τε καὶ τὸ Ἰστρικὸν, ἢ διά τινος τῶν γλυκέων ἄνευ στύψεως ἢ διὰ παλαιοῦ.

term_table.greek_sentence: τοῦ στέατος τοὺς ὑμένας ἐξελὼν καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν θλάσας, ὡς εὔτηκτον γενέσθαι μετὰ τοῦτο τῆξον ἐπὶ πυρὸς, εἶτα λαβὼν ἠθμὸν διήθησον, ὡς καθαρὸν αὐτὸ γενέσθαι, μηδὲν ὑμένος ἔχον, ἕλκον σταθμὸν τὰς προειρημένας δύο λίτρας, εἶτα λελειωμένας τὰς δ΄.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Having removed the membranes of the fat and crushed the remainder so that it becomes easy to melt, after this melt it over a fire, then take a strainer and strain it, so that it becomes pure, containing nothing of membrane, drawing in weight the aforesaid two litrai; then you will mix the 4 ounces of chalcitis, finely ground, together with the three litrai of oil, with the fat, adding in also the 3 litrai of litharge, and having united everything in a mortar, put it into the cauldron, stirring with a stick of palm-wood.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Then take a strainer and strain it, so that it becomes clean, with nothing of membrane in it, and weighing the aforesaid two litrai. Then you will mix the 4 ounces of chalcitis, ground smooth, together with the three litrai of oil, into the fat, adding also the 3 litrai of litharge.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Having removed the membranes of the fat and crushed the remainder so that it becomes easy to melt, after this melt it over a fire, then take a strainer and strain it, so that it becomes pure, containing nothing of membrane, drawing in weight the aforesaid two litrai; then you will mix the 4 ounces of chalcitis, finely ground, together with the three litrai of oil, with the fat, adding in also the 3 litrai of litharge, and having united everything in a mortar, put it into the cauldron, stirring with a stick of palm-wood.
term_table.english_sentence_B: When you have united everything in a mortar, put it into the cooking-pot (kakkabē), stirring with a stick of palm wood.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κακκάβη [α] (A), ἡ, three-legged pot (= Χύτρα, Ath. 4.169c ), Ar. Fr. 215 , Antiph. 217.3 , Dorioap. Ath. 8.338a : κάκκαβος, ὁ, Nicoch. 14 , Antiph. 182.4 , 249 : κάκαβος, ἡ, Alex.Trall. 3.7 : κακάβη, ἡ, Gal. 14.309 .
term_table.greek_sentence: λίτρας τῆς λιθαργύρου, καὶ πάντα κατὰ θυείαν ἑνώσας ἔμβαλλε ἐν τῇ κακκάβῃ, κινῶν ξύλῳ φοίνικος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: A single branch of the large ones will suffice for you, so as to use the thick part of the wood for stirring, in the function of the so-called spathe; for thus they name that with which they stir the things being prepared, and we, holding to clarity, shall call it the same as they do.
term_table.english_sentence_B: One of the large branches will suffice you, so that you use the thick part of the wood for stirring, serving the purpose of the so-called spatha.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἁδρός, ά, όν, thick, stout, bulky: of things, χιόνα ἁ. πίπτουσαν ἰδεῖν falling thick, Hdt. 4.31 ; τῶν ἀνθράκων οἱ ἁδρότατοι the most solid, Hp. Mul. 2.133 ; κίονες ἁ. large, D.S. 3.47 ; τοὺς ἁδροτάτους τῶνλέμβων Id. 20.85 :—strong, violent, πόλεμος Ar. Ra. 1099 ; τὰ ἁδρότατατῶν . . συμβάντων Hell.Oxy. 4.1 ; ῥεύματα full, swollen, Arist. Pr. 949b5 ; of raindrops, Id. Mu. 394a31 ( Comp. ); δῆγμα D.S. 1.35 ; δωρεάστε καὶ τιμὰς ἁ. δοῦναι in abundance, Id. 19.86 ; κοιλότης severe deficiency, Phld. Oec. p.71 J. :—of style, powerful, Longin. 40.4 ( Comp. ), cf. Phld. Rh. 1.182 S. ; ἁ. νοήματα dub. in D.H. Comp. 4 ; ἀπειλή Phld. Hom. p.35 O.; τὸ ἁ. the grand style, opp. τὸ ἰσχνόν, Ps.- Plu. Vit.Hom. 72 . Adv., Comp. ἁδροτέρως, διαιτᾶν live more freely, Hp. Aph. 1.7 ; ἁ. φαρμακεύειν ib. 4.9 ; neut. as Adv., ἁδρὸν γελάσαι laugh loud, Antiph. 144 ; ἁδρότερον πιεῖν drink more deeply, Diph. 5 . of persons, fine, well-grown, ἐπεὰν τὸ παιδίον ἁ. γένηται Hdt. 4.180 ; τῷ παιδί, ἐπὴν ἁ. ἔῃ Hp. Genit. 2 ; τῶν παίδων ὅσοι ἁ. Pl. R. 466e ; οἱ -ότεροι the bestgrown, the stronger, Isoc. 12.110 ; οἱ ἁ. chiefs, princes, LXX 4 Ki. 10.6 ; also ἁ. τὴν ψυχήν Democh. 3 ; ἡ κατὰ ψυχὴν ἁ. ὑπεροχή Procl. in Alc. p.94 C. of animals, fine, fat, χοῖρος X. Oec. 17.10 ; λύκος Babr. 101 ; freq. in Com. of flesh, fish, etc., Antiph. 20.5 , 26.21 , Alex. 170 , etc. of fruit or corn, full-grown, ripe, ὅκως εἴη καρπὸς ἁ. Hdt. 1.17 , cf. Arist. Metaph. 1017b8 . ἁ. ῥίζα, = ἀριστολοχεία στρογγύλη , Ps.- Dsc. 3.4 . of an egg, ready to be laid, Arist. HA 559b11 ( Comp. ).—First in Hdt. , never in Trag., rare in Att. ; but the derivs. ἁδροτής, ἁδροσύνη occur in Ep. and ἁδρύνω in Trag.
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀρκέσει δέ σοι κλάδος εἷς τῶν μεγάλων, ὡς τῷ μὲν ἁδρῷ μέρει τοῦ ξύλου χρῆσθαι κινοῦντα, κατὰ τὴν τῆς καλουμένης σπάθης χρείαν· οὕτω γὰρ ὀνομάζουσιν ᾧ κινοῦσι τὰ σκευαζόμενα, καὶ ἡμεῖς τοῦ σαφοῦς ἐχόμενοι καλέσομεν ὡσαύτως αὐτοῖς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: A single branch of the large ones will suffice for you, so as to use the thick part of the wood for stirring, in the function of the so-called spathe; for thus they name that with which they stir the things being prepared, and we, holding to clarity, shall call it the same as they do.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For that is the name they give to the implement with which they stir the things being prepared, and we too, holding to what is clear, shall call it the same as they do.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σπάθ-η, ἡ, any broad blade, of wood or metal: flat wooden blade used by weavers in the upright loom (instead of the comb (κτείς) used in the horizontal), for striking the threads of the woof home, so as to make the web close, A. Ch. 232 , Philyll. 12 , Pl. Ly. 208d ; Dor. acc. pl. σπάθας AP 6.288 ( Leon. ). spattle for stirring anything, Alex. 60 ; esp. for medical purposes, Gal. 13.378 , Heraclid.Tar. ap. eund. 13.812 . blade of an oar, Lyc. 23 . pl., broad ribs, Poll. 2.181 , Ruf. Oss. 25 , and so prob. in Hp. Gland. 14 , PMag.Par. 1.3116 , Paul.Aeg. 3.78 . broad blade of a sword, Χαλκίδικαι σπάθαι Alc. 15.6 ; σπάθῃ κολούων φασγάνου E. HP 2.6.6 , 2.8.4 , Poll. 1.244 . pl., flukes of an anchor, PLond. 3.1164 (h). 9 (iii A.D.). pl.,= ἀγκῶνες 11.1 , in machines, Orib. 49.4.10 .

term_table.greek_sentence: τὸ [379] δὲ συνεχὲς τῷ ἁδρῷ μέρει τοῦ κλάδου περικαθῄρας καὶ τὰς ἑκατέρωθεν ἐκφύσεις τὰς λεπτὰς ἀποτρίψας κατάτεμνε, προπεριξύσας τὸν φλοιὸν, ὅπως ἐμβληθέντα τὰ τμήματα τῷ φαρμάκῳ μεταδῷ τοῦ καθ’ ἑαυτὰ χυλοῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But the part [379] continuous with the thick part of the branch you should clean all around, and, having rubbed off the thin outgrowths on either side, cut it up, having first scraped off the bark all round, so that the pieces, when thrown into the drug, may impart to it the juice within themselves.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: λεπτός, ή, όν, (λέπω) rare in lit. sense, peeled, husked, ῥίμφα τε λέπτ' ἐγένοντο, of barley being threshed out, Il. 20.497 . fine, small, κονίη 23.506 ; κόνις S. Ant. 256 ; τέφρα Ar. Nu. 177 ; λεπτοῖς ἁλσί Alex. 187.5 : freq. in Hp. , διατρήσεις λ. Loc.Hom. 10 , al.; of soil, light, Thphr. HP 1.8.1 . thin, fine, delicate, freq. in Hom. , mostly of garments and the like , ὀθόναι Il. 18.595 ; πέπλοι, φᾶρος, Od. 7.97 , 10.544 ; ἀράχνια 8.280 ; μήρινθος Il. 23.854 ; - ότατος χαλκός 20.275 ; ἔβενος, ἐλέφας, σίδηρος BCH 35.286 (Delos, ii B.C.); ῥινὸς βοός Il. 20.276 ( Sup. ); δέρμα Arist. HA 517b27 ( Sup. ); τρίχες Id. GA 783a4 ( Comp. ); σάρξ E. Med. 1189 ; χαλκὸς καὶ δόνακες Pi. P. 12.25 , cf. E. Med. 949 , Th. 2.49 , etc.; λεπτὰ τὰ πρῴραθεν ἔχειν, of ships, to have the bows thin and weak, Id. 7.36 . of the human figure, mostly in bad sense, thin, lean, Alc. 39 ; opp. παχύς, Hp. Art. 8 ( Comp. ); ἐγὼ δὲ λεπτὴ κἀσθενής Ar. Ec. 539 ; σοφιστῶν λεπτῶν, ἀσίτων Antiph. 122.4 ; λ. καὶ αὐχμῶν Thphr. Char. 26.5 , cf. Ceb. 10 ; λ. χείρ Hes. Op. 497 ; στῆθος Ar. Nu. 1018 (anap.); τράχηλος X. Cyn. 5.30 ; λεπτὸς <ἐκ> τοῖν σκελοῖν Luc. Nav. 2 ; λ. ὑπὸ μεριμνῶν Pl. Amat. 134b ; of animals, X. Cyr. 1.4.11 ; also, slender, taper (opp. παχύς) , δάκτυλος Pl. R. 523d ; ἀπολήγειν εἰς λεπτόν, of the fingers of a statue, Luc. Im. 6 . of space, strait, narrow, εἰσίθμη Od. 6.264 ; ἀταρπός Alcm. 81 ; ἐπὶ λεπτὸν τετάχθαι in a thin line, X. Cyr. 5.4.46 , cf. Plb. 3.115.6 ; οὔτε εὐρεῖαν οὔτε λεπτὴν . . ὁδόν Plu. 2.964c (ap. Porph. Abst. 1.6 ). generally, small, weak, impotent, λεπτὴ μῆτις Il. 10.226 , 23.590 ; ἐλπίς Ar. Eq. 1244 , cf. ὀχέω 11.3 ; ἀσφάλεια D. Ep. 2.20 ; λ. ἴχνη faint traces, X. Cyn. 5.5 ; λ. οὖας, of a child's ear, tiny, Simon. 37.14 ; τὰ λ. τῶν προβάτων small cattle, i.e. sheep and goats, Hdt. 8.137 ; λ. πλοῖα small craft, Id. 7.36 ; ἄκραι λ. small headlands, Id. 8.107 ; λ. κλιμάκια Ar. Pax 69 ; τὸ -ότατον τοῦ χαλκοῦ νομίσματος Plu. Cic. 29 ; λ. χαλκός OGI 485.12 ( Magn. Mae.): without χαλκός, Inscr.Perg. 374 D 7 ; ἀργύριον Ῥόδιον λ. CIG 2693e5 (Mylasa), cf. TAM 2(1).15 (Telmessus); v. infr. 111.2 . Adv. -τῶς, ζῆν poorly, meanly, Men. Mon. 682 : neut. pl. as Adv., λεπτὰ λεύσσω κόραις E. Or. 224 . light, slight, λεπταῖς ὑπαὶ κώνωπος . . ῥιπαῖσι A. Ag. 892 ; λ. πνοαί light breezes, E. IA 813 ; λεπταῖς ἐπὶ ῥοπῇσιν on slight turns of fortune, S. Fr. 555 . of size or quantity, λ. πυρίδια small, Ar. Lys. 1206 ; λ. κύλικες Pherecr. 143.5 (but f.l.): neut. pl. as Adv., λ. τῖλαι 'pluck into small pieces', Theoc. 3.21 . of liquids, thin, γάλα Hp. Vict. 2.46 ; λεπτὰ ἀνεμέειν Id. Coac. 310 ; λ. οἶνος light wine, Luc. Merc.Cond. 18 ; also of food, λ. δίαιται Hp. Aph. 1.4 ; λ. ὀψάρια OGI 484.16 (Pergam.). Adv. -τῶς, διαιτᾶσθαι, διαιτᾶν, Gal. 19.191 , Paul.Aeg. 3.43 . = λεπτομερής , consisting of fine parts, ὅσῳ -ότερον ἀὴρ ὕδατος Arist. Ph. 215b4 , cf. Cael. 303b26 , al. metaph., subtle, refined, νοῦς E. Med. 529 ; -ότεροι μῦθοι ib. 1082 (anap.); - ότατοι λῆροι Ar. Nu. 359 ; πυκνῇ . . λεπτὰ μηχανᾷ φρενί Id. Ach. 445 ; λ. λογιστά Id. Av. 318 ; λ. καὶ ἀκριβής Antipho 3.4.2 ; ἐς τὰς τέχνας παχέες, οὐ λεπτοί Hp. Aër. 24 ; λόγοι λ. . . τρέφουσ' ἐκείνους Alex. 220.8 ; cf. λεπτολόγος. Adv. - τῶς, μεριμνᾶν Lyr.Adesp. 135 ; λ. καὶ πυκνῶς ἐξετάζειν Amphis 33.5 : Comp. -οτέρως Anaxandr. 36 : also κατὰ λεπτόν in detail, PPetr. 2p.118 (iii B.C.), Cic. Att. 2.18.2 , Phryn. PS p.83 B. , Phot. s.v. νιφετός ; cf. κατάλεπτον, καταλεπτολογέω: τὰ κατὰ λεπτόν, title of poems by Aratus, Ach.Tat. Intr.Arat. p.79 M., Str. 10.5.3 ; also of minor poems of Virgil; τῶν κατὰ λεπτὸν πόρων ἀραίωσις, perh. small pores, Gal. 15.201 . rarely of the voice, fine, delicate, Arist. HA 545a7 , Lyc. 687 ; ἁρμονία E. Fr. 773.23 (lyr.): neut. as Adv., λεπτὸν ἀμφιτιττυβίζειν Ar. Av. 235 (lyr.); of sound, λ. ὑποτρύζουσα AP 11.352.5 ( Agath. ); cf. λεπταλέος. of smell, Pl. Ti. 66e ( Comp. ). of persons, οἱ λ. the poor, Plb. 24.7.3 ; λεπτὴν πλέκειν, prov. of poor people, Hsch. ; λεπτὰ ξαίνεις Suid. Subst. λεπτόν (sc. ἔντερον), τό, the small intestine, Hp. Coac. 311 , 449 . (sc. νόμισμα) a very small coin, Ev.Luc. 21.2 , Phot. s.v. ὀβολός ; cf.supr. 1.6 . (sc. κεράμιον) jar, POxy. 920.4 (ii/iii A.D.), PStrassb. 40.48 (vi A.D.); cf. λεπτίον, λεπτοκεραμεύς. Astron. (sc. ἑξηκοστόν), division of a degree, πρῶτα λεπτά, = minutes, δεύτερα λ., = seconds, Gem. 18.11 , 18 ; λεπτά alone, = minutes, PLond. 1.98r . 47 (i/ii A.D.), POxy. 1476 (iii A.D.).

term_table.lsj_entry_text: δυσεπούλωτος, ον, hard to cicatrize, Gal. 6.751 , v.l. in Dsc. 4.41 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὅταν δ’ οὕτως [380] ἑψόμενον ἀμόλυντον γένηται τὸ φάρμακον, αὐτῷ μὲν ἐμπλαστῷ χρήσῃ κατά τε τῶν δυσεπουλώτων ἑλκῶν καὶ τῶν ἐναίμων ἐλαίῳ διατήκων, ἐπὶ τῶν φλεγμαινόντων, ἐν ποδάγραις, ἐν ἀρθρίτισιν, ἐν βουβῶσιν, ἐν φύμασιν, ἐν κατακαύμασιν, ἐν χειμέθλοις, ἐν κατάγμασιν, ἐν θλάσμασιν, ἐν ταῖς ῥευματικαῖς καλουμέναις διαθέσεσιν ἁπάσαις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But when the drug, being boiled in this way, [380] has become non-staining (ἀμόλυντον), you will use it as a plaster both upon ulcers that are hard to cicatrize and upon fresh bleeding wounds; and, melting it down with oil, upon inflamed parts, in podagra, in arthritis, in buboes, in phymata, in burns, in chilblains, in fractures, in contusions, and in all the so-called rheumatic conditions.
term_table.english_sentence_B: When the drug, boiled [380] in this way, has become non-staining, you will use it by itself as a plaster on ulcers that are hard to cicatrise and on bloody ones; dissolved in oil, on inflamed parts, in podagra, in arthritis, in buboes, in phymata, in burns, in chilblains, in fractures, in contusions, and in all the so-called fluxional conditions.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀρχομένων οὖν καὶ αὐξομένων ἔτι τῶν τοιούτων διαθέσεως, ἐπειδὰν τήξῃς τὸ φάρμακον, ἐάσας ἀποψυχθῆναι, καὶ ξύων σπαθομήλῃ τὸ ξυσθὲν ἔμβαλε εἰς θυείαν παραχέων οἴνου καὶ τρίβων ταῖς χερσὶ πρὸς τῇ θυείᾳ, χάριν τοῦ δέξασθαι τὸν οἶνον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: When, then, such conditions (διαθέσεως) are beginning and still increasing, once you have melted the drug, having let it cool and scraping it with a spatula-probe, throw what has been scraped into a mortar, pouring in wine and rubbing it with the hands against the mortar, so that it takes up the wine.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So while such conditions (διαθέσεως, apparently for διαθέσεων) are beginning and still increasing, once you have melted the drug, let it cool. Then scrape it with a spatula-probe, put the scrapings into a mortar, pour in wine, and work it with the hands at the mortar so that it takes up the wine.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὅταν δ’ εἰς τὴν οἰκείαν ἀκμὴν ﻿ [382] ὁ τῆς φλεγμονῆς ὄγκος ἀφίκηται, παραπλησίας ἀλ λήλαις εἶναι χρὴ τὰς δυνάμεις τήν τε ἀποκρουστικὴν καὶ διαφορητικὴν, ἐάν γε μή τις ὀδύνη σφοδρὰ παρηγορικοῦ δέηται φαρμάκου.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δ’ ἀποροίης προσφάτου, διὰ τὴν ὥραν τοῦ ἔτους [385] ἢ τὸ χωρίον οὐδὲν μεῖον ἕξεις ἐπεμβάλλων τὸν ἀποτεθέντα διὰ τοῦ θέρους, οἷος καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ Κρήτης ἐστὶ κομιζόμενος ἡμῖν εἰς Ῥώμην καθ’ ἕκαστον ἔτος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if you should be at a loss for fresh (juice), on account of the season of the year [385] or the locality, you will have no less (benefit) by adding in that which was put away during the summer, such as is the kind brought to us at Rome from Crete every year.

Prose or Com., nor in Hdt. ; younger, S. OC 374 : neut. μεῖον as Adv., less, μ. ἰσχύσειν Διός A. Pr. 510 , cf. Ch. 707 : regul. Adv., μειόνως ἔχειν to be of less value, S. OC 104 , cf. J. AJ 19.2.2 :—also μειότερος, α, ον, A.R. 2.368 , Arat. 43 , AP 14.41 , Man. 2.147 , IG 14.2064 . (μεί-yων, cf. μ<*>νύθω, Lat. minuo, minus.)
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δ’ ἀποροίης προσφάτου, διὰ τὴν ὥραν τοῦ ἔτους [385] ἢ τὸ χωρίον οὐδὲν μεῖον ἕξεις ἐπεμβάλλων τὸν ἀποτεθέντα διὰ τοῦ θέρους, οἷος καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ Κρήτης ἐστὶ κομιζόμενος ἡμῖν εἰς Ῥώμην καθ’ ἕκαστον ἔτος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if you should be at a loss for fresh (juice), on account of the season of the year [385] or the locality, you will have no less (benefit) by adding in that which was put away during the summer, such as is the kind brought to us at Rome from Crete every year.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If you lack fresh [henbane], on account of the season of the year [385] or the locality, you will have no less [benefit] by adding instead that which has been stored through the summer, such as is also brought to us to Rome from Crete every year.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μανδραγόρ-ας, ου or α, ὁ, mandrake (μ. ἄρρην = Mandragora officinalis, μ. θῆλυς, = M. autumnalis, Dsc. 4.75 ), Thphr. HP 9.8.8 , CP 6.4.5 , etc.; μανδραγόρου ῥίζα Hp. Loc.Hom. 39 ; ὁ μ. τοὺς ἀνθρώπους κοιμίζει X. Smp. 2.24 ; μανδραγόρᾳ ἢ μέθῃ συμποδίσαι Pl. R. 488c ; μανδραγόραν πεπωκόσιν ἐοίκαμεν D. 10.6 ; ἐκ μανδραγόρου, ὑπὸ μανδραγόρα καθεύδειν, Luc. Dem.Enc. 36 , Tim. 2 . belladonna, Atropa Belladonna, Thphr. HP 6.2.9 . epith. of Zeus, Hsch.
term_table.greek_sentence: ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον τούτου τὸν χυλὸν τοῦ μανδραγόρου μιγνύων, ἀνώδυνον ἐργάσῃ τὸ φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And still more than this, by mixing in the juice of mandrake you will make the drug anodyne.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And still more than this, by mixing in the juice of mandrake you will make the drug anodyne.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὀστράκ-ινος, η, ον, earthen, made of clay, of vessels, Hp. Nat.Mul. 34 , al., Pl.Com. 114 , AP 7.645 ( Crin. ), 11.74 ( Nicarch. ), 2 Ep.Ti. 2.20 , 2 Ep.Cor. 4.7 , PLond. 3.1177.95 (ii A. D.). like earthenware, ὀστράκινατὸ δέρμα, = ὀστρακόδερμα , v.l. in Luc. Lex. 6 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἴστε δ’ ὅτι καὶ οὗτος ἀπὸ Κρήτης κομίζεται κάλλιστος ἐν ὀστρακίνοις ποτηρίοις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Know that this too is brought from Crete, of the finest quality, in earthenware cups.
term_table.english_sentence_B: You know that this too is brought from Crete, of the finest quality, in earthenware cups.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀρκεῖ δὲ μίαν οὐγγίαν μῖξαι τοῦ χυλοῦ, λίτρᾳ ἐλαίου τῆς τηκομένης ἐμπλάστρου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It suffices to mix one ounce of the juice to a pound of oil of the plaster that is being melted; and at times you may put in more, and at times less, according to the need of the condition.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It suffices to mix one ounce of the juice with a litra of the oil of the plaster being melted.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κατά-πτωσις, εως, ἡ, fall, Hp. Art. 42 ; ἐξ ὀχήματος Gal. 7.560 ; λίθου Simp. in Ph. 261.17 . Medic., collapse, ἡ συγκοπή ἐστι κ. δυνάμεως Gal. 10.837 ; of epileptic seizures, Alex.Aphr. Pr. 2.64 , cf. Vett.Val. 38.13 (pl.): hence of a spell which induces a trance, PMag.Par. 1.850 . downfall, calamity, LXX 3 Ma. 2.14 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὅσα δὲ ἐκ καταπτώσεως ἐθλάσθη μέρη τοῦ σώματος ἢ πληγέντα ξύλῳ καὶ λίθῳ, κᾂν ἐκχύμωμά τι γένηται, κατὰ τὰς ἀρχὰς εὐθέως ἐπιτιθέναι χρὴ τὸ τετηκὸς φάρμακον, ὡς εἴρηται, μιχθέντος οἴνου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: As for those parts of the body that have been bruised from a fall, or struck with wood or stone, even if some ecchymoma arises, one must at the very beginning immediately apply the melted drug, as has been said, with wine mixed in.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Parts of the body that have been bruised by a fall, or struck with wood or stone, even if some ecchymosis occurs, should have the melted drug applied immediately at the beginning, as has been said, with wine mixed in.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: προσήκει δὲ κατὰ τὴν τρίτην ἡμέραν ἢ πάντως γε τὴν τετάρτην, ἐὰν ἀφλέγμαντον εἴη τὸ μόριον, ἀφαιρεῖν μὲν τὸν οἶνον, ἐλαίῳ δὲ τήκειν παλαιῷ τὴν ἔμπλαστρον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But it is fitting on the third day, or at all events the fourth, if the part should be free of inflammation, to remove the wine and to melt the plaster with old oil.
term_table.english_sentence_B: On the third day, or at any rate the fourth, if the part is free of inflammation, one should remove the wine and melt the plaster in old oil.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: δυσδια-φόρητος, ον, hard to disperse or dissipate, Gal. 11.119 . hardly evaporating, Id. 10.657 ; not excreting readily, Id. 17(1).188 ; διάθεσις Alex.Trall. 8.2 ; cf. δυσδιαχώρητος.
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐὰν γὰρ ἐπὶ πλέον στύφηται τὰ ἐκχυμώματα δυσδιαφόρητα γίνεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if the ecchymomata are astringed further, they become difficult to disperse.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if the ecchymoses are astringed further, they become hard to disperse.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐρυσί-πελας, πέλατος, τό, erysipelas, Hp. VM 19 (pl.), Prog. 23 , Aph. 5.23 , Gal. 10.949 , Orib. 45.1.3 (pl.), Gp. 12.23.5 (pl.), etc.
term_table.greek_sentence: τούτῳ τῷ φαρμάκῳ καὶ πρὸς ἐρυσιπέλατα χρῶμαι καὶ μάλιστα [386] φλεγμονώδη καὶ πολὺ δὴ μᾶλλον ἔτι πρὸς τὰς ἐρυσιπελατώδεις φλεγμονάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I use this drug also for erysipelata, and especially [386] those of a phlegmonous character, and still much more for erysipelatous phlegmonai.
term_table.english_sentence_B: This drug I also use for erysipelases, and especially [386] for phlegmonous ones, and still much more for erysipelatous inflammations.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐρυσι-πελατώδης, ες, of the nature of ἐρυσίπελας, οἴδημα Hp. VC 20 ; φλεγμοναί Dsc. 1.26 ; διάθεσις Ruf. ap. Orib. 8.24.16 . Adv. -δῶς, ἔχειν Gal. 18(1).448 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τούτῳ τῷ φαρμάκῳ καὶ πρὸς ἐρυσιπέλατα χρῶμαι καὶ μάλιστα [386] φλεγμονώδη καὶ πολὺ δὴ μᾶλλον ἔτι πρὸς τὰς ἐρυσιπελατώδεις φλεγμονάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I use this drug also for erysipelata, and especially [386] those of a phlegmonous character, and still much more for erysipelatous phlegmonai.
term_table.english_sentence_B: This drug I also use for erysipelases, and especially [386] for phlegmonous ones, and still much more for erysipelatous inflammations.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὠμο-τριβής, ές, pressed raw, ὠ. ἔλαιον oil from unripe olives, preferred for many purposes, Thphr. Od. 15 , Dsc. 1.30 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν ἀρχῇ μὲν οὖν ἐπιτίθημι τήκων αὐτὸ ῥοδίνῳ δι’ ὠμοτριβοῦς ἐλαίου καὶ ἀνάλου σκευασθέντι, κάλλιστον μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ἐρυσιπέλατα τὸ τοιοῦτον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At the beginning, then, I apply it after melting it in rose-oil prepared from oil of unripe olives (omotribes) and unsalted; for such oil is best for erysipelata.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At the beginning, then, I apply it melted in rose oil prepared from omotribes oil (oil of unripe olives) without salt; for such an oil is the finest for erysipelases.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: θυεία, Ion. θυγατρο-είη Nic. Th. 91 : ἡ:— mortar, Ar. Nu. 676 , Ra. 124 , al., Lys. Fr. 62a . cup of the cottabus, Pl.Com. 46.3 .—Later θυία, θυΐα, Ph. Bel. 88.49 , Dsc. 2.76.3 and 4 ; in the sense of oil-press, PFay. 42 (a) i 10 (ii A.D.): θυίη [ι], Androm. ap. Gal. 14.41 : θυεῖον, τό, PLond. 2.193.23 (ii A.D.). θύεια, v. θυία 1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τακέντι δ’ οὕτως αὐτῷ μιγνύσθω κατὰ τὴν θυείαν, ἀναφυρόμενός τε καὶ δευόμενος ἀκριβῶς ὅλος δι’ ὅλου στρυχνοῦ χυλὸς ἢ εἰ μὴ τοῦτο παρείη ψυλλίου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And when it has been thus melted, let there be mixed with it in the mortar, kneaded in and thoroughly soaked through whole and entire, juice of strychnos, or, if this is not available, of psyllion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: With it, once melted in this way, let there be mixed in the mortar the juice of strychnos (nightshade), being kneaded in and moistened precisely, wholly through the whole; or, if this is not at hand, that of psyllion (fleawort).

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὄμφαξ, ακος , ἡ (ὁ Plu. 2.138e , 648f , Gp. 4.15.13 ), unripe grape (cf. Dsc. 5.5 ), πάροιθε δέ τ' ὄμφακές εἰσιν ἄνθος ἀφιεῖσαι Od. 7.125 ; ὅτ' ὄ. αἰόλλονται Hes. Sc. 399 : sg. as collective, ὅταν δὲ τεύχῃ Ζεὺς ἀπ' ὄμφακος πικρᾶς οἶνον A. Ag. 970 ; so freq. in Hp., Ulc. 12 ,Acut.(Sp.) 65 , al., cf. Plu. 2.648f ; εἶτ' ἦμαρ αὔξει μέσσον ὄμφακος τύπον S. Fr. 255.5 ; also of other fruits, as olives, Poll. 5.67 . metaph., young girl not yet ripe for marriage, AP 5.19 ( Honest. ), 12.205 ( Strat. ), JRS 18.30 (Tembris) ; τί τρυγᾷς ὄμφακας ἡλικίης ; (epitaph of a boy, addressed to Pluto) IG 14.769 (Naples). the unripe hard breasts of a young girl, ὄμφακα μαζοῦ Tryph. 34 ; but ὄμφακι μαζῷ, as Adj., Nonn. D. 1.71 , 48.957 ; cf. ὀμφάκιον 11 . ὄμφακας βλέπειν look sour grapes, look sour (cf. βλέπω II), Com.Adesp. 877 : hence τὰς ὀφρῦς σχάσασθε καὶ τὰς ὄ. your scornful brows and sourgrape looks, Pl.Com. 32 ; cf. ὀμφακίας 11 . prov., ὑγιέστερος ὄμφακος Com.Adesp. 910 . a gem, used for seals, Thphr. Lap. 30 . [Always α, since στόμφακα has been restored by Gaisf. in Ar. Fr. 624 .]
term_table.greek_sentence: θέρους δὲ ὄντος καὶ ὁ τῆς ὄμφακος μετὰ τοῦ τῆς ἀνδράχνης ἤ ἀειζώου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And when it is summer, also the juice of unripe grape (omphax) together with that of purslane or houseleek.
term_table.english_sentence_B: When it is summer, also the juice of the unripe grape together with that of purslane or of aeizoon (houseleek).

term_table.greek_sentence: ἄριστον οὖν ἐστιν ἐκθλίψαντα τὸν τῆς ὄμφακος χυλὸν ἐπιβάλλειν ἐν ὅλμῳ κεκομμένης τῇ ἀνδράχνῃ καὶ οὕτως αὖθις κόπτειν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is best, therefore, after pressing out the juice of unripe grape, to pour it upon the purslane that has been pounded in a mortar, and so to pound it again; then, when the mixture of both has been thoroughly unified, to press out the juice.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Best, therefore, is to press out the juice of the unripe grape and pour it onto purslane that has been pounded in a pounding-mortar, and so pound it again; then, when the mixture of both has been precisely united, press out the juice.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἄμφω, τώ, τά, τώ, also οἱ, αἱ , τά; gen. ἀμφοῖν S. Ph. 25 , etc., dat. ἀμφοῖν Aj. 1264 , etc.:—both, of individuals, Il. 1.363 ; of armies or nations, 2.124 :— Hom. uses only nom. and acc.: from Hom. downwards freq. with pl. Noun or Verb, Il. 2.767 , 7.255 , etc.; ἐξ ἀμφοῖν, = ἐξ ἀλλήλοιν , S. OC 1425 : sts. indecl., h.Cer. 15 , Arist. Top. 118a28 , Theoc. 17.26 , A.R. 1.165 . (For the root cf. ἀμφί.)
term_table.greek_sentence: εἶθ’ ὅταν ἀκριβῶς ἑνωθῇ τὸ μικτὸν ἐξ ἀμφοῖν ἐκθλίβειν τὸν χυλόν.

term_table.english_sentence_B: Best, therefore, is to press out the juice of the unripe grape and pour it onto purslane that has been pounded in a pounding-mortar, and so pound it again; then, when the mixture of both has been precisely united, press out the juice.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δὲ καὶ τῶν τοῦ μανδραγόρου ﻿ [387] μήλων ἀκμαίων ὄντων ἐκθλίψετε πρόσφατον χυλὸν, ἐπιτηδειότερον ἐργάσεσθε τὸ φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And if you also press out fresh juice from the apples of the mandrake [387] when they are at their peak, you will make the drug more suitable.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And if you also press out fresh juice from the apples of the mandrake [387] when they are ripe, you will make the drug more suitable.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μηκών-ειος, α, ον, flavoured with opium, ἄρτοι Philostr. Gym. 44 . μηκών-ειον, τό, opium, S.E. P. 1.81 , Sch. Nic. Al. 434 . v. μηκώνιον .
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ ὑοσκυάμου δὲ χυλὸν εἴωθα μιγνύειν αὐτῷ καί ποτε καὶ μηκώνειον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I am also accustomed to mix henbane juice with it, and sometimes mekoneion as well; this is the name given to the sap of the poppy.
term_table.english_sentence_B: I am also accustomed to mix in juice of henbane, and sometimes poppy juice (mēkōneion) as well; for this is the name given to the sap of the poppy.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μήκων, Dor. , Arc. μάκ-, Theoc. 7.157 , IG 5(2).514.16 (Lycosura, ii B. C.): ωνος , ἡ (ὁ Arist. (v. infr. 11.2 ), Polem.Hist. 88 , Polyaen. 8.6.1 ):— poppy, esp. opium poppy, Papaver somniferum, μήκων δ' ἑτέρωσε κάρη βάλεν ἐνὶ κήπῳ Il. 8.306 , cf. Ar. Av. 160 , Thphr. HP 1.12.2 (s. v.l.), Theoc.l.c.; μάκωνσι λευκαῖς IGl.c.; μ. ἥμερος, κηπευτή, Dsc. 4.64 , Gal. 6.548 ; μ. Ἡρακλεία frothy poppy, Silene venosa, Thphr. HP 9.12.5 ; μ. ἀφρώδης Dsc. 4.66 ; μ. κερατῖτις horned poppy, Glaucium flavum, Thphr. HP 9.12.3 , Dsc. 4.65 (but = λεοντοπέταλον , Ps.- Dsc. 3.96 ); μ. μέλαινα corn poppy, Papaver Rhoeas, Thphr. HP 9.11.9 , Dsc. 4.64 (μέλας Ps.- Dsc. ibid.); μ. ῥοιάς P. hybridum, Thphr. HP 9.12.4 , Dsc. 4.63 ; μ. ἀγρία, = μ. μέλαινα , ib. 64 ; μ. ἀγριωτέρα windrose, Papaver argemone, ibid. a single poppy-seed, Archim. Aren. 2.4 ; collectively, μ. ἁδρά Hp. Mul. 2.192 ; μ. μεμελιτωμένη Th. 4.26 ; ὀπὸς μήκωνος opium, Asclep. ap. Gal. 14.138 , etc. poppy-head, Thphr. (Etym. dub.; OHG. māgo, Germ. mohn, OSlav.makû are prob. borrowed.)
term_table.greek_sentence: ὀνομάζεται δὲ οὕτως ὁ τῆς μήκωνος ὀπός.
