term_table.lsj_entry_text: πρᾶος, ον, also πραΰς, Ion. πρηΰς, εῖα , ΰ:—πρᾶος supplies sg. in Att. , Trag., and Com., exc. that the fem. is always πραεια (πρᾶος as fem. only in Plu. 2.168d ); but sg. πραΰς, Ion. πρηΰς, is used in Ep. and Lyr. (also in X. and usu. in LXX , Plb. , etc.):—pl., nom. πρηέες Hp. Epid. 1.10 , πρηεῖς AP 5.208 ( Posidipp. or Asclep. ), πρᾶοι Pl. R. 562d , etc.; fem. πρηεῖαι AP 6.244 ( Crin. ); neut. πραέα X. Oec. 15.4 , Eq. 9.10 , etc., πρᾶα Arist. HA 488b22 , f.l. in Ph. 2.351 ; gen. πραέων X. An. 1.4.9 ; dat. πραέσι Pl. Lg. 888a , 930a , fem. πραίαις written for πραείαις IG 7.3101 (Lebad., iii A.D.); acc. πραεῖς Plb. 18.37.7 , πράους Isoc. 3.55 : Comp. πραότερος Lys. 20.21 , πραΰτερος Epich. 153 , Pl. Ti. 85a , etc., Ion. πρηΰτ- Hdt. 2.181 : Sup. πραότατος Pl. Phd. 116c , etc., πραΰτατος Syria 5.337 (Sidon); Ep. and Ion. πρηΰτατος A.R. 2.937 , AP 6.349 ( Phld. ); πράϋστος MAMA 1.237 (Phrygia). (The ι subscr. is freq. written in codd., but Πρᾶος is written in IG 22.1928.20 (pr. n., iv B.C.), IGRom. 4.504 (Pergam.), cf. Phot., Et.Gud. 478.31 ; πραύτερος is found once in codd., Pl. Ti. l.c. (proved wrong by πραΰς Com.Adesp.in Gött. Nachr. 1922.31 , πραέα (neut. pl.) in PCair.Zen. 33.12 (iii B.C.), πραέως UPZ 144.6 (ii B.C.), and by the absence of iota in Ion. πρηΰς)):—mild, soft, gentle (not in Il. or Od. ): of things, πρηῢ σέλας H.Hom. 8.10 ; πραῢς ὄαρος Pi. P. 4.136 ; mild, πυρετοί Hp.l.c.; ἰητρείη πρηεῖα Id. Art. 69 ; of sound, soft, gentle, τὴν φωνὴν πραοτέραν ποιοῦνται X. Smp. 1.10 ; ἀνέμων πρηΰτατε Ζέφυρε AP 6.349 ( Phld. ); ὠδῖνες ib. 244 ( Crin. ); κέντρον ib. 229 (Id.). of persons, mild, gentle, meek, πραῢς ἀστοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 ; πᾶσιν ἵλεώς τε καὶ πρᾶος Pl. R. 566e ; πρὸς τοὺς οἰκείους π. ib. 375c ; π. τὸ ἦθος Id. Phdr. 243c ; π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Id. Euthd. 303d ; esp. after having been angry, Hdt. 2.181 ( Comp. ); ὁ θὴρ ὅδ' ἡμῖν π., of Dionysus, E. Ba. 436 ; of a horse, gentle, ἀλλήλοις πραότεροι X. Cyr. 2.1.29 ; of other animals, tame, ἰχθύων μεγάλων καὶ πραέων Id. An. 1.4.9 , cf. Arist. HA 488b22 ; ζῷα . . πραέα πρὸς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους X. Oec. 15.4 : prov., πραΰτερος μολόχας Epich. 153 ; also, τόπος ἡμερώτερος καὶ πραότερος Isoc. 9.67 . of actions, feelings, etc., mild, τιμωρίαι πραότεραι Pl. Lg. 867b ; πραότεραι ἡδοναί ib. 815e ; λόγοι, ἤθη, φύσις, ib. 888a , 930a , R. 375c ; ὄσσοισι πρηέσιν δέρκευ BMus.Inscr. 921b8 (Branchidae, i/ii A.D.); τὰ πραέα caresses, X. Eq. 9.10 ; πραότερα πάσχειν Pl Cri. 49b . making mild, taming, φάρμακον πραῢ τείνων ἀμφὶ γένυι, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; προκινεῖν αὐτὸν [τὸν ἵππον] ὡς πραοτάτοις σημείοις X. Eq. 9.3 . Adv. πράως, mildly, gently, πράως πείθειν τινά, φέρειν τι, Pl. R. 589c , Cri. 43b ; πράως ἔχειν πρός τι Id. Ly. 211e ; πράως λέγειν τὸ πάθος to speak lightly of it, X. An. 1.5.14 ; πράως διακεῖσθαι, opp. ὀργίζεσθαι, D. 21.183 ; πράως, μὴ πικρῶς Id. 18.265 ; in physical sense, gently, Orib. Fr. 134 : Comp. , πραότερον προδιδάσκειν, κολάζειν, Pl. Grg. 489d , Phd. 94d ; πραοτέρως ( v.l. -υτέρως ) ἔχειν τινί J. AJ 17.6.4 : Sup. , φέρειν . . ὡς πραότωτα Pl. term_table.english_sentence_A: And in this way it would become milder and more flesh-producing, more adhesive and more widely useful.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And in this way it would become milder and more flesh-producing, more adhesive and of more manifold use.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐμπλαστρώδης, ες, like a plaster, Dsc. Eup. 1.196 , Gal. 12.512 , 13.396 ; ἐμ-τώδης, Antyll. ap. Orib. Syn. 2.60.36 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐπαινεῖν δὲ χρὴ τὴν τοῦ λιβάνου μίξιν, εἰς σύστασιν ἐμπλαστρώδη βοηθοῦντος· ἀνώδυνός τε γάρ ἐστι καὶ πεπτικός.
term_table.english_sentence_A: One must praise the admixture of frankincense, which helps towards a plaster-like consistency; for it is both pain-relieving and concoctive.
term_table.english_sentence_B: One must praise the admixture of the frankincense, since it helps towards a plaster-like consistency; for it is both anodyne and concoctive.

Smp. 1.10 ; ἀνέμων πρηΰτατε Ζέφυρε AP 6.349 ( Phld. ); ὠδῖνες ib. 244 ( Crin. ); κέντρον ib. 229 (Id.). of persons, mild, gentle, meek, πραῢς ἀστοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 ; πᾶσιν ἵλεώς τε καὶ πρᾶος Pl. R. 566e ; πρὸς τοὺς οἰκείους π. ib. 375c ; π. τὸ ἦθος Id. Phdr. 243c ; π. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Id. Euthd. 303d ; esp. after having been angry, Hdt. 2.181 ( Comp. ); ὁ θὴρ ὅδ' ἡμῖν π., of Dionysus, E. term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν ἡμῖν οὖν ἐστι καὶ σφοδρότερον ἐργάζεσθαι καὶ πρᾳότερον ﻿ [478] αὐτὸ, μιγνύουσι ἤτοι πλέον ἢ ἔλαττον ὄξους, ὡσαύτως δὲ δριμύτερον ἢ ἀδηκτότερον.

term_table.english_sentence_A: It is better, in the composition, to grind the verdigris with sharp vinegar for several days in a hot sun; for its biting quality will be mitigated, while nothing of its power will be diminished.

term_table.greek_sentence: μεμνῆσθαι γὰρ ὑμᾶς νομίζω καὶ τούτου πολλάκις εἰρημένου τῶν μὲν ἰσχυρῶν φαρμάκων, ὁποῖός ἐστιν ὅ τε ἰὸς καὶ τὸ μίσυ καὶ ἡ χαλκῖτις καὶ τὸ σῶρυ καὶ ἡ λεπὶς ἥ τε χάλκανθος ἐν ὄξει λειουμένων ἡμέραις πλείοσι, τὴν μὲν δῆξιν ἀμβλύνεσθαι, τὴν δ’ ἀρετὴν αὐξάνεσθαι.

term_table.greek_sentence: προσέρχεται δέ τι καὶ ἄλλο χρηστὸν ἐν ταῖς τοιαύταις παρασκευαῖς τῶν φαρμάκων, ἀκριβῶς γὰρ κατεργασθέντα διεξέρχεται τοὺς κατὰ τὸ σῶμα πόρους, μηδαμόθεν κατὰ τὴν ὁδοιπορίαν ἰσχόμενα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο, κᾂν ᾖ θερμότερα φύσει, χωρὶς τοῦ δάκνειν ἐνεργεῖ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And there accrues also another benefit in such preparations of drugs: for having been thoroughly worked up, they pass through the pores in the body, being held back nowhere on their journey, and for this reason, even if they are hotter by nature, they act without biting.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And there accrues also another benefit in such preparations of drugs: for, when thoroughly processed, they pass through the pores throughout the body, being held back nowhere on their passage, and for this reason, even if they are hotter by nature, they act without biting.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: δῆξις, εως, ἡ, (δάκνω) bite, biting, Arist. HA 623a1 ; δήξιες σπλάγχνων gnawings, Hp. VM 19 : metaph., of mental anguish, pangs, Zeno Stoic. 1.51 (pl.), Chrysipp.ib. 3.119 , Phld. D. 3 . Fr. 22 ; also, biting jokes, Plu. Lyc. 14 .
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ τῶν χυμῶν οὖν αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ σῶμα γεννωμένων οἱ μὲν λεπτοὶ διαπνέονται ῥᾳδίως ἄνευ δήξεως, οἱ παχύτεροι δὲ κατεχόμενοί τε καὶ σφηνούμενοι λυποῦσιν, ὅταν ὦσι δακνώδεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And so too of the humours themselves that are generated in the body, the thin ones are easily dispersed by transpiration without bitingness, whereas the thicker ones, being retained and wedged in, cause distress, when they are biting.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So too, of the humours themselves that are generated in the body, the thin ones are readily dispersed by transpiration without biting, whereas the thicker ones, being retained and wedged in, cause distress whenever they are biting.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὁ δ’ αὐτὸς λόγος ἐστὶ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν καυθέντων μεταλλικῶν φαρμάκων, ἀλλ’ ἐκεῖνα μὲν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς ὁμιλίας διασώζει τι δακνῶδες, ὃ κατὰ τὰς πλύσεις ἀποθέμενα παντάπασι ἄδηκτα γίνεται.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀγαθός [αγ], ή, όν, Lacon. ἀγασός Ar. Lys. 1301 , Cypr. ἀζαθός GDI 57 :— good: of persons, well-born, gentle, opp. κακός, δειλός, οἷά τε τοῖς ἀγαθοῖσι παραδρώωσι χέρηες Od. 15.324 , cf. Il. 1.275 ; ἀφνειός τ' ἀ. τε Il. 13.664 , cf. Od. 18.276 ; πατρὸς δ' εἴμ' ἀγαθοῖο, θεὰ δέ με γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 21.109 , cf. Od. 4.611 ; κακὸς ἐξ ἀ. Thgn. 190 , cf. 57 sq.; πραῢς ἀστοῖς, οὐ φθονέων ἀγαθοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 , cf. 2.96 , 4.285 ; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστοι; οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀ. κτλ. S. El. 1082 ; οἵ τ' ἀ. πρὸς τῶν ἀγενῶν κατανικῶνται Id. Fr. 84 ; τοὺς εὐγενεῖς γὰρ κἀγαθοὺς . . φιλεῖ Ἄρης ἐναίρειν ib. 649 , cf. E. Alc. 600 , al.: ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν Pl. Phdr. 274a :—in political sense, aristocrats, esp. in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (v. sub καλοκἀγαθός). brave, valiant, since courage was attributed to Chiefs and Nobles, Il. 1.131 , al.; τῷ κ' ἀγαθὸς μὲν ἔπεφν', ἀγαθὸν δέ κεν ἐξενάριξεν 21.280 ; cf. Hdt. 5.109 , etc. good, capable, in reference to ability, ἀ. βασιλεύς Il. 3.179 ; ἰητήρ 2.732 ; θεράπων 16.165 , 17.388 ; πύκτης Xenoph. 2.15 ; ἰητρός Hp. Prog. 1 ; προβατογνώμων A. Ag. 795 ; ἄρχοντες Democr. 266 : freq. with qualifying words, ἀ. ἐν ὑσμίνῃ Il. 13.314 ; βοὴν ἀ. 2.408 , 563 , al.; πύξ Od. 11.300 ; βίην Il. 6.478 ; γνώμην S. OT 687 ; πᾶσαν ἀρετήν Pl. Lg. 899b , cf. Alc. 1.124e ; τέχνην Id. Prt. 323b ; τὰ πολέμια, τὰ πολιτικά, Hdt. 9.122 , Pl. Grg. 516b , etc.: more rarely c. dat., ἀ. πολέμῳ X. Oec. 4.15 : with Preps., ἄνδρες ἀ. περὶ τὸ πλῆθος Lys. 13.2 ; εἴς τι Pl. Alc. 1.125a ; πρός τι Id. R. 407e : c. inf., ἀ. μάχεσθαι Hdt. 1.136 ; ἱππεύεσθαι 1.79 ; ἀ. ἱστάναι good at weighing, Pl. Prt. 356b . good, in moral sense, first in Thgn. 438 , cf. Heraclit. 104 , S. El. 1082 , X. Mem. 1.7.1 , Pl. Ap. 41d , etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος Democr. 247 : freq. with other Adjs., ὁ πιστὸς κἀ. S. Tr. 541 ; δικαίων κἀ. ib. 1050 :—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα Id. Ant. 31 . ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, Pl. Prt. 311a , etc. ἀ. δαίμων, v. sub δαίμων; ἀ. τύχη, v. sub τύχη; ἀ. θεός = Lat. bona dea, Plu. Caes. 9 , Cic. 19 . of things, good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη . . ἀ. κουροτρόφος Od. 9.27 , etc.; ἀ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει X. Cyn. 13.17 : c. gen., εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀ. good for it, Id. Mem. 3.8.3 ; ἑλκῶν Thphr. HP 9.11.1 . of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347 ; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, Il. 9.102 ; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, 11.789 ; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204 :—ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so<*> Il. 7.282 , 24.130 , Od. 3.196 , etc. morally good, πρῆξις Democr. 177 ; ἔργα Emp. 112.2 , cf. Ep.Rom. 2.7 , etc. ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις X. Cyr. 5.3.20 ; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι Id. Mem. 2.4.2 , cf. Ar. Ra. 74 , etc; as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, Men. Sam. 28 :— ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on . . , Th. 3.68 , Lys. 13.92 ; ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, Th. 5.27 , X. Cyr. 7.4.3 ; ἐπ' ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις Ar. Ra. 1487 ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀ. for no good end, Th. 1.131 ; ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος X. HG 5.2.35 :—in pl., ἡ ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά PFlor. 21.10 (iii A.D.):—τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, Epich. 171.5 , cf. Pl. R. 506b , 508e , Arist. Metaph. 1091a31 , etc.:—in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, Hdt. 2.172 , Lys. 13.91 , X. Mem. 1.2.63 , etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν fare well, Ar. Av. 1706 ; also, good things, dainties, Thgn. 1000 , Ar. Ach. 873 , etc.: good qualities, τοῖς ἀ., οἷς ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ Isoc. 8.32 , cf. Democr. 37 ; good points, of a horse, εἰ τἄλλα πάντα ἀ. ἔχοι, κακόπους δ' εἴη X. Eq. 1.2 . Comp. and Sup. are usu. supplied from other stems, viz. Comp. ἀμείνων, ἀρείων<*> βελτίων, κρείσσων ʽκάρρωνʼ, λωΐων (λώʽωνʼ), Ep. βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος:— Sup. ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος (λῷστος), Ep. βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος:— later, reg. Comp. ἀγαθώτερος LXX Jd. 11.25 , 15.2 , D.S. 8 Fr. 12 , Plot. 5.5.9 , Diod.Rh. p.53.9H. : Sup. ἀγαθώτατος D.S. 16.85 , Hld. 5.15 , etc. ( -ότατος POxy. 1757.26 (ii A.D.)). Adv. usually εὖ, q.v.: ἀγαθῶς Hp. Off. 9 , Arist. Rh. 1388b6 , LXX 1 Ki. 20.7 . (Etym. dub. ( ὅτι ἄγει ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ὀρθὸν βίον Stoic. 3.49 ); perh. cognate with ἄγαμαι, hence admirable.)

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: τὴν γοῦν προκειμένην ἔμπλαστρον, εἰ τήξας μετὰ ῥοδίνου χρῷο, χρησίμη μὲν ἐπὶ ῥυπαρῶν τε καὶ ὑγρῶν ἔσται ἑλκῶν, δακνώδης δ’ ἐπὶ τῶν ἀπεριστάτων, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο δεήσει μιγνύειν αὐτῇ κηρωτὴν ὑγρὰν ἐκ κηροῦ καὶ ῥητίνης γεγονυῖαν ἤτοι διὰ ῥοδίνου τετηγμένην ἢ δι’ ἐλαίου.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὕτως δὲ καὶ τὸ μὲν ἁλῶν ἔχον, εἰς ὅσον ἂν ἐκείνων μεταλάβῃ, θερμαντικώτερόν τε καὶ ξηραντικώτερον τοῦ μὴ προσλαβόντος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So too the oil containing salt, to the extent that it has taken a share of it, is more heating and more drying than that which has not received any; while the oil with tender shoots of olive, which they call thalloi, is more astringent.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So too the oil that contains salt, in proportion to how much of it it has taken up, is more heating and more drying than the oil that has not taken any in.

term_table.english_sentence_B: And that which [contains] tender shoots of the olive, which they call thalloi, is more astringent.

term_table.english_sentence_B: If, then, someone keeps these things always ready in memory, and remembers, as I said, the powers of all the simple drugs, he will himself compose green plasters of many kinds, and will make the best use of each of those already compounded.

term_table.greek_sentence: τὴν γοῦν προτεθεῖσαν ἄχρι δεῦρο κατὰ τὸν λόγον ἔμπλαστρον, ἣν πρώτην τῶν χλωρῶν ἔγραψεν ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος, ἔνεστι μεταῤῥυθμίζειν πολυειδῶς, τοῦτο μὲν ἀντὶ τῆς στροβιλίνης ῥητίνης ἄλλην τινὰ βάλλοντα, τοῦτο δ’ αὐξάνοντα τὸν λιβανωτὸν ἢ σὺν αὐτῷ βάλλοντά τι τῶν ξηρῶν σαρκωτικῶν, οἶον ἴριν, ἀριστολοχίαν, ὀρόβινον ἄλευρον, ὅσα τ’ ἄλλα τοιαῦτα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, the plaster set forth up to this point in our discussion, which Andromachus wrote first among the green ones, can be remodelled in many ways: on the one hand by putting in some other resin in place of the strobilos (pine-cone) resin, on the other by increasing the frankincense or putting in along with it one of the dry flesh-producing drugs, such as iris, aristolochia, bitter-vetch meal, and whatever others are of this kind.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ μὴν καὶ ὅσοι τὰ δυσαλθῆ θεραπεῦσαι ἠβουλήθησαν, ὡς πολύχρηστον εἶναι τὸ φάρμακον, ἔμιξαν τοῖς προειρημένοις χρυσόκολλαν ἢ διφρυγὲς ἢ χαλκὸν κεκαυμένον ἢ λεπίδα, τινὲς μὲν χαλκοῦ, τινὲς δὲ στομώματος ἢ σιδήρου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed all those who also wished to treat ulcers hard to heal, so that the drug should be a polychreston (of many uses), mixed with the aforesaid ingredients chrysocolla or diphryges or burnt copper or scale, some of copper, some of steel (stomoma) or of iron.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And indeed all those who wished to treat the hard-to-heal ulcers, so that the drug might be a polychrest, mixed into the aforementioned ingredients chrysocolla or diphryges or burnt copper or scale, some of copper, some of steel or of iron.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ σχεδὸν ἅπαντα τὰ νῦν εἰρημένα φυλάττει τὴν χρόαν τῶν χλωρῶν ἐμπλάστρων, ἕτερα δὲ τῶν αὐτῶν ὄντα δυνάμεων, εἰ μιχθείη, διαφθείρει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And nearly all the things just mentioned preserve the colour of the green plasters, whereas others, though of the same powers, destroy it if they are mixed in.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And nearly all the things now mentioned preserve the colour of the green plasters, whereas others, though of the same properties, spoil it if they are mixed in.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: προετέθη γὰρ οὐχ ἁπλῶς εἰπεῖν ὑπὲρ ἐμπλάστρων κολλητικῶν ἢ σαρκωτικῶν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ τοῦ χλωρὰς ὑπάρχειν αὐτὰς, ὥστε καὶ ταῦτα τὰ νῦν εἰρημένα καὶ χάλκανθος ﻿ [483] καὶ ὠμὴ χαλκῖτις βραχεῖ μέτρῳ μιγνύμενα φυλάττει τὴν χρόαν τῶν προκειμένων ἐν τῷ λόγῳ φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it was proposed not simply to speak about agglutinative or flesh-producing plasters, but with the condition that they be green ones, so that both these just mentioned and chalcanthum [483] and raw chalcitis, when mixed in a small measure, preserve the colour of the drugs that are the subject of the discussion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For the proposal was not simply to speak about agglutinative or flesh-producing plasters, but about these with the further condition that they be green. Consequently both the things just mentioned, and chalcanthum [483] and raw chalcitis, when mixed in in a small measure, preserve the colour of the drugs under discussion.

term_table.greek_sentence: διαλεκτικῶν δὲ ἀνδρῶν ἐστιν ἔργον τὸ τοιοῦτον, τὰς κατὰ μέρος ἐπὶ πασῶν γράφειν αὐτοῖς, ὡς ὁ Ἥρας καὶ Κρίτων καὶ ὁ Ἀσκληπιάδης καὶ ἕτεροι δὲ πολλοί.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But such a thing is the task of dialectical men (διαλεκτικῶν), to write the particular [uses] for them in the case of all [the drugs], as Heras and Criton and Asclepiades and many others do.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Such a procedure is the work of men trained in dialectic; [the other is] to write out for them the particular [uses] in the case of all [the drugs], as Heras and Crito and Asclepiades and many others besides have done.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed there is also a third kind of teaching, which we ourselves practise, neither writing the use in the case of all the particular drugs, nor yet entrusting the whole to the universal, common teaching of the method alone, but teaching this first, and after it writing one, or a second, or even a third example for the sake of clarity and of the exercise of the learners.

term_table.greek_sentence: τὸ δ’ ἧττόν τε καὶ μᾶλλον ἐν αὐτῷ παρὰ τῆς τοῦ θεραπευομένου φύσεως εὑρίσκειν προσήκει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And the less and the more in this it is fitting to discover from the nature of the person being treated.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σκληρός, ά, όν, also Dor. , Pi. O. 7.29 , Epich. Alex.Praef. ; ὀσμαί Thphr. CP 6.14.12 ( Comp. ): metaph., ς. φράσις D.H. Pomp. 2 . stiff, unyielding, opp. ὑγρός (lithe and supple), τιτθία ς. καὶ κυδώνια Ar. Ach. 1199 ; σκληρότεροι μαστοί Arist. Pr. 873a34 , al. κοιλίη ς. costive, Hp. Aph. 3.25 , cf. Arist. PA 670b9 . of light, strong, ἐν ς. αὐγῇ ἢ μαλακῇ Id. Col. 793b17 . of a wind, strong, Ep.Jac. 3.4 , Poll. 1.110 , Ael. NA 9.57 . metaph., of things, hard, austere, μὴ τὰ μαλακὰ μῶσο, μὴ τὰ ς. ἔχῃς Epich. l.c.; τροφή S. OC 1615 ; δίαιται E. Fr. 525.5 ; βίος Men. 522 ; τὰ ς. hard words, S. OC 1406 ; ς. συμφοραί E. term_table.greek_sentence: τοῖς μὲν γὰρ σκληροτέροις σώμασιν ἢ διὰ φυσικὴν κρᾶσιν ἢ διὰ ἡλικίαν ἢ διὰ χώραν ἢ ἐπιτηδεύματα μᾶλλον ξηραίνοντα προσφέρειν χρὴ, τοῖς δ’ ὑγροτέροις τὰ ἧττον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For to harder bodies, whether through natural temperament or through age or through region or pursuits, one must apply drugs that dry more, and to moister bodies those that dry less.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For to harder bodies, whether hard through natural krasis, or through age, or through region, or through their occupations, one must apply more strongly drying drugs, and to moister bodies those that dry less.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ξηρ-αντικός, ή, όν, causing to dry up, c.gen., πνεύμονος Hp. Acut. 16 , 22 : abs., ξ. [χυλόσ] Thphr. CP 6.1.3 ; ξ. δίαιτα Diocl.Fr. 141 , cf. Arist. Pr. 925a34 ( Comp. ) ; ξ. δύναμις Dsc. 1.13 . Adv. -κῶς by drying. Herod.Med. ap. Orib. 5.28.23 .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἀφλέγμαντόν τε καὶ [485] καθαρὸν εὑρίσκοιτο τὸ κοῖλον ἕλκος, οὐδὲν χρὴ νεωτερίζειν· εἰ δ’ ὑγρότερον ἢ ῥυπαρώτερον, ἐπιτείνειν χρὴ τὸ ξηραντικὸν καὶ ῥυπτικὸν φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if the hollow ulcer is found to be free of inflammation and [485] clean, one should make no innovation; but if it is moister or fouler, one should intensify the drying and cleansing drug; and if it is more hollow than before, one should relax it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if the hollow ulcer is found to be free of inflammation and [485] clean, one should make no change; but if it is moister or dirtier, one must intensify the drying and cleansing drug.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And if one of the lovers of fault-finding should charge us with leading the argument, contrary to what was set out from the beginning, towards the uses of the drugs, when we had promised to speak about their composition, let him consider that a kind of composition also takes place in the course of use, and hold his peace.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σύν-θεσις, εως, ἡ, putting together, composition, combination, Pl. Phd. 93a , R. 611b ; τῶν λίθων Arist. EN 1174a23 , cf. IG 42(1).103.56 (Epid., iv B.C.), 7.3073.92 (Lebad., ii B.C.); τῶν σπονδύλων Sor. 1.102 ; storage, τῶν μήλων (quinces in a ῥίσκος) Phylarch. 10 J. ; but ἐλαιῶν ς. a preserve of olives, Gp. 9.28.2 . in concrete sense, junction, ὀστῶν Arist. PA 658b19 ; συνθέσεις (λέγω τὰς γωνίας) Id. Pr. 910b14 . in various technical senses: in Grammar, composition, γραμμάτων τε συνθέσεις, i.e. syllables and words, A. Pr. 460 , cf. Arist. Metaph. 1092a26 ; ς. ἔκ τε ῥημάτων γιγνομένη καὶ ὀνομάτων, i.e. sentences, Pl. Sph. 263d , cf. Cra. 431c , Arist. Po. 1458a28 , Gal. 15.487 ; περὶ συνθέσεως ὀνομάτων, title of work by D.H. ; also, the juxtaposition of letters in a word, Arist. Rh.Al. 1434b34 ; of an author's composition, Isoc. 10.11 ; so ἡ τῶν μέτρων ς. metrical composition, Arist. Po. 1449b35 ; ἡ τῶν ἐπῶν ς. D.S. 5.74 ; ἡ τοῦ παίωνος ξ. the way the paeon is made up, Plu. 2.1143d ; the constitution of things, Hp. Virg. 1 . Math., synthesis of a problem (opp. ἀνάλυσις), Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.7 , explained in Papp. 634 ; ἡ κατὰ ς. ἀγωγή synthetic procedure, Id. 412.2 . Math., ς. λόγου transformation of a ratio known as componendo, Euc. 5 Def. 14 ; κατὰ -σιν, = componendo, Archim. Aequil. 2.9 . Math., addition, Ph. 1.11 , Plu. 2.1018c , Dioph. 1 Intr.; καθ' ἁντινοῦν -σιν however many times added, i.e. whatever number of times taken (multiplied), Archim. Spir. 1 :—also as Pythag. name for 2 , Anatol. ap. Theol.Ar. 8 . in Logic, union of noun and verb or of two objects of thought in a statement, Arist. Int. 16a12 , de An. 430a27 ; also ὁ παρὰ τὴν ς. [λόγος] the fallacy of composition, opp. διαίρεσις, Id. SE 177a33 . in Physics, composition of substances, parts of organisms, from their elementary constituents, Id. PA 646a12 , Top. 151a23 ; opp μίξις (combination), Id. GC 328a6 . in Medicine, compounding of essences and drugs, τῶν μύρων Thphr. Od. 14 , al., cf. D.S. 4.45 , Aglaïas 8 . combination of parts so as to form a whole, γενέσεις καὶ ς. Pl. R. 533b ; ἡ τῶν στρωμάτων ς. Id. Plt. 280b , cf. Arist. PA 645a35 , Metaph. 1014b37 ; in plants, Thphr. HP 5.5.2 . in concrete sense, a social or political combination, Arist. Pol. 1276b7 ; a military formation, Ael. Tact. 18.5 . agreement, treaty, Pi. P. 4.168 , Fr. 205 ; πὸς τὰς συνθέσις in accordance with the agreements, IG 5(2).343.41 , 60 (Orchom. Arc. , iv B.C.); ἐκ συνθέσεως by arrangement, D.S. 13.112 , etc.; συνθέσεις περὶ γάμων Plu. Sull. 35 . ς. λόγων making up accounts, Stud.Pal. 4.70.391 (i A.D.); so ς. alone, εἰς σύνθεσιν τῷ βασιλεῖ PTeb. 714.6 (ii B.C.). set, service (most freq. in Lat. synthesis): collection of clothes, wardrobe, Dig. 34.2.38.1 ; also, dress, gown, costume, suit, ς. τελείας λευκὰς δεκατρεῖς, γυναικείας ς. PHamb. 10.13 , 21 (ii A.D.), cf. POxy. 1153.23 (i A.D.), 496.4 (ii A.D.), PSI 10.1117.11 , 13 (ii A.D.), Mart. 2.46.4 , 5.79.2 ; synthesinam indutus, Suet. Ner. 51 . service of plate, ς. πινακίων BGU 781 i 5 (i A.D.), cf. Mart. 4.46.15 , Stat. Silv. 4.9.44 .

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μικρός and σμικρός, ά, όν, Dor. , Ion. μικκός (q.v.): σμικρός is corroborated by metre in Il. 17.757 , Hes. Op. 361 , and might be restored in Il. 5.801 , Od. 3.296 (μικρός codd.); it is prob. the only form in Hdt. ( μικρός Hdt. 2.74 codd.): freq. in Lyr. and prob. always in Trag. (exc. where metre requires μικρός, as S. Aj. 161 (anap., Comp. )); most freq. in Pl. ; but in Th. , also Ar. and other Com., μικρός prevails, σμικρός being found Th. 4.13 , 7.75 , 8.81 , Ar. Ach. 523 , V. 5 ; Att. Inscrr. have σμικρός IG 12.313.111 , al., μικρός ib. 369.10 , al.:—small, little, in Size, μ. ἔην δέμας Il. 5.801 ; μ. λίθος Od. 3.296 ; κίρκον, ὅ τε σμικρῇσι φόνον φέρει ὀρνίθεσσιν Il. 17.757 ; σμ. ἄστεα Hdt. 1.5 ; μεγάθεϊ σμικροί Id. 2.74 : with Dims., μ. πολίχνιον, γῄδιον, παιδάρια, Isoc. 5.145 , X. Cyr. 8.3.38 , Ages. 1.21 : as a Com. exaggeration, δικαστηρίδιον μ. πάνυ Ar. V. 803 ; σκαλαθυρμάτι' ἄττα μ. Id. Nu. 630 , etc.: c. inf., μικροὶ δ' ὁρᾶν Id. Pax 821 : as a term of reproach, Κλειγενὴς ὁ μικρός Id. Ra. 709 , cf. Pl. Prt. 323d , Arist. EN 1123b7 , Alex. 98.7 ; Ἀμύντας ὁ μ. Arist. Pol. 1311b3 ; οἱ ἐν μικρῷ μεγάλοι short but stoutly built, Philostr. Gym. 36 ; ὁ μ. δάκτυλος SIG 1172.4 (Lebena). in Quantity, σμικρὸν ἐπὶ σμικρῷ καταθεῖναι Hes. Op. 361 ; μέλιτος μικρόν Ar. V. 878 ; μ. ὄψον, ἀργυρίδιον, X. Mem. 3.14.1 , Ar. Pl. 240 , cf. Antiph. 44 . in Amount or Importance, petty, trivial, slight, σμ. πρόφασις Thgn. 323 ; ἔπος, ἔγκλημα, ῥοπή, etc., S. OC 443 , Tr. 361 , OT 961 , etc.; ἐκ σμικροῦ λόγου on some slight pretext, Id. OC 620 ; ἐν σμικρῷ λόγῳ παρῆκεν as of small account, ib. 569 ; αἰτίας μικρᾶς πέρι E. Andr. 387 , etc.; οὐδὲ μικρόν, = οὐδὲ γρῦ , D. 19.37 ; of persons, of small account, opp. μέγας, σμ. ἐν σμικροῖς, μέγας ἐν μεγάλοις Pi. P. 3.107 ; ἄριστ' ἂν καὶ μέγας ὀρθοῖθ' ὑπὸ μικροτέρων S. Aj. 161 (anap.), etc.; σμ. τίθησί με Id. OC 958 ; βίος ὁ μ., = μέτριος , E. Fr. 504 ; τίνος σμικροτάτου μεταβαλόντος, σμικρότατος τὴν δύναμιν, Pl. R. 473b ; of the mind, οὐ σμικρὸν φρονεῖ S. Aj. 1120 ; of style, mean, [ Φίλιστοσ] μικρὸς ταῖς ἐκφράσεσιν D.H. Vett.Cens. 3.2 ; of festivals, of lesser importance, Ἁλίεια τὰ μεγάλα καὶ τὰ μ. SIG 1067.14 (Cedreae). of Time, short, Pi. O. 12.12 , Ar. Pl. 126 , etc.; εἰς μ. χρόνον Pl. R. 498d ; ἐν μικρῷ (sc. χρόνῳ) shortly, X. Cyn. 5.32 , Eq. 8.7 ; πρὸ μικροῦ Poll. 1.72 ; ἔτι μικρὸν καὶ καταλιθοβολήσουσί με LXX Ex. 17.4 . of Age, young, Ostr.Bodl. i237 (ii B.C.), etc. Adverbial usages, regul. Adv. σμικρῶς, but little, Pl. Criti. 107d ; μικρῶς by a little, prob. in Archim. Stom. 1 : Sup. σμικρότατα X. Mem. 3.11.12 . σμικροῦ or μικροῦ within a little, almost, Id. Cyr. 1.4.8 , D. 18.151 , etc.; in full, μικροῦ δεῖν, v. δεῖ 11 , δέω (B) 1 ; μικροῦ τινος ἀπελείφθη τοῦ μή . . Ach.Tat. 7.13 ; but μικροῦ πρίασθαι for a little, cheap, X. Mem. 2.10.4 . σμικρῷ by a little, with Comp. , Pl. Plt. 262c , etc.; also σμικρῷ πρόσθεν a little before, Id. Lg. 719b , etc.; μικρῷ ἄνωθεν D. 44.6 . μικρόν a little, σμικρὸν ὑπολείπεσθαι, σμ. τι παρακλίνειν, X. An. 5.4.22 , Pl. Cra. 410a ; of Time, X. An. 3.1.11 , etc.; repeated, μικρὸν μικρόν Antiph. 10 : pl., of Degree, σμικρὰ γεωμετρίας ἔμπειροι Pl. R. 527a , etc.; σμίκρ' ἄττα διατρίψαντες Id. Prt. 316a ; μικρὰ διακινήσω σε περὶ τοῦ πράγματος Sosip. 1.22 ; περιπάτησον μικρὰ μετ' ἐμοῦ Men. Sam. 243 , cf. Plu. Luc. 31 . with Preps., ἐπὶ σμικρόν but a little, S. El. 414 , Antipho 6.18 , Hdt. 4.129 . κατὰ μικρόν into small pieces, X. An. 7.3.22 ; so κατὰ μικρὰ γενομένης τῆς δυνάμεως ib. 5.6.32 ; also, little by little, κατὰ μικρὸν ἀεί Ar. V. 702 , cf. Nu. 741 ; opp. συλλήβδην, Pl. R. 344a ; καὶ κατὰ σμ. or μ. ever so little, Id. Sph. 241c , Isoc. 3.10 , D. 2.22 . παρὰ μικρόν within a little, παρὰ μ. ἐλθεῖν c. inf., to be within an ace of doing, E. Heracl. 295 (anap.), cf. Isoc. 7.6 , etc.; παρὰ μ. ἦλθον ἀποθανεῖν Id. 17.42 ; τὸ παρὰ μ. ὥσπερ οὐδὲν ἀπέχειν δοκεῖ Arist. Ph. 197a30 ; but τὸ παρὰ μ. σῴζεσθαι to be only just saved, Id. Rh. 1371b11 , cf. Simp. in Ph. 344.10 ; gradual, imperceptible change, Arist. Pol. 1303a20 ; οὐδὲ παρὰ μ. ἦν κρεῖττον c. inf., Plb. 12.20.7 ; [ ἡ τύχη] παρὰ μ. εἰς ἑκάτερα ποιεῖ μεγάλας ῥοπάς Id. 15.6.8 , cf. Isoc. 4.59 ; but also παρὰ μ. ποιεῖσθαι, ἡγεῖσθαι, to think little of . . , D. 61.51 , Isoc. 5.79 . μετὰ μικρόν a little after, Ev.Matt. 26.73 . besides regul. Comp. and Sup. μικρότερος, -ότατος ( Ar. Eq. 789 , D. Prooem. 48 , etc.), there are the irreg. ἐλάσσων, ἐλάχιστος, from ἐλαχύς, and μείων, μεῖστος, also μειότερος; v. μείων. [ι by nature; ι only in late Poetry, Epigr. ap. Phleg. Fr. 36.17 J. ] (Perh. cf. Lat. mīca, mīcidus, OHG. smāhi, ONorse smár 'little'.)

O. 8.19 : freq. of parts of the body, fair, shapely, κ. πρόσωπα, ὅμματα, παρήϊα, σφυρά, Il. 19.285 , 23.66 , Od. 19.208 , Il. 4.147 ; Χρώς 5.354 , al.; of clothes, εἵματα, φάρεα, Χιτών, Χλαῖνα, πέδιλα, Od. 6.111 , 24.277 , Il. 2.43 , Od. 10.365 , 1.96 ; πέπλος κάλλιστος ποικίλμασιν ἠδὲ μέγιστος Il. 6.294 ; of arms and armour, κνημῖδες, ἀσπίς, σάκος, κόρυς, φάσγανα, ἔντεα, 3.331 , 11.33 , 22.314 , 18.612 , 15.713 , Od. 19.18 ; of buildings, manufactured articles, etc., αὐλὴ κ. τε μεγάλη τε 14.7 ; κ. δώματα, τεῖχος, πόλιες, 3.387 , Il. 21.447 , 18.491 ; ἄμαξα, τράπεζα, θρόνος, 24.267 , 11.629 , Od. 1.131 ; also τέμενος, ἀγρός, Il. 12.314 , Od. 24.206 ; so after Hom. , Λύδιον κ. ἔργον Sapph. 19 , etc.; ἐέρσα κ. ead. Supp. 25.12 . in Att. added to a name in token of love or admiration, as Ἀρίσημος κ. IG 12.921 , etc.; ἐν τοῖσι τοίχοις ἔγραφ' "Ἀθηναῖοι καλοί" Ar. Ach. 144 , cf. V. 98 ; Ἀλκιβιάδης ὁ καλός, Σαπφὼ ἡ καλή, Pl. Alc. 1.113b , Phdr. 235c . ἡ Καλή or Καλλίστη, as epith., A. Ag. 140 (lyr.), Paus. 1.29.2 , CIG 4445 (Beroea). Καλοί, οἱ , divinities worshipped in childbirth, IG 5(1).1445 (Messene, ii B. C.). τὸ καλόν beauty, Sapph. 79 , E. IA 21 (anap.), etc.; τὰ καλά the proprieties or elegancies of life, Hdt. 1.8 , 207 ; ἁπάντων καλῶν ἄμμορος Pi. O. 1.84 ; αἱ τέχναι ἃς πηγάς φασι τῶν κ. εἶναι X. Cyr. 7.2.13 . with ref. to use, good, of fine quality, κ. λιμήν Od. 6.263 ; Βορέῃ ἀνέμῳ . . καλῷ fair, 14.253 , 299 ; κ. ἀργύριον, opp. κίβδηλον, genuine silver, X. Mem. 3.1.9 ; opp. ἀποτετριμμένον, good silver currency, PCair.Zen. 21.33 (iii B. C.); ἐλαῖαι PHib. 1.49.12 (iii B. C.); γῆ Ev.Luc. 8.15 ; κ. οἶνος PFay. 133.8 (iv A. D.); στρατόπεδον κάλλιστον Th. 5.60 ; ἀνταπεδώκατε πονηρὰ ἀντὶ καλῶν LXX Ge. 44.4 ; κ. ἐς στρατιάν X. Cyr. 3.3.6 ; πρός τι Pl. Hp.Ma. 295c , Grg. 474d , etc.: c. inf., λόφος κάλλιστος τρέχειν X. An. 4.8.26 ; ἐν καλῷ [τόπῳ] in a good place, καθίζεσθαι, ὁρμεῖν, Ar. Th. 292 , X. HG 2.1.25 ; ἐν καλῷ μὲν τοῦ κόλπου καὶ τῶν πόλεων, ἐν κ. δὲ τοῦ τὴν Χώραν βλάπτειν, ib. 6.2.9 ; ἐν καλῷ under favourable circumstances, Th. 5.59.60 ; ἐν κ. (sc. Χρόνῳ) in good time, in season, E. IA 1106 ; ἐν οὐ κ. Id. Or. 579 ; ἐν καλῷ [ἐστι] c. inf., S. El. 384 (so καλόν ἐστι c. inf., Id. Ph. 1155 (lyr.), Ar. Pax 278 , Th. 8.2 ); ἐς καλόν S. OT 78 , Pl. Men. 89e , Smp. 174e ; τί γὰρ ἐμοὶ ζῆν καλόν; what is the good of life to me? Ph. 2.594 ; καλῇ πίστει, = Lat.bona fide, PTeb. 418.14 (iii A. D.). of sacrifices, auspicious, σφάγια A. Th. 379 ; οἰωνοί E. Ion 1333 ; ἱερά Th. 4.92 ; τὸ τέλος κ. τῆς ἐξόδου X. An. 5.2.9 ; κ. τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν αὐτῷ Id. Cyr. 3.2.3 : c. inf., ἰέναι . . κ. ἡμῖν τὰ ἱερὰ ἦν Id. An. 2.2.3 : Com., τὰ τῆς πυγῆς κ. (for τοῦ θεοῦ) Ar. Pax 868 . in a moral sense, beautiful, noble, honourable, in Hom. only in neut., οὐ καλὸν ἔειπες Od. 8.166 , cf. 17.381 ; μεῖζον κλέος . . καὶ κάλλιον 18.255 ; freq. καλόν [ἐστι] c. inf., κ. τοι σὺν ἐμοὶ τὸν κήδειν ὅς κ' ἐμὲ κήδῃ Il. 9.615 ; οὐ γὰρ ἔμοιγε κ. (sc. ἄρχειν) 21.440 ; οὐ κ. ἀτέμβειν οὐδὲ δίκαιον Od. 20.294 ; so in Trag., καλόν μοι τοῦτο ποιούσῃ θανεῖν S. Ant. 72 , etc.; μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν LXX Is. 1.17 : Comp. , οὐ μέν τοι τόδε κάλλιον οὐδὲ ἔοικε Od. 7.159 , cf. Il. 24.52 ; after Hom. freq. of actions, etc., κάλων κἄσλων Sapph. Supp. 2.4 (unless of persons here); κ. ἔργματα noble deeds, Pi. I. 4(3).42 , cf. S. Fr. 839 , etc.; ἀναστροφὴ κ. 1 Ep.Pet. 2.12 : in pl., excellences, πλῆθος καλῶν Pi. O. 13.45 ; πολλῶν καλῶν δεῖ τῷ καλόν τι μωμένῳ S. Fr. 938 ; τὰ τοῦ παιδὸς κ. X. Smp. 8.17 . τὸ κ. moral beauty, virtue, honour, opp. τὸ αἰσχρόν, Id. Mem. 1.1.16 , cf. Pl. Smp. 183d , etc.; ὅττι καλόν, φίλον ἐστί, τὸ δ' οὐ καλὸν οὐ φίλον ἐστίν Thgn. 17 , cf. E. Ba. 881 (lyr.), Pl. Ly. 216c ; οὐ ταὐτὸν ἡγῇ σύ, ὡς ἔοικας, κ. τε καὶ ἀγαθὸν καὶ κακὸν καὶ αἰσχρόν Id. Grg. 474d , cf. Smp. 201e ; τοὐμὸν κ. E. Supp. 300 . of persons, in early writers coupled with ἀγαθός, v. καλοκἀγαθός ; later κ. ποιμήν Ev.Jo. 10.11 ; κ. στρατιώτης 2 Ep.Tim. 2.3 . in Att. and Trag. freq. ironically, fine, specious, γέρας κ. A. Eu. 209 ; κ. γὰρ οὑμὸς βίοτος ὥστε θαυμάσαι S. El. 393 , cf. E. Ba. 652 ; κ. Χάρις D. 9.65 ; κ. ὕβριν ὑβρισμένοι Id. 23.121 ; καί σοι . . θωπεῦσαι καλόν S. OC 1003 ; μετ' ὀνομάτων καλῶν Th. 5.89 . Degrees of Comp. : Comp. καλλίων, ον , Il. 24.52 , Od. 10.396 , etc.: neut. κάλιον [α] Alc. 134 : Sup. κάλλιστος, η, ον , Il. 20.233 , etc.; late καλλιώτερος or -ότερος, POxy. 1672.6 (i A. D.), Sch. E. Tr. 966 ; also καλώτερος Hdn. Epim. 69 . Adv.:—Poets freq. use neut. καλόν as Adv., κ. ἀείδειν Il. 18.570 , Od. 1.155 ; καλά Il. 6.326 ; later τὸ κ. Theoc. 3.3 , 18 , Call. Epigr. 53 , Herod. 1.54 . regul. Adv. καλῶς ( Dor. καλώς Sophr. 22 ), well, rightly, οὐδ' ἔτι κ. οἶκος ἐμὸς διόλωλε Od. 2.64 ; κ. ζῆν, τεθνηκέναι, etc., S. Aj. 479 , etc.; κ. φρονεῖν to be in one's right mind, Id. Fr. 836 ; οὐ κ. ταρβεῖς Id. Tr. 457 ; κ. ἀγωνιεῖσθαι fairly, on the merits of the case, Lys. 13.88 ; Χρήματα δατῆθθαι κ. Leg.Gort. 4.39 ; κ. εἰρημένα S. Fr. 576.6 ; κάλλιον λέγεις Pl. Tht. 161b ; κάλλιστ' ἂν εἴποι S. OT 1172 : freq. in phrase καλῶς καὶ εὖ, καλῶς τε καὶ εὖ, Pl. Prt. 319e , Prm. 128b , etc. of good fortune, well, happily, κ. πράσσειν, = εὖ π ., A. Pr. 979 , S. Ant. 271 ; κ. καὶ εὖ πράττειν Pl. Chrm. 172a ; κ. ἔχειν to be well, A. Th. 799 , etc.; κ. ἔχει σοι Ar. Ach. 946 , cf. S. El. 816 ; κ. ἔχει c. inf., 'tis well to . . , X. Mem. 3.11.1 : c. gen., κ. ἔχειν τινός to be well off in respect to a thing, Hp. Superf. 29 ; κ. παράπλου κεῖσθαι Th. 1.36 ; εἰ κ. σφίσιν ἔχοι Id. 4.117 ; οὔτε τοῖς θεοῖς ἔφη κ. ἔχειν, εἰ . . X. Mem. 1.3.3 ; καλλιόνως ἔχει Pl. Tht. 169e , etc.; κάλλιστα ἕζει Id. Hp.Ma. 295b . καλῶς, = πάνυ , thoroughly, altogether, τὸν κ. εὐδαίμονα A. Fr. 317 , = S. Fr. 934 ; κ. ἔξοιδα Id. OC 269 , cf. OT 1008 ; κ. ὑπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς διεφθάρθαι D.S. 13.108 : Comp. , κάλλιον εἰδέναι Pl. Hp.Ma. 300d ; κάλλιον ἐοικέναι to be just like , Hp. Genit. 8 . κ. ἀκούειν to be well spoken of, Men. Mon. 285 , Plu. 2.177e . κ. ποιῶν rightly, deservedly, κ. ποιῶν ἀπόλλυται Ar. Pl. 863 , cf. D. 1.28 , al., Aeschin. 3.232 ; in requests, κ. ποιήσεις πριάμενος, etc., PPetr. 3p.143 (iii B. C.), etc.; also c. inf., κ. π. γράψαι BGU 1203.7 (i B. C.), etc. in answers, to approve the words of the former speaker, well said! E. Or. 1216 , D. 39.15 ; also, to decline an offer courteously, no, thank you! Ar. Ra. 888 ; κ. ἔχει Antiph. 165 , Men. Pk. 266 ; πάνυ κ. Ar. Ra. 512 ; ἀμέλει κ. ib. 532 : Sup. , κάλλιστ', ἐπαινῶ ib. 508 ; ἔχει κάλλιστα Theoc. 15.3 . ironically, finely, καλῶς ἐρήμης γ' ἂν σὺ γῆς ἄρχοις μόνος S. Ant. 739 , cf. E. Med. 588 , Ar. Eq. 344 , Din. 1.69 . κ. ὁ ἱερεύς hurrah for the priest! SIG 1109.14 (Athens, ii A. D.). repeated with the Adj., καλὴ καλῶς Ar. Ach. 253 , Pax 1330 , Ec. 730 ; καλὸς κάλλιστά τε ῥέξαις Pi. O. 9.94 . Comp. καλλιόνως Pl. Tht. l.c., Lg. 660d : Sup. καλλίστως PMag.Par. 1.2443 , 2465 , Sch. E. Hec. 310 . for compds., v. καλλι-, καλο- . Quantity: α in Ep. and early Iamb. Poets (exc. h.Ven. 29 , Hes. Op. 63 , Th. 585 ): α in Lyr. (exc. καλῶς B. 12.206 ) and Trag. ( A. Fr. 314 , S. Ph. 1381 are corrupt).--In Eleg., Epigr., and Bucol. Poets α or α (the latter usu. in thesi); τὰ μὴ καλὰ καλὰ πέφανται Theoc. 6.19 , cf. Herod. 7.115 , Call. Jov. 55 .--In Comp. , ι in Hom. , ι in Trag. and later.
term_table.greek_sentence: [487] καλλίων δὲ σύνθεσις ἔσται τὸ μὲν ὄγδοον μέρος ἰοῦ μιξάντων τῇ διὰ τοῦ κηροῦ καὶ τῆς ῥητίνης συνθέσει, προλειωσάντων δὲ πλείοσιν ἡμέραις τὸν ἰὸν μετὰ ὄξους δριμυτάτου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [487] But a finer composition will result if one mixes the eighth part of verdigris with the composition made from wax and resin, having first triturated the verdigris for several days with the most acrid vinegar.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [487] A finer composition will result if one mixes an eighth part of verdigris into the composition made with wax and resin, having first ground the verdigris for several days with the most acrid vinegar.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακός, ή, όν, soft: of things subject to touch, εὐνή Il. 9 . 618 ; κώεα Od. 3.38 ; τάπης μαλακοῦ ἐρίοιο 4.124 ; χιτών Il. 2.42 , PSI 4.364.5 (iii B.C.); πέπλοι Il. 24.796 ; νειὸς μ. fresh-ploughed fallow, 18.541 ; λειμῶνες μ. soft grassy meadows, Od. 5.72 , cf. Mem. 3.10.1 ; πρόβατα μ. soft-fleeced, D. 47.52 ; τόποι πεδινοὶ καὶ μ., opp. hard, rugged ground, Arist. HA 607a10 ; οἱ κρημνοὶ οἱ μ. ib. 615b31 ; μ. πέτρα SIG 970.8 (iii B.C.), PPetr. 2p.6 (iii B.C.); μ. τέφρα a slow fire, Ph. Bel. 89.36 ; so μ. πῦρ Androm. ap. Per.Fr. 3 , Diph. 19 . of things not subject to touch, gentle, θάνατος Od. 18.202 ; ὕπνος Il. 10.2 ; κῶμα 14.359 ; μ. ἔπεα soft, fair words, 1.582 , 6.337 ; λόγοι Od. 1.56 ; ἐπαοιδαί Pi. Rh. 1408b9 . light, mild, - ώτεραι ζημίαι Th. 3.45 . of persons or modes of life, soft, mild, gentle, μαλακώτερος ἀμφαφάασθαι easier to handle, of a fallen hero, Il. 22.373 ; ἐκ τῶν μ. χώρων μ. ἄνδρας γίνεσθαι Hdt. 9.122 ; - ώτερον ἐκ σκληροτέρου τὸ τῆς ψυχῆς ἦθος Pl. term_table.english_sentence_A: Of oil you will mix in, whenever you prepare the drug without vinegar and frankincense, cyathi equal in number to the ounces of verdigris; but whenever you mix in frankincense and vinegar, if the phryktē (roasted resin) is somewhat fattier and softer and you are preparing it in summer, you will mix in none; but when it is hard and it is winter, one cyathus.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But when you mix in frankincense and vinegar, if the roasted [resin] is somewhat fattier and softer and you are preparing it in summer, you will mix in none; but when it is hard, and in winter, one cyathus.

term_table.english_sentence_A: It is also possible for you, by mixing one of the liquid resins with the wax, to have no need of oil at all.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is also possible for you, if you mix one of the liquid resins with the wax, to need no oil at all.

term_table.greek_sentence: μίξεις δὲ τῆς μὲν ὑγροτάτης τὸ τρίτον τοῦ κατὰ τὸν κηρὸν σταθμοῦ, τῆς δ’ ἧσσον ὑγρᾶς τὸ ἥμισυ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: You will mix in, of the most liquid resin, a third of the weight of the wax, and of the less liquid, a half.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Of the most liquid you will mix in a third of the weight of the wax, and of the less liquid one a half.

term_table.greek_sentence: τὸν κηρὸν καὶ τὴν ῥητίνην τήξας καὶ ψύξας μῖξον ἰοῦ μέρει ποτὲ μὲν ὀγδόῳ, ποτὲ δὲ δεκάτῳ, ποτὲ δὲ δωδεκάτῳ, γιγνώσκων ἐπὶ μὲν τῶν σκληρῶν σωμάτων τήν τε πρώτην συμμετρίαν ἁρμόττειν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν μαλακῶν τὴν τρίτην, ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν μέσων τὴν μέσην.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The composition will evidently turn out to be something like this: having melted the wax and the resin and cooled them, mix them with a part of verdigris, sometimes an eighth, sometimes a tenth, sometimes a twelfth, knowing that for hard bodies the first proportion is suitable, for soft ones the third, and for intermediate ones the intermediate.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Such a composition, clearly, will come about as follows: having melted and cooled the wax and the resin, mix them with a part of verdigris, sometimes an eighth, sometimes a tenth, sometimes a twelfth, recognising that for hard bodies the first proportion is suitable, for soft ones the third, and for intermediate ones the intermediate.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δὲ πρᾳότερον βουληθείης ἐργάσασθαι τὸ φάρμακον, ἐμβάλλῃς τοῦ λιβανωτοῦ σταθμὸν ἥμισυν οὗ κατὰ τὸν ἰὸν ἐποιήσω.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And if you should wish to make the drug milder, you may add a weight of frankincense half of that which you used for the verdigris.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If you should wish to make the drug milder, put in a weight of frankincense half of that which you used of the verdigris.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: αὗται μὲν οὖν αἱ πρῶται συνθέσεις ἐμπλάστρου χλωρᾶς, κολλητικῆς μὲν ἐναίμων τραυμάτων, ὅσα μὴ μεγάλα καὶ μέχρι συνουλώσεως δὲ τἄλλα δυναμένης ἰᾶσθαι καὶ σαρκούσης, εἰ τακείη μετά τινος ἐλαιώδους ὑγροῦ, λέγω δὲ ἐλαιώδη τό τε ῥόδινον, ᾧ μάλιστα χρῆσθαι προσήκει καθ’ ὃν εἴρηκα τρόπον ἐσκευασμένῳ, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο τῷ μυρσίνῳ καὶ τῷ κυπρίνῳ καὶ τῷ σχινίνῳ, αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ ἔλαιον, ἐφ’ ὧν μὲν βούλει θερμότητός τι προσθεῖναι τῷ τηκομένῳ φαρμάκῳ τὸ κοινὸν τοῦτο μίξεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: These, then, are the first compositions of the green plaster, which is agglutinative of bloody wounds, those that are not large, and which is able to heal the others as far as cicatrization and to produce flesh, if it is melted with some oily liquid.
term_table.english_sentence_B: These, then, are the first compositions of the green plaster: agglutinative of bloody wounds, such as are not large, and able to heal the other [lesions] up to cicatrisation, and fleshing, if it is melted with some oily liquid. By 'oily' I mean rose-oil, which it is most fitting to use, prepared in the way I have described, and after this myrtle-oil, cyprus-oil and mastic-oil.

term_table.english_sentence_A: It is quite evident, then, that he wants the vinegar to be triturated together with the two pounds of verdigris and the pound of frankincense, just as I said before, and then the meltable ingredients to be mixed with these.
term_table.english_sentence_B: He writes, then, word for word as follows: 'Another simple green plaster, which I use. ♃ Resin, twelve litrai; wax, 8 litrai; scraped verdigris, two litrai; calf's fat, two litrai; vinegar, one litra; and I put in one litra of manna.' It is quite clear, then, that he wants the vinegar to be ground smooth with the two litrai of verdigris and the litra of frankincense, just as I said before, and then the meltable ingredients to be mixed with these.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χρώς, ὁ, gen. χρωτός, dat. χρωτί, acc. χρῶτα ( Att. χρώ only in Choerob. in Theod. 1.248H. ): Ep. and Ion. gen. χροός, dat. χροΐ, acc. χρόα (also in Lesbian, Sapph. Supp. 10.6 , al.), as always in Hom.and Hes. , exc. gen. χρωτός in Il. 10.575 , acc. χρῶτα Od. 18.172 , 179 , Hes. Op. 556 ; Emp. uses χρωτός, 76.3 (but χροΐ 100.17 ); Pi. uses χρωτί, χρῶτα, P. 1.55 , I. 4(3).23(41) ; these forms are freq. in Trag., but Ion. dat. χροΐ occurs in S. Tr. 605 , and χροός, χροΐ, χρόα are freq. in E., Hec. 548 , Med. 1175 , Ph. 264 , al. :—dat. χρῷ occurs in the phrase ἐν χρῷ v. infr.1.2 and in Sapph. 2.10 .—rare in Com.and Att. Prose. of the human body, skin or flesh, οὔ σφι λίθος χρὼς οὐδὲ σίδηρος Il. 4.510 ; καὶ γάρ θην τούτῳ τρωτὸς χρώς 21.568 ; χρῶτ' ἀπονιψαμένη Od. 18.172 ; ἀκρότατον δ' ἄρ' ὀϊστὸς ἐπέγραψε χρόα Il. 4.139 ; ταμέειν χρόα νηλέϊ χαλκῷ 13.501 ; λιλαιου|ένη χροὸς ἆσαι, of a spear, 21.168 ; κακὰ χροΐ εἵματ' ἔχοντα Od. 14.506 ; χρῷ πῦρ ὐπαδεδρόμακεν Sapph. 2.10 ; μύροις χρῶτα λιπαίνων Anaxil. 18.1 (anap.): esp. flesh, opp. bone, φθινύθει δ' ἀμφ' ὀστεόφι χρώς Od. 16.145 ; οὐδέ τί οἱ χρὼς σήπεται Il. 24.414 , cf. 19.33 (which usage is said by Gal. to have been Ionic, 18(2).435 , with reference to Hp. Fract. 9 ); τὸ δέρμα τοῦ χρωτός LXX Le. 13.11 , etc.; τοῦ χρωτὸς ἥδιστον ἀπέπνει Aristox. Fr.Hist. 84 : generally, one's body, frame, Pi. P. 1.55 , A. Fr. 192.6 (anap.); χριμφθῆναι χροΐ Id. Supp. 790 (lyr.); στεῖλαί νυν ἀμφὶ χρωτὶ . . πέπλους E. Ba. 821 , cf. S. Tr. 605 : pl., διὰ τί . . οἱ χρῶτες ὄζουσι; Arist. Pr. 877b21 ; also κατεδήσαντο . . τοὺς ὑγιεῖς χρῶτας, ὡς τραυματίαι D.H. 9.50 . ἐν χροΐ, or ἐν χρῷ, close to the skin, ἐν χροΐ κείρειν to shave close, Hdt. 4.175 ; ἐν χρῷ κεκαρμένοι X. HG 1.7.8 ; ἐν χρῷ κουριῶντας Pherecr. 30 :—metaph., to the quick, ξυρεῖ γὰρ ἐν χρῷ τοῦτο S. Aj. 786 ; ἐν χρῷ παραπλεῖν sail past so as to shave or graze, Th. 2.84 ; τὴν μάχην συνάψαι ἐν χρῷ to fight at close quarters, Plu. Thes. 27 ; ἡ ἐν χρῷ συνουσία close acquaintance, Luc. Ind. 3 : c. gen., ἐν χρῷ τινος close to, hard by a person or thing, τοῦ θώρακος ( v.l. σώματος ) Plu. 2.345a ; τῆς γῆς ib. 925b , Luc. Herm. 5 : abs., ἐν χρῷ near at hand, Id. Hist.Conscr. 24 , al.; cf. EM 313.53 , Hsch. the colour of the skin, complexion, μελαίνετο δὲ χρόα καλόν Il. 5.354 ; τρέπεται χ. his colour changes, i. e. he turns pale, 13.279 , cf. 17.733 ; ὠχρήσαντα χρόα Od. 11.529 ; χρόα . . ἀμείβειν Parm. 8.41 ; μεθίστη χρωτὸς . . φύσιν E. Alc. 174 ; μεταλλακτῆρα πουλύπουν χροός Ion Trag. 36 ; τί χρὼς τέτραπται; (paratrag.) Ar. Lys. 127 ; φεῦγε δ' ἀπὸ χρώς Theocr. 23.13 ; rare in Att. Prose, ἐπὶ τῷ χρωτὶ μέγα φρονεῖν X. Smp. 4.54 , cf. Oec. 10.5 : in Ion. Prose, of the colour of a finger, χροΐ δῆλα Pherecyd.Syr. ap. D.L. 1.118 ( v.l. χρωΐ , cf. Vorsokr. 5i . 44 ). generally, colour, ἀμείβων χρῶτα πορφυρᾷ βαφῇ A. Pers. 317 ; τὸν χρῶτα [μεταβάλλει] ὁ χαμαιλέων Arist. Mir. 832b14 ; χρὼς αἵματος Orph. L. 660 .
term_table.greek_sentence: [Πῶς χλωραὶ γίνονται.] Βάλλεται μὲν εἰς αὐτὰ ἰὸς οὐκ ὀλίγος, ἀλλ’ ὥστε κρατῆσαι τῆς τῶν ἄλλων [497] χρόας, αὐτῷ τε συνομοιῶσαι τὸ πᾶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [How green ones come about.] Verdigris is put into them in no small quantity, but so much as to prevail over the colour of the other [497] ingredients and to make the whole like itself.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [How green plasters are made.] Verdigris is put into them, and not a little of it: enough to overpower the colour of the other [497] ingredients and to make the whole like itself.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐστοχάσθαι δὲ δεῖ τὴν τοιαύτην ἔμπλαστρον συντιθέντα πρὸς τῇ ποσότητι τοῦ ἰοῦ καὶ τῆς τῶν μιγνυμένων αὐτῷ χροιᾶς καὶ τοῦ τρόπου τῆς ἑψήσεως, ἐπὶ μὲν τῶν μιγνυμένων φυλαττόμενον τὰς δυσκινήτους χροιὰς, ὁπόσαι τῶν ξανθῶν εἰσι καὶ πυῤῥῶν καὶ μελάνων φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The one compounding such a plaster must take aim, besides the quantity of the verdigris, also at the colour of the things mixed with it and at the manner of the boiling: in the case of the things mixed, guarding against the colours that are hard to shift, such as are those of the yellow and reddish and black drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Whoever compounds such a plaster must attend, besides the quantity of the verdigris, to the colour of the ingredients mixed with it and to the manner of the boiling. In the ingredients mixed in, he must guard against the colours that are hard to change, such as those of yellow, russet and black drugs.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ξανθός, ή, όν, yellow, of various shades, freq. with a tinge of red, brown, auburn, λαμπρὸν ἐρυθρῷ λευκῷ τε μειγνύμενον Pl. Ti. 68b ; ἔστι δὲ τὸ ξ. ἐν τῇ ἴριδι χρῶμα μεταξὺ τοῦ τε φοινικοῦ καὶ πρασίνου χρώματος Arist. Mete. 375a11 ; ξανθὸν ἐρεύθεσθαι AP 12.97 (Antip.) : in Ep. mostly used of fair, golden hair, ξ. κόμη, χαίτη, of Achilles, Il. 1.197 , 23.141 ; ξ. τρίχες, of Odysseus, Od. 13.399 , 431 ; κάρη ξ. Μενέλαος (but usu. ξ. M. alone) 15.133 ; also of women, ξ. Ἀγαμήδη Il. 11.740 ; Ἀριάδνη Hes. Th. 947 (but ξ. Δημήτηρ golden corn, Il. 5.500 , etc.) ; so later, of Helen, Sapph. Supp. 13.5 ; of Athena and the Graces, Pi. N. 10.7 , 5.54 ; of Harmonia, E. Med. 834 (lyr.) (but in later Gr. of complexion, Cleom. 2.1 ) ; of dyed hair, τὴν γυναῖκα τὴν σώφρον' οὐ δεῖ τὰς τρίχας ξ. ποιεῖν Men. 610 ; also of horses, bay, ἵππων ξ. κάρηνα Il. 9.407 , cf. 11.680 ; ξ. πῶλοι Alc. Supp. 8.14 , S. El. 705 ; βοῶν ξανθὰς ἀγέλας Pi. P. 4.149 ; ξ. λέων Id. Fr. 237 ; πώλου δίκην, ἥ τις . . θέρος θερισθῇ ξανθὸν αὐχένων ἄπο S. Fr. 659.4 , etc. after Hom. of all kinds of objects, ἄρτοι ξ. Xenoph. 1.9 ; ξανθῶν σπονδὰς μελιτῶν v.l. in Emp. 128.7 ; ἴων ξ. ἀκτῖνες Pi. O. 6.55 ; ξ. νεφέλα, of gold, ib. 7.49 ; μέλι Simon. 47 ; φλόξ B. Fr. 3.4 ; ἀκτῖνες πυρός Sopat. 13 ; ἐλαία A. Pers. 617 ; of wine, ξ. Ἀφροδισία λάταξ S. Fr. 277 (lyr.) ; of a roast pigeon, Ar. Ach. 1106 ; ξανθαῖσιν αὔραις ἀγάλλεται exults in its yellow fragrance, of a fried fish, Antiph. 217.22 : in Medic., freq. of bile, Hp. VM 19 , etc. : Comp. -ότερος Pl. R. 617a : Sup. -ότατος, βόστρυχοι Pherecr. 189 . Ξάνθος, parox., as pr. n., a stream of the Troad, so called by gods, by men Scamander, Il. 20.74 , etc. a horse of Achilles, Bayard, the other being Βαλίος, Piebald, 16.149 . name of a man, D.H. 1.28 , etc. fem., a city of Lycia, Hdt. 1.176 , etc.
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐστοχάσθαι δὲ δεῖ τὴν τοιαύτην ἔμπλαστρον συντιθέντα πρὸς τῇ ποσότητι τοῦ ἰοῦ καὶ τῆς τῶν μιγνυμένων αὐτῷ χροιᾶς καὶ τοῦ τρόπου τῆς ἑψήσεως, ἐπὶ μὲν τῶν μιγνυμένων φυλαττόμενον τὰς δυσκινήτους χροιὰς, ὁπόσαι τῶν ξανθῶν εἰσι καὶ πυῤῥῶν καὶ μελάνων φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The one compounding such a plaster must take aim, besides the quantity of the verdigris, also at the colour of the things mixed with it and at the manner of the boiling: in the case of the things mixed, guarding against the colours that are hard to shift, such as are those of the yellow and reddish and black drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Whoever compounds such a plaster must attend, besides the quantity of the verdigris, to the colour of the ingredients mixed with it and to the manner of the boiling. In the ingredients mixed in, he must guard against the colours that are hard to change, such as those of yellow, russet and black drugs.

term_table.greek_sentence: μελάνων δὲ, οἷά περ πίττης τε καὶ ἀσφάλτου καὶ γῆς ἀμπελίτιδος καὶ λίθου γαγάτου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I mean by yellow and reddish such as is that of melite (μηλίτου) and that of burnt chalcitis, of arsenic and of sandarach; by black, such as are those of pitch and asphalt and ampelitis earth and gagates stone.
term_table.english_sentence_B: By black I mean such as those of pitch, asphalt, ampelitis earth and gagates stone.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: Γαγάτης (sc. λίθος), ου, ὁ, lignite, Orph. L. 474 , Plin. HN 36.141 , Dsc. 5.128 , Gal. 12.203 , Gp. 15.1.32 . jet, Solin. 22.11 . = ἀστράγαλος , cj. in Ps.- Dsc. 4.61 . (From Γάγας or Γάγγαι, a town and river in Lycia.)
term_table.greek_sentence: μελάνων δὲ, οἷά περ πίττης τε καὶ ἀσφάλτου καὶ γῆς ἀμπελίτιδος καὶ λίθου γαγάτου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I mean by yellow and reddish such as is that of melite (μηλίτου) and that of burnt chalcitis, of arsenic and of sandarach; by black, such as are those of pitch and asphalt and ampelitis earth and gagates stone.
term_table.english_sentence_B: By black I mean such as those of pitch, asphalt, ampelitis earth and gagates stone.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἕψ-ησις, εως, ἡ, boiling, Hp. VM 5 ; ἡ ἕ. τῶν κρεῶν Hdt. 4.61 , cf. SIG 57.34 (Milet., v B. C.); λινῶν PTeb. 406.22 (iii A. D.); smelting of ore, Thphr. HP 5.9.1 ; concoction, softening, Gal. 13.415 , Aret. SA 2.6 : pl., Pl. Plt. 303e .
term_table.greek_sentence: κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἕψησιν οὐ χρὴ τοῖς ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρὸς ἑνουμένοις συμβάλλεσθαι τὸν ἰὸν, ἀλλ’ ἑνωθεῖσι μίγνυσθαι κατὰ τὴν θυείαν, εἴπερ ἐθέλοις τῇ χρόᾳ χλωρὸν διαμεῖναι τὸ φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And in the boiling the verdigris must not be put in together with the things being united over the fire, but be mixed with them, once united, in the mortar, if you wish the drug to remain green in colour.
term_table.english_sentence_B: As for the boiling, the verdigris should not be added to the ingredients while they are being united over the fire; it should be mixed with them in the mortar once they have been united, if you want the drug to stay green in colour.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κιρρός, ά, όν, orange-tawny, between πυρρός and ξανθός, οἶνος Hp. Acut. 52 , cf. Arist. Fr. 307 , Mnesith. ap. Ath. 1.32d , Nic. Al. 44 ; τροχίσκος ὁ κ. Antyll. ap. Orib. 10.24.10 .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δέ γε μηλίνην βούλοιο ποιῆσαι τὴν ἔμπλαστρον, εἰδέναι χρή σε κατὰ τὴν ἕψησιν, εἰς πρώτην μὲν ταύτην τὴν χρόαν μεταβαλόντα τὸν ἰὸν, ὕστερον δὲ εἰς τὴν κιῤῥὰν, ὡς γενέσθαι τὴν ὀνομαζομένην δίχρωμον ἔμπλαστρον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if you wish to make the plaster quince-yellow, you must know that in the boiling the verdigris changes first into this colour, and later into the tawny, so that what is called the two-coloured plaster comes about.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if you wish to make the plaster quince-yellow, you must know that in the boiling the verdigris changes first into this colour, and later into tawny, so that the plaster called two-coloured results.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κιρρός, ά, όν, orange-tawny, between πυρρός and ξανθός, οἶνος Hp. Acut. 52 , cf. Arist. Fr. 307 , Mnesith. ap. Ath. 1.32d , Nic. Al. 44 ; τροχίσκος ὁ κ. Antyll. ap. Orib. 10.24.10 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν γὰρ τῷ μετὰ τὴν ἕψησιν χρόνῳ, μετ’ ὀλίγας ἡμέρας ἐπιπολῆς μὲν αὐτῇ γίγνεται τὸ φαιότερον, εἰς τὸ βάθος δὲ τοῦ φαρμάκου συντρέχει τὸ κιῤῥόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in the time after the boiling, after a few days, the greyer part forms on its surface, while the tawny runs together into the depth of the drug.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in the time after the boiling, after a few days, the duskier part forms on its surface, while the tawny part gathers into the depth of the drug.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χρώς, ὁ, gen. χρωτός, dat. χρωτί, acc. χρῶτα ( Att. χρώ only in Choerob. in Theod. 1.248H. ): Ep. and Ion. gen. χροός, dat. χροΐ, acc. χρόα (also in Lesbian, Sapph. Supp. 10.6 , al.), as always in Hom.and Hes. , exc. gen. χρωτός in Il. 10.575 , acc. χρῶτα Od. 18.172 , 179 , Hes. Op. 556 ; Emp. uses χρωτός, 76.3 (but χροΐ 100.17 ); Pi. uses χρωτί, χρῶτα, P. 1.55 , I. 4(3).23(41) ; these forms are freq. in Trag., but Ion. dat. χροΐ occurs in S. Tr. 605 , and χροός, χροΐ, χρόα are freq. in E., Hec. 548 , Med. 1175 , Ph. 264 , al. :—dat. χρῷ occurs in the phrase ἐν χρῷ v. infr.1.2 and in Sapph. 2.10 .—rare in Com.and Att. Prose. of the human body, skin or flesh, οὔ σφι λίθος χρὼς οὐδὲ σίδηρος Il. 4.510 ; καὶ γάρ θην τούτῳ τρωτὸς χρώς 21.568 ; χρῶτ' ἀπονιψαμένη Od. 18.172 ; ἀκρότατον δ' ἄρ' ὀϊστὸς ἐπέγραψε χρόα Il. 4.139 ; ταμέειν χρόα νηλέϊ χαλκῷ 13.501 ; λιλαιου|ένη χροὸς ἆσαι, of a spear, 21.168 ; κακὰ χροΐ εἵματ' ἔχοντα Od. 14.506 ; χρῷ πῦρ ὐπαδεδρόμακεν Sapph. 2.10 ; μύροις χρῶτα λιπαίνων Anaxil. 18.1 (anap.): esp. flesh, opp. bone, φθινύθει δ' ἀμφ' ὀστεόφι χρώς Od. 16.145 ; οὐδέ τί οἱ χρὼς σήπεται Il. 24.414 , cf. 19.33 (which usage is said by Gal. to have been Ionic, 18(2).435 , with reference to Hp. Fract. 9 ); τὸ δέρμα τοῦ χρωτός LXX Le. 13.11 , etc.; τοῦ χρωτὸς ἥδιστον ἀπέπνει Aristox. Fr.Hist. 84 : generally, one's body, frame, Pi. P. 1.55 , A. Fr. 192.6 (anap.); χριμφθῆναι χροΐ Id. Supp. 790 (lyr.); στεῖλαί νυν ἀμφὶ χρωτὶ . . πέπλους E. Ba. 821 , cf. S. Tr. 605 : pl., διὰ τί . . οἱ χρῶτες ὄζουσι; Arist. Pr. 877b21 ; also κατεδήσαντο . . τοὺς ὑγιεῖς χρῶτας, ὡς τραυματίαι D.H. 9.50 . ἐν χροΐ, or ἐν χρῷ, close to the skin, ἐν χροΐ κείρειν to shave close, Hdt. 4.175 ; ἐν χρῷ κεκαρμένοι X. HG 1.7.8 ; ἐν χρῷ κουριῶντας Pherecr. 30 :—metaph., to the quick, ξυρεῖ γὰρ ἐν χρῷ τοῦτο S. Aj. 786 ; ἐν χρῷ παραπλεῖν sail past so as to shave or graze, Th. 2.84 ; τὴν μάχην συνάψαι ἐν χρῷ to fight at close quarters, Plu. Thes. 27 ; ἡ ἐν χρῷ συνουσία close acquaintance, Luc. Ind. 3 : c. gen., ἐν χρῷ τινος close to, hard by a person or thing, τοῦ θώρακος ( v.l. σώματος ) Plu. 2.345a ; τῆς γῆς ib. 925b , Luc. Herm. 5 : abs., ἐν χρῷ near at hand, Id. Hist.Conscr. 24 , al.; cf. EM 313.53 , Hsch. the colour of the skin, complexion, μελαίνετο δὲ χρόα καλόν Il. 5.354 ; τρέπεται χ. his colour changes, i. e. he turns pale, 13.279 , cf. 17.733 ; ὠχρήσαντα χρόα Od. 11.529 ; χρόα . . ἀμείβειν Parm. 8.41 ; μεθίστη χρωτὸς . . φύσιν E. Alc. 174 ; μεταλλακτῆρα πουλύπουν χροός Ion Trag. 36 ; τί χρὼς τέτραπται; (paratrag.) Ar. Lys. 127 ; φεῦγε δ' ἀπὸ χρώς Theocr. 23.13 ; rare in Att. Prose, ἐπὶ τῷ χρωτὶ μέγα φρονεῖν X. Smp. 4.54 , cf. Oec. 10.5 : in Ion. Prose, of the colour of a finger, χροΐ δῆλα Pherecyd.Syr. ap. D.L. 1.118 ( v.l. χρωΐ , cf. Vorsokr. 5i . 44 ). generally, colour, ἀμείβων χρῶτα πορφυρᾷ βαφῇ A. Pers. 317 ; τὸν χρῶτα [μεταβάλλει] ὁ χαμαιλέων Arist. Mir. 832b14 ; χρὼς αἵματος Orph. L. 660 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐπεὶ δὲ περὶ τῆς χρόας αὐτῶν ﻿ [498] εἴρηται τὰ προσήκοντα, μεταβήσομαι πάλιν ἐπὶ τὸν περὶ τῶν δυνάμεων λόγον, ἀναμνήσας ὅθεν πρώτως ὡρμήθην κατὰ τόδε τὸ βιβλίον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But since what is appropriate has been said about their colour, [498] I shall pass again to the discussion of their powers, having recalled the point from which I first set out in this book.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Since what is fitting has been said about their colour, [498] I shall pass again to the account of the powers, recalling from where I first set out in this book.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σαρκ-ωτικός, ή, όν, making flesh grow, Id. 1.261 , 11.799 ; πληγῶν ς. interpol. in Dsc. 1.126 ; κόλπων ς. Id. 1.1.2 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὡρμήθην δὲ, εἴ τι μεμνήμεθα, περὶ τῶν σαρκωτικῶν φαρμάκων εἰπεῖν, ὧν ὁ μὲν τῆς δυνάμεως σκοπός ἐστιν ἐν τῷ μετρίως τε καὶ ἀδήκτως ῥύπτειν τε καὶ ξηραίνειν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I set out, if we remember, to speak about the flesh-producing drugs, whose aim with respect to their power lies in cleansing and drying moderately and without biting; but the compositions according to species are different, being varied according to the materials of the simple drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: I set out, if we remember at all, to speak about the flesh-producing drugs, the aim of whose power lies in cleansing and drying moderately and without biting.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σύν-θεσις, εως, ἡ, putting together, composition, combination, Pl. Phd. 93a , R. 611b ; τῶν λίθων Arist. EN 1174a23 , cf. IG 42(1).103.56 (Epid., iv B.C.), 7.3073.92 (Lebad., ii B.C.); τῶν σπονδύλων Sor. 1.102 ; storage, τῶν μήλων (quinces in a ῥίσκος) Phylarch. 10 J. ; but ἐλαιῶν ς. a preserve of olives, Gp. 9.28.2 . in concrete sense, junction, ὀστῶν Arist. PA 658b19 ; συνθέσεις (λέγω τὰς γωνίας) Id. Pr. 910b14 . in various technical senses: in Grammar, composition, γραμμάτων τε συνθέσεις, i.e. syllables and words, A. Pr. 460 , cf. Arist. Metaph. 1092a26 ; ς. ἔκ τε ῥημάτων γιγνομένη καὶ ὀνομάτων, i.e. sentences, Pl. Sph. 263d , cf. Cra. 431c , Arist. Po. 1458a28 , Gal. 15.487 ; περὶ συνθέσεως ὀνομάτων, title of work by D.H. ; also, the juxtaposition of letters in a word, Arist. Rh.Al. 1434b34 ; of an author's composition, Isoc. 10.11 ; so ἡ τῶν μέτρων ς. metrical composition, Arist. Po. 1449b35 ; ἡ τῶν ἐπῶν ς. D.S. 5.74 ; ἡ τοῦ παίωνος ξ. the way the paeon is made up, Plu. 2.1143d ; the constitution of things, Hp. Virg. 1 . Math., synthesis of a problem (opp. ἀνάλυσις), Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.7 , explained in Papp. 634 ; ἡ κατὰ ς. ἀγωγή synthetic procedure, Id. 412.2 . Math., ς. λόγου transformation of a ratio known as componendo, Euc. 5 Def. 14 ; κατὰ -σιν, = componendo, Archim. Aequil. 2.9 . Math., addition, Ph. 1.11 , Plu. 2.1018c , Dioph. 1 Intr.; καθ' ἁντινοῦν -σιν however many times added, i.e. whatever number of times taken (multiplied), Archim. Spir. 1 :—also as Pythag. name for 2 , Anatol. ap. Theol.Ar. 8 . in Logic, union of noun and verb or of two objects of thought in a statement, Arist. Int. 16a12 , de An. 430a27 ; also ὁ παρὰ τὴν ς. [λόγος] the fallacy of composition, opp. διαίρεσις, Id. SE 177a33 . in Physics, composition of substances, parts of organisms, from their elementary constituents, Id. PA 646a12 , Top. 151a23 ; opp μίξις (combination), Id. GC 328a6 . in Medicine, compounding of essences and drugs, τῶν μύρων Thphr. Od. 14 , al., cf. D.S. 4.45 , Aglaïas 8 . combination of parts so as to form a whole, γενέσεις καὶ ς. Pl. R. 533b ; ἡ τῶν στρωμάτων ς. Id. Plt. 280b , cf. Arist. PA 645a35 , Metaph. 1014b37 ; in plants, Thphr. HP 5.5.2 . in concrete sense, a social or political combination, Arist. Pol. 1276b7 ; a military formation, Ael. Tact. 18.5 . agreement, treaty, Pi. P. 4.168 , Fr. 205 ; πὸς τὰς συνθέσις in accordance with the agreements, IG 5(2).343.41 , 60 (Orchom. Arc. , iv B.C.); ἐκ συνθέσεως by arrangement, D.S. 13.112 , etc.; συνθέσεις περὶ γάμων Plu. Sull. 35 . ς. λόγων making up accounts, Stud.Pal. 4.70.391 (i A.D.); so ς. alone, εἰς σύνθεσιν τῷ βασιλεῖ PTeb. 714.6 (ii B.C.). set, service (most freq. in Lat. synthesis): collection of clothes, wardrobe, Dig. 34.2.38.1 ; also, dress, gown, costume, suit, ς. τελείας λευκὰς δεκατρεῖς, γυναικείας ς. PHamb. 10.13 , 21 (ii A.D.), cf. POxy. 1153.23 (i A.D.), 496.4 (ii A.D.), PSI 10.1117.11 , 13 (ii A.D.), Mart. 2.46.4 , 5.79.2 ; synthesinam indutus, Suet. Ner. 51 . service of plate, ς. πινακίων BGU 781 i 5 (i A.D.), cf. Mart. 4.46.15 , Stat. Silv. 4.9.44 .
term_table.greek_sentence: αἱ δὲ κατ’ εἴδη συνθέσεις διάφοροι κατὰ τὰς τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων ὕλας ὑπαλλαττόμεναι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: I set out, if we remember, to speak about the flesh-producing drugs, whose aim with respect to their power lies in cleansing and drying moderately and without biting; but the compositions according to species are different, being varied according to the materials of the simple drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Their compoundings by species, however, are various, varying according to the materials of the simple drugs.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐπιρροή, ἡ , ʽἐπιρρέω) afflux, influx, κακαῖς ἐ. ὕδωρ μιαίνων A. Eu. 694 ; ἐπιρροαῖσιν αἱμάτων Id. Ag. 1510 (lyr.); δακρύων ἐπιρροαί E. Fr. 573 ; ἐ. αἵματος determination of blood to . . , Hp. VC 13 ; opp. ἀπορροή (efflux), Ti.Locr. 102b ; τῆς τροφῆς Thphr. CP 5.4.6 ; κατ' ἐπιρροάν Ti. Locr. 101d : metaph., αὔξην τε καὶ ἐ. (sc. νοσημάτων) Pl. Lg. 783b ; ἐ. κακῶν E. Andr. 349 (pl.); ἀνάμνησίς ἐστιν ἐ. φρονήσεως ἀπολιπούσης Pl. Lg. 732b . . stream of a river, A. Fr. 143 (pl.), A.R. 4.623 (pl.). . channel, duct, Hp. Gland. 12 (pl.). . irrigation, Ph. 1.249 .
term_table.greek_sentence: πρόδηλον δ’ ὅτι τὰ κυρίως τε καὶ πρώτως ὀνομαζόμενα σαρκωτικὰ τῶν ἀπεριστάτων ἐλκῶν ἐστι σαρκωτικὰ, τουτέστιν ὅσα κοῖλα μὲν οὐ μὴν ῥύπον ἢ φλεγμονὴν ἔχει συνοῦσαν, ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον οὐδ’ ἐπιῤῥοὴν ὑγρῶν μοχθηρῶν, οὐδὲ δύσκρατον κατὰ τὸ κοῖλον ἕλκος σάρκα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is evident that those properly and primarily called flesh-producing are flesh-producing for uncomplicated ulcers, that is, those which are hollow but do not have filth or inflammation attending them, and still less an influx of bad humours, nor dyscratic flesh in the hollow ulcer.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is evident that the drugs properly and primarily called flesh-producing are flesh-producing for uncomplicated wounds, that is, those which are hollow but do not have filth or inflammation present with them, and still more, have no influx of bad fluids, nor badly tempered flesh in the hollow wound.

term_table.greek_sentence: πρόδηλον δ’ ὅτι τὰ κυρίως τε καὶ πρώτως ὀνομαζόμενα σαρκωτικὰ τῶν ἀπεριστάτων ἐλκῶν ἐστι σαρκωτικὰ, τουτέστιν ὅσα κοῖλα μὲν οὐ μὴν ῥύπον ἢ φλεγμονὴν ἔχει συνοῦσαν, ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον οὐδ’ ἐπιῤῥοὴν ὑγρῶν μοχθηρῶν, οὐδὲ δύσκρατον κατὰ τὸ κοῖλον ἕλκος σάρκα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is evident that those properly and primarily called flesh-producing are flesh-producing for uncomplicated ulcers, that is, those which are hollow but do not have filth or inflammation attending them, and still less an influx of bad humours, nor dyscratic flesh in the hollow ulcer.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is evident that the drugs properly and primarily called flesh-producing are flesh-producing for uncomplicated wounds, that is, those which are hollow but do not have filth or inflammation present with them, and still more, have no influx of bad fluids, nor badly tempered flesh in the hollow wound.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κοῖλος, η, ον, Aeol. and Ion. κοίϊλος, prob. in Alc. 15.5 , Mimn. 12.6 ; κόϊλος, α, ον, Anacr. 9 ( Comp. -ώτερα), cf. A.D. term_table.greek_sentence: πρόδηλον δ’ ὅτι τὰ κυρίως τε καὶ πρώτως ὀνομαζόμενα σαρκωτικὰ τῶν ἀπεριστάτων ἐλκῶν ἐστι σαρκωτικὰ, τουτέστιν ὅσα κοῖλα μὲν οὐ μὴν ῥύπον ἢ φλεγμονὴν ἔχει συνοῦσαν, ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον οὐδ’ ἐπιῤῥοὴν ὑγρῶν μοχθηρῶν, οὐδὲ δύσκρατον κατὰ τὸ κοῖλον ἕλκος σάρκα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is evident that those properly and primarily called flesh-producing are flesh-producing for uncomplicated ulcers, that is, those which are hollow but do not have filth or inflammation attending them, and still less an influx of bad humours, nor dyscratic flesh in the hollow ulcer.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is evident that the drugs properly and primarily called flesh-producing are flesh-producing for uncomplicated wounds, that is, those which are hollow but do not have filth or inflammation present with them, and still more, have no influx of bad fluids, nor badly tempered flesh in the hollow wound.

Gland. 12 (pl.). . irrigation, Ph. 1.249 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τῶν δ’ ἐξ ἐπιῤῥοῆς ὑγροῦ τὸ ξηραίνειν τε καὶ ἀποκρούεσθαι τὸ ἐπιῤῥέον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And the aims of their treatment are, in the case of the filthy ones, the drugs capable of cleansing; in the case of those arising from an influx of humour, drying and repelling that which flows in; and if it should be abundant and hard to overcome, to cut off the cause of the influx first.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The aims of their treatment are, in the case of filthy wounds, the drugs that are able to cleanse; in the case of those arising from an influx of fluid, to dry and to repel what flows in.

term_table.greek_sentence: εὔδηλον δ’ ὅτι καὶ τῶν μὲν φλεγμαινόντων τὴν φλεγμονὴν [499] ἰᾶσθαι χρὴ, τῶν δὲ δύσκρατον ἐχόντων τὴν σάρκα μορίων, εὔκρατον ταύτην ἐργάσασθαι, δυσκράτου δὲ αὐτῆς γιγνομένης, κατὰ τρόπους ἁπλοῦς μὲν τέτταρας, συνθέτους δὲ ἄλλους τέτταρας, ἡ ἴασις ἔσται διὰ τῶν ἐναντίων ποιοτήτων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And it is quite evident that, in the case of inflamed parts, one must cure the inflammation [499], while in the case of parts whose flesh is dyscratic, one must render it eucratic; and since it becomes dyscratic in four simple modes and in four other composite ones, the cure will be effected by means of the opposite qualities.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is quite clear that, in the case of inflamed parts, one must also [499] heal the inflammation, and in the case of parts that have their flesh badly tempered, one must make it well tempered. Since the flesh becomes badly tempered in four simple ways and in four other, compound, ways, the cure will be by means of the opposite qualities.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐπιτεταμένην δὲ τὴν ῥυπτικὴν δύναμιν ἔχει τὰ τὸν πολὺν ἀφαιροῦντα ῥύπον, ὥστ’ ἔνια τῶν εἰρημένων φαρμάκων χλωρῶν ἑνὶ μόνῳ τῶν ἁπλῶς σαρκωτικῶν διαφέρει τῷ πλήθει τοῦ ἰοῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But those which remove abundant filth have the cleansing power intensified, so that some of the green drugs mentioned differ from the simply flesh-producing ones in one thing only, the quantity of verdigris; and some differ also by the admixture of other ingredients, such as cleanse vigorously, as for instance the one called Isis and that of Machairion, and the one which we habitually use, called 'oily' (elaiōdes) on account of its use.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Those that remove a great deal of filth have an intensified cleansing power, so that some of the green drugs already mentioned differ from the simply flesh-producing ones in one thing alone, the quantity of verdigris.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κύστις, εως, ιος, also ιδος Aen.Tact. 31.12 (cf. infr. 11 ), ἡ: (κύω):— bladder, Il. 5.67 , 13.652 , S. Fr. 394 , Hp. Art. 41 , Pl. Ti. 91a , Ph. Bel. 102.40 , etc.; ὥσπερ κύστιν φυσᾶν, of the wind swelling out the clouds, Ar. Nu. 405 ; κ. ὑεία used as a pouch, Id. term_table.greek_sentence: ἔνθα γὰρ ἡμῖν πρόκειται σαρκῶσαι κόλπον, ἐλαίῳ πολλῷ τήκοντες ἐγχέομεν αὐτὸ δι’ εὐθυτρήτου κέρατος, ἐν τρόπῳ κλυστῆρος [500] ὑείᾳ κύστει συνημμένου, χρώμεθα καὶ τοῖς καλουμένοις πυουλκοῖς ἐπ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ γὰρ καὶ τούτων, ὅσοις εὐρύτερόν ἐστι τὸ τρῆμα, χρήσιμοι πρὸς τὴν τοιαύτην ὑπηρεσίαν εἰσί.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For where it is our task to produce flesh in a sinus, we melt it in a large quantity of oil and pour it in through a horn bored straight through, in the manner of a clyster [500] attached to a pig's bladder; we also use the so-called pus-drawers (pyoulkoi) for this purpose, for of these too, those which have a wider bore are useful for such a service.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For where our task is to fill a sinus with flesh, we melt it in a large quantity of oil and pour it in through a straight-bored horn joined, in the manner of a clyster, [500] to a pig's bladder; we also use for this the so-called pus-drawers (pyulci). Of these too, those with a wider bore are serviceable for such a purpose.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ μὲν οὖν ὑποψία τις εἴη μεμιγμένης φλεγμονῆς ἔτι βραχείας τῷ κόλπῳ, διὰ ῥοδίνου πάντως τηκέσθω τὸ φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: If, then, there should be some suspicion that a still slight inflammation is mingled with the sinus, let the drug by all means be melted in rose-oil; but if it is free of inflammation, in olive oil, and if it tolerates without biting the admixture of old oil, let the drug be melted in that.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If, then, there should be some suspicion of a slight inflammation still mixed in with the sinus, let the drug by all means be melted in rose oil.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δ’ ἀφλέγμαντος εἴη, δι’ ἐλαίου, κᾂν ἀδήκτως ἀνέχηται τῆς τοῦ παλαιοῦ μίξεως, ἐκείνῳ διατηκέσθω τὸ φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: If, then, there should be some suspicion that a still slight inflammation is mingled with the sinus, let the drug by all means be melted in rose-oil; but if it is free of inflammation, in olive oil, and if it tolerates without biting the admixture of old oil, let the drug be melted in that.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if the sinus is free of inflammation, let it be melted in oil; and if it tolerates the admixture of old oil without being bitten, let the drug be dissolved in that.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ δὲ οἱ κόλποι τῶν ὑγροτέρων δέονται φαρμάκων οὐ δυναμένων ἐνίεσθαι τῶν παχυτέρων, οὕτως ὅσα τῶν κοίλων ἑλκῶν ἐπιπολῆς ἐστι, παχυτέρου χρῄζει φαρμάκου διὰ τὸ ταχέως αὐτῶν ἀποῤῥεῖν τὰ ὑγρὰ καὶ καταλείπεσθαι ξηροὺς τοὺς μότους.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And just as sinuses need the more liquid drugs, since the thicker ones cannot be injected, so those of the hollow ulcers that lie on the surface require a thicker drug, because the liquids flow off them quickly and the lint-plugs are left dry.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Just as sinuses need the more liquid drugs, since the thicker ones cannot be injected, so those hollow ulcers that are superficial require a thicker drug, because the liquids quickly run off them and the lint-tents are left dry.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κηρωτή, ἡ , ʽκηρόὠ = κήρωμα 1 , cerate or salve, used medically, Hp. Off. 12 , Art. 14 , Ar. Ach. 1176 , Ph. Bel. 96.18 ; κ. οἰνανθίνη, ῥοδίνη, Dsc. 1.109 , 2.110 ; κ. ὑγρά Gal. 11.391 ; used as a cosmetic, Ar. Fr. 320.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰκότως οὖν ἐπὶ μὲν τῶν τοιούτων τοῖς ἰσχυρῶς ῥυπτικοῖς μίγνυμεν κηρωτὴν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν κόλπων ἔλαιον ἢ ῥόδινον πάμπολυ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Reasonably, then, in such cases we mix cerate with the strongly detergent drugs, whereas in the case of sinuses we mix in a very great quantity of oil or rose-oil.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Reasonably, then, in such cases we mix cerate with the strongly detergent drugs, but in the case of sinuses we mix in a very large quantity of olive oil or rose oil.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πολύ-χρηστος, ον, useful for many purposes, very useful, Arist. GA 789b9 , Pol. 1337b26 , Dsc. 1.1 , Gal. 6.534 , 480 ( Sup. ); τὸ π. Corn. ND 9 : Comp. , Muson. Fr. 20p.112H. , Alex.Aphr. in Top. 277.4 . Adv. -τως v.l. in Paul.Aeg. 7.16 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ταυτὶ δὲ τὰ οὕτως ῥυπτικὰ φάρμακα πάντως ἐστὶ καὶ διαφορητικὰ, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ξηραντικὰ σφοδρῶς, καὶ γίγνεταί τι γένος αὐτῶν κοινὸν, ὃ καλοῦσι πολύχρηστον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: These drugs that are detergent in this way are in every case also discutient, and for this reason also strongly desiccative, and there arises a certain common kind of them, which they call 'polychreston' (of many uses).
term_table.english_sentence_B: These drugs that are detergent in this way are certainly also discutient, and for this reason also strongly desiccant, and there arises a certain common class of them which they call polychrest.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐπέκεινα δὲ τούτου τοῦ γένους ἐστὶ τὸ τῶν πάνυ δριμέων ἐμπλάστρων, ὁποῖαι καὶ αἱ καλούμεναι δι’ ἁλῶν εἰσιν, ἃς οὐ χρὴ προσφέρειν ἔνθα σαρκῶσαί τι βουλόμεθα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Beyond this kind lies that of the very acrid plasters, such as those called 'through salts' (di' halōn), which one must not apply where we wish to produce flesh in some part.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Beyond this class lies that of the very acrid plasters, such as also those called 'with salts', which one must not apply where we wish to promote the growth of flesh.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀφρόνιτρον, Att. ἀφρόλιτρον (the two distd. by Gal.l.c., cf. term_table.greek_sentence: ἐπὶ τό γε ξηραίνειν οὐδὲν ἧττον ἔχουσιν ἀφρονίτρου καὶ νίτρου, ἀλλ’ ἐκείνοις μὲν οὐ μέτεστι τῆς στυπτικῆς δυνάμεως, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ [502] τῷ τῆς Ἀσίας πέτρας ἄνθει καὶ διὰ τοῦτο διαφορεῖν τε δύναται καὶ κηρωταῖς μιγνύμενα καθαίρειν ἕλκη ῥυπαρά.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For as regards drying, at least, they are in no way inferior to aphronitron and nitron; but those two have no share in the astringent power, just as neither does [502] the flower of the stone of Asia, and for this reason they are able both to disperse and, when mixed with cerates, to cleanse foul ulcers.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Accordingly, for you who bear these things in mind and have heard the method both of the composition and of the use of all such drugs, I shall write in what follows those drugs that have been approved by experience on the part of the physicians renowned for their knowledge of the best drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For you, then, who remember these things and have heard the method both of the composition and of the use of all such drugs, I shall write down in what follows the drugs that have been tested by experience at the hands of the reputable physicians, with a view to knowledge of the best drugs.

term_table.greek_sentence: πρώτων δὲ τῶν περὶ Μαντίαν καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν αὐτοῦ τὸν Ταραντῖνον Ἡρακλεί δην πολλὰ φάρμακα γραψάντων, ἃ τοῖς μετὰ ταῦτα διὰ πείρας ἀφικόμενα διωρίσθη.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Mantias and his pupil Heraclides of Tarentum were the first to write down many drugs, which, having come to the test of experience among those who followed them, were sorted out (διωρίσθη); and the best among them these men in turn wrote down again, while those that seemed to act less effectively than the others they left aside.
term_table.english_sentence_B: First came Mantias and his pupil Heraclides of Tarentum, who wrote down many drugs; these, having come down to their successors, were sifted by experience.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And there is also one book of Menecrates entitled [503] 'Autokrator hologrammatos (The Emperor, written out in full letters) of noteworthy drugs'.

D. 18.165 ; ἐπὶ μετρίοις Th. 4.22 ; μηδὲν μ. λέγειν nothing tolerably accurate, Pl. Tht. 181b ; -ωτάτη ἡ δημοκρατία least intolerable, Arist. Pol. 1289b4 , cf. Fr. 967 (lyr.); εἰ δ' ἦσθα μ. τἄλλα γ' ἡδίστη θεῶν πέφυκας Id. Hel. 1105 ; also, moderate, fair, Thgn. 615 , Pl. term_table.lsj_entry_text: χρώς, ὁ, gen. χρωτός, dat. χρωτί, acc. χρῶτα ( Att. χρώ only in Choerob. in Theod. 1.248H. ): Ep. and Ion. gen. χροός, dat. χροΐ, acc. χρόα (also in Lesbian, Sapph. Supp. 10.6 , al.), as always in Hom.and Hes. , exc. gen. χρωτός in Il. 10.575 , acc. χρῶτα Od. 18.172 , 179 , Hes. Op. 556 ; Emp. uses χρωτός, 76.3 (but χροΐ 100.17 ); Pi. uses χρωτί, χρῶτα, P. 1.55 , I. 4(3).23(41) ; these forms are freq. in Trag., but Ion. dat. χροΐ occurs in S. Tr. 605 , and χροός, χροΐ, χρόα are freq. in E., Hec. 548 , Med. 1175 , Ph. 264 , al. :—dat. χρῷ occurs in the phrase ἐν χρῷ v. infr.1.2 and in Sapph. 2.10 .—rare in Com.and Att. Prose. of the human body, skin or flesh, οὔ σφι λίθος χρὼς οὐδὲ σίδηρος Il. 4.510 ; καὶ γάρ θην τούτῳ τρωτὸς χρώς 21.568 ; χρῶτ' ἀπονιψαμένη Od. 18.172 ; ἀκρότατον δ' ἄρ' ὀϊστὸς ἐπέγραψε χρόα Il. 4.139 ; ταμέειν χρόα νηλέϊ χαλκῷ 13.501 ; λιλαιου|ένη χροὸς ἆσαι, of a spear, 21.168 ; κακὰ χροΐ εἵματ' ἔχοντα Od. 14.506 ; χρῷ πῦρ ὐπαδεδρόμακεν Sapph. 2.10 ; μύροις χρῶτα λιπαίνων Anaxil. 18.1 (anap.): esp. flesh, opp. bone, φθινύθει δ' ἀμφ' ὀστεόφι χρώς Od. 16.145 ; οὐδέ τί οἱ χρὼς σήπεται Il. 24.414 , cf. 19.33 (which usage is said by Gal. to have been Ionic, 18(2).435 , with reference to Hp. Fract. 9 ); τὸ δέρμα τοῦ χρωτός LXX Le. 13.11 , etc.; τοῦ χρωτὸς ἥδιστον ἀπέπνει Aristox. Fr.Hist. 84 : generally, one's body, frame, Pi. P. 1.55 , A. Fr. 192.6 (anap.); χριμφθῆναι χροΐ Id. Supp. 790 (lyr.); στεῖλαί νυν ἀμφὶ χρωτὶ . . πέπλους E. Ba. 821 , cf. S. Tr. 605 : pl., διὰ τί . . οἱ χρῶτες ὄζουσι; Arist. Pr. 877b21 ; also κατεδήσαντο . . τοὺς ὑγιεῖς χρῶτας, ὡς τραυματίαι D.H. 9.50 . ἐν χροΐ, or ἐν χρῷ, close to the skin, ἐν χροΐ κείρειν to shave close, Hdt. 4.175 ; ἐν χρῷ κεκαρμένοι X. HG 1.7.8 ; ἐν χρῷ κουριῶντας Pherecr. 30 :—metaph., to the quick, ξυρεῖ γὰρ ἐν χρῷ τοῦτο S. Aj. 786 ; ἐν χρῷ παραπλεῖν sail past so as to shave or graze, Th. 2.84 ; τὴν μάχην συνάψαι ἐν χρῷ to fight at close quarters, Plu. Thes. 27 ; ἡ ἐν χρῷ συνουσία close acquaintance, Luc. Ind. 3 : c. gen., ἐν χρῷ τινος close to, hard by a person or thing, τοῦ θώρακος ( v.l. σώματος ) Plu. 2.345a ; τῆς γῆς ib. 925b , Luc. Herm. 5 : abs., ἐν χρῷ near at hand, Id. Hist.Conscr. 24 , al.; cf. EM 313.53 , Hsch. the colour of the skin, complexion, μελαίνετο δὲ χρόα καλόν Il. 5.354 ; τρέπεται χ. his colour changes, i. e. he turns pale, 13.279 , cf. 17.733 ; ὠχρήσαντα χρόα Od. 11.529 ; χρόα . . ἀμείβειν Parm. 8.41 ; μεθίστη χρωτὸς . . φύσιν E. Alc. 174 ; μεταλλακτῆρα πουλύπουν χροός Ion Trag. 36 ; τί χρὼς τέτραπται; (paratrag.) Ar. Lys. 127 ; φεῦγε δ' ἀπὸ χρώς Theocr. 23.13 ; rare in Att. Prose, ἐπὶ τῷ χρωτὶ μέγα φρονεῖν X. Smp. 4.54 , cf. Oec. 10.5 : in Ion. Prose, of the colour of a finger, χροΐ δῆλα Pherecyd.Syr. ap. D.L. 1.118 ( v.l. χρωΐ , cf. Vorsokr. 5i . 44 ). generally, colour, ἀμείβων χρῶτα πορφυρᾷ βαφῇ A. Pers. 317 ; τὸν χρῶτα [μεταβάλλει] ὁ χαμαιλέων Arist. Mir. 832b14 ; χρὼς αἵματος Orph. L. 660 .

term_table.english_sentence_A: And when these have dissolved well, set the cauldron down and let it cool well, then add the verdigris, and having stirred it while it is down, boil again over a gentle fire until it becomes quince-like in colour; then, having triturated the galbanum and the frankincense and having poured [the mixture] out into a mortar, where the ammoniac has previously been triturated in vinegar so as to be glutinous, and having kneaded it, take it up at once, and having poured on a little vinegar, leave it until the following day, and then, having kneaded it again, store it away.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Then, having ground the galbanum and the frankincense, pour it off into a mortar in which the ammoniac has previously been ground in vinegar so as to be viscous, and after kneading, take it up at once; pour on a little vinegar and leave it until the following day, and then knead it again and store it.
