term_table.lsj_entry_text: κηρωτή, ἡ , ʽκηρόὠ = κήρωμα 1 , cerate or salve, used medically, Hp. Off. 12 , Art. 14 , Ar. Ach. 1176 , Ph. Bel. 96.18 ; κ. οἰνανθίνη, ῥοδίνη, Dsc. 1.109 , 2.110 ; κ. ὑγρά Gal. 11.391 ; used as a cosmetic, Ar. Fr. 320.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀνειμένη αὕτη τῆς ἀκράτου μέρος ἓν, κηρωτῆς μέρη β΄.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And in cases where another malagma does not work, this works exactly: nails loosened by a stumble it either fixes firm or casts off, and teeth loosened by a blow it fixes firm; and in general there are countless conditions for which it works when handled in different ways.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It also treats fistulas, applied over them and inserted as a collyrium, removing their callus and agglutinating them.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πάροδος (B), ἡ, way by or past, passage, Th. 3.21 , Arist. Cael. 294b26 ; π. καὶ τροπαὶ τῶν ἄστρων ib. 296b4 , cf. Simp. in Cael. 507.24 ; π. τοῦ χρόνου passage, lapse of time, Porph. Sent. 44 . Astrol., rotation of chronocratory, Vett. Val. 37.9 , cf. Ptol. Tetr. 109 . going by or past, passing, entrance, Th. 4.82 ; ἐν τῃ ͂ π. as they passed by, Id. 1.126 , cf. Plb. 5.68.8 ; κατὰ τὴν π. Id. 21.46.12 ; ἐκ π., ἐν π., by the way, cursorily, Arist. Cael. 306b27 , Phld. Rh. 1.245 S. , D.S. 18.16 ; π. τινὶ ἐπὶ τὰς ὕστερον πράξεις διδόναι Plu. 2.345c ; τὴν π. ἵν' ἔχῃς τῶν θυρῶν εὐνουστέραν entrance by the door, Dionys. Com. 3.17 . narrow entrance or approach, mountain-pass, as Thermopylae, etc., Lys. 2.30 , X. An. 4.7.4 , etc.; λαβεῖν τὰς π. take the pass, D. 5.20 , cf. 9.32 , Phld. Rh. 1.334 S. ; opp. δίοδοι, X. Cyn. 6.6 . esp. side-entrance on the stage, Semus 20 , Poll. 4.126 . gallery or passage-way surmounting fortifications, IG 22.463.49 , 52 , 1672.110 . coming forward, appearance, esp. before the assembly, D. Ep. 3.29 , Jul. Or. 7.205b , etc. first entrance of a chorus in the orchestra, which was made from the side wings, Arist. EN 1123a23 , Poll. 4.108 ; ὥσπερ δράματος Plu. 2.805d . first song sung by the chorus after its entrance, Arist. Po. 1452b22 , Plu. 2.785a . use of stage for an artist's performance, ἡ π. εὗρεν δραχμήν Michel 908 , 909 (lasos). public recitation, AP 11.422 ( Antioch. ). in a ship, gangway, passage along the deck, Plu. Demetr. 43 : metaph., π. καὶ ἐπιβάθρα τοῦ συγγράφειν Artem. 3 Praef.
term_table.greek_sentence: οὐ γὰρ δίδωσι τῇ ὕλῃ πάροδον εἰς ἐπίτασιν τοῦ πάθους.

Ἀτρεῖ because of his relationship to Atreus, Th. 1.9 . friendly, εἴχομέν ποτε . . τὸν τόπον τοῦτον οἰ. D. 4.4 ; οὓς ἂν ἡγήσαιτο -οτάτους τε καὶ ἑταιροτάτους Pl. Phd. 89e . of things. belonging to one's house or family, one's own (defined as ὅταν ἐφ' αὑτῷ ᾖ ἀπαλλοτριῶσαι Arist. Rh. 1361a21 ), οἰ. ἄρουραι Pi. O. 12.19 ; σταθμοῖς ἐν οἰκείοισι A. Ag. 1220 , v. βορά. in Stoic Philos., endeared by nature to all animals, including man, τὸ πρῶτον οἰ. what is earliest endeared, Chrysipp.Stoic. 3.43 , Hierocl. p.7A. proper to a thing, fitting, suitable, οὔτε . . καλὸν οὐδὲν [οὐδ'] οἰκήϊον Hdt. 3.81 , cf. term_table.english_sentence_A: And I have mentioned many of them by name in the present treatise and shall mention them again; and indeed I have added this drug here too, wishing to remind you of these very things which I have just said, since in fact it too is of the same kind as those written before in the book preceding this one, and it would have been more appropriate for it to have been written together with those.

term_table.english_sentence_A: [The black Hicesian plaster of Andromachus.] This plaster Andromachus wrote not in the place where he wrote the green ones, but higher up, near the beginning, and in a proportion differing greatly from that in which, as I showed earlier, both Crito and Heras wrote it.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And although others too have written this plaster of Hicesius, those who prepared it more accurately, in accordance both with the Tarentine and with the [prescription] judged by us through boiling to be the true one, have turned out in agreement; but those who [did so] more carelessly, whether in one only or two of the ingredients mixed in or even more, are seen to disagree with Heracleides.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And although others have also written up this plaster of Hicesius, those who prepared it more precisely have turned out to be in agreement both with the Tarentine and with the recipe judged by us to be truly correct by means of the boiling; but those who prepared it more carelessly appear to disagree with Heraclides either in only one or two of the ingredients mixed, or even in more.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Heracleides says that the following is the plain [plaster] of Hicesius: Take asphalt 50 drachms, litharge 50 drachms, oil 10 kotylai; boil, and when it sets, add wax 5 drachms, galbanum 5 drachms, myrrh 5 drachms.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Heraclides says that the simple plaster of Hicesius is as follows. ℞ Asphalt, 50 drachms; litharge, 50 dr.; oil, 10 kotylai.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: [Κυζικηνὴ τοῦ Ἥρα.] Τῶν ἐνδόξων ἐμπλάστρων ἐστὶ καὶ αὕτη, σχεδὸν ὑπὸ πάντων γεγραμμένη, τὰ πλεῖστα μὲν ἐν τῇ συμμετρίᾳ τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων ὁμολογούμενα γραψάντων αὐτῶν, ἐνίοις δὲ καὶ διαφωνησάντων, [815] ὡς ἔσται φανερὸν ὑπογραψάντων ἡμῶν ὡς ἕκαστος αὐτῶν ἀξιοῖ συντίθεσθαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [The Cyzicene of Heras.] This too is one of the celebrated plasters, written down by nearly everyone, these authors having for the most part written things that agree as regards the proportion of the simple drugs, but having also disagreed in some, [815] as will be evident when we have set down below how each of them thinks it ought to be compounded.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐσχάρ-α, Ion. ἐσχαρ-άρη [α], ἡ, Ep. gen. and dat. ἐσχαρόφιν (ἀπ' ἐσχ- Od. 7.169 , ἐπ' ἐσχ- 5.59 , 19.389 ):—hearth, fire-place, like ἑστία , Hom. (esp. in Od. ), ἡ μὲν ἐπ' ἐσχάρῃ ἧστο Od. 6.52 ; ἧσται ἐπ' ἐσχάρῃ ἐν πυρὸς αὐγῇ ib. 305 ; of suppliants, ἕζετ' ἐπ' ἐσχάρῃ ἐν κονίῃσι 7.153 . pan of coals, brazier, Ar. Ach. 888 , V. 938 , cf. Poll. 10.94 , 95 . Τρώων πυρὸς ἐσχάραι watch-fires of the camp, Il. 10.418 . sacrificial hearth (hollowed out in the ground and so dist. from βωμός, structural altar, St.Byz. s.v. βωμοί , Phot. ; used esp. in heroworship, Neanth. 7J. ), Od. 14.420 , S. Ant. 1016 : but freq. used generally, altar of burnt-offering, πρὸς ἐσχάραν Φοίβου A. Pers. 205 ; ἐπ' ἐσχάρᾳ πυρός Id. Eu. 108 ; ἡμένας ἐπ' ἐσχάραις ib. 806 ; Πυθική E. Andr. 1240 ; at Eleusis, D. 59.116 , cf. Lycurg. Fr. 37 ; Ἡρακλειδῶν ἐ. IG 2.1658 (iv B.C.) ; so βώμιοι ἐσχάραι structured altars, E. Ph. 274 ; sometimes movable, X. Cyr. 8.3.12 , Callix. 2 , PCair.Zen. 13 (iii B.C.). fire-stick (bored with the τρύπανον, q. v.), Thphr. HP 5.9.7 , Ign. 64 . platform, stand, basis, Ph. Bel. 92.13 , Ath.Mech. 32.10 , Vitr. 10.11.9 . grating, LXX Ex. 27.4 , al. Medic., scab, eschar on a wound caused by burning or otherwise, τὰς ἐκπτώσιας τῶν ἐ. Hp. Art. 11 , cf. Pl.Com. 184.4 , Arist. Pr. 863a12 , Dsc. 1.56 , Gal. 10.315 , etc. in pl., = τὰ χείλη τῶν γυναικείων αἰδοίων , Ar. Eq. 1286 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐκτινάσσει δ’ ἀλύπως καὶ ἐσχάρας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It especially disperses the hardnesses in the breasts, draws, cleanses, fills up, agglutinates, cicatrizes.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It disperses above all the indurations in the breasts; it draws, cleanses out, fills up, agglutinates and cicatrises.

term_table.greek_sentence: ταῦτα γραψάντων περὶ τῆς Κυζικηνῆς τοῦ τε Ἥρα καὶ τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου δόξει μέν τισιν εἶναι διαφωνία μεγίστη, τοῦ μὲν Ἥρα λιβάνου καὶ κρόκου καὶ σμύρνης καὶ τοῦ ἐφεξῆς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένου βάλλοντος δραχ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But what I was already saying before too, that we must keep in view, this I shall say now as well: if, in the case of all the simple drugs, someone were to put in even double the quantities written by others, the same proportion results, just as also if all were triple.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But what I have already said before, that we must necessarily watch for, I shall say now as well: if all the simple drugs are put in at double the amounts written by others, the same proportion results, just as it does if all are tripled.

term_table.english_sentence_B: Andromachus has also added poppy juice for the sake of freedom from pain, and acacia and rose flower as astringent.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἕψ-ησις, εως, ἡ, boiling, Hp. VM 5 ; ἡ ἕ. τῶν κρεῶν Hdt. 4.61 , cf. SIG 57.34 (Milet., v B. C.); λινῶν PTeb. 406.22 (iii A. D.); smelting of ore, Thphr. HP 5.9.1 ; concoction, softening, Gal. 13.415 , Aret. SA 2.6 : pl., Pl. Plt. 303e .
term_table.greek_sentence: τὴν δὲ ἕψησιν ὁ μὲν Ἥρας ἔγραψεν ὡς ἔθος αὐτῷ, παραλείπει δὲ ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος, ὡς καὶ τούτῳ πάλιν ἔθος ἐστὶ σπανιάκις γράφοντι τὴν ἕψησιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The boiling Heras wrote, as is his custom, but Andromachus omits it, as it is again this man's custom too, since he rarely writes the boiling.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The boiling Heras wrote out, as is his custom, but Andromachus omits it, since this too, again, is his custom: he rarely writes out the boiling.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: δῆλος (also Dor. , Archyt. 1 , Theoc. 11.79 , etc., and Aeol. , cf. πρόδηλος), η, ον, also ος, ον E. Med. 1197 : Ep. δέελος: prop. visible, conspicuous, δέελον δ' ἐπὶ σῆμά τ' ἔθηκε Il. 10.466 , but: commonly, clear to the mind, manifest, νῦν δ' ἤδη τόδε δ. Od. 20.333 , etc. δ. εἰμι is freq. used c. part., δ. ἐστιν ἀλγεινῶς φέρων i.e. it is clear that he takes it ill, S. Ph. 1011 , cf. OT 673 , 1008 , etc.; οἳ ἂν δ. ὦσι μὴ ἐπιτρέψοντες who are clearly not going to permit, Th. 1.71 ; with ὡς, δ. ἐστιν ὥς τι δρασείων κακόν S. Aj. 326 ; δ. ἔσεσθε ὡς ὀργιζόμενοι Lys. 12.90 , cf. X. An. 1.5.9 ; δ. ὁρᾶσθαι . . ὤν being as was plainly to be seen, E. Or. 350 : with ὅτι and a Verb, δ. ἐστιν ὅτι . . ἀκήκοεν Ar. Pl. 333 ; δ. ἡ οἰκοδομία ὅτι κατὰ σπουδὴν ἐγένετο Th. 1.9 <*>; δ. ἔσται ὅτι . . Lys. 12.50 : sts. the part. or relat. clause must be supplied, καταγελᾷς μου, δ. εἶ (sc. καταγελῶν) Ar. Av. 1407 , cf. Id. Lys. 919 ; δῆλοι δέ (sc. οὐ μένοντες) Th. 5.10 . δῆλον ποιεῖν show plainly, τινὶ ὅτι . . Id. 6.34 , etc.: c. part., δῆλον ἐποιήσατε . . μηδίσαντες Id. 3.64 . δῆλον (sc. ἐστί) it is manifest, αὐτὸς πρὸς αὑτοῦ· δῆλον S. Aj. 906 ; ἀλγεινά, Πρόκνη, δῆλον Id. Fr. 585 ; ἐκ πίθω ἀντλεῖς, δῆλον Theoc. 10.13 ; δῆλον δέ, to introduce a proof, folld. by γάρ, Th. 1.11 , Arist. Col. 799a5 , etc.; δῆλον γάρ S. Fr. 63 ; δῆλον ὅτι Th. 3.38 , etc.; τὰ Κύρου δῆλον ὅτι οὕτως ἔχει X. An. 1.3.9 , cf. Cyr. 2.4.24 , etc., v. δηλονότι : in pl., δῆλα δή, δ. δ. καὶ ταῦτα Pl. Cri. 48b ; ἢ δ. δ. ὅτι . .; Id. Prt. 309a , etc.: hence as Adv., usu. written δηλαδή (q.v.). Adv. δήλως is rejected by Att. , Poll. 6.207 . δῆλοι, οἱ, Urim, LXX 1 Ki. 28.6 ,al. (Cf. δέατο.)
term_table.greek_sentence: οἶνος εἰς τὰ ξηρὰ, δῆλός ἐστι βουλόμενος λειοῦσθαι τὰ ξηρὰ μετὰ τοῦ οἴνου ἢ τοῦ ὄξους, εἶτα τὰ τηκτὰ τακέντα καταχεῖσθαι τούτων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Nevertheless, from his adding at the end "two kotylai of common vinegar; wine for the dry ingredients", it is clear that he wishes the dry ingredients to be ground fine with the wine or the vinegar, and then the meltable ingredients, once melted, to be poured over these.

Oec. 4.15 : with Preps., ἄνδρες ἀ. περὶ τὸ πλῆθος Lys. 13.2 ; εἴς τι Pl. Alc. 1.125a ; πρός τι Id. R. 407e : c. inf., ἀ. μάχεσθαι Hdt. 1.136 ; ἱππεύεσθαι 1.79 ; ἀ. ἱστάναι good at weighing, Pl. Prt. 356b . good, in moral sense, first in Thgn. 438 , cf. Heraclit. 104 , S. El. 1082 , X. Mem. 1.7.1 , Pl. Ap. 41d , etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος Democr. 247 : freq. with other Adjs., ὁ πιστὸς κἀ. S. Tr. 541 ; δικαίων κἀ. ib. 1050 :—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα Id. Ant. 31 . ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, Pl. Prt. 311a , etc. ἀ. δαίμων, v. sub δαίμων; ἀ. τύχη, v. sub τύχη; ἀ. θεός = Lat. bona dea, Plu. Caes. 9 , Cic. 19 . of things, good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη . . ἀ. κουροτρόφος Od. 9.27 , etc.; ἀ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει X. Cyn. 13.17 : c. gen., εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀ. good for it, Id. Mem. 3.8.3 ; ἑλκῶν Thphr. HP 9.11.1 . of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347 ; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, Il. 9.102 ; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, 11.789 ; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204 :—ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so<*> Il. 7.282 , 24.130 , Od. 3.196 , etc. morally good, πρῆξις Democr. 177 ; ἔργα Emp. 112.2 , cf. Ep.Rom. 2.7 , etc. ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις X. Cyr. 5.3.20 ; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι Id. Mem. 2.4.2 , cf. Ar. Ra. 74 , etc; as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, Men. Sam. 28 :— ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on . . , Th. 3.68 , Lys. 13.92 ; ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, Th. 5.27 , X. Cyr. 7.4.3 ; ἐπ' ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις Ar. Ra. 1487 ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀ. for no good end, Th. 1.131 ; ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος X. HG 5.2.35 :—in pl., ἡ ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά PFlor. 21.10 (iii A.D.):—τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, Epich. 171.5 , cf. Pl. R. 506b , 508e , Arist. Metaph. 1091a31 , etc.:—in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, Hdt. 2.172 , Lys. 13.91 , X. Mem. 1.2.63 , etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν fare well, Ar. Av. 1706 ; also, good things, dainties, Thgn. 1000 , Ar. Ach. 873 , etc.: good qualities, τοῖς ἀ., οἷς ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ Isoc. 8.32 , cf. Democr. 37 ; good points, of a horse, εἰ τἄλλα πάντα ἀ. ἔχοι, κακόπους δ' εἴη X. Eq. 1.2 . Comp. and Sup. are usu. supplied from other stems, viz. Comp. ἀμείνων, ἀρείων<*> βελτίων, κρείσσων ʽκάρρωνʼ, λωΐων (λώʽωνʼ), Ep. βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος:— Sup. ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος (λῷστος), Ep. βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος:— later, reg. Comp. ἀγαθώτερος LXX Jd. 11.25 , 15.2 , D.S. 8 Fr. 12 , Plot. 5.5.9 , Diod.Rh. p.53.9H. : Sup. ἀγαθώτατος D.S. 16.85 , Hld. 5.15 , etc. ( -ότατος POxy. 1757.26 (ii A.D.)). Adv. usually εὖ, q.v.: ἀγαθῶς Hp. Off. 9 , Arist. Rh. 1388b6 , LXX 1 Ki. 20.7 . (Etym. dub. ( ὅτι ἄγει ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ὀρθὸν βίον Stoic. 3.49 ); perh. cognate with ἄγαμαι, hence admirable.)
term_table.greek_sentence: Ταύτην ἀγαθὴν σφόδρ’ οὖσαν ἔνιοι καὶ μόνην Δοκοῦσι πασῶν τῶν καλῶν βελτίονα, Πολλῶν διὰ πείρας οὐκ ἔχοντες φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: This plaster, being exceedingly good, some think to be even the only one better than all the good ones, not having experience of many drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Since it is very good, some think it the only one better than all the good ones, because they have no experience of many drugs.'

term_table.lsj_entry_text: Κολοφώνιος, α, ον, of or from Colophon in Ionia, Hdt. 1.147 , etc.; K. σχῆμα, a figure of speech, such as using ἡ κεφαλὴ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ for τοῦ -που, Lesb.Gramm. 7 : Subst., ἡ Κολοφωνία (sc. ῥητίνη), Colophonian gum, resin, Dsc. 1.71 , Gal. 13.475 , Hippiatr. 20 , al., PGrenf. 1.52.7 (iii A.D.); also, = σκαμμωνία , Ps.- Dsc. 4.170 ; Κολοφώνιον (sc. ὑπόδημα), τό, kind of shoe, Rhinth. 4 ; also, a measure used in Egypt, Ostr. 1166 , 1265 (ii A.D.); but also, a kind of vegetable, PTeb. 419.21 (iii A.D.).
term_table.lsj_first_sense_gloss: of or from Colophon in Ionia
term_table.greek_sentence: Δὶς δ’ εἴκοσι πέντε Ποντικοῦ κηροῦ δραχμὰς, Κολοφωνίας δὲ τῆς καλῆς, κηροῦ διπλοῦν, Τινὲς δὲ μᾶλλον, ταὐτὸ τῆς τερμινθίνης.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It contains litharge, twice one hundred drachmas, [822] and of old oil a quarter of a litra (though some say rather a quarter of a kotyle); twice twenty-five drachmas of Pontic wax; of good Colophonian resin, double the wax—but some rather [use] the same amount of terebinth resin; of verdigris of copper and of Indian aloe, of burnt copper and of good diphryges, sixteen and a half [drachmas] from each ingredient; twenty-four drachmas of galbanum; of manna and of frankincense equal amounts, twice twelve; of ammoniac twice five and twice twenty; sixteen drachmas of Attic propolis; of long aristolochia twice ten drachmas; twice six drachmas of scale of Cyprian copper, and of the driest gentian root an equal amount.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: Ἄμμων, ωνος, ὁ, the Libyan Zeus, Ζεὺς Ἄ. Pi. P. 4.16 : said to be Egyptian, Hdt. 2.42 ; Ἄμμωνος ʽκέρασʼ, = κορωνόπους , Ps.- Dsc. 2.130 , etc.:—fem. Adj. term_table.lsj_entry_text: πόα, ἡ, Ion. and Ep. ποίη, Dor. ποία Pi. (v. infr.), also in E. Cyc. 333 (trim.), Ar. Eq. 606 (troch.); Boeot. πύας, αο, ὁ, Schwyzer 485.1 , al. (Thespiae, iii B.C.):— grass, νέμεαι τέρεν' ἄνθεα ποίης Od. 9.449 ; κεκορηότε ποίης, of oxen, 18.372 ; ἐν ποίῃ ib. 368 ; χθὼν . . φύεν νεοθηλέα π. Il. 14.347 ; ἀμφὶ δὲ ποίη . . ἀέξετο Hes. Th. 194 , cf. Hdt. 4.53 , E. l.c., etc.; π. Μηδική, v. Μηδικός. generally, herb, π. τὸ ἀπὸ ῥίζης φυλλοφόρον προϊὸν ἀστέλεχες Thphr. HP 1.3.1 ; collect., herbaceous plants, τῆς π. τὸ ἡλιοτρόπιον ib. 7.3.1 ; esp. of medicinal herbs, καλοῦσι πόαν ἔνια τῶν φαρμακωδῶν οἱ ῥιζοτόμοι ib. 9.8.1 ; of φυλλώδεις δυνάμεις, ibid.; ποίαν τρίψας IG 42(1).122.121 (Epid., iv B.C.); freq. in Hsch. , s.v. ἀβρότονον , al. lye, LXX Je. 2.22 , Mal. 3.2 . plant in general, π. ἡ βοτάνη EM 677.49 ,al.; π. Παρνασίς, i.e. the bay or laurel, Pi. P. 8.20 ; στεφάνοισί νιν ποίας ἔρεπτον ib. 4.240 : hence, metaph., κεῖραι μελιαδέα ποίαν ib. 9.37 . the grass, i.e. a grassy place, πόα καθίζεσθαι grass to sit on, Pl. Phdr. 229b , cf. X. HG 4.1.30 , Plu. Ages. 36 ; meadow, Schwyzer l.c. (pl.). in later Poets, of Time, hay-harvest, i.e. summer, ἐπ' ἐννέα . . ποίας for nine summers, Call. Fr. 182 ; χείματά τε ποίας τε δύω Rhian. 54 ; ἢ τρεῖς ἢ πίσυρας ποίας AP 7.731 ( Leon. ), cf. 627 ( Diod. ), 6.252 ( Antiphil. ): in this signf. ποιά (oxyt.) acc. to Sch. E. Tr. 20 , EM 677.49 . (Cf. Lith. pieva 'meadow'.)

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κοῦφος, η, ον, light, nimble, Hom. only in neut. pl. as Adv., κοῦφα ποσὶ προβιβάς stepping lightly on, Il. 13.158 , cf. Hes. Sc. 323 ; κοῦφα βιβῶν Pi. O. 14.16 ; κ. ποσὶν ἄγ' ἐς κύκλον Ar. Th. 954 (lyr.); also κούφοις ποσί Pi. O. 13.114 ; κουφοτάταις πτερύγων ἀκμαῖς Ar. Ra. 1353 ; πήδημα κ. ἐκ νεὼς ἀφήλατο A. Pers. 305 ; κ. ἐξᾶραι πόδα S. Ant. 224 ; κ. ἅλμα E. El. 439 (lyr.); κ. αἴρειν βῆμα Id. Tr. 343 ; οὐ τοῖς κούφοις ὁ δρόμος LXX Ec. 9.11 : metaph., κουφότεραι . . ἀπειράτων φρένες too buoyant, Pi. O. 8.61 . metaph., easy, light, τελεῖν . . κούφαν κτίσιν to make achievement easy, ib. 13.83 ; κ. εἰ δοίης τέλος A. Th. 260 ; κ. νύξ an easier night, of a sick person, Jul. Mis. 342a ( Comp. ); περίπατος Sor. 1.46 ; τὸ ὅσιον ἅπαν κ. ἔργον OGI 383.120 (Nemrud Dagh, i B. C.); of government, light, κουφοτέραν βασιλείαν less oppressive, Isoc. 9.51 ; ἡ εὔκλεια κουφοτέρα φέρειν X. Cyr. 8.2.22 ; of an antagonist, easy-going, κουφότατος ἦν κρατήσας Id. Ages. 11.12 ; δεσπότην ἀπράγμονα καὶ κ. ἐξαπατᾷ θεράπων Men. Per.Fr. 1 . unsubstantial, airy, vain, τὸ νέον . . κούφας ἀφροσύνας φέρον S. OC 1230 (lyr.); οὐδὲν ἄλλο πλὴν . . κούφην σκιάν Id. Aj. 126 ; ἐλπίδος τι εἶχον κούφης Th. 2.51 ; κ. καὶ πτηνοὶ λόγοι Pl. Lg. 717c ; κ. πρᾶγμα a trifle, ib. 935a ; κ. γράμματα a small letter, E. IT 594 ; of persons, = κουφόνους , Hdn. 5.7.1 ; τὸ κοῦφον τοῦ νοῦ levity, Paus. 5.21.14 , cf. Hdn. 7.8.6 . light in point of weight, opp. βαρύς, Pl. Phlb. 14d , R. 438c ( Comp. ), etc.; κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνωθε πέσοι may earth lie lightly on thee, E. Alc. 462 (lyr.), cf. Hel. 853 ; κούφη σοι κόνις ἥδε πέλοι IG 14.1942.4 ; κούφη σεῖο γαῖ' ὀστέα κεύθοι ib. 329 (Himera); κ. πνεύματα light airs, S. Aj. 558 ; ὀστᾶ τε καὶ κ. κόνις Men. 538.3 ; τὸ κουφότατον . . τῶν κακῶν . . πενία Id. Kith.Fr. 2 . Medic. in various uses, σικύαι κοῦφαι dry cuppings, Philum. ap. Orib. 45.29.17 , cf. Sor. 2.11 , etc.; also κούφου μένοντος τοῦ ἰοῦ on the surface, Philum. Ven. 7.3 ; μὴν κ. the eighth month of pregnancy, Sor. 1.56 ; of food, easy to digest, light, Arist. EN 1141b18 , etc. of troops, light-armed, οἱ κ. τῶν στρατιωτῶν Hell.Oxy. 6.4 ; ὡπλισμένοι κουφοτέροις ὅπλοις X. Mem. 3.5.27 ; κούφη στρατιά Plu. Fab. 11 ; τὰ κ. τῆς δυνάμεως Plb. 10.25.2 . of ships, lightly-laden, Th. 6.37 , 8.27 . light, slight, ἁμαρτήματα Pl. Lg. 863c ; κουφότερα γυμνάσια, opp. ἀναγκαῖα, Arist. Pol. 1338b40 ; κ. ἐργασίαι ib. 1321a25 . empty, κεράμια Gp. 7.24.2 , cf. PLond. 5.1656.6 (iv A. D.), PFlor. 314.8 (v. A. D. ): hence as Subst., κοῦφον (sc. κεράμιον), τό, jar, in pl., POxy. 1631.16 (iii A. D.), PFay. 133.6 (iv A. D.), PStrassb. 1.10 (vi A. D.). Act. , relieving, assisting, χερὶ κούφᾳ Pi. P. 9.11 : prob. to be taken in this sense in Theoc. 11.3 . Adv. -φως lightly, nimbly, κ. ὀροῦσαι A. Eu. 112 ; κ. ἐσκευασμένοι, of soldiers, Th. 4.33 ; ὡπλισμένοι X. Mem. 3.5.26 , etc.; κ. ἔχειν to be relieved, Arist. Pr. 873a16 . metaph., lightly, with light heart, κουφότερον μετεφώνεε Od. 8.201 ; κ. νοῆσαι Sapph. Supp. 5.14 ; κ. φέρειν, opp. δεινῶς φ., E. Med. 449 , 1018 ; ὡς κουφότατα φέρειν Hdt. 1.35 ; διάγουσα κούφως doing well, of a patient, Hp. Epid. 1.26 .δ ́. lightly, with ease, A. Pr. 701 .
term_table.greek_sentence: λιθάργυρον δὲ μετ’ ἐλαίου βαλὼν, [823] Εἰς λοπάδα καινὴν κεραμίαν πλατύστομον, Ἕψε πυρὶ κούφῳ καὶ μαλακῷ, κινῶν σπάθῃ Ἕως γένηται μέλιτος Ἀττικοῦ πάχος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: and having put the litharge with the oil [823] into a new, wide-mouthed earthenware pan, boil over a light and gentle fire, stirring with a spatula, until it acquires the thickness of Attic honey.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Putting the litharge with the oil [823] into a new, wide-mouthed earthenware dish, boil it over a light and gentle fire, stirring with a spatula, until it takes on the thickness of Attic honey.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ῥητίν-η [ι], ἡ , resin of the pine, Hp. Art. 63 , Arist. HA 617a19 , Thphr. HP 9.2.1 , al., Nic. Al. 300 , 554 , Dsc. 1.71 , etc. (Prob. a foreign word.)
term_table.greek_sentence: Ἴσον δὲ καὶ τῆς λεπίδος προσβαλὼν πάλιν Ἕψε λαβρότερον, εἶτα κιῤῥοῦ γενομένου Τοῦ φαρμάκου, πρόσβαλε χαλκὸν καὶ διφρυγὲς, Ποιῶν τ’ ἀμόλυντον καὶ πεπηγὸς φάρμακον Πρόσβαλλε κηρὸν τήν τε ῥητίνην ἅμα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And having added also an equal amount of the scale, boil again more vigorously; then, when the drug has become tawny, add the copper and the diphryges, and, making the drug non-staining and set, add the wax together with the resin.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Then add an equal amount of the scale as well and boil again more vigorously; next, when the drug has become tawny, add the copper and the diphryges, and, to make the drug non-staining and set, add the wax and the resin together. When these have melted together and you see that the plaster is blended, take the pot off the fire, and add some propolis and the galbanum, ammoniac, manna and aloe.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: Ὧν συντακέντων, ὅταν ἴδῃς κεκραμένην Ἔμπλαστρον, αἴρεις τὴν χύτραν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς Καὶ προσβαλὼν προπόλεώς τε καὶ χαλβάνην, Ἀμμωνιακὸν, μάνναν τε καὶ ἀλόην, τότε Ψύξας τὸ πυρῶδες καὶ ζέον τοῦ φαρμάκου, Ἀριστολοχίαν λειοτάτην προσεμπάσεις Καὶ γεντιανὴν, τήν τε δίκταμνον πόαν Καὶ προσανακόψας τῇ σπάθῃ τὸ φάρμακον Χερσὶ καὶ μαγδαλιὰς ποιῶν, ἔχε, Εἰς ἃς προεῖπον χρώμενος περιστάσεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: When these have melted together, when you see the plaster blended, you lift the pot from the fire, and, having added propolis and galbanum, ammoniac, manna and aloe, then, having cooled the fiery and boiling heat of the drug, you will sprinkle in aristolochia, very finely ground, and gentian and the herb dittany; and having beaten the drug up further with the spatula and with the hands, and making it into cakes, keep it, using it for the circumstances I mentioned before.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Then, having cooled the fiery and seething heat of the drug, sprinkle in the aristolochia ground very smooth, and the gentian and the dittany herb. term_table.lsj_entry_text: χρώς, ὁ, gen. χρωτός, dat. χρωτί, acc. χρῶτα ( Att. χρώ only in Choerob. in Theod. 1.248H. ): Ep. and Ion. gen. χροός, dat. χροΐ, acc. χρόα (also in Lesbian, Sapph. Supp. 10.6 , al.), as always in Hom.and Hes. , exc. gen. χρωτός in Il. 10.575 , acc. χρῶτα Od. 18.172 , 179 , Hes. Op. 556 ; Emp. uses χρωτός, 76.3 (but χροΐ 100.17 ); Pi. uses χρωτί, χρῶτα, P. 1.55 , I. 4(3).23(41) ; these forms are freq. in Trag., but Ion. dat. χροΐ occurs in S. Tr. 605 , and χροός, χροΐ, χρόα are freq. in E., Hec. 548 , Med. 1175 , Ph. 264 , al. :—dat. χρῷ occurs in the phrase ἐν χρῷ v. infr.1.2 and in Sapph. 2.10 .—rare in Com.and Att. Prose. of the human body, skin or flesh, οὔ σφι λίθος χρὼς οὐδὲ σίδηρος Il. 4.510 ; καὶ γάρ θην τούτῳ τρωτὸς χρώς 21.568 ; χρῶτ' ἀπονιψαμένη Od. 18.172 ; ἀκρότατον δ' ἄρ' ὀϊστὸς ἐπέγραψε χρόα Il. 4.139 ; ταμέειν χρόα νηλέϊ χαλκῷ 13.501 ; λιλαιου|ένη χροὸς ἆσαι, of a spear, 21.168 ; κακὰ χροΐ εἵματ' ἔχοντα Od. 14.506 ; χρῷ πῦρ ὐπαδεδρόμακεν Sapph. 2.10 ; μύροις χρῶτα λιπαίνων Anaxil. 18.1 (anap.): esp. flesh, opp. bone, φθινύθει δ' ἀμφ' ὀστεόφι χρώς Od. 16.145 ; οὐδέ τί οἱ χρὼς σήπεται Il. 24.414 , cf. 19.33 (which usage is said by Gal. to have been Ionic, 18(2).435 , with reference to Hp. Fract. 9 ); τὸ δέρμα τοῦ χρωτός LXX Le. 13.11 , etc.; τοῦ χρωτὸς ἥδιστον ἀπέπνει Aristox. Fr.Hist. 84 : generally, one's body, frame, Pi. P. 1.55 , A. Fr. 192.6 (anap.); χριμφθῆναι χροΐ Id. Supp. 790 (lyr.); στεῖλαί νυν ἀμφὶ χρωτὶ . . πέπλους E. Ba. 821 , cf. S. Tr. 605 : pl., διὰ τί . . οἱ χρῶτες ὄζουσι; Arist. Pr. 877b21 ; also κατεδήσαντο . . τοὺς ὑγιεῖς χρῶτας, ὡς τραυματίαι D.H. 9.50 . ἐν χροΐ, or ἐν χρῷ, close to the skin, ἐν χροΐ κείρειν to shave close, Hdt. 4.175 ; ἐν χρῷ κεκαρμένοι X. HG 1.7.8 ; ἐν χρῷ κουριῶντας Pherecr. 30 :—metaph., to the quick, ξυρεῖ γὰρ ἐν χρῷ τοῦτο S. Aj. 786 ; ἐν χρῷ παραπλεῖν sail past so as to shave or graze, Th. 2.84 ; τὴν μάχην συνάψαι ἐν χρῷ to fight at close quarters, Plu. Thes. 27 ; ἡ ἐν χρῷ συνουσία close acquaintance, Luc. Ind. 3 : c. gen., ἐν χρῷ τινος close to, hard by a person or thing, τοῦ θώρακος ( v.l. σώματος ) Plu. 2.345a ; τῆς γῆς ib. 925b , Luc. Herm. 5 : abs., ἐν χρῷ near at hand, Id. Hist.Conscr. 24 , al.; cf. EM 313.53 , Hsch. the colour of the skin, complexion, μελαίνετο δὲ χρόα καλόν Il. 5.354 ; τρέπεται χ. his colour changes, i. e. he turns pale, 13.279 , cf. 17.733 ; ὠχρήσαντα χρόα Od. 11.529 ; χρόα . . ἀμείβειν Parm. 8.41 ; μεθίστη χρωτὸς . . φύσιν E. term_table.english_sentence_A: [824] [On the troches of Asclepiades.] Just as some of the physicians named plasters from their colour, and not from the profession of their power, as quince-yellow, white, grey and tawny, so too they name troches from the shape given them in moulding, though they differ not with respect to one affection but with respect to very many.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [824] [On the troches of Asclepiades.] Just as some of the physicians named plasters from their colour, and not from what they promise to do by their power, calling them quince-yellow, white, grey and tawny, so they name troches (trochiskoi) from the shape given them in the moulding, although these differ from one another and are not for one affection but for a great many.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κυκλ-ίσκος, ὁ, Dim. of κύκλος, small circle in a diagram, Ptol. Hyp. 1.9 , al.; as part of an instrument, Id. Alm. 1.12 . small round cake of wax, Dsc. 2.83 ; lozenge, = τροχίσκος , Hp. Mul. 2.188 , Gal. 12.276 , Lycusap. Orib. 8.25.23 , Aët. 15.37 . ring to pass the reins through, Gal. 2.323 . circular opening of a coop, Ph. Bel. 78.1 . f.l. for κοιλίσκος (q.v.). round spot, Clytus 1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀκολουθήσαντες οὖν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐφεξῆς γράψομεν πάντας· τούς γε δοκίμους, εἴτε κυκλίσκους, εἴτε τροχίσκους, ἑκατέρως γὰρ αὐτοὺς ὀνομάζουσι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Following them, therefore, we too shall write out all of them in order—those at least that are approved—whether one calls them cyclisci (small disks) or trochisci (troches), for they name them in both ways.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Following them, then, we too shall write all of them in order, at least the approved ones, whether they are called little discs (kykliskoi) or troches (trochiskoi), for they name them in both ways.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἄκανθ-α [ακ], ης, ἡ, (ἀκή A) thorn, prickle, Arist. PA 655a19 , Thphr. HP 6.1.3 : hence, any thorny or prickly plant (in Od. 5.328 (pl.) prob. Eryngium campestre), S. Fr. 718 , Eub. 107.19 , Theoc. 1.132 , etc.: prov., οὐ γὰρ ἄκανθαι no thistles, i.e. 'an easy job', Ar. Fr. 272 , 483 :—special kinds: ἄ. Ἀραβική smaller milk-thistle, Notobasis syriaca, Dsc. 3.13 ; ἄ. βασιλική fish-thistle, Cnicus Acarna, Thphr. CP 1.10.5 ; ἄ. Ἰνδική, = Balsamodendron Mukul, Id. HP 9.1.2 ; ἄ. λευκή Acacia albida, ib. 4.2.8 ; = ἄ. βασιλική , Dsc. 3.12 ; ἄ. λευκὴ τρίοζος, = Euphorbia antiquorum, Thphr. HP 4.4.12 ; ἄ. ἀκανώδης (prob.) cornthistle, Carduus arvensis, ib. 10.6 . of other plants, e.g. Spanish broom, Spartium junceum, Str. 3.5.10 :— = ἀκακία, ἄ. Αἰγυπτία , Thphr. HP 9.1.2 . cf. POxy. 1188.10 ( 13 A. D. ), etc.; ἄ. μέλαινα Acacia arabica, Thphr. HP 4.2.8 , cf. Hdt. 2.96 , Thd. Is. 41.19 ; ἄ. δψάς, = Acacia tortilis, Thphr. HP 4.7.1 . centralflowering-bud of χαμαιλέων λευκός, ib. 9.12.1 , Dsc. 3.8 . = ἄκανθος , Ps.- Dsc. 3.17 . in pl., prickles or spines of the hedgehog and of certain fish, Ion Trag. 38 , Arist. HA 530b8 . backbone or spine of fish, A. Fr. 275 , Ar. V. 969 , Alex. 110.11 ,al.; of serpents, Hdt. 2.75 , Theoc. 24.32 , A.R. 4.150 ; of men, Hdt. 4.72 , Hp. Art. 14 , E. El. 492 , Arist. PA 654a26 , Gal. 2.451 , etc.; improperly used of mammalia, acc. to Arist. AP 0.98a22 ; of the spinous processes of the vertebrae, Gal. 2.758 ; χονδρώδεις ἄ. false ribs, Ruf. Oss. 25 . metaph. in pl., thorny questions, Luc. Hes. 5 , Ath. 3.97d .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀκάνθης καρποῦ δραχ.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐπουλ-ωτικός, ή, όν, promoting cicatrization, Id. 11.756 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἄνευ μὲν γὰρ τόπου γέγραπται πρὸς αὐτοῦ τὰ ἐπουλωτικὰ καὶ τὰ ἐσχαρωτικὰ καὶ τὰ πρὸς νομὰς ἁρμόττοντα καὶ ἄνθρακας καὶ τὰ καλούμενα ἴσχαιμα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For without a place there have been written by him the cicatrizing remedies and the escharotic ones and those suited for spreading sores (nomai) and carbuncles and the so-called haemostatic remedies (ischaima).
term_table.english_sentence_B: Without reference to place he has written the cicatrizing and the escharotic [drugs], those suited to spreading ulcers and carbuncles, and the so-called haemostatics.

term_table.greek_sentence: μετὰ τόπου δὲ πεπονθότος, ὅσα πρὸς πολύποδα καὶ ὀζαίνας καὶ τὰς ἐκ μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας καὶ τὰς ἐν στόματι νομὰς καὶ οὖλα πλαδῶντα καὶ τὰς ἐπὶ τῶν γενείων ὀχθώδεις ἐπαναστάσεις καὶ πρὸς παρωνυχίας καὶ πτερύγια καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν δακτυλίῳ ῥαγάδας καὶ πρὸς τὰς αἱμοῤῥοΐδας.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Some, moreover, have even received their name from the affected part, yet are suited also to the other parts, such as are the remedies called 'cephalic' by physicians, which are suited pre-eminently in the case of the bones but are also able to make flesh grow in the ulcerations that arise in the whole body.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Some have also acquired their name from the affected part.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἁρμόττει δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις μέρεσιν, ὁποῖα καὶ τὰ κεφαλικὰ καλούμενα πρὸς τῶν ἰατρῶν ἐστιν, ἁρμόττοντα μὲν ἐξαιρέτως ἐν τοῖς ὀστοῖς, δυνάμενα δὲ καὶ τὰς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ σώματι γιγνομένας ἑλκώσεις σαρκοῦν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Some, moreover, have even received their name from the affected part, yet are suited also to the other parts, such as are the remedies called 'cephalic' by physicians, which are suited pre-eminently in the case of the bones but are also able to make flesh grow in the ulcerations that arise in the whole body.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Yet they suit other parts too. Such are the [drugs] called cephalic by the physicians: they are suited especially to the bones, but they are also able to incarn ulcerations arising in the whole body.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Indeed, when the bone has not been laid bare, we have no need of them at all; but in cases where it has been laid bare, [845] since we are wary of the use of drugs that make greasy, we use the dry ones alone, avoiding what are called by physicians emmota (lint-dressings), which are applied by means of lint-pledgets that have been smeared.
term_table.rendering_B: emmota, that is, drugs applied by means of lint
term_table.english_sentence_B: Indeed, when the bone has not been laid bare, we have no need of any of them; but in cases where it has been laid bare, [845] since we are wary of using greasy drugs, we use the dry ones alone, avoiding what physicians call emmota, that is, drugs applied by means of lint smeared with them.

term_table.greek_sentence: διὸ κᾀγὼ τὰ ὑπ’ Ἀσκληπιάδου γεγραμμένα ξηρὰ μέλλων ἐφεξῆς γράφειν, εὑρὼν αὐτὸν ἁπάντων πρῶτα γεγραφότα τὰ κεφαλικὰ καὶ αὐτὸς γράψω πρῶτα διὰ τὸ μὴ μόνον ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ γεγυμνωμένων ὀστῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁπάντων ὁμοίως πεπονθότων, ὑπάρχειν αὐτὰ χρήσιμα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Therefore I too, being about to write out in sequence the dry remedies recorded by Asclepiades, having found that he wrote the cephalic remedies first of all, will myself also write them first, because they are useful not only for the bones laid bare in the head, but also for all the others that are similarly affected.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Therefore I too, being about to write out next the dry drugs written by Asclepiades, and having found that he wrote the cephalics first of all, will myself also write them first, because they are useful not only for laid-bare bones in the head but also for all the other bones affected in the same way.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τίνα κάλλιστα νομίζω τῶν ἐπουλωτικῶν εἶναι, προείρηταί μοι διὰ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου, καθ’ ἣν ἁπάντων παθῶν τῆς ἰάσεως αἱ μέθοδοι δελήλωνται καὶ τῶν εἰς ἕλκη διαφερουσῶν ἔμπροσθεν ἐν τῇδε τῇ νῦν προκειμένῃ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed which of the cicatrizing ones I consider the best has been stated by me earlier in the Therapeutic Method, in which the methods of cure of all affections have been set out, and, of those pertaining to wounds, earlier in this treatise now before us.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Moreover, which of the cicatrizing drugs I consider the best has also been stated by me before, in the Therapeutic Method, in which the methods of cure of all affections have been set out, and of those pertaining to ulcers earlier in this present [treatise] now before us.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλ’ ἐξ ὧν ἐγὼ διῆλθον, ἔν τε τῇ θεραπευτικῇ πραγματείᾳ καὶ τῇ νῦν ἐνεστώσῃ δῆλον ἔσται τοῖς προσέχουσι τὸν νοῦν, ὅπως ἑκάστῳ τῶν γεγραμμένων χρηστέον.

term_table.greek_sentence: [Πρὸς ἄνθρακας.] Ὁ ἄνθραξ ἕλκος ἐστὶν, ἐσχάραν ταχὺ ποιοῦν, μετὰ φλεγμονῆς ἰσχυρᾶς τοῦ πέριξ μορίου παντὸς, ὥστε καὶ πυρετοὺς ἐπιφέρεσθαι σφοδροὺς [855] καὶ κινδύνους ἐσχάτους, ὥστε χρὴ κατ’ αὐτῆς μὲν τῆς ἐσχάρας ἰσχυρὸν τιθέναι φάρμακον, καὶ τούτων γε ὁποῖα πρὸς νομὰς ἁρμόζειν εἴρηται, τὰ δὲ πέριξ καταπλάσσειν καταπλάσμασιν ὁμαλὴν ἔχουσι δύναμιν, ὡς ἀποκρούεσθαί τε καὶ μετρίως ἐμψύχειν καὶ διαφορεῖν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [For anthrakes.] The anthrax is an ulcer that quickly produces an eschar, with strong phlegmone of the whole surrounding part, so that violent fevers too are brought on [855] and extreme dangers; hence one must place upon the eschar itself a strong drug, and indeed such of these as have been said to be suitable for nomai, while the surrounding parts one must plaster with cataplasms that have an even power, so as both to repel and to cool moderately and to disperse.

Pol. 1259b23 ; ὀ. καὶ μηχανικαὶ κατασκευαί Plu. 2.718f ; esp. of war-engines, ἡ ὀ. βία D.S. 17.43 ; ὀ. κατασκευαί Onos. 42.3 : metaph., ὁ ὀ. εἰς πλήθη λόγος speech which is brought to bear on the mob, Plu. Cat.Mi. 4 ; of musicians, practical, opp. λογικοί (theoretical), Id. 2.657e ; ἐποιεῖτο ἀκροάσεις λογικάς τε καὶ ὀ. Supp.Epigr. 2.184.6 (Tanagra, ii B.C.) ; so of surgeons, τῶν ὀ. οἱ διασημότεροι PMed.Lond. 155.2.13 ; ἡ ὀ. (sc. τέχνη) Plu. Marc. 14 ; but ὀργανικός, = λογικός , logical, Elias in Porph. 115.17 . Adv. -κῶς by way of instruments, Arist. EN 1099b28 ; -κώτερον making more use of instruments, Simp. in Cael. 504.33 ; τὸ κινοῦν ὀ. Arist. de An. 433b21 .
term_table.greek_sentence: Ἀπολλωνίου ὀργανικοῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [Of Apion, for carbuncles.] ♃ Of red nitron, arsenic, sandarach, chalcitis, chalcanthum, diphryges, an equal amount of each; grinding fine with vinegar, drying and grinding again, use.
term_table.english_sentence_B: In Demosthenes of Massalia, who also compounded the drug, it has two kotylai of oil.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χρυσο-κόλλα, ἡ, gold-solder, malachite, basic copper carbonate, Arist. Mir. 834b20 , Thphr. Lap. 26.40 , Dsc. 5.74 , 89 , Plin. HN 33.86 . a dish of linseed and honey, Alcm. 74B.
term_table.greek_sentence: ♃ χρυσοκόλλης δραχμὴν μίαν, στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς δραχμὴν α΄.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Of Apollonius Organicus. ♃ Of chrysocolla one drachm, of split alum one drachm and of round [alum] one drachm, of sandarach one drachm, of ochre one drachm, of raw misy one drachm, of chalcanthum one drachm; use finely ground.
term_table.english_sentence_B: In Demosthenes of Massalia, who also compounded the drug, it has two kotylai of oil.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μίσυ, υος and εως, τό, a copper ore found in Cyprus, Hp. Mul. 1.103 , Gal. 12.241 , 15.32 , Dsc. 5.100 , cf. 74 . truffle, Tuber aestivum, growing near Cyrene, Thphr. Fr. 167 .
term_table.greek_sentence: μίσυος ὠμοῦ δραχμὴν α΄.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [Apion's, for carbuncles.] Take red natron, arsenic, sandarach, chalcitis, chalcanthum, diphryges, an equal amount of each; grind smooth with vinegar, dry, grind again, and use.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ ἀνθίζουσα Μάγνου πρὸς σηπεδόνας, νομὰς, ἄνθρακας, πτερύγια, ὦτα πυοῤῥοοῦντα, ποιεῖ καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν τῷ στόματι νομάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The anthizousa ("blooming") remedy of Magnus for putrefactions, spreading sores, carbuncles, pterygia, ears flowing with pus; it also works for spreading sores in the mouth. ♃ Of split alum 8 drachms, of chalcitis 6 drachms, of sandarach 3 drachms, of dry pomegranate rinds 2 drachms, of chalcanthum 1 drachm.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Take 1 drachm of chrysocolla, 1 drachm of split alum and 1 drachm of round alum, 1 drachm of sandarach, 1 drachm of ochre, 1 drachm of raw misy, 1 drachm of chalcanthum.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μίσυ, υος and εως, τό, a copper ore found in Cyprus, Hp. Mul. 1.103 , Gal. 12.241 , 15.32 , Dsc. 5.100 , cf. 74 . truffle, Tuber aestivum, growing near Cyrene, Thphr. Fr. 167 .
term_table.greek_sentence: [857] μίσυος δραχ.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: νίτρ-ον, τό, in Hdt. and Att. λίτρον (q.v.), sodium carbonate, Sapph. 165 , Hp. Aër. 7 , Arist. Mete. 383b12 , IG 9(1).691 (Corc., iii B.C.), PCair.Zen. 304.7 (iii B.C.), PTeb. 182 (ii B.C.), Gal. 13.265 ; ν. ἐρυθρόν Hp. Nat.Mul. 32 , cf. term_table.greek_sentence: νίτρου δραχ.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὀμφάκ-ινος, η, ον, made from unripe grapes, ὀ. οἶνος, = ὀμφακίας, ὀμφακίτης , Hp. Mul. 2.189 (vulg., ὀμφακίῳ codd. opt.), PFlor. 140v . 7 (iii A.D.) ; ὀ. ἔλαιον oil made from unripe olives, Dsc. 1.30 , cf. Gal. 6.196 . ὀμφάκινον (sc. ἱμάτιον), τό, a garment named prob. from its colour, Poll. 7.56 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ♃ κηκίδος ὀμφακίνης δραχ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Use it dry and also with honey.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Use it dry, and also with honey.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σχισ-τός, ή, όν, (σχίζω) cloven, divided, κέλευθος A. Fr. 173 ; ὁδός S. OT 733 , E. Ph. 38 ; ἄντυξ Id. Rh. 373 (lyr.); λίνον ς. lint, Hp. Nat.Mul. 53 (but cf. 4 infr.); πέρκη ς. a split perch, Antiph. 132 ; Ἀργεῖαι ς. a kind of women's shoes, Eup. 266 ; ς. χιτωνίσκος a tunic open at the side, Apollod.Com. 12 ; without χιτωνίσκος, PSI 4.341.7 (iii B.C.), Schwyzer 462 B 30 (Tanagra, iii B.C.); σχιστὰς ἕλκειν, of a certain dance (cf. σχίσμα IV), Poll. 4.105 . clovenhoofed, opp. μῶνυξ, Pl. Plt. 265d ; similarly of wings, etc., Arist PA 692b12 , etc. ς. γάλα curdled milk (v. σχίζω 1.3 ), Dsc. 2.70 , Gal. 12.292 . λίνον ς. fine flax, LXX Is. 19.9 . that may be split or cleft, divisible, ς. κατὰ μῆκος Arist. HA 515b15 , cf. Mete. 386b26 , etc.; ς. λίθος, prob. talc, Dsc. 5.127 , cf. 106 , etc.; ς. κρόμμυα (v. κρόμμυον 11 ) Thphr. HP 7.4.7 .
term_table.greek_sentence: στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς, χαλκάνθου, λίθου Ἀσίου, διφρυγοῦς, νίτρου ἐρυθροῦ ἀνὰ δραχ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Another, of Diodorus. ♃ Of omphacine oak-gall 4 drachms, of misy 2 drachms, of chalcitis 2 drachms, of arsenic 2 drachms, of sandarach 2 drachms, of split alum, chalcanthum, Asian stone, diphryges, red nitron, 1 drachm each.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Another, of Diodorus. ℞ Omphacine oak-gall, 4 dr.; misy, 2 dr.; chalcitis, 2 dr.; arsenikon, 2 dr.; sandarach, 2 dr.; split alum, chalcanthum, Assian stone, diphryges, red nitre, 1 dr. of each.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐρυθρός, ά, όν, [υ by nature, Ar. Ach. 787 , al.: hence the later Comp. and Sup. are perh. -ώτερος, -ώτατος, as in Pl. Ti. 83b , Epin. 987c ; but the metre requires -ότερος in Anaxandr. 22 , Dromo 1 , cf. Choerob. in Theod. 2.76 ]:— red, νέκταρ ἐ. Il. 19.38 , Od. 5.93 ; χαλκός Il. 9.365 ; χρυσὸν ἐ. ἰδεῖν Thgn. 450 ; κῆρυξ ἐ., a ship painted with vermilion, Orac. ap. Hdt. 3.57 ; -ότερον κόκκον Dromo l.c.; ἐ. πέλανος, of blood, A. Eu. 265 (lyr.); ἐρυθρά, τά, red pimples, eruption, Hp. Liqu. 6 ; but ἐ. διελθόντα red motions, Id. Coac. 178 . ἐρυθρά, ἡ,=μελισσόφυλλον, Ps.- Dsc. 3.104 ; ἐρυθρός, ὁ (sc. ῥους), fruit of the ῥους βυρσοδεψική, Dsc. 1.108 . ἐρυθρόν, τό, ᾠοῦ yolk, Sor. 1.124 , Orib. Syn. 5.13 . Ἐρυθρὴ θάλασσα in Hdt. the Indian Ocean, in which the Red Sea (Ἀράβιος κόλπος) is sts. included (of the existence of the Persian Gulf he was ignorant), 1.180 , 2.11 , 158 , 4.42 , al.; πόντος Ἐ. Pi. P. 4.251 —later the Red Sea only, OGI 69 , 186 , 190 , al.: also of the Persian Gulf, X. Cyr. 8.6.20 , D.S. 2.11 ; Peripl.M.Rubr. prob. mentions Zanzibar and China ; used of remote and unknown places, μόνον οὐκ ἐπὶ τὴν Ἐ. θάλατταν πρεσβείας πέμπειν D. 19.304 : really ἡ Ἐρύθρα θάλασσα sea of Erythras, acc. to Agatharch. 5 . (Lat. rubrofr. *rudhro-, cf. Skt. rudhirá- ; v. ἐρεύθω. )
term_table.greek_sentence: στυπτηρίας σχιστῆς, χαλκάνθου, λίθου Ἀσίου, διφρυγοῦς, νίτρου ἐρυθροῦ ἀνὰ δραχ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Another, of Diodorus. ♃ Of omphacine oak-gall 4 drachms, of misy 2 drachms, of chalcitis 2 drachms, of arsenic 2 drachms, of sandarach 2 drachms, of split alum, chalcanthum, Asian stone, diphryges, red nitron, 1 drachm each.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Another, of Diodorus. ℞ Omphacine oak-gall, 4 dr.; misy, 2 dr.; chalcitis, 2 dr.; arsenikon, 2 dr.; sandarach, 2 dr.; split alum, chalcanthum, Assian stone, diphryges, red nitre, 1 dr. of each.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μάννα, ἡ , μάννα λιβάνου frankincense powder or granules, Dsc. 1.68.6 ; but μ. λιβανωτοῦ gum of λίβανος, Aen.Tact. 35 ; μ. alone, of the powder, Hp. Art. 36 , Epid. 2.2.18 , Antyll. ap. Orib. 7.21.8 , Gal. 12.722 ; = λιβάνου τὸ λεπτόν , AB 108 . μάννα, τό, = Hebr. mān, manna, LXX Ex. 16.35 ( v.l. μάν ), Nu. 11.6 , al., cf. J. AJ 3.1.6 .
term_table.greek_sentence: μάννης δραχ.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: τερμίνθινος, η, ον, of the terebinth-tree, ῥητίνη turpentine, Diocl. Fr. 140 , Thphr. HP 9.2.2 , Dsc. 4.150 (τερεμ- cod. E, τερεβ- cett., Wellm.), Sor. 2.14 , al. (τερεβ-), PHolm. 6.33 (τερεβ-), Gal. 6.288 ( v.l. τερεβ- ), 292 , 354 ; οἶνος Dsc. 5.30 , etc.; prob. to be restored for τερεβίνθινος in X. An. 4.4.13 :—pecul. fem. τερμινθίς, ίδος, Nic. Al. 300 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τερμινθίνης ὄξει πεφυρμένης, ξηροῖς κατάπασσε τοὺς αἱμοῤῥαγοῦντας τόπους.
term_table.english_sentence_A: A well-tested drug of Lucius the teacher. ♃ Of chalcitis 16 drachms, of manna 12 drachms, of terebinth kneaded with vinegar; with these dry, sprinkle the places that are haemorrhaging.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Sprinkle the bleeding places with the dry ingredients.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: αἱμο-ρραγία, ἡ, haemorrhage, Hp. Art. 69 , Aph. 7.21 ; any violent bleeding, ib. 5.16 ; nose-bleeding, Gal. 17(1).50 , etc.
term_table.greek_sentence: ὡς δὲ Διοσκορίδης ὁ Ταρσεὺς ἔδωκεν Ἀρείῳ τῷ Ἀσκληπιαδείῳ θαυμαστῶς κατέχον τὰς αἱμοῤῥαγίας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And as Dioscorides of Tarsus gave it to Areius the Asclepiadean, checking haemorrhages marvellously: ♃ of chalcitis 8 drachms, of manna 16 drachms, of dry resin 8 drachms, of gypsum 8 drachms.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And as Dioscorides of Tarsus gave it to Areius the Asclepiadean, wonderfully checking haemorrhages: ℞ Chalcitis, 8 dr.; manna, 16 dr.; dry resin, 8 dr.; gypsum, 8 dr.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔριον, τό, Ion. εἴριον GDIiv p.876 (Chios, iv B. C., also written ἔρια ibid.), Hdt. , Hp. , and always in Hom. (indicating ἐρv-) exc. gen. ἐρίοιο in Od. 4.124 :— wool, Il. 12.434 , Od.l.c., Pl. Smp. 175d ; ἐρίῳ στέψαντες, i.e. with woollen fillets, Id. R. 398a , etc.: freq. in pl., Il. 3.388 , Od. 18.316 ; εἴρια ῥυπαρά, ἔρια οἰσυπηρά, greasy wool, Hp. Fract. 21 , Dsc. 2.74 ; ἔρια καθαρά PCair.Zen. 12.62 (iii B. C.); τἄρια, crasis for τὰ ἔ., Ar. Ra. 1387 ; οὖλα ἔρια ib. 1067 ; ἔ. πεπταμένα outspread flocks of wool, Id. Nu. 343 ; ἐρίων τάλαντον Id. V. 1147 ; τὰ Μιλήσια ἔ. Eub. 90.3 , cf. Amphis 27.1 ; εἴρια ἀπὸ ξύλου cotton, Hdt. 3 . 47 , cf. 106 ; τὸ ἔ. [τῆς ἀράχνησ] a spider's web, Philostr. Im. 2.28 ; τὰ ἐκ τῆς θαλάττης ἔ., of the byssus of the pinna, Alciphr. 1.2 . ( ἔρια Schwyzer 180 (Crete) without initial v-; Lat. vervex perh. not cogn.)
term_table.greek_sentence: τούτῳ ἐχρήσατο πρὸς [858] τὰς τῶν μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας, ἔριον καταβάπτων καὶ συστρέφων ὥσπερ ἐλλύχνιον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: He used this for [858] haemorrhages of the nostrils, dipping wool in it and twisting it like a lamp-wick.
term_table.english_sentence_B: He used this for [858] haemorrhages of the nostrils, dipping wool into it and twisting it like a lamp-wick.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σίδιον, τό, (σίδη) pomegranate-peel, Hp. Nat.Mul. 33 , Ulc. 12 , Thphr. CP 5.6.1 : pl., Ar. Nu. 881 , Dsc. 1.110 , Alciphr. 3.60 . [ σι- Ar. l.c.; σι- Luc. Trag. 156 .]
term_table.greek_sentence: ♃ σιδίων ὀξείας ῥοιᾶς οὐγγίας γ΄.
term_table.english_sentence_A: He used this for [858] haemorrhages of the nostrils, dipping wool in it and twisting it like a lamp-wick.
term_table.english_sentence_B: He used this for [858] haemorrhages of the nostrils, dipping wool into it and twisting it like a lamp-wick.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐσχαρ-ωτικός, ή, όν, tending to form an eschar, Dsc. 2.73 ; φάρμακα caustics, Lycus ap. Orib. 8.25.24 , Gal. 10.324 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τούτῳ ἀντὶ καυτηρίου ἐχρήσατο, ἔστι δὲ ἐσχαρωτικόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: In the case of the nostrils, fill a piece of wool with the drug and insert it.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χάλκ-ανθος, ὁ and ἡ, = foreg. 1 , acc. to Gal. 12.721 , cf. Ruf. ap. Orib. 7.26.38 (v.l.).
term_table.greek_sentence: χαλκάνθου δραχ.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: βυρσοδεψ-ικός, ή, όν, of or for tanning, Hp. Mul. 1.78 , Thphr. CP 3.9.3 : hence -ική, ἡ , art of tanning, Socr. Ep. 14.2 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ῥοὸς βυρσοδεψικοῦ δραχ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: He used this in place of a cautery; it is escharotic.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The so-called 'Heracles', for haemorrhages.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πίτυς [ι], υος, ἡ , Ep. dat. pl. πίτυσσιν, pine, esp. Pinus Laricio, Corsican pine, π. βλωθρή, τήν τ' οὔρεσι τέκτονες ἄνδρες ἐξέταμον Il. 13.390 ; μακρῇσίν τε πίτυσσιν ἰδὲ δρυσίν Od. 9.186 ; also, Aleppo pine, P. halepensis, Thphr. HP 3.9.5 , Nic. term_table.english_sentence_A: (others: 20); gypsum, 4 dr.; use them finely ground.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Use ground fine.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πολύ-χρηστος, ον, useful for many purposes, very useful, Arist. GA 789b9 , Pol. 1337b26 , Dsc. 1.1 , Gal. 6.534 , 480 ( Sup. ); τὸ π. Corn. ND 9 : Comp. , Muson. Fr. 20p.112H. , Alex.Aphr. in Top. 277.4 . Adv. -τως v.l. in Paul.Aeg. 7.16 .
term_table.greek_sentence: Τὰς πολυχρήστους ὀνομαζομένας ἐμπλάστρους, ἐπειδὴ πολλαῖς διαθέσεσιν ἁρμόττουσι, διελόμενος, ἐν μὲν τῷ πρὸ τούτου γράμματι τὰς δυναμένας ἅμα τοῖς ἄλλοις οἷς ἐπαγγέλλονται καὶ τὰ δυσθεράπευτα τῶν ἑλκῶν ἰᾶσθαι, συνήθροισα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Having divided up the plasters called polychrēsta (of many uses), since they are suited to many conditions, in the book before this one I gathered together those that are able, along with the other things they profess to do, also to heal the hard-to-treat among ulcers.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Having divided up the so-called polychrest plasters, since they suit many dispositions, in the book before this one I gathered together those that are able, along with the other things they promise, also to heal the hard-to-treat among ulcers.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: διάθεσις, εως, ἡ, (διατίθημι) placing in order, arrangement ( ἡ τοῦ ἔχοντος μέρη τάξις Arist. Metaph. 1022b1 ), Antipho Soph. 24a ; πολιτείας Pl. Lg. 710b ; τῶν ξενίων Id. Ti. 27a . disposition or composition in a work of art (opp.εὕρεσις), Id. Phdr. 236a ; opp.ἱστορία, μῦθος, Plb. 34.4.1 , Plu. Arat. 32 , etc.; δ. ᾠδῆς Eup. 303 ; τῶν ἐπῶν Phryn.Com. 55 ; plan of a building, Plu. Per. 13 ; subject of a picture, etc., Polem. ap. Ath. 5.210b ; δ. μυθολογίας Plu. 2.16b ; representation in a play, Hero Aut. 20.2 : in pl., word-painting, Plu. 2.17b ; of geographical description, Str. 1.1.16 ; rhetorical art, μετ' αὐξήσεως καὶ διαθέσεως Plb. 2.61.1 . in oratory, delivery, Plu. Dem. 7 ; δ. σώματός τε καὶ τόνου φωνῆς Longin. Rh. p.194H. disposition of property, will, testament, = διαθήκη , Lys. Fr. 44 , Pl. Lg. 922b . disposing of, sale, τῶν περιόντων Isoc. 11.14 , cf. PTeb. 38.10 (ii B.C.), Str. 11.2.12 , Plu. Sol. 24 ; οἷς δ. εὔπορος, perh. means of disposing of it, of making away with it, Arist. term_table.greek_sentence: Τὰς πολυχρήστους ὀνομαζομένας ἐμπλάστρους, ἐπειδὴ πολλαῖς διαθέσεσιν ἁρμόττουσι, διελόμενος, ἐν μὲν τῷ πρὸ τούτου γράμματι τὰς δυναμένας ἅμα τοῖς ἄλλοις οἷς ἐπαγγέλλονται καὶ τὰ δυσθεράπευτα τῶν ἑλκῶν ἰᾶσθαι, συνήθροισα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Having divided up the plasters called polychrēsta (of many uses), since they are suited to many conditions, in the book before this one I gathered together those that are able, along with the other things they profess to do, also to heal the hard-to-treat among ulcers.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Having divided up the so-called polychrest plasters, since they suit many dispositions, in the book before this one I gathered together those that are able, along with the other things they promise, also to heal the hard-to-treat among ulcers.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πολύ-χρηστος, ον, useful for many purposes, very useful, Arist. GA 789b9 , Pol. 1337b26 , Dsc. 1.1 , Gal. 6.534 , 480 ( Sup. ); τὸ π. Corn. ND 9 : Comp. , Muson. Fr. 20p.112H. , Alex.Aphr. in Top. 277.4 . Adv. -τως v.l. in Paul.Aeg. 7.16 .
term_table.greek_sentence: νυνὶ δ’ ἐφ’ ἕτερον γένος τῶν πολυχρήστων ἐμπλάστρων μεταβήσομαι πρὸς ἄλλα τε πολλὰ ποιούσης ἑκάστης καὶ μέντοι καὶ πρὸς τὰ σηπόμενα τῶν μορίων, [860] ἑτέρας ὄντα διαθέσεως, ταῦτα τῶν ἰδίως δυσθεραπεύτων ὀνομαζομένων ἑλκῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But now I shall pass to another kind of the plasters of many uses (polychrēsta), each of which acts upon many other things and indeed also upon the putrefying parts, [860] these being of a different condition from the ulcers that are properly called hard-to-treat.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now I shall pass on to another kind of polychrest plasters, each of which acts against many other things and, indeed, also against the putrefying parts, [860] these being of a different condition from the ulcers specifically called hard-to-treat.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σηπεδών, όνος, ἡ, (σήπομαι) decay, putrefaction, in animal bodies or wood, or even stone, Hp. Epid. 3.4 , Antipho Soph. 15 , Pl. Phd. 110e , Thphr. CP 6.1.5 ; σηπεδόνα λαβεῖν Pl. Phd. 96b . of live flesh, mortification, of two kinds, ς. χλωρή (v. σῆψις) when a humour discharges, and ξηρή when it is dry, Hp. Epid. 5.4 . pl., putrid humours, Id. Aph. 3.16 (sg. in 7.20 ), Plb. 1.81.7 , Com.Adesp. 344 , etc. a serpent whose bite causes putrefaction, Nic. Th. 327 , Ael. NA 15.18 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐπὶ μὲν γὰρ τούτων ἡ σηπεδὼν ἐπινέμεται καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καλοῦσι τὰς διαθέσεις ταύτας οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἰατρῶν νομὰς, ἐπ’ ἐκείνων δὲ περιγέγραπται καθ’ ἓν χωρίον ἄνευ σηπεδόνος, ὥστε καὶ τὰς φαγεδαίνας ὀνομαζομένας ἀνεσθίειν μὲν τὰ συνεχῆ, χωρὶς μέντοι τοῦ σήπειν αὐτὰ καὶ πυρετοὺς ἐπιφέρειν, ὅπερ εἴωθεν ἀκολουθεῖν τοῖς μετὰ σηπεδόνος νομώδεσι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in the former the putrefaction spreads, and for this reason most physicians call these conditions nomai (spreading sores); whereas in the latter it is circumscribed in a single place without putrefaction, so that even the so-called phagedainai eat away the adjoining parts, yet without putrefying them and bringing on fevers, which is what usually follows upon the spreading sores accompanied by putrefaction.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in the former the putrefaction spreads, and for this reason most physicians call these conditions nomai (spreading sores); in the latter, however, the condition is circumscribed in a single place without putrefaction, so that even the so-called phagedaenas eat away the contiguous parts, yet without making them putrefy and bringing on fevers, which usually follows the spreading conditions accompanied by putrefaction.

term_table.greek_sentence: κεφάλαιον δὲ τῆς ἰάσεως ἦν, ἐπὶ μὲν τοῦ προειρημένου γένους τῶν δυσθεραπεύτων ἑλκῶν, ἃ καὶ χειρώνεια καλοῦσιν, εὑρεῖν φάρμακα, καθόσον οἷόν τε μὴ δάκνοντα μὲν, ἰσχυρῶς δὲ ξηραίνοντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The chief point of the cure was, in the case of the previously mentioned kind of hard-to-treat ulcers, which they also call Chironian, to find drugs that, as far as possible, do not bite, but dry strongly.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The chief point of the cure, in the case of the aforementioned kind of hard-to-treat ulcers, which they also call Chironian, was to find drugs that, as far as possible, do not bite but dry strongly.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κηρωτή, ἡ , ʽκηρόὠ = κήρωμα 1 , cerate or salve, used medically, Hp. Off. 12 , Art. 14 , Ar. Ach. 1176 , Ph. Bel. 96.18 ; κ. οἰνανθίνη, ῥοδίνη, Dsc. 1.109 , 2.110 ; κ. ὑγρά Gal. 11.391 ; used as a cosmetic, Ar. Fr. 320.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ταυτὶ δὲ τὰ νῦν γραφησόμενα δακνώδη πάντ’ ἐστὶν, εἴ τις αὐτοῖς ἀκράτοις ἄνευ τοῦ μιχθῆναι κηρωτῇ χρῷτο.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But these which are now to be written down are all biting, if one were to use them unmixed, without their being mixed with cerate.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But the drugs now to be written down are all biting if one uses them unmixed, without their being mixed with cerate.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κηρωτή, ἡ , ʽκηρόὠ = κήρωμα 1 , cerate or salve, used medically, Hp. Off. 12 , Art. 14 , Ar. Ach. 1176 , Ph. Bel. 96.18 ; κ. οἰνανθίνη, ῥοδίνη, Dsc. 1.109 , 2.110 ; κ. ὑγρά Gal. 11.391 ; used as a cosmetic, Ar. Fr. 320.1 .
term_table.greek_sentence: μιγνύμενα δὲ κηρωτῇ καθῇραι μὲν ἕλκος ῥυπαρὸν καὶ σαρκῶσαι δύναται καί τινα καὶ διαφορῆσαι σκληρότητα καὶ τάσιν, οὐ μὴν τὰ δυσθεράπευτά γε ἰᾶσθαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: When mixed with cerate they are able to cleanse a foul ulcer and to produce flesh, and also to disperse a certain hardness and tension, yet not to cure the hard-to-treat ones.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Mixed with cerate, however, they are able to cleanse a foul ulcer and fill it with flesh, and also to disperse some hardness and tension, but not to cure the hard-to-treat ones.

term_table.greek_sentence: δηλοῖ δ’ αὐτῶν τὴν δύναμιν τὰ πάθη πρὸς ἃ πεπίστευται παραλαμβάνεσθαι καλῶς· ὃ καὶ κατὰ τὸν ἔμπροσθεν εἴρηται λόγον καὶ νῦν ἐρῶ, μεμνῆσθαι [861] χρὴ τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τῇ περὶ τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων πραγματείᾳ, κατὰ μὲν τὰ πρῶτα βιβλία τὴν μέθοδον εἰπόντος μου, καθ’ ἣν εὑρίσκονται τῶν φαρμάκων αἱ δυνάμεις, μετὰ τοῦ καὶ γυμνάσασθαι κατ’ αὐτὴν ἐπὶ παραδειγμάτων πλειόνων, ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἑξῆς ἑκάστου κατ’ ὄνομα μνημονεύσαντος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Their power is shown by the affections for which they are trusted to be employed with good effect; and what was said in the preceding discussion I shall say now as well: one must remember [861] what has been written in the treatise on simple drugs, where in the first books I set out the method by which the powers of drugs are discovered, together with exercising oneself in it on a good many examples, and in the following books I made mention of each one by name.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Their power is made plain by the affections for which they are trusted to be properly employed. And, as was said in the earlier discussion and as I shall say now as well, one must remember [861] what was written in the treatise on simple drugs: in its first books I stated the method by which the powers of drugs are discovered, and also exercised myself in it on a number of examples, while in the books that follow I recorded each drug by name.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀποδημ-ία, Ion. -ιη, ἡ, going or being abroad, ἀ. ἐξ οἴκου Hdt. 6.130 , cf. Lys. 3.10 ; ἀ. ποιεῖσθαι Pl. Cri. 52b ; ἔξω τῆς χώρας Id. Lg. 949e , cf. 950a ; ἀ. ἡ εἰς Ὀλυμπίαν And. 4.30 ; περὶ τῆς ἀ. τῆς ἐκεῖ as to my life in that foreign land, i.e. beyond the grave, Pl. term_table.greek_sentence: πολλὰ γὰρ τοιαῦτα συμβαίνει πολλοῖς ἐν ἀποδημίαις, ταῖς τε ἄλλαις καὶ μάλιστα ταῖς κατὰ πλοῦν, ὅπου γε καὶ κατὰ χώραν μενόντων ἀπώλετό τινων ἡ παρασκευὴ τῶν φαρμάκων, ἐξ ὧν ἐθεράπευον τοὺς δεομένους, ὥσθ’ ὑπὸ λύπης αὐτοὺς συντακέντας ἀποθανεῖν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For many such things happen to many people on journeys abroad, both other journeys and especially those by sea, seeing that even while remaining in their own place some have lost the stock of drugs by which they used to treat those in need, so that they wasted away from grief and died.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For many such things happen to many people on journeys abroad, both on other kinds and above all on those by sea; indeed, even with some who stayed at home, the stock of drugs from which they treated those in need was lost, so that they wasted away from grief and died.

Mem. 4.2.6 ; ἡ π. τῆς πραγματείας Plb. 3.26.5 (elsewh. προκατασκευή, q.v.) ; λέγειν ἀπὸ παρασκευῆς, opp. αὐτοσχεδίως, Alex. Fig. 1.2 ; also, in a speech, preparatory section, D.H. Is. 15 (pl.) ; cf. παρασκευάζω A. 3 fin. with Preps., ἐκ παρασκευῆς of set purpose, by arrangement, Antipho 6.19 , Lys. 31.30 ; μάχη ἐγένετο ἐκ π. a pitched battle, Th. 5.56 ; ἀπὸ παρασκευῆς Id. 1.133 ; ἀπὸ π. οὐδεμιᾶς Antipho 5.22 ; δι' ὀλίγης παρασκευῆς at short notice, offhand, Th. 4.8 ; τὸ ναυτικὸν ἐν π. ἦν Id. 2.80 ; ἦσαν ἐν π. πολέμου were engaged in preparing for it (cf. κατασκευή), Id. 8.14 ; ἐν παρασκευῇ εἶναι Arist. Rh. 1382b3 ; μετὰ παρασκευῆς πλείστης ἠδίκησεν Id. Rh.Al. 1427a4 ; ἄνευ παρασκευῆς Pl. Ep. 326a . providing, procuring, φίλων καὶ οὐσίας Id. R. 361b ; ὑγιείας σώματι π. Id. Lg. 962a ; way or means of providing, τίς . . τέχνη τῆς π. τοῦ μηδὲν ἀδικεῖσθαι; Id. Grg. 510a ; δύ' εἶναι τὰς π. ἐπὶ τὸ θεραπεύειν ib. 513d ; in E. Ba. 457 , λευκὴν . . χροιὰν εἰς παρασκευὴν ἔχεις, ἐκ π. shd. be read. intrigue, cabal, for the purpose of gaining a verdict or carrying a measure, Cratin. 185 , Antipho 5.79 , And. 1.1 , Lys. 12.75 , al., D. 43.32 . that which is prepared, equipage, πλοῦτοί τε καὶ πᾶσα ἡ τοιαύτη π. Pl. R. 495a , cf. X. Cyr. 8.3.14 . freq. in military sense (v. supr. 1.1 ), armament, And. 1.107 , Th. 6.31 , X. Ages. 1.13 , HG 5.2.23 ; ἵπποι καὶ ὅπλα καὶ ἡ ἄλλη π. Th. 2.100 , cf. 5.17 ; γίγνεσθαι τὰς παρασκευὰς ἐποίης αI got the armaments ready for service, D. 18.102 ; αἱ πρὸς πόλεμον π. Arist. Rh. 1383b3 . generally, power, means, Th. 1.1 ; natural equipment, Arr. Epict. 1.2.30 , 2.19.30 ; φύσις καὶ π. ib. 4.8.42 , cf. 1.6.37 ; of the physical constitution of a new-born infant, Gal. 6.32 ; of mental faculties, predisposition, δύναμις καὶ π. Plot. 4.6.3 . among the Jews, the day of Preparation, before the sabbath of the Passover, Ev.Marc. 15.42 , Ev.Jo. 19.14 , 31 , etc. ; ἡμέρα παρασκευῆς Ev.Luc. 23.54 .
term_table.greek_sentence: πολλὰ γὰρ τοιαῦτα συμβαίνει πολλοῖς ἐν ἀποδημίαις, ταῖς τε ἄλλαις καὶ μάλιστα ταῖς κατὰ πλοῦν, ὅπου γε καὶ κατὰ χώραν μενόντων ἀπώλετό τινων ἡ παρασκευὴ τῶν φαρμάκων, ἐξ ὧν ἐθεράπευον τοὺς δεομένους, ὥσθ’ ὑπὸ λύπης αὐτοὺς συντακέντας ἀποθανεῖν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For many such things happen to many people on journeys abroad, both other journeys and especially those by sea, seeing that even while remaining in their own place some have lost the stock of drugs by which they used to treat those in need, so that they wasted away from grief and died.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For many such things happen to many people on journeys abroad, both on other kinds and above all on those by sea; indeed, even with some who stayed at home, the stock of drugs from which they treated those in need was lost, so that they wasted away from grief and died.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. Herm. 62 . healing remedy, medicine, in Hom. mostly of those applied outwardly, ἐπιθήσει φάρμαχ' ἅ κεν παύσῃσι μελαινάων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.191 ; ἐπ' ἄρ' ἤπια φάρμακα πάσσε ib. 218 ; ὀδυνήφατα φ. πάσσων 5.401 , 900 , cf. 11.515 , 830 , 15.394 ; προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φ. Od. 10.392 ; φ. περιαλείφειν Ar. Eq. 906 ; also of potions, πιὼν φάρμακ' Od. 10.326 ; φ. πεπωκώς Hdt. 4.160 , cf. Pi. l. c.; παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ Pl. R. 406d , cf. Grg. 467c ; φ. χριστόν E. Hipp. 516 ; ἔγχριστον Theoc. 11.1 ; ἐπίχριστον Str. 17.1.10 ; ἐπίπαστον Theoc. l. c.; καταπλαστόν Ar. Pl. 716 ; ποτόν E. Hipp. l.c.; freq. in Medic. writers, Sor. 1.4 , Gal. 6.265 , etc.; of medicines for cattle, PFlor. 222.11 (iii A. D.). c. gen. (v. infr. 11 ), φ. νόσου a medicine for it, remedy against it, A. Pr. 251 , 606 (lyr.); βηχός Phryn.Com. 60 : κεφαλῆς for a head-ache, Pl. Chrm. 155b ; στραγγουρίας Arist. HA 612b16 , cf. 624a16 ; μέθης Amphis 37 ; δίψης AP 6.170 ( Thyill. ); but ὑγιείας φ. a medicine to restore or maintain health, Aristid. Or. 37(2).11 . enchanted potion, philtre: hence, charm, spell, Od. 4.220 sq., Ar. Pl. 302 , Theoc. 2.15 , PSI 1.64.20 (i B. C.); φαρμάκοις τὸν ἄνδρ' ἔμηνεν Ar. Th. 561 ; τοιαῦτα ἔχω φ. such charms have I, Hdt. 3.85 , cf. Apoc. 9.21 . poison, S. Tr. 685 , E. Med. 385 ; πιεῖν τὸ φ. Antipho 6.15 , Pl. Phd. 57a , 115a ; φάρμακα ἐσβεβληκέναι ἐς τὰ φρέατα Th. 2.48 ; φ. δηλητήρια SIG 37 A 1 (Teos, v B. C.); τοξικὸν φ. BGU 21 ii 14 (iv A. D.). lye for laundering, Stud.Pal. 22.56.12 (iii A. D.). generally, remedy, cure, Hes. Op. 485 , Alc. 35 , etc.; μεῖζον . . τῆς νόσου τὸ φ. the cure too strong for, i. e. worse than, the disease, S. Fr. 589.4 , cf. Com.Adesp. 455 ; φ. πραΰ, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; φ. τινι for a thing, Thgn. 1134 (pl.), Archil. 9 ; πρός τι Arist. Pol. 1321a16 ; ποττὸν ἔρωτα Theoc. 11.1 ; but most freq. φ. τινός remedy against . . χλαῖνα . . φ. ῥίγευς Hippon. 19 ; Ζεὺς πάντων φ. μοῦνος ἔχει Simon. 87 ; τὸ σιγᾶν φ. βλάβης ἔχω A. Ag. 548 ; φ. πόνων, λύπης, E. Ba. 283 , Fr. 1079 ; δόλοι . . χρείας ἀνάνδρου φ. ib. 288 ; φόβου Pl. Lg. 647e ; λήθης φάρμακα (of γράμματα) E. Fr. 578.1 ; v. εὐδιανός. c. gen. also, a means of producing something, φ. σωτηρίας Id. Ph. 893 ; μνήμης καὶ σοφίας φ. Pl. Phdr. 274e ; ὑπομνήσεως ib. 275a , cf. 230d ; ἀθανασίας Antiph. 86.6 ; ἡσυχίας Arist. Pol. 1273b23 ; φ. μανίας, of the oil applied to wrestlers, D.L. 1.104 . ἐπὶ θανάτῳ φ. ἑᾶς ἀρετᾶς εὑρέσθαι a remedy or consolation in his own virtue, Pi. P. 4.187 . dye, paint, colour, Emp. 23.3 , Hdt. 1.98 , A. Fr. 134 , Ar. Ec. 735 , Pl. R. 420c , Plt. 277c , PCair.Zen. 789.13 (iii B. C.), etc. chemical reagent, PLeid.X. 25 , PHolm. 13.46 , 22.10 , Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch. p.160 B. ; used by tanners, Sch. Ar. Eq. 44 , 368 .—Cf. φαρμάσσω. [μα; but μα in φαρμακός.]
term_table.greek_sentence: ἄριστον μὲν οὖν ἤδη τοῖς πεῖραν δεδωκόσι φαρμάκοις χρῆσθαι κατὰ τὴν εἰρημένην μέθοδον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is best, then, to use drugs that have already given proof of themselves, in accordance with the method described.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Best, then, is to use drugs that have already given proof, in accordance with the method stated.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μέθοδ-ος, ἡ, (μετά, ὁδός) following after, pursuit, νύμφης μέθοδον ποιεῖσθαι Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. ζεῦγος ἡμιονικόν ( EM 409.35 ):—hence, pursuit of knowledge, investigation, Pl. Sph. 218d , 235c , al.; μ. ποιεῖσθαι to pursue one's inquiry, ib. 243d ; ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ μ. Arist. Pol. 1289a26 : hence, treatise, Dam. Pr. 451 . mode of prosecuting such inquiry, method, system, Pl. Phdr. 270c , Arist. EN 1129a6 , Pol. 1252a18 , etc.; ἡ διαλεκτικὴ μ. Pl. R. 533c , Arist. Rh. 1358a4 ; joined with τέχνη, Id. EN 1094a1 , cf. Phld. Rh. 1.32 S. ; μ. ἔχειν to have a plan or system, Arist. Top. 101a29 ; ἡ περὶ τὸν πίνακα μ. Plu. Rom. 12 . ἡ τοῦ πάντα κινεῖσθαι μ. the doctrine of motion, Pl. Tht. 183c . 'methodic' medicine, ἰητὴρ μεθόδου . . προστάτα Epigr.Gr. 306 (Smyrna), cf. Julian. ap. Gal. 18(1).256 . Rhet., means, τῆς εὑρέσεως, τοῦ κατορθοῦν, τοῦ ἀνεπαχθῶς ἑαυτὸν ἐπαινεῖν, Hermog. Meth. 2 , 22 , 25 . means of recognizing, τῶν στάσεων Id. Stat. 1 , 2 . mode of treating the subject-matter, Id. Id. 1.1 . trick, ruse, Plu. 2.176a : pl., Vett. Val. 242.11 ; μ. ἐρωτικαί Aristaenet. 1.17 ; stratagem, LXX 2 Ma. 13.18 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἄριστον μὲν οὖν ἤδη τοῖς πεῖραν δεδωκόσι φαρμάκοις χρῆσθαι κατὰ τὴν εἰρημένην μέθοδον.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀποδημ-ία, Ion. -ιη, ἡ, going or being abroad, ἀ. ἐξ οἴκου Hdt. 6.130 , cf. Lys. 3.10 ; ἀ. ποιεῖσθαι Pl. Cri. 52b ; ἔξω τῆς χώρας Id. Lg. 949e , cf. 950a ; ἀ. ἡ εἰς Ὀλυμπίαν And. 4.30 ; περὶ τῆς ἀ. τῆς ἐκεῖ as to my life in that foreign land, i.e. beyond the grave, Pl. Phd. 61e , cf. 67c , Ap. 41a (but in pl. of earthly life, as exile from heaven, Porph. Marc. 5 ); ἐξ ἀποδημίας τινὸς προσῄει from a long journey, X. Cyr. 3.1.7 .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δ’, ὡς ἔφην, ἀπορήσαιμέν ποτε τούτων, ἕξιν ἔχειν αὐτοὺς τοιαύτην, ὡς δύνασθαι συντιθέναι παραπλήσια τοῖς ἤδη δεδωκόσιν ἱκανὴν πεῖραν, ὥσπερ πολλάκις κᾀμὲ ὁρᾶτε πράττοντα [862] κατά γε τὰς ἀποδημίας καὶ ἄλλως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if, as I said, we should ever be at a loss for these, [it is best] that they themselves possess such a habit as to be able to compose drugs resembling those that have already given sufficient proof, just as you often see me too doing, [862] both on journeys abroad and otherwise.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if, as I said, we should at some time lack these, [it is best] that we ourselves have such a trained disposition as to be able to compound drugs similar to those that have already given sufficient proof by experience, as you often see me doing too, [862] at least on journeys abroad, and in other circumstances as well.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔνιοι, αι, α, some; never in Ep. , Lyr., or Att. Poets before Men. , exc. Ar. Pl. 867 (cf. however ἐνίοτε); first used in Ion. Prose, as Hdt. 1.120 , 8.56 , Hp. Praec. 6 ; πολλοὶ μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Lys. 25.19 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Pl. Tht. 151a , X. Mem. 4.2.38 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . οἱ δὲ . . Pl. term_table.greek_sentence: ἔνια γοῦν τῶν αὐτοσχεδιασθέντων ἐν τοιαύταις περιστάσεσι βασανισθέντα τῇ πείρᾳ τῶν ἐνδοξοτάτων οὐδὲν ἐφάνη χείρω.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, some of the ones improvised in such circumstances, when tested by experience, appeared in no way inferior to the most renowned.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At any rate, some of the drugs improvised in such circumstances, when tested by experience, proved in no way inferior to the most renowned.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔνδοξ-ος, ον, (δόξα) held in esteem or honour, of high repute, πρός τινος by one, X. Oec. 6.10 codd. ( Sup. ); -ότατοι ποιηταί Id. Mem. 1.2.56 ; πόλις -οτέρα εἰς τὰ πολεμικά ib. 3.5.1 ; νέοι πλούσιοι καὶ ἔ. Pl. Sph. 223b ; μὴ πλουσιώτερος ἀλλ' -ότερος Isoc. 1.37 ; ὀλίγοι καὶ ἔ. ἄνδρες Arist. EN 1098b28 , cf. Epicur. Sent. 7 , etc. of things, notable, πράγματα Aeschin. 3.231 , cf. Diod.Com. 2.21 ; generally approved, τὸ καλόν, = τὸ ἔ. , Epicur. Fr. 513 ; glorious, ταφαί Plu. Per. 28 ; ἡδὺ καὶ ἔ. καὶ ὠφέλιμον Id. 2.99f . Adv. -ξως, freq. in Inscrr., SIG 442.7 (Erythrae, iii B. C.), etc., cf. Vit.Philonid. p.12C. , Plu. C.): Sup. -ότατα, ἐβουλεύσασθε D. 18.65 . resting on opinion, probable, generally admitted, ἔ. τὰ δοκοῦντα πᾶσιν ἢ τοῖς πλείστοις ἢ τοῖς σοφοῖς, opp. to what is necessarily true (τὰ πρῶτα καὶ ἀληθῆ), Arist. term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, some of the ones improvised in such circumstances, when tested by experience, appeared in no way inferior to the most renowned.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At any rate, some of the drugs improvised in such circumstances, when tested by experience, proved in no way inferior to the most renowned.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: στοχ-ασμός, ὁ, guessing, μελέτης ς. the power of guessing which comes from practice. Pl. Phlb. 56a ; στοχασμῷ λαμβάνων, ς. πινομένη, 'quantum sufficit', Dsc. 1.48 , Eup. 2.21 ; τὸν ς. ἀεὶ καὶ μᾶλλον ἐξακριβοῦν Gal. 6.129 ; as a technical term in Rhet., Phld. term_table.greek_sentence: τὴν μὲν γὰρ πρώτην αὐτῶν σύνθεσιν ἐκ στοχασμοῦ τεχνικοῦ ποιούμεθα, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς πείρας, ἐνίων μὲν φανέντων δοκιμωτάτων, ἐνίων δ’ ἀπολειπομένων τοῦ σκοποῦ, δευτέρα πάλιν ἐπανόρθωσις γίνεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For we make their first composition from technical conjecture, and after this, on the basis of experience—some having appeared most approved, others falling short of the aim—a second correction in turn comes about, and sometimes also a third, bringing them to the perfection of what they promise.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For we make their first composition from skilled estimation; after that, on the basis of experience, since some prove most excellent while others fall short of the aim, a second correction is made in turn; and sometimes a third as well, which brings them to the full accomplishment of what they promise.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: ἤδη τοίνυν ἄρξομαι τῶν τοιούτων ἐμπλάστρων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Now then I shall begin with plasters of this sort.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now then I shall begin on plasters of this kind.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: βοτάνη [α], ἡ, (βόσκω) pasture, Il. 13.493 , Pl. Prt. 321b , etc.; ἐκ βοτάνης ἀνιόντα Theoc. 25.87 ; ἐν β. Id. 28.12 ; ἔγρονται ἐς βοτάναν E. Fr. 773.29 ; β. ἁ λέοντος the lion's pasture, i.e. Nemea, Pi. N. 6.42 : metaph., ὥσπερ ἐν κακῇ β. τρεφόμενοι Pl. R. 401c . fodder, Od. 10.411 . herb, Thphr. HP 4.4.13 , Dsc. 1 Praef. 1 (pl.), etc. in pl., plants, as material for making clothes, opp. δοραί, Diog. Oen. 10 . weeds, Thphr. HP 2.7.5 , POxy. 729.22 (ii A. D.): in pl., Gp. 2.46.2 . ἱερὰ β., = περιστερεών , Dsc. 4.60 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τὴν διὰ βοτανῶν γεγράφασιν ἅπαντες σχεδὸν οἱ τὰς ἐνδόξους ἐμπλάστρους ἀθροίσαντες ἐν γραφαῖς βίβλου μιᾶς ἢ πλειόνων, οὐ πολὺ διαφερόμενοι τῇ συμμετρίᾳ τῶν μιγνυμένων φαρμάκων ἁπλῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The plaster made of herbs has been written up by almost all who have collected the renowned plasters in the writings of one book or of several, not differing much in the proportion of the simple drugs that are mixed.

term_table.greek_sentence: [863] [Ἡ διὰ βοτανῶν Κρίτωνος.] Ἡ διὰ βοτανῶν, ᾗ χρῶμαι, ποιεῖ πρὸς καρκινώματα, σηπεδόνας· χοιράδας εἰς διαπύησιν ἄγουσα καὶ ἐξιποῦσα λέπρας ἀφίστησι καὶ δοθιῆνας διαλύει, ποδαγρικοῖς ἁρμόζει, πώρους διαλύει, ἡ αὐτὴ κεφαλικὴ ἄνευ ἀνατρήσεως λεπίδας ἀφίστησιν, ἀνάγει ὀστᾶ, ἐπιξύει δὲ τὰ ὀστᾶ ἐπὶ ποσὸν, ἡ αὐτὴ πρὸς τὰ νεότρωτα πρὸς νομὰς ἔμμοτος ἀνακαθαίρει, πληροῖ σὺν ῥοδίνῃ κηρωτῇ ἑνὸς μέρους πρὸς δύο κηρωτῆς μέρη, ἐνίοτε δὲ γ΄ ἢ δ΄.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [863] [The plaster through herbs, of Crito.] The plaster through herbs, which I use, works against carcinomata and putrefactions; it brings scrofulous swellings (choirades) to suppuration and, pressing them out, removes leprai and dissolves boils (dothienes); it is suited to gouty patients and dissolves calluses (poroi); the same is a cephalic plaster, which without trepanation detaches scales of bone, brings up bones, and scrapes the bones to some extent; the same, for freshly inflicted wounds and for spreading sores (nomai), applied on lint, cleanses thoroughly and fills up, together with rose cerate, one part being mixed to two parts of cerate, and sometimes three or four; and with myrtle cerate, in two or three parts, it cicatrizes.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [863] [The plaster from herbs of Criton.] The plaster from herbs, which I use, is effective against carcinomas and putrefactions; bringing choirades to suppuration and squeezing them out, it removes lepras and dissolves boils; it is suitable for gouty patients; it dissolves calluses; the same, as a cephalic, removes scales of bone without trepanation, brings up bones, and scrapes the bones to some extent; the same is for freshly inflicted wounds; for spreading ulcers, applied on lint, it cleans them out; it fills in with rose cerate, one part being mixed to two parts of cerate, and sometimes to three or four.

term_table.english_sentence_A: For this reason, then, Criton too, in the case of the drug under discussion, orders that to one part [868] of it there be mixed sometimes two parts of the cerate, sometimes three or four; he did not, however, define when one ought to mix the two parts and when the more, on the assumption that the person who is going to use the drug already has some practice in the art and is able to reason out what is now being said by me.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For this reason, then, Criton too, in the case of the drug under discussion, directs that to one part [868] of it one should mix sometimes two parts of the cerate, sometimes three or four. He did not, however, specify when two parts and when more should be mixed, as though whoever was going to use the drug already had some practice in the art and were able to work out for himself what is now being said by me.

Lys. 1301 , Cypr. ἀζαθός GDI 57 :— good: of persons, well-born, gentle, opp. κακός, δειλός, οἷά τε τοῖς ἀγαθοῖσι παραδρώωσι χέρηες Od. 15.324 , cf. Il. 1.275 ; ἀφνειός τ' ἀ. τε Il. 13.664 , cf. Od. 18.276 ; πατρὸς δ' εἴμ' ἀγαθοῖο, θεὰ δέ με γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 21.109 , cf. Od. 4.611 ; κακὸς ἐξ ἀ. Thgn. 190 , cf. 57 sq.; πραῢς ἀστοῖς, οὐ φθονέων ἀγαθοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 , cf. 2.96 , 4.285 ; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστοι; οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀ. κτλ. S. El. 1082 ; οἵ τ' ἀ. πρὸς τῶν ἀγενῶν κατανικῶνται Id. Fr. 84 ; τοὺς εὐγενεῖς γὰρ κἀγαθοὺς . . φιλεῖ Ἄρης ἐναίρειν ib. 649 , cf. E. Alc. 600 , al.: ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν Pl. Phdr. 274a :—in political sense, aristocrats, esp. in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (v. sub καλοκἀγαθός). brave, valiant, since courage was attributed to Chiefs and Nobles, Il. 1.131 , al.; τῷ κ' ἀγαθὸς μὲν ἔπεφν', ἀγαθὸν δέ κεν ἐξενάριξεν 21.280 ; cf. Hdt. 5.109 , etc. good, capable, in reference to ability, ἀ. βασιλεύς Il. 3.179 ; ἰητήρ 2.732 ; θεράπων 16.165 , 17.388 ; πύκτης Xenoph. 2.15 ; ἰητρός Hp. Prog. 1 ; προβατογνώμων A. Ag. 795 ; ἄρχοντες Democr. 266 : freq. with qualifying words, ἀ. ἐν ὑσμίνῃ Il. 13.314 ; βοὴν ἀ. 2.408 , 563 , al.; πύξ Od. 11.300 ; βίην Il. 6.478 ; γνώμην S. OT 687 ; πᾶσαν ἀρετήν Pl. Lg. 899b , cf. Alc. 1.124e ; τέχνην Id. Prt. 323b ; τὰ πολέμια, τὰ πολιτικά, Hdt. 9.122 , Pl. Grg. 516b , etc.: more rarely c. dat., ἀ. πολέμῳ X. Oec. 4.15 : with Preps., ἄνδρες ἀ. περὶ τὸ πλῆθος Lys. 13.2 ; εἴς τι Pl. Alc. 1.125a ; πρός τι Id. R. 407e : c. inf., ἀ. μάχεσθαι Hdt. 1.136 ; ἱππεύεσθαι 1.79 ; ἀ. ἱστάναι good at weighing, Pl. Prt. 356b . good, in moral sense, first in Thgn. 438 , cf. Heraclit. 104 , S. El. 1082 , X. Mem. 1.7.1 , Pl. Ap. 41d , etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος Democr. 247 : freq. with other Adjs., ὁ πιστὸς κἀ. S. Tr. 541 ; δικαίων κἀ. ib. 1050 :—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα Id. Ant. 31 . ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, Pl. Prt. 311a , etc. ἀ. δαίμων, v. sub δαίμων; ἀ. τύχη, v. sub τύχη; ἀ. θεός = Lat. bona dea, Plu. Caes. 9 , Cic. 19 . of things, good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη . . ἀ. κουροτρόφος Od. 9.27 , etc.; ἀ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει X. Cyn. 13.17 : c. gen., εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀ. good for it, Id. Mem. 3.8.3 ; ἑλκῶν Thphr. HP 9.11.1 . of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347 ; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, Il. 9.102 ; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, 11.789 ; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204 :—ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so<*> Il. 7.282 , 24.130 , Od. 3.196 , etc. morally good, πρῆξις Democr. 177 ; ἔργα Emp. 112.2 , cf. Ep.Rom. 2.7 , etc. ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις X. Cyr. 5.3.20 ; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι Id. Mem. 2.4.2 , cf. Ar. Ra. 74 , etc; as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, Men. Sam. 28 :— ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on . . , Th. 3.68 , Lys. 13.92 ; ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, Th. 5.27 , X. Cyr. 7.4.3 ; ἐπ' ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις Ar. Ra. 1487 ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀ. for no good end, Th. 1.131 ; ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος X. HG 5.2.35 :—in pl., ἡ ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά PFlor. 21.10 (iii A.D.):—τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, Epich. 171.5 , cf. Pl. R. 506b , 508e , Arist. Metaph. 1091a31 , etc.:—in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, Hdt. 2.172 , Lys. 13.91 , X. Mem. 1.2.63 , etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν fare well, Ar. Av. 1706 ; also, good things, dainties, Thgn. 1000 , Ar. Ach. 873 , etc.: good qualities, τοῖς ἀ., οἷς ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ Isoc. 8.32 , cf. Democr. 37 ; good points, of a horse, εἰ τἄλλα πάντα ἀ. ἔχοι, κακόπους δ' εἴη X. Eq. 1.2 . Comp. and Sup. are usu. supplied from other stems, viz. Comp. ἀμείνων, ἀρείων<*> βελτίων, κρείσσων ʽκάρρωνʼ, λωΐων (λώʽωνʼ), Ep. βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος:— Sup. ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος (λῷστος), Ep. βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος:— later, reg. Comp. ἀγαθώτερος LXX Jd. 11.25 , 15.2 , D.S. 8 Fr. 12 , Plot. 5.5.9 , Diod.Rh. p.53.9H. : Sup. ἀγαθώτατος D.S. 16.85 , Hld. 5.15 , etc. ( -ότατος POxy. 1757.26 (ii A.D.)). Adv. usually εὖ, q.v.: ἀγαθῶς Hp. Off. 9 , Arist. Rh. 1388b6 , LXX 1 Ki. 20.7 . (Etym. dub. ( ὅτι ἄγει ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ὀρθὸν βίον Stoic. 3.49 ); perh. cognate with ἄγαμαι, hence admirable.)
