term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ μὲν οὖν ἀρίστη θεραπεία τῶν σκληρυνομένων, ἃ δὴ καὶ σκιῤῥοῦται μὴ θεραπευθέντα διὰ τῆς κατὰ μέθοδον ἰατρικῆς, γίνεται τοῦ θεραπεύοντος θεωροῦντος ἐπὶ πόσον ἡ τοῦ θεραπευομένου σώματος οὐσία προήκει φύσεως παρὰ τὴν σύμμετρον ὑγρότητα καὶ ξηρότητα, καθάπερ γε καὶ τὴν τοῦ πάθους αὐτοῦ σύστασιν, εἰς ὅσον ηὔξηται, καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἐν αὐτοῖς τοῖς μαλάττουσι φαρμάκοις τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον, εἰς ταῦτα γὰρ ἀποβλέποντί σοι στοχαστικὴ μὲν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ τέχνης ἡ πρώτη χρῆσις τοῦ μαλακτικοῦ ἔσται φαρμάκου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The best treatment, then, of parts that are hardening—which indeed become scirrhous if they are not treated by medicine according to method—comes about when the one treating considers how far by nature the substance of the body under treatment departs from the commensurate moisture and dryness, as also the constitution of the affection itself, to what degree it has increased, and in addition to these the more and the less in the softening drugs themselves; for if you look to these things, the first use of the emollient drug will be conjectural, yet with art.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The best treatment, then, of parts that are becoming hardened, which indeed also become scirrhous if they are not treated by medicine according to method, comes about when the practitioner considers how far the substance of the body under treatment has advanced in its nature beyond the well-proportioned moisture and dryness, and likewise the constitution of the affection itself, to what extent it has increased, and in addition to these, the more and less in the softening drugs themselves. For if you look to these things, your first use of the emollient drug will be conjectural, but with art.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ μὲν οὖν ἀρίστη θεραπεία τῶν σκληρυνομένων, ἃ δὴ καὶ σκιῤῥοῦται μὴ θεραπευθέντα διὰ τῆς κατὰ μέθοδον ἰατρικῆς, γίνεται τοῦ θεραπεύοντος θεωροῦντος ἐπὶ πόσον ἡ τοῦ θεραπευομένου σώματος οὐσία προήκει φύσεως παρὰ τὴν σύμμετρον ὑγρότητα καὶ ξηρότητα, καθάπερ γε καὶ τὴν τοῦ πάθους αὐτοῦ σύστασιν, εἰς ὅσον ηὔξηται, καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἐν αὐτοῖς τοῖς μαλάττουσι φαρμάκοις τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον, εἰς ταῦτα γὰρ ἀποβλέποντί σοι στοχαστικὴ μὲν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ τέχνης ἡ πρώτη χρῆσις τοῦ μαλακτικοῦ ἔσται φαρμάκου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The best treatment, then, of parts that are hardening—which indeed become scirrhous if they are not treated by medicine according to method—comes about when the one treating considers how far by nature the substance of the body under treatment departs from the commensurate moisture and dryness, as also the constitution of the affection itself, to what degree it has increased, and in addition to these the more and the less in the softening drugs themselves; for if you look to these things, the first use of the emollient drug will be conjectural, yet with art.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The best treatment, then, of parts that are becoming hardened, which indeed also become scirrhous if they are not treated by medicine according to method, comes about when the practitioner considers how far the substance of the body under treatment has advanced in its nature beyond the well-proportioned moisture and dryness, and likewise the constitution of the affection itself, to what extent it has increased, and in addition to these, the more and less in the softening drugs themselves. For if you look to these things, your first use of the emollient drug will be conjectural, but with art.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
term_table.greek_sentence: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἰατροὶ συνέθεσαν φάρμακα μαλακτικὰ καὶ διαφορητικὰ ὡς πρὸς ἀμφοτέρους ἀποβλεπόντει τοὺς σκοποὺς, τόν τε τῆς χύσεως τοῦ ἐσκληρυσμένου καὶ σκιῤῥουμένου μορίου, τόν τε τῆς διαφορήσεως, οὐκ ἐναλλὰξ ἑκατέρῳ χρώμενοι, καθάπερ ἐμὲ πράττοντα βλέπετε πολλάκις, ἀλλ’ ἀεὶ τὰ δύο διὰ τοῦ συνθέτου φαρμάκου ποιοῦντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Now the physicians have compounded emollient and discutient drugs as looking to both aims at once, that of the liquefaction of the hardened and scirrhous part and that of discussion, not using each of the two alternately, as you often see me doing, but always effecting the two things through the compound drug.

term_table.greek_sentence: εὔδηλον δὲ ὅτι πολλάκις ἴσα ταῖς δυνάμεσι μίγνυνται, καὶ χρὴ καθάπερ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων φαρμάκων, οὕτως κᾀπὶ τούτων παρασκευάσασθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ καλῶς ἰατρεύειν πλείω φάρμακα τῶν ὁμογενῶν, ἢ πάντως γε δύο μίγνυσθαι, τό τε ἰσχυρότατον ἐν τῷ γένει καὶ τὸ μετριώτατον, ἵνα ἐκ τῆς διαφόρου μίξεως αὐτῶν ἐπικαίρου γενομένης ἐργάζηται τὰ μεταξὺ τῶν ἄκρων πάμπολλα φάρμακα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is quite evident too that often they are mixed in equal proportions as regards their powers; and it is necessary, just as in the case of the other drugs, so also in the case of these, for one who wishes to practise medicine well to prepare for himself several drugs of the same kind, or at any rate to have two to mix, the strongest in the kind and the most moderate, in order that from their varied mixture, made in a manner suited to the occasion, he may produce the very many drugs that lie between the extremes.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is quite clear too that they are often mixed in equal potencies. Just as with the other drugs, so with these, the one who wishes to treat well must have prepared several drugs of the same kind, or at any rate two to be mixed, the strongest in the kind and the most moderate, so that from their differing mixture, made at the opportune moment, he may produce a great many drugs between the extremes.

term_table.greek_sentence: εὔδηλον δὲ ὅτι πολλάκις ἴσα ταῖς δυνάμεσι μίγνυνται, καὶ χρὴ καθάπερ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων φαρμάκων, οὕτως κᾀπὶ τούτων παρασκευάσασθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ καλῶς ἰατρεύειν πλείω φάρμακα τῶν ὁμογενῶν, ἢ πάντως γε δύο μίγνυσθαι, τό τε ἰσχυρότατον ἐν τῷ γένει καὶ τὸ μετριώτατον, ἵνα ἐκ τῆς διαφόρου μίξεως αὐτῶν ἐπικαίρου γενομένης ἐργάζηται τὰ μεταξὺ τῶν ἄκρων πάμπολλα φάρμακα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is quite evident too that often they are mixed in equal proportions as regards their powers; and it is necessary, just as in the case of the other drugs, so also in the case of these, for one who wishes to practise medicine well to prepare for himself several drugs of the same kind, or at any rate to have two to mix, the strongest in the kind and the most moderate, in order that from their varied mixture, made in a manner suited to the occasion, he may produce the very many drugs that lie between the extremes.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is quite clear too that they are often mixed in equal potencies. Just as with the other drugs, so with these, the one who wishes to treat well must have prepared several drugs of the same kind, or at any rate two to be mixed, the strongest in the kind and the most moderate, so that from their differing mixture, made at the opportune moment, he may produce a great many drugs between the extremes.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὐ γὰρ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει δύναμιν τὸ στέαρ βδελλίῳ τε καὶ στύρακι καὶ ἀμμωνιακῷ θυμιάματι, καθάπερ οὐδὲ αὐτῶν τῶν στεάτων τὸ χήνειόν τε [949] καὶ ὀρνίθειον ἢ παρδάλειον ἢ λεόντειον ἡ ὑαίνης ἤ τινος ἄλλου ζώου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For fat does not have the same power as bdellium and storax and ammoniac incense, just as, among the fats themselves, neither do the goose [949] and the hen's, or leopard's or lion's or hyena's, or that of some other animal.

term_table.greek_sentence: κατὰ γὰρ τὴν κρᾶσιν τοῦ ζώου καὶ τὸ στέαρ ἐστι, τῶν μὲν θερμοτέρων θερμαντικώτερον, τῶν δὲ ξηροτέρων ξηραντικώτερον, καὶ γινώσκουσί γε οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἰσχυρότατον μὲν εἶναι κατ’ ἄμφω, λέγω δὴ τὸ θερμαίνειν τε καὶ διαφορεῖν, τὸ τοῦ λέοντος στέαρ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For the fat too is in accordance with the temperament of the animal: that of the hotter animals is more heating, that of the drier more drying; and most physicians know that the strongest in both respects, I mean in heating and in dispersing, is the fat of the lion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For the fat too is according to the temperament (krasis) of the animal: that of the hotter animals is more heating, that of the drier more drying. And indeed most physicians know that the strongest in both respects, I mean heating and dispersing, is the fat of the lion.

term_table.english_sentence_A: To all of these, moreover, belongs also being finer-parted than those in four-footed animals.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now all of these also have the property of being finer-particled than those in four-footed animals.

term_table.english_sentence_A: But again among those there is a very great difference, pig's fat being the softest and moistest and for this reason the weakest of the others, so that it suits tender bodies, such as those of women and children and eunuchs and of delicately-living men, bodies made effeminate by rearing in the shade, by lack of exercise, and by rather frequent baths of fresh waters.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Among those, in turn, there is a very great difference: pig's fat is the softest and moistest and for this reason the weakest of the others, so that it suits soft bodies, such as are those of women and children and eunuchs and of men of delicate living, made effeminate by rearing in the shade, lack of exercise, and frequent baths of drinkable water.

term_table.greek_sentence: τὸ δὲ τῶν αἰγῶν τε καὶ βοῶν, εἰς ὅσον ἰσχυρότερον τοῦ τῶν ὑῶν ἐστιν, εἰς τοσοῦτον σώμασί [950] τε καὶ φύσει σκληροτέροις καὶ τοῖς σκιῤῥωδεστέροις τῶν σκληροτέρων ἁρμόττει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But that of goats and of cattle, to the extent that it is stronger than that of swine, to that same extent is suited to bodies [950] that are harder, both by nature, and to the more scirrhous among the harder ones.
term_table.english_sentence_B: That of goats and oxen, by as much as it is stronger than that of swine, by so much is it suited to bodies [950] that are harder, also by nature, and to the more scirrhous among the harder [conditions].

term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ δὲ ἐν τοῖς ἄλλοις ἅπασιν ὅσα μεταπίπτειν εἰς ἄλληλα πέφυκεν, ἔνεστι μεθόριον ἀμφοτέρων ἠρέμα μέτοχον, οὕτως καὶ τῶν φλεγμονωδῶν ὄγκων πρὸς τοὺς ἄνευ φλεγμονῆς σκίῤῥους, οἷοί περ οἱ τῶν ἐσκληρυσμένων εἰσὶν, ὑπάρχει τις ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ διάθεσις, ἀνώδυνος μὲν, εἰ μὴ τοὺς δακτύλους ἐπερείδοις, ὀδυνωμένη δὲ τοῦτο πραττόντων, ἣν σαφοῦς τε καὶ συντόμου διδασκαλίας ἕνεκα ἤτοι φλεγμονὴν σκιῤῥώδη λεκτέον ἢ σκίῤῥον φλεγμονώδη, μὴ προσέχοντας ἐνταῦθα τῷ [951] κατὰ τὸν ὄγκον μεγέθει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Just as in all other things that are naturally such as to change into one another there is a borderland partaking slightly of both, so too between the inflammatory swellings and the scirrhi without inflammation, such as those of indurated parts are, there exists a certain intermediate condition, painless, unless you press the fingers upon it, but painful when one does this; which, for the sake of clear and concise teaching, must be called either scirrhous inflammation or inflammatory scirrhus, not attending here to the [951] magnitude of the swelling.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Just as in all other things whose nature is to pass over into one another there is a borderland between the two that shares moderately in both, so also between phlegmonous swellings and the scirrhi without phlegmone, such as are those of parts that have become hardened, there exists a certain intermediate condition. It is painless unless you press the fingers on it, but painful when people do so.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Just as in all other things that are naturally such as to change into one another there is a borderland partaking slightly of both, so too between the inflammatory swellings and the scirrhi without inflammation, such as those of indurated parts are, there exists a certain intermediate condition, painless, unless you press the fingers upon it, but painful when one does this; which, for the sake of clear and concise teaching, must be called either scirrhous inflammation or inflammatory scirrhus, not attending here to the [951] magnitude of the swelling.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Just as in all other things whose nature is to pass over into one another there is a borderland between the two that shares moderately in both, so also between phlegmonous swellings and the scirrhi without phlegmone, such as are those of parts that have become hardened, there exists a certain intermediate condition. It is painless unless you press the fingers on it, but painful when people do so.

term_table.greek_sentence: τῆς γὰρ ἰδέας τῶν παθῶν ἐστιν, οὐ τοῦ καθ’ ἕτερον αὐτῶν ποσοῦ φλεγ μονὴ καὶ σκιῤῥος ὀνόματα, μεγάλης μὲν φλεγμονῆς γενομένης ἢ διὰ τὸ τοῦ φλεγμαίνοντος μορίου μέγεθος ἢ διὰ τὴν τοῦ παρὰ φύσιν ὄγκου, μικρᾶς δὲ τῆς ἤτοι μικρὸν τόπον κατειληφυίας ἢ βραχὺν ὄγκον ἐχούσης.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For 'inflammation' and 'scirrhus' are names of the form of the affections, not of the quantity in either of them, an inflammation being large either on account of the size of the inflamed part or on account of that of the swelling contrary to nature, and small when it has either occupied a small place or has a slight swelling.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For the sake of clear and concise teaching it must be called either a scirrhous phlegmone or a phlegmonous scirrhus, without attending here to the [951] magnitude of the swelling. For 'phlegmone' and 'scirrhus' are names of the form of the affections, not of the quantity in either of them.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κατά-πλασμα, ατος, τό, plaster, poultice, Hp. Art. 40 (pl.), Ar. Fr. 320.12 , Arist. Pr. 863a6 , Thphr. HP 9.11.4 , Od. 59 , PLit.Lond. 170 (pl., i A. D.), etc.
term_table.greek_sentence: φλεγμονῆς μὲν οὖν μεγάλης διὰ καταπλασμάτων ἴασις γίνεται καί τινων ὑγρῶν φαρμάκων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The cure of a large inflammation, then, comes about through cataplasms and certain liquid drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For from these the treatment of the other things called large and small will also be understood.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τῆς δὲ μικρᾶς, ὅταν σκιῤῥώδει σκληρότητι μιχθῇ, καὶ διὰ καταπλασμάτων μὲν ἔστιν ὅτε, καὶ διὰ φαρμάκων δὲ κηρωτοειδῶν τε καὶ ὑγρῶν, ἔτι τε τῶν μαλακτικῶν ἐμπλάστρων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: That of a small one, when it is mixed with a scirrhous hardness, comes about sometimes through cataplasms, and also through drugs that are cerate-like and liquid, and further through the emollient plasters.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The cure of a large phlegmone, then, comes about through poultices and certain liquid drugs. The cure of a small one, when it has been mixed with scirrhous hardness, comes about sometimes through poultices, but also through cerate-like and liquid drugs, and further through the emollient plasters.

term_table.english_sentence_A: In the case of a hardness that has something inflammatory, however, the aim too becomes composite.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But in the case of a hardness that has something phlegmonous in it, the aim too becomes compound.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πάρυγρ-ος, ον, somewhat wet, Man. 1.87 (leg. πάνυγρος) ; τὸ π. a kind of plaster invented by Heras, Gal. 2.703 , 13.952 ; also ἡ π. Orib. Fr. 90 . πάρυγρα πράσσοντες plying waterside trades, Vett. Val. 2.6 .
term_table.greek_sentence: [Περὶ τῆς παρύγρου.] Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο [952] καὶ φάρμακον σύνθετόν πώς ἐστιν, οἷον καὶ τοῦτο τὸ πᾶσι γινωσκόμενον, ἐπῃνημένον δὲ μεγάλως ὑπ’ ἄλλων τέ τινων καὶ μάλιστα τοῦ Ἥρα, τὸ καλούμενον πάρυγρον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [On the parhygros.] And for this reason [952] the drug too is in a way composite, such as this one which is known to everyone and greatly praised by certain others and especially by Heras, the one called parhygron (moist).
term_table.english_sentence_B: [On the parhygros.] And for this reason [952] the drug too is in a way compound, such as this one known to everyone and highly praised by certain others and above all by Heras, the so-called parhygron.

term_table.english_sentence_B: Galbanum too, and what is called opopanax, have, besides dispersing, something emollient as well.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. Herm. 62 . healing remedy, medicine, in Hom. mostly of those applied outwardly, ἐπιθήσει φάρμαχ' ἅ κεν παύσῃσι μελαινάων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.191 ; ἐπ' ἄρ' ἤπια φάρμακα πάσσε ib. 218 ; ὀδυνήφατα φ. πάσσων 5.401 , 900 , cf. 11.515 , 830 , 15.394 ; προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φ. Od. 10.392 ; φ. περιαλείφειν Ar. Eq. 906 ; also of potions, πιὼν φάρμακ' Od. 10.326 ; φ. πεπωκώς Hdt. 4.160 , cf. Pi. l. c.; παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ Pl. R. 406d , cf. Grg. 467c ; φ. χριστόν E. Hipp. 516 ; ἔγχριστον Theoc. 11.1 ; ἐπίχριστον Str. 17.1.10 ; ἐπίπαστον Theoc. l. c.; καταπλαστόν Ar. Pl. 716 ; ποτόν E. Hipp. l.c.; freq. in Medic. writers, Sor. 1.4 , Gal. 6.265 , etc.; of medicines for cattle, PFlor. 222.11 (iii A. D.). c. gen. (v. infr. 11 ), φ. νόσου a medicine for it, remedy against it, A. Pr. 251 , 606 (lyr.); βηχός Phryn.Com. 60 : κεφαλῆς for a head-ache, Pl. Chrm. 155b ; στραγγουρίας Arist. HA 612b16 , cf. 624a16 ; μέθης Amphis 37 ; δίψης AP 6.170 ( Thyill. ); but ὑγιείας φ. a medicine to restore or maintain health, Aristid. Or. 37(2).11 . enchanted potion, philtre: hence, charm, spell, Od. 4.220 sq., Ar. Pl. 302 , Theoc. 2.15 , PSI 1.64.20 (i B. C.); φαρμάκοις τὸν ἄνδρ' ἔμηνεν Ar. Th. 561 ; τοιαῦτα ἔχω φ. such charms have I, Hdt. 3.85 , cf. Apoc. 9.21 . poison, S. Tr. 685 , E. Med. 385 ; πιεῖν τὸ φ. Antipho 6.15 , Pl. Phd. 57a , 115a ; φάρμακα ἐσβεβληκέναι ἐς τὰ φρέατα Th. 2.48 ; φ. δηλητήρια SIG 37 A 1 (Teos, v B. C.); τοξικὸν φ. BGU 21 ii 14 (iv A. D.). lye for laundering, Stud.Pal. 22.56.12 (iii A. D.). generally, remedy, cure, Hes. Op. 485 , Alc. 35 , etc.; μεῖζον . . τῆς νόσου τὸ φ. the cure too strong for, i. e. worse than, the disease, S. Fr. 589.4 , cf. Com.Adesp. 455 ; φ. πραΰ, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; φ. τινι for a thing, Thgn. 1134 (pl.), Archil. 9 ; πρός τι Arist. Pol. 1321a16 ; ποττὸν ἔρωτα Theoc. 11.1 ; but most freq. φ. τινός remedy against . . χλαῖνα . . φ. ῥίγευς Hippon. 19 ; Ζεὺς πάντων φ. μοῦνος ἔχει Simon. 87 ; τὸ σιγᾶν φ. βλάβης ἔχω A. Ag. 548 ; φ. πόνων, λύπης, E. Ba. 283 , Fr. 1079 ; δόλοι . . χρείας ἀνάνδρου φ. ib. 288 ; φόβου Pl. Lg. 647e ; λήθης φάρμακα (of γράμματα) E. Fr. 578.1 ; v. εὐδιανός. c. gen. also, a means of producing something, φ. σωτηρίας Id. Ph. 893 ; μνήμης καὶ σοφίας φ. Pl. Phdr. 274e ; ὑπομνήσεως ib. 275a , cf. 230d ; ἀθανασίας Antiph. 86.6 ; ἡσυχίας Arist. Pol. 1273b23 ; φ. μανίας, of the oil applied to wrestlers, D.L. 1.104 . ἐπὶ θανάτῳ φ. ἑᾶς ἀρετᾶς εὑρέσθαι a remedy or consolation in his own virtue, Pi. P. 4.187 . dye, paint, colour, Emp. 23.3 , Hdt. 1.98 , A. Fr. 134 , Ar. Ec. 735 , Pl. R. 420c , Plt. 277c , PCair.Zen. 789.13 (iii B. C.), etc. chemical reagent, PLeid.X. 25 , PHolm. 13.46 , 22.10 , Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch. p.160 B. ; used by tanners, Sch. Ar. Eq. 44 , 368 .—Cf. φαρμάσσω. [μα; but μα in φαρμακός.]
term_table.greek_sentence: σὺ δ’ ὅταν ἤτοι τι τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν ταῖς φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις ἐξετάσῃς τε καὶ κρίνῃς ἢ συντιθῇς αὐτὸς, ἀκηκοὼς ἄρτι τὰς κατὰ τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον ἐν τοῖς φαρμάκοις διαφορὰς, ἀκηκοὼς δὲ καὶ τὰς τῶν σωμάτων τε καὶ παθῶν, τὰ μὲν ἰσχυρὰ τοῖς ἰσχυροῖς, τὰ δὲ ἀσθενῆ τοῖς ἀσθενέσι προσάξεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And you, whenever you either examine and judge one of the drugs recorded in the pharmacological books or compound one yourself, having just now heard the differences among drugs according to the more and the less, and having heard also those of bodies and of affections, will apply the strong ones to the strong and the weak ones to the weak.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And you, whenever you either examine and judge one of the remedies written in the pharmacological books, or compound one yourself, having just heard of the differences of more and less among drugs, and having heard also of the differences of bodies and of affections, will apply the strong ones to the strong and the weak ones to the weak.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πάθος [α], εος, τό, (πάσχω) that which happens to a person or thing, τὰ ἐν τοῖς κατόπτροις τῆς ὄψεως π. Pl. Tht. 193c ; τὰ ἐν τῷ ἀνθρωπίνῳ βίῳ [τῆς ψυχῆσ] π. Id. R. 612a ; incident, accident, τὰ ἀνθρωπήϊα π. Hdt. 5.4 ; τὸ συντυχὸν π. S. Aj. 313 ; οὗ τόδ' ἦν π. where this incident took place, Id. OT 732 ; ἔξωθεν π. Pl. R. 381a ; unfortunate accident, Antipho 3.4.10 . what one has experienced, good or bad, experience, τὸν πάθει μάθος θέντα κυρίως ἔχειν A. Ag. 177 (lyr.); τά γ' ἐμὰ π. my experiences, Pl. Phd. 96a ; τὸ δρᾶμα τοῦ πάθους πλέον A. Ag. 533 ; opp. ἔργα, Pl. Phdr. 245c , Arist. Cael. 298a28 ; opp. πρᾶξις, Pl. Lg. 876d ; ἤθη καὶ π. καὶ πράξεις Arist. Po. 1447a28 . in bad sense, misfortune, calamity, A. Pr. 703 , Hdt. 1.91 , Lys. 32.10 , etc.; οὐλίῳ σὺν πάθει S. Aj. 932 (lyr.); τὰ τῆς Νιόβης π. Pl. R. 380a , etc.; ἀνήκεστον π. ἔρδειν to do an act which is an irreparable mischief to one, Hdt. 1.137 ; μετὰ τῆς θυγατρὸς τὸ π., i.e. her death, Id. 2.133 ; π. μέγα πεπονθέναι, of a great defeat, Id. 3.147 , cf. 5.87 , al. = πάθημα 11.2 , Arist. GA 738a16 , 750a30 , Gal. 10.91 . of the soul, emotion, passion ( λέγω δὲ πάθη . . ὅλως οἷς ἕπεται ἡδονὴ ἢ λύπη Arist. EN 1105b21 ), σοφίη ψυχὴν παθῶν ἀφαιρεῖται Democr. 31 ; διὰ πάθους Th. 3.84 ; ἐρωτικὸν π. Pl. Phdr. 265b ; π. ποιεῖν to excite passion, Arist. Rh. 1418a12 ; ἐν π. εἶναι Id. Pol. 1287b3 ; ἐκτὸς τοῦ π. εἶναι to be exempt from passion, Teles p.56 H.; ἔξω τῶν π. γίγνεσθαι D.C. 60.3 ; περὶ παθῶν, title of work by Zeno the Stoic, D.L. 7.4 ; in Epicur. , sensation (including pleasure and pain), ἀκουστικὸν π. Ep. 1p.13U. , cf. p.19 U. (pl.); ὡς κανόνι τῷ π. πᾶν ἀγαθὸν κρίνοντες ib. 3p.63U. state, condition, τὸ τῆς παντοδαπῆς ἀγνοίας π. Pl. Sph. 228e , cf. 243c , Plt. 277d , Ap. 22c ; opp. ἐνέργεια, A.D. Synt. 12.17 ; opp. ποίημα, Pl. Sph. 248d . incidents of things, changes or happenings occurring in them, τὰ οὐράνια π. Pl. Hp.Ma. 285c ; τὰ περὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν π. Id. Phd. 96c ; τὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ π. καὶ μέρη Arist. Metaph. 986a5 ; π. τοῦτο, ὃ καλεῖν εἰώθαμεν σεισμόν Id. Mu. 395b36 . properties, qualities of things, opp. οὐσία, Pl. Euthphr. 11a ; π. λέγεται . . ποιότης καθ' ἣν ἀλλοιοῦσθαι ἐνδέχεται, οἷον τὸ λευκὸν καὶ τὸ μέλαν, καὶ γλυκὺ καὶ πικρόν, καὶ βαρύτης καὶ κουφότης, κτλ. Arist. Metaph. 1022b15 ; τῶν ἀριθμῶν π. ib. 985b29 ; ἀριθμοῖς καὶ γραμμαῖς καὶ τοῖς τούτων π. Iamb. Comm.Math. 23 ; γεωμετρία περὶ τὰ συμβεβηκότα πάθη τοῖς μεγέθεσι Arist. Rh. 1355b31 , cf. APo. 75b1 ; τῶν φυτῶν τὰ μέρη καὶ τὰ π. Thphr. HP 1.1.1 ; αἱ δυνάμεις καὶ τὰ π. ib. 8.4.2 . Gramm., modification in form of words (esp. dialectal), πάθη τῆς λέξεως Arist. Rh. 1460b12 , cf. A.D. Pron. 38.24 , al. in Syntax, modified construction, of omission or redundancy, Id. Synt. 6.15 , 267.8 . passivity, D.T. 637.30 , A.D. Synt. 12.17 , al. in writing, signs other than accents and breathings (ἀπόστροφος, ὑφέν, ὑποδιαστολή), D.T. Supp. 1p.107U. Rhet., emotional style or treatment, τὸ σφοδρὸν καὶ ἐνθουσιαστικὸν π. Longin. 8.1 ; πάθος ποιεῖν Arist. Rh. 1418a12 ; πράγματα π. ἔχοντα Plu. 2.711e , etc.: pl., πάθη διεστῶτα ὕψους Longin. 8.2 .

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἁπλόος, η, ον, contr. ἁπλοῦς, ῆ, οῦν, opp. διπλόος twofold, and so, single, ἁπλῆ γὰρ οἶμος εἰς Ἁ ́ιδου φέρει A. Fr. 239 , cf. X. Cyr. 1.3.4 ( Comp. ); ἁπλῷ τείχει περιτειχίζειν Th. 3.18 ; δὶς τόσ' ἐξ ἁπλῶν κακά S. Aj. 277 ; ὅπως ἂν ἡ χάρις ἐξ ἁπλῆς διπλῆ φανῇ Id. Tr. 619 ; ἁπλᾶς δὲ λύπας ἐξὸν οὐκ οἴσω διπλᾶς E. IT 688 . ἁπλαῖ (sc. κρηπῖδες), αἱ, single-soled shoes, Stratt. 24 , D. 54.34 . simple, plain, straightforward, κελεύθοις ἁπλόαις ζωᾶς Pi. N. 8.36 ; ἁ. ὁ μῦθος A. Ch. 554 ; ἁ. λόγῳ Id. Pr. 610 ,al.; ὡς ἁ. λόγῳ ib. 46 , Ar. Ach. 1151 ; ἁ. λόγος the matter is simple, E. Hel. 979 ; ἁ. διήγησις simple narrative (without dialogue), Pl. R. 392d ; οὐκ ἐς ἁπλοῦν φέρει leads to no simple issue, S. OT 519 ; ἁπλᾶ γε καὶ σαφῆ λέγω μαθεῖν Alex. 240.7 ; οὐδὲν ἔχω ἁπλούστερον λέγειν X. Cyr. 3.1.32 ; of single-membered periods, Demetr. Eloc. 17 , etc.; of habits, ἁπλούστατος βίος Plb. 9.10.5 ; νόμοι λίαν ἁ. καὶ βαρβαρικοί Arist. Pol. 1268b39 ; ἁπλοῦν ἦν . . ἀποθανεῖν a plain course, Men. 14 . of persons, or their words, thoughts, and acts, simple, open, frank, ἁπλᾶ γάρ ἐστι τῆς ἀληθείας ἔπη A. Fr. 176 ; ἁ. καὶ γενναῖος Pl. R. 361b , etc.; ἁ. τρόποι E. IA 927 ; opp. δόλος, Ar. Pl. 1158 ; πρὸς τοὺς φίλους ὡς ἁπλούστατον εἶναι X. Mem. 4.2.16 . simple-minded, ὁ κριτὴς ὑπόκειται εἶναι ἁ. Arist. Rh. 1357a12 , cf. HA 608b4 ( Comp. ), Rh. 1367a37 ; in bad sense, simple, silly, Isoc. 2.46 ; λίαν γὰρ ἁπλοῦν τὸ νομίζειν . . Arist. Mete. 339b34 . simple, opp. compound or mixed, Pl. R. 547e , etc.; opp. μεμιγμένος, κεκραμένος, Arist. Metaph. 989b17 , Sens. 447a18 ; ἁ. χρώματα Id. Col. 791a1 ; ἁ. ὀνόματα, opp. διπλᾶ, Id. Po. 1457a31 ; also of nouns, without the article, A.D. Synt. 98.17 , al.; of the positive adjective, Plu. 2.412e , etc. ἁ. βιβλία rolls containing a single author, Id. Ant. 58 . of precious metals, unalloyed, pure, SIG 901.9 (Delph., iv A. D.), PCair. 67041 . ἁ. ἐπίδεσμος, a kind of bandage, Hp. Off. 7 , etc. absolute, sheer, ἀκρασία Arist. EN 1149a2 ; συμφορά Lys. 24.8 , etc. simple, unqualified (cf. ἁπλῶς 11.3 ), οὐ πάνυ μοι δοκεῖ . . οὕτως ἁπλοῦν εἶναι ὥστε . . Pl. Prt. 331b , cf. Smp. 206a , Tht. 188d , al. general, opp. ἀκριβής, Arist. Metaph. 1025b7 ( Comp. ), cf. 1030a16 . Adv. ἁπλῶς, v. sub voc. Comp. and Sup. ἁπλούστερος, ἁπλούστατος, v. supr.; irreg. Sup. ἁπλότατος AP 6.185 ( Zos. ). (Cf. δι-πλόος; ἁ- = sṃ; -πλόος perh. identical with πλοῦς 'voyage', cf. Serb. jedan put '(one journey, hence) once'; transition from 'once' to 'simple' as in Lett. vienkars^s 'simple' (cf. Lith. vienkart 'once').)
term_table.greek_sentence: [958] ἐν δὲ τῷ μετὰ τὸ πρόσθεν ἐπιτεθὲν ἕτερον ἐπιτιθέναι, καταντλεῖν ἔλαιον ἁπλοῦν, λιπαρὸν ἁρμόττει τῷ πεπονθότι μορίῳ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [958] And in the interval, when one applies another after the one previously applied, it is fitting to pour simple, oily oil over the affected part.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [958] In the interval of applying another [drug] after the one applied before, it is fitting to pour simple oil over the affected part, and something oily suits it.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: λιπαρ-ός, ά, όν, (λίπα) prop. oily, shiny with oil, once in Hom. , anointed, λιπαροὶ κεφαλὰς καὶ καλὰ πρόσωπα Od. 15.332 ; λ. χωρεῖν ἐκ βαλανείου Ar. Pl. 616 ; θεᾶσθαι λιπαρὸν παρὰ τῷ Διονύσῳ Id. Eq. 536 , cf. Nu. 1002 ; σοὶ δὲ μελήσει . . λιπαρῷ (Bentl. for -ρῶς) χωρεῖν ἐπὶ δεῖπνον Id. Ec. 652 ; of oil or oily objects, shiny, Simon. 148.4 , X. Mem. 2.1.31 , Pl. Ti. 60a , 84a , Arist. HA 520a27 . fatty, greasy, ἄρτος Ar. Fr. 109 ; τὰ λ. unctuous dishes, ib. 506.1 ; τὸ λ. fatty substance, Arist. PA 651a24 ; λιπαραί (sc. ἔμπλαστροι), αἱ, oily plasters, Dsc. 1.112 , Gal. 12.468 : sts. opp. τὸ πῖον (which implies resinous substance), Arist. Mete. 387b6 , cf. Col. 791b23 ; of vegetables boiled in grease, Hp. Mul. 1.66 . Adv. -ρῶς, ἕψειν boil in grease, Hp. Mul. l. c.; so λ. ἠρτυμένον Gal. 9.677 ; ἀνατρίβειν massage with a greasy or oily lubricant, Hp. Art. 9 . of the healthy look of the human body or skin, shining, sleek, in Hom. in phrase λιπαροὶ πόδες bright, smooth feet, without a wrinkle on the skin, mostly of men's feet, in the line ποσσὶ δ' ὑπὸ λιπαροῖσιν ἐδήσατο καλὰ πέδιλα Il. 2.44 , al.; of Hera, 14.186 ; of Themis, Hes. Th. 901 ; - ώτεροι ἐγένοντο Hdt. 3.23 ; λ. στῆθος Ar. Nu. 1012 ; θηρία X. Cyr. 1.4.11 ; χείλεα Luc. Am. 13 ; radiant, θυγάτηρ Χρόνου B. 7.1 ; ἄκοιτις Id. 5.169 . of condition or state of life, rich, comfortable, easy, γῆρας Od. 11.136 , 19.368 , Pi. N. 7.99 ; λ. εὐφροσύνη AP 11.63 ( Maced. ). Adv. - ρῶς, γηρασκέμεν Od. 4.210 ; πλήσαντα λ. κύκλον ἐτῶν ἑκατόν Epigr.Gr. 451 . of things, bright, brilliant, λιπαρὴ καλύπτρη Il. 22.406 ; λ. κρήδεμνα Od. 1.334 , etc.; χοροί Hes. Th. 63 ; of city walls, Od. 13.388 ; λ. δόμος B. 15.29 ; νίκα Id. 10.38 ; στέφανοι Id. 1.47 ; λιπαρὰς τελέουσι θέμιστας splendid or rich tribute, Il. 9.156 , 298 ; also, of the oily smoothness of a calm sea, λ. γαλάνα Theoc. 22.19 , cf. Call. Epigr. 6.5 ; also σέλας Theoc. 23.8 ; and of smells, λ. ὀσμή rich, savoury, Arist. de An. 421a30 , cf. Sens. 443b10 . of soil, fat, rich, fruitful, as epith. of places, Χίος, ἣ νήσων λιπαρωτάτη εἰν ἁλὶ κεῖται h.Ap. 38 ; λ. πόλις Thgn. 947 ; λ. Ὀρχομενός, Θῆβαι, Νάξος, Μαραθών, Pi. O. 14.2 , P. 2.3 , 4.88 , O. 13.110 ; λιπαραὶ Ἀθῆναι, favourite epith. with the Athenians, prob. with allusion to the Attic olive, first in Pi. I. 2.20 , Fr. 76 , cf. Ar. Ach. 639 , 640 (where he plays on the double sense of brilliant and greasy), Nu. 300 , Fr. 110 ; λ. τὸ χρῆμα τῆς πόλεως, of Nephelococcygia, Id. Av. 826 ; λ. χεύματα, of rivers, A. Supp. 1028 (lyr.); λ. ὅρμος Call. Del. 155 ; ἄντρον Orph. H. 59.4 (Hermann), etc. Adv. λιπαρῶς, v. supr. 1 , 111 .

term_table.lsj_entry_text: αὐτό-ματος, η, ον, Hom. and Att. ; ος, ον Hes. Op. 103 , Arist. GA 762a9 , Philetaer. 1 D. , Hp. EP 19 in Hermes 53.65 . of persons, acting of one's own will, of oneself, αὐ. δέ οἱ ἦλθε Il. 2.408 ; αὐ. φοιτῶσι Νοῦσοι Hes. Op. 103 ; αὐ. ἥκω Ar. Pl. 1190 , cf. Th. 6.91 , D.S. 2.25 , etc. of inanimate things, self-acting, spontaneous, of the gates of Olympus, αὐτόμαται δὲ πύλαι μύκον οὐρανοῦ Il. 5.749 ; of the tripods of Hephaistos, which ran of themselves, ὄφρα οἱ αὐτόματοι . . δυσαίατ' ἀγῶνα 18.376 , cf. Pl.Com. 188 ; ὅπλα . . αὐ. φανῆναι ἔξω προκείμενα τοῦ νηοῦ Hdt. 8.37 ; τὰ αὐ. marionettes, Arist. GA 734b10 , Hero Aut. passim: generally, spontaneous, βίος Pl. Plt. 271e ; ἔπαινος Epicur. Sent.Vat. 64 . of natural agencies, ὁ ποταμὸς αὐ. ἐπελθών of itself, Hdt. 2.14 ; of plants, growing of themselves, αὐ. ἐκ τῆς γῆς γίνεται Id. 3.100 ; αὐ. φύεσθαι Id. 2.94 , Thphr. Fr. 171.11 ; κύτισος αὐ. ἔρχεται Cratin. 98.8 : metaph., αὐτόματα πάντ' ἀγαθὰ . . ποριζεται Ar. Ach. 976 , cf. Cratin. 160 ; of philosophers, αὐ. ἀναφύονται Pl. Tht. 180c . of events, happening of themselves, without external agency, αὐ. δεσμὰ διελύθη E. Ba. 447 ; αὐ. θάνατος natural death, D. 18.205 ; κόποι αὐ. not to be accounted for externally, Hp. Aph. 2.5 ; ἀπό τινος αἰτίας αὐτομάτης Pl. Sph. 265c ; without visible cause, accidental, opp. ἀπὸ πείρης, Hdt. 7.9 .γ ́. αὐτόματον, τό, accident, τὸ αὐ. αἰτιᾶσθαι Lys. 6.25 ; σε ταὐ. ἀποσέσωκε Men. Epit. 568 ; διὰ τὸ αὐ. Arist. Ph. 195b33 ; τὸ αὐ. ἀγαπῶντες Id. Ath. 8.5 ; τῷ αὐ., opp. τέχνῃ, Id. Metaph. 1070a7 : most freq. in the form ἀπὸ τοῦ αὐτομάτου or ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου, ἀποθανέειν ἀπὸ τοῦ αὐ. Hdt. 2.66 , cf. Th. 2.77 , Pl. Ap. 38c , al., Arist. Po. 1452a5 , al., Men. Pk. 31 ; ἐκ τοῦ αὐ. X. term_table.english_sentence_A: Of the drugs called adhesive (echekolla), none should be removed before it comes away of its own accord; rather, even if one bathes, it should be allowed to remain in place.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Of the drugs called echekolla ('adhesive'), none should be removed before it comes away of its own accord; rather, even if the patient bathes, one should let it stay in place.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
term_table.greek_sentence: [Αἱ τῶν μαλακτικῶν φαρμάκων κατ’ εἴδη διαφοραὶ καὶ δυνάμεις.] Ἐπεὶ δὲ οὐ πάντες εἰσὶ τοιοῦτοι καὶ πρόκειται κατὰ τήνδε τὴν πραγματείαν, οὐχ ὥσπερ ἐν τῇ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου, μόνην εἰπεῖν τὴν μέθοδον, ἀλλ’ ἅμα παραδείγματι τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἑνί τε καὶ δευτέρῳ, προστεθῆναι δεῖ καὶ τὰ πείρᾳ προκείμενα φάρμακα, ἃ πρόσκειται τοῖς πρὸ ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ φαρμακευτικῷ μέρει τῆς τέχνης ἐνδόξοις, ἐπὶ τὰς κατ’ εἴδη διαφορὰς ἐπὶ τῶν μαλακτικῶν φαρμάκων ἀφίξομαι τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀπὸ τῶν μαλακωτάτων ποιησάμενος [959] αὐτοῖς, ἃ καὶ τὰς μικρὰς ἰᾶται φλεγμονάς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [The differences and powers of emollient drugs according to kinds.] But since not all are such men, and since it is proposed in this treatise not, as in that of the Therapeutic Method, to state the method alone, but together with one or two examples of the particular cases, there must also be added the drugs that are established by experience, which are set down by those before us who are esteemed in the pharmaceutical part of the art;
term_table.english_sentence_B: [The differences by species, and the potencies, of emollient drugs.] But since not all are of this kind, and since what is proposed in this treatise is not, as in the Therapeutic Method, to state the method alone, but to state it together with an example of the particulars, one or a second, and the drugs established by experience must also be added, those set down by the men before us who were renowned in the pharmaceutical part of the art, I shall come to the differences by species among the emollient drugs, making my beginning from the mildest of them, which also cure small inflammations.

term_table.english_sentence_A: I shall therefore proceed to the differences according to kinds among the emollient drugs, making my beginning from the softest [959] of them, which cure even small inflammations.
term_table.english_sentence_B: One should use, as has been said before, for slight indurations and for soft bodies those of the first order; for bodies and affections stronger than these, those of the second; and likewise those of the third and of the fourth in proportion.

term_table.greek_sentence: χρῆσθαι δὲ προσῆκεν, ὡς προείρηται, πρὸς μὲν τὰς βραχείας σκληρότητας καὶ τὰ μαλακὰ σώματα τοῖς τῆς πρώτης τάξεως.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὡς ἐν τοῖς ἁπλοῖς φαρμάκοις, ἐποιήσαμεν τέσσαρας τάξεις τῶν ὁμογενῶν, τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον ἐν αὐτοῖς ὁριζούσας, ἐνίων δ’ ἔφην ἀμφίβολον εἶναι τὴν δύναμιν, εἴτ’ ἐπὶ τελευτῇ τῆς πρώτης τάξεως εἴτ’ ἐν ἀρχῇ τῆς δευτέρας, θετέον ἐστὶ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτῶν, ὡσαύτως καὶ περὶ τῆς δευτέρας τε καὶ τρίτης τῶν τε ταύταις ἐφεξῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: As in the case of the simple drugs, we made four orders of those of the same kind, defining the more and the less among them, and of some I said that the power is ambiguous, whether their power is to be placed at the end of the first order or at the beginning of the second, and likewise concerning the second and the third and those following upon these.
term_table.english_sentence_B: As in the case of the simple drugs, we made four orders of things of the same kind, defining the more and the less among them.

Onom. 139 ; τὰς ὑ. αὐτῶν (sc. τῶν μαστῶν) Sor. 1.55 : abs., an eminence, Plb. 3.104.3 . rising of a star, ἀνατολὴν εἶναι . . ὑ. ἄστρου ὑπὲρ γῆς Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.200 ; raising, τῆς ἑαυτῶν κεφαλῆς Plot. 5.8.3 . metaph., pre-eminence, superiority, ὑπεροχῆς ἐπιθυμεῖ ἡ νεότης, ἡ δὲ νίκη ὑ. τις Arist. Rh. 1389a13 ; ἡ ἰσχὺς καὶ ἡ ὑ. Id. Pol. 1297b18 ; τὴν ὑ. ἀπονέμειν τοῖς ἀρίστοις ib. 1293b41 ; τὴν ὑ. τῆς πολιτείας λαμβάνειν superiority in the government, ib. 1296a31 ; διὰ τὴν ὑ. τοῦ πλήθους because of superiority in multitude, ib. 1293a4 ; ἡ ἐν τῷ ἐπιτηδεύματι ὑ. IG 22.3800 : pl., πρὸς τὰς ὑ. οὕτω διακεῖσθαι Isoc. 12.16 ; διαφέρεσθαι ἐν τῷ ποσῷ καὶ ταις ὑ. Arist. Pol. 1323a35 . like ὑπερβολή , excess, opp. ἔλλειψις (defect), in many senses, as in Arithm., one of the ἀριθμοῦ ᾗ ἀριθμὸς πάθη, Id. Metaph. 1004b12 , cf. Archim. Archyt. 2 , Porph. in Harm. p.266 W.; excess, of a sum of money, SIG 976.66 (Samos, ii B.C.); in Physics, Arist. Ph. 187a16 , 189b10 , HA 486b8 , al.; διαφέρειν καθ' ὑπεροχήν Id. term_table.greek_sentence: ἅτε γὰρ καὶ τῶν σωμάτων τῆς διαφορᾶς, οἷς προσάγεται τὰ φάρμακα καὶ τῶν παθῶν αὐτῶν οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐχόντων ἐν τῷ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον τὴν ὑπεροχὴν, χαλεπώτατόν ἐστιν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἀπόφασιν ποιήσασθαι μίαν, ἐξ ἐπιμέτρου δὲ καὶ αὐτῶν τῶν φαρμάκων τῶν ἁπλῶν οὐ μικρὰν ἐχόντων διαφοράν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For since the difference of the bodies to which the drugs are applied, and of the affections themselves, has no small excess in the more and the less, it is most difficult to make a single pronouncement upon all of them, and in addition the simple drugs themselves have no small difference.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For since the bodies to which the drugs are applied, and the affections themselves, show no small excess in the more and the less, it is most difficult to make a single pronouncement for all cases; and, in addition, the simple drugs themselves have no small difference among themselves.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐμοῦ δὲ ἐπὶ τῶν ἀρίστων καθ’ ἕκαστον εἶδός τε καὶ γένος ἀποφηναμένου τὴν δύναμιν, ἐὰν ἐπὶ τοῦ χειρίστου ποιήσηταί τις τήνδε διὰ τῆς πείρας ἐξέτασιν, ποιήσεται μὲν ψευδῶς, οὐ διώρικε δὲ τὰς τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτῶν τάξεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And since I have pronounced on the power in the case of the best of each species and kind, if someone makes this examination by experience on the worst, he will make it falsely, and he has not defined the ranks of their power.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And since I pronounced on the power in the case of the best of each species and genus, if someone makes this examination through experience on the worst, he will make it falsely, and he has not determined the orders of their power.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
term_table.greek_sentence: [Διαφόρους γίγνεσθαι διαφορὰς ἐν τῷ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον κατὰ τὴν μαλακτικὴν τοῦ Μνασαίου ἔμπλαστρον κατὰ διάφορον τῶν ἁπλῶν ποσότητά τε καὶ ἡλικίαν καὶ ἕψησιν.] Κατὰ γάρ τοι τὴν δευτέραν τάξιν τῶν μαλακτικῶν οὐχ ἥκιστα ἄν τις θείη τὴν ὑπὸ τοῦ Μνασαίου συντεθεῖσαν ἔμπλαστρον, ὁμολογούντων μὲν ἁπάντων ἀλλήλοις τῶν μνημονευσάντων αὐτῆς, ἐξ ἐλαίου τοῦ παλαιοῦ καὶ λιθαργύρου καὶ στέατος ὑείου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [That different differences in respect of more and less arise in the emollient plaster of Mnaseas according to the differing quantity, age and boiling of the simples.] For indeed in the second rank of the emollients one would not least place the plaster composed by Mnaseas, since all who have mentioned it agree with one another that it is made from old oil, litharge and pig's fat, but differ both in the quantity of each of these and in that some compose it from fresh fat, others from old fat, which is now customarily called by everyone axoungion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [That various differences in respect of the more and the less arise in the emollient plaster of Mnasaeus, according to the differing quantity, age and boiling of the simple ingredients.] For in the second order of emollients one might quite justifiably place the plaster composed by Mnasaeus. All who have recorded it agree with one another that it is made of old oil, litharge and pig's fat.

term_table.english_sentence_A: For on these grounds the weakest would be that made from litharge, pig's fat and oil, neither of the latter being old; the stronger, when of these the oil is old but the other is put in new; and the one stronger than this, when both are old.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ δ’ ἰσχυροτέρα ἐλαίου μὲν αὐτῶν παλαιοῦ, θατέρου δὲ νέου βληθέντος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For on these grounds the weakest would be that made from litharge, pig's fat and oil, neither of the latter being old; the stronger, when of these the oil is old but the other is put in new; and the one stronger than this, when both are old.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The stronger is the one in which the oil is old and the other ingredient, the fat, is put in new.

term_table.greek_sentence: [963] ἔσονται ποτὲ μὲν ἀμφοῖν νέων, ποτὲ δὲ ἀμφοῖν παλαιῶν, ποτὲ δὲ τοῦ μὲν ἐλαίου παλαιοῦ, τοῦ στέατος δὲ προσφάτου ἢ τοὐναντίον, ἐλαίου μὲν προσφάτου, παλαιοῦ δὲ στέατος ἐμβαλλομένου.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σταθμός, ὁ, in Trag., etc., with heterocl. pl. σταθμά, S. Ph. 489 , OT 1139 , E. HF 999 , X. Eq. 4.3 , etc.; σταθμοί however occurs not only in Hom. (v. infr.), but in E. Andr. 280 , Or. 1474 (both lyr.):— standing-place for animals, farmstead, steading, τὼ μὲν (the lions) ἄρ', ἁρπάζοντε βόας καὶ ἴφια μῆλα, σταθμοὺς ἀνθρώπων κεραΐζετον Il. 5.557 , cf. 12.304 ; κατὰ σταθμοὺς δύεται 5.140 ; κατὰ ς. ποιμνήϊον 2.470 ; σταθμῷ ἐν οἰοπόλῳ 19.377 , cf. Hes. Th. 294 ; sts. including the human dwelling, Od. 14.504 ; of a swineherd's steading, ib. 32 ; of a sheepstation, Il. 5.140 , 18.589 , cf. E. Rh. 293 ; of the stable of the griffin of Oceanus, A. Pr. 398 ; of a deer's lair, Arist. HA 578b21 , 611a20 . of men, dwelling, abode, Pi. O. 5.10 (pl.), P. 4.76 (pl.); Ἀΐδα Id. O. 10 ( 11 ). 92 ; οὐρανοῦ Id. I. 7(6).45 ; Εὐβοίας σταθμά S. Ph. 489 , cf. PCair.Zen. 344.2 (iii B.C.), BGU 1185.13 (i B.C.), etc. quarters, lodgings for travellers or soldiers, Hdt. 7.119 , X. An. 1.8.1 , al., SIG 880.15 (Pizus, iii A.D.), etc.; soldier's billet, PStrassb. 92.4 (iii B.C.), etc. quarter of a town, PRyl. 102.8 (ii A.D.). in Persia, of stations or stages on the royal road, where the king rested in travelling, ς. βασιλήϊοι Hdt. 5.52 , cf. 6.119 , Plu. Art. 25 : hence in reference to Persia, of distances, a day's march (about 5 parasangs or 150 stades), X. An. 1.2.10 ; posting-station in the desert, ς. καὶ φρούρια OGI 701.13 (Egypt, ii A.D., pl.). station for ships, E. Rh. 43 (lyr.), Lyc. 290 . upright standing-post, freq. in Hom. ; sts. of the bearing pillar of the roof, παρὰ σταθμὸν τέγεος Od. 1.333 , 8.458 , 18.209 ; παρὰ ς. μεγάροιο 17.96 , cf. 22.120 , 257 : in pl., E. IT 49 ; also doorpost, Od. 4.838 , 17.340 : pl., ἀργύρεοι ς. ἐν χαλκέῳ ἕστασαν οὐδῷ 7.89 , cf. 10.62 , Il. 14.167 , Hdt. 1.179 , S. El. 1331 , E. Or. 1474 (lyr.): later, pl. σταθμά in this sense, Id. HF 999 , Ar. Ach. 449 , IG 22.1672.70 , 173 , 42(1).103.94 (Epid., iv B.C.); ς. θυράων Theoc. 24.15 : σταθμός alone, = threshold, door, LXX 4 Ki. 12.9 , al. ( ἵστημι A. Ra. 1365 ; ἐς τὸν ς. ἐμβάς ib. 1407 ; ἕλκειν ς. weigh so much, Hdt. 1.50 , cf. Eup. 116 . weight, σίτου ς. Hdt. 2.168 ; ς. ἔχοντες τριήκοντα τάλαντα Id. 1.14 ; διαφέρειν ἐν τῷ ς. Hp. term_table.greek_sentence: ἤτοι γὰρ ἴσα τῷ σταθμῷ καὶ μέτρῳ μίγνυται τὰ τρία καὶ πολλοί φασι τὴν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Μνασαίου συντεθεῖσαν ἐκ τριῶν ἴσων συγκεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ δύο μὲν ἴσα, τὸ τρίτον δὲ οὐκ ἴσον ἀλλ’ ἔλαττον ἢ πλέον ἢ τῶν τριῶν ἀνίσων μιγνυμένων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For either the three are mixed in equal amounts by weight and measure—and many say that the one compounded by Mnaseas himself is composed of three equal parts—or two are equal and the third not equal but less or more, or the three are mixed in unequal amounts.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For either the three are mixed in equal amounts by weight and measure (and many say that the plaster composed by Mnasaeus himself consists of three equal parts), or two are equal and the third not equal but less or more, or the three are mixed unequal.

term_table.english_sentence_A: It is quite evident, then, that many differences will arise.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is quite clear, then, that many differences will arise.

term_table.greek_sentence: πλέονος μὲν γὰρ τῆς λιθαργύρου βληθείσης μαλακώτερον τῇ δυνάμει γενήσεται τὸ φάρμακον, ἐλάττονος δὲ ἰσχυρότερον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For when more litharge is put in, the drug will become milder in its power, and when less, stronger.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For when more of the litharge is put in, the drug will become softer in its power, and when less, stronger.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And it will be more emollient if we put in more of the fat, but more discutient if more of the oil.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It will also be more emollient if we put in more of the fat, and more discutient if more of the oil.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ μαλακτικώτερον μὲν, εἰ τοῦ στέατος ἐμβάλλοιμεν πλέον, διαφορητικώτερον δ’ εἰ τοῦ ἐλαίου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And it will be more emollient if we put in more of the fat, but more discutient if more of the oil.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It will also be more emollient if we put in more of the fat, and more discutient if more of the oil.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ξηρ-αντικός, ή, όν, causing to dry up, c.gen., πνεύμονος Hp. Acut. 16 , 22 : abs., ξ. [χυλόσ] Thphr. CP 6.1.3 ; ξ. δίαιτα Diocl.Fr. 141 , cf. Arist. Pr. 925a34 ( Comp. ) ; ξ. δύναμις Dsc. 1.13 . Adv. -κῶς by drying. Herod.Med. ap. Orib. 5.28.23 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐὰν γοῦν μόνην τὴν λιθάργυρον ἑψήσεις ἐν ἐλαίῳ πλέονι, ξηραντικώτερον ἔσται τὸ φάρμακον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, if you boil the litharge alone in a greater quantity of oil, the drug will be more drying.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At any rate, if you boil the litharge alone in a larger quantity of oil, the drug will be more drying.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν [964] πλέονι δὲ ἑψήσεις πλέον ἐλαίου βαλὼν, εἴ γε μέλλοι σύστασιν ἕξειν ἐμπλάστρου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: and [964] you will boil it for longer when you have put in more oil, if indeed it is going to have the consistency of a plaster.
term_table.english_sentence_B: [964] And you will boil it for a longer time if you have put in more oil, that is, if it is to have the consistency of a plaster.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὡς εἴ γε τούτου μὴ φροντίζοι τις, ἀλλὰ ἴσῳ χρόνῳ τό θ’ ἧσσον ἔχον ἐλαίου κατὰ τὸ πλέον ἑψήσει, πρόδηλον ὅτι μαλακτικώτερον ἔσται κατὰ τὴν δύναμιν, ᾧ πλέον ἔλαιον μέμικται, καθάπερ εἰ καὶ ὠμήν τις ἄκοπον τὴν λιθάργυρον ἐλαίῳ μίξας βούλοιτο χρῆσθαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if someone were not to attend to this, but were to boil for an equal time both that which has less oil and that which has more (κατὰ τὸ πλέον), it is obvious that the one with which more oil has been mixed will be more emollient in its power, just as if someone, having mixed raw litharge with oil, should wish to use it as an akopon.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So if someone pays no attention to this, but boils the preparation having less oil and the one having more for an equal time, it is evident that the one in which more oil has been mixed will be more emollient in its power, just as if someone should wish to use the litharge raw and unground, mixed with oil.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἔνιοι, αι, α, some; never in Ep. , Lyr., or Att. Poets before Men. , exc. Ar. Pl. 867 (cf. however ἐνίοτε); first used in Ion. Prose, as Hdt. 1.120 , 8.56 , Hp. Praec. 6 ; πολλοὶ μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Lys. 25.19 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Pl. Tht. 151a , X. Mem. 4.2.38 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . οἱ δὲ . . Pl. Mx. 238e ; ἔνιοί τινες Isoc. 15.258 : later in sg., οὐ πᾶσα κίνησις θερμαίνει, ἀλλ' ἐνία ψύχει Arist. Pr. 884b13 , cf. Thphr. Vert. 1 ; περὶ ψυχῆς ἐνίας θεωρῆσαι Arist. Metaph. 1026a5 : neut. pl. as Adv., συμμανῆναι ἔνια δεῖ Men. 421 ; ἔστι καὶ ταὐτόματον ἔνια χρήσιμον Id. 486 .
term_table.greek_sentence: διό περ ὃ πολλάκις ἤδη μοι λέλεκται, μεμνῆσθαι διὰ παντὸς αὐτοῦ κελεύω, μὴ καθάπερ ἔνιοι τὰς ἀποφάσεις ἁπλῶς ὑπὲρ τῶν φαρμάκων ποιοῦνται καὶ ἡμᾶς οὕτω πράττειν, βελτίονα λέγοντας ἁπλῶς εἶναι τήνδε τὴν σύνθεσιν τοῦ φαρμάκου τῆσδε.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Wherefore I bid you always keep in mind what has already often been said by me: that we should not, as some make their pronouncements about drugs without qualification, act in the same way ourselves, saying without qualification that this composition of a drug is better than that one.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For this reason I bid you always remember what I have often said already: that we should not, as some make their pronouncements about drugs without qualification, act in this way ourselves, saying without qualification that this composition of the drug is better than that one.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀγαθός [αγ], ή, όν, Lacon. ἀγασός Ar. Lys. 1301 , Cypr. ἀζαθός GDI 57 :— good: of persons, well-born, gentle, opp. κακός, δειλός, οἷά τε τοῖς ἀγαθοῖσι παραδρώωσι χέρηες Od. 15.324 , cf. Il. 1.275 ; ἀφνειός τ' ἀ. τε Il. 13.664 , cf. Od. 18.276 ; πατρὸς δ' εἴμ' ἀγαθοῖο, θεὰ δέ με γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 21.109 , cf. Od. 4.611 ; κακὸς ἐξ ἀ. Thgn. 190 , cf. 57 sq.; πραῢς ἀστοῖς, οὐ φθονέων ἀγαθοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 , cf. 2.96 , 4.285 ; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστοι; οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀ. κτλ. S. El. 1082 ; οἵ τ' ἀ. πρὸς τῶν ἀγενῶν κατανικῶνται Id. Fr. 84 ; τοὺς εὐγενεῖς γὰρ κἀγαθοὺς . . φιλεῖ Ἄρης ἐναίρειν ib. 649 , cf. E. Alc. 600 , al.: ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν Pl. Phdr. 274a :—in political sense, aristocrats, esp. in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (v. sub καλοκἀγαθός). brave, valiant, since courage was attributed to Chiefs and Nobles, Il. 1.131 , al.; τῷ κ' ἀγαθὸς μὲν ἔπεφν', ἀγαθὸν δέ κεν ἐξενάριξεν 21.280 ; cf. Hdt. 5.109 , etc. good, capable, in reference to ability, ἀ. βασιλεύς Il. 3.179 ; ἰητήρ 2.732 ; θεράπων 16.165 , 17.388 ; πύκτης Xenoph. 2.15 ; ἰητρός Hp. Prog. 1 ; προβατογνώμων A. Ag. 795 ; ἄρχοντες Democr. 266 : freq. with qualifying words, ἀ. ἐν ὑσμίνῃ Il. 13.314 ; βοὴν ἀ. 2.408 , 563 , al.; πύξ Od. 11.300 ; βίην Il. 6.478 ; γνώμην S. OT 687 ; πᾶσαν ἀρετήν Pl. Lg. 899b , cf. Alc. 1.124e ; τέχνην Id. Prt. 323b ; τὰ πολέμια, τὰ πολιτικά, Hdt. 9.122 , Pl. Grg. 516b , etc.: more rarely c. dat., ἀ. πολέμῳ X. Oec. 4.15 : with Preps., ἄνδρες ἀ. περὶ τὸ πλῆθος Lys. 13.2 ; εἴς τι Pl. Alc. 1.125a ; πρός τι Id. R. 407e : c. inf., ἀ. μάχεσθαι Hdt. 1.136 ; ἱππεύεσθαι 1.79 ; ἀ. ἱστάναι good at weighing, Pl. Prt. 356b . good, in moral sense, first in Thgn. 438 , cf. Heraclit. 104 , S. El. 1082 , X. Mem. 1.7.1 , Pl. Ap. 41d , etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος Democr. 247 : freq. with other Adjs., ὁ πιστὸς κἀ. S. Tr. 541 ; δικαίων κἀ. ib. 1050 :—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα Id. Ant. 31 . ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, Pl. Prt. 311a , etc. ἀ. δαίμων, v. sub δαίμων; ἀ. τύχη, v. sub τύχη; ἀ. θεός = Lat. bona dea, Plu. Caes. 9 , Cic. 19 . of things, good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη . . ἀ. κουροτρόφος Od. 9.27 , etc.; ἀ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει X. Cyn. 13.17 : c. gen., εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀ. good for it, Id. Mem. 3.8.3 ; ἑλκῶν Thphr. HP 9.11.1 . of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347 ; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, Il. 9.102 ; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, 11.789 ; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204 :—ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so<*> Il. 7.282 , 24.130 , Od. 3.196 , etc. morally good, πρῆξις Democr. 177 ; ἔργα Emp. 112.2 , cf. Ep.Rom. 2.7 , etc. ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις X. Cyr. 5.3.20 ; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι Id. Mem. 2.4.2 , cf. Ar. Ra. 74 , etc; as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, Men. Sam. 28 :— ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on . . , Th. 3.68 , Lys. 13.92 ; ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, Th. 5.27 , X. Cyr. 7.4.3 ; ἐπ' ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις Ar. Ra. 1487 ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀ. for no good end, Th. 1.131 ; ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος X. HG 5.2.35 :—in pl., ἡ ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά PFlor. 21.10 (iii A.D.):—τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, Epich. 171.5 , cf. Pl. R. 506b , 508e , Arist. Metaph. 1091a31 , etc.:—in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, Hdt. 2.172 , Lys. 13.91 , X. Mem. 1.2.63 , etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν fare well, Ar. Av. 1706 ; also, good things, dainties, Thgn. 1000 , Ar. Ach. 873 , etc.: good qualities, τοῖς ἀ., οἷς ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ Isoc. 8.32 , cf. Democr. 37 ; good points, of a horse, εἰ τἄλλα πάντα ἀ. ἔχοι, κακόπους δ' εἴη X. Eq. 1.2 . Comp. and Sup. are usu. supplied from other stems, viz. Comp. ἀμείνων, ἀρείων<*> βελτίων, κρείσσων ʽκάρρωνʼ, λωΐων (λώʽωνʼ), Ep. βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος:— Sup. ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος (λῷστος), Ep. βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος:— later, reg. Comp. ἀγαθώτερος LXX Jd. 11.25 , 15.2 , D.S. 8 Fr. 12 , Plot. 5.5.9 , Diod.Rh. p.53.9H. : Sup. ἀγαθώτατος D.S. 16.85 , Hld. 5.15 , etc. ( -ότατος POxy. 1757.26 (ii A.D.)). Adv. usually εὖ, q.v.: ἀγαθῶς Hp. Off. 9 , Arist. Rh. 1388b6 , LXX 1 Ki. 20.7 . (Etym. dub. ( ὅτι ἄγει ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ὀρθὸν βίον Stoic. 3.49 ); perh. cognate with ἄγαμαι, hence admirable.)

term_table.greek_sentence: ταῦτα τοίνυν ἅπαντα τὰ νῦν εἰρημένα μοι προακούσας τις, οὐ φιλόπονος μόνον ἢ μνήμων, ἀλλὰ καὶ φύσει συνετὸς ὢν, ὠφελίμως ἀναγνώσεται τὰ μετὰ διορισμῶν γεγραμμένα τε καὶ γραφησόμενά μοι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Accordingly, anyone who has first heard all these things now said by me, being not only industrious or retentive in memory but also intelligent by nature, will read with profit what has been written and what will be written by me with distinctions.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Therefore anyone who has heard beforehand all these things I have now said, being not only diligent or retentive of memory but also naturally intelligent, will read with profit what has been written, and will be written, by me with distinctions.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ λέξω δέ σοι τοὺς διορισμοὺς ἐπὶ τῶν προκειμένων φαρμάκων ἐν προσθήκῃ τριῶν ἢ τεττάρων συλλαβῶν γινομένους, [965] ὁποίαν προσθήκην ἐπὶ τοῦ προκειμένου κατὰ τὸν ἐνεστῶτα λόγον φαρμάκου τοῦ Μνασαίου φαίνεται πεποιημένος ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And I shall also tell you the distinctions in the case of the drugs under consideration, which come about through the addition of three or four syllables, [965] an addition of just the kind that Andromachus appears to have made in the case of the drug of Mnaseas that is under consideration in the present discussion.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And I shall tell you that the distinctions in the case of the drugs before us come about by the addition of three or four syllables, [965] the kind of addition which Andromachus appears to have made in the case of the drug of Mnasaeus that is before us in the present account.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν γὰρ τῷ καταλόγῳ τῶν μηλίνων ἐμπλάστρων ἑνδεκάτην τῇ τάξει γράψας αὐτὴν οὐχ ἁπλῶς εἰπεῖν ἠρκέσθη, καθάπερ ἐπὶ τῶν ἔμπροσθεν εἰρημένων, ἄλλῃ καὶ ἄλλῃ προγράφων αὐτῶν, ἀλλὰ προσέθηκε τὸ ἁπαλή.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in his catalogue of the quince-yellow plasters, having written it eleventh in order, he was not content to state it simply, as with those mentioned before it, where he heads each of them with 'another' and 'another', but he added the word 'soft' (ἁπαλή).

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ αὖ πάλιν, εἴ τινα ἴσην ᾤετο δύναμιν ἔχειν, αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσγράψαι, ἢ εἴπερ εὐλαβοῖτο κινδυνεύειν ἔν γε ταῖς τοιαύταις ἀποφάσεσιν, ἀλλὰ τά γε ἁπλᾶ μαλακτικὰ φάρμακα προδιδάξαι, τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον ἐν αὐτοῖς διορισάμενον, ὅπως ὁ ἀναγινώσκων ἐφεξῆς τὰς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένας μαλακτικὰς ἐμπλάστρους πολλὰς, ἰσχυροτέραν μὲν εἶναι γνωρίζῃ τὴν διὰ στύρακος, ἀμμωνιακοῦ τε καὶ βδελλίου καὶ προπόλεως καὶ χαλβάνης, στέατός τε [966] ταυρείου καὶ τραγείου καὶ τῶν μυελῶν συγκειμένην, ἀσθενῆ δὲ τὴν μηδὲν τούτων ἔχουσαν, ἀλλ’ ἤτοι πάντα ἀσθενῆ κατὰ τὴν δύναμιν, ἢ τούτων μὲν αὐτῶν ἰσχυρότερα, μέσα δὲ ταῖς κράσεσί τε καὶ δυνάμεσιν ἢ μετὰ τοῦ μεμίχθαι τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν ἕν τι τῶν ἰσχυρῶν ἢ δύο.
term_table.english_sentence_A: just as, again, if he thought that some had an equal power, he should have added this very thing; or, if he were wary of running a risk in such pronouncements, he should at least have taught beforehand the simple emollient drugs, distinguishing the more and the less among them, so that the reader of the many emollient plasters written by him in sequence might recognise that the one composed of storax, ammoniac, bdellium, propolis and galbanum, of bull's [966] and goat's fat and of the marrows is stronger, while the one that has none of these is weak—but either all its ingredients are weak in power, or they are stronger than these themselves yet intermediate in their mixtures and powers, or one or two of the strong ones have been mixed in with the weak ones.
term_table.english_sentence_B: just as, again, if he thought that some had equal potency, he should have added this very fact in writing; or, if he was wary of running a risk in such pronouncements, he should at least have taught beforehand the simple emollient drugs, distinguishing the more and the less among them, so that one reading in sequence the many emollient plasters he wrote might recognise as stronger the one compounded of storax, ammoniac, bdellium, propolis and galbanum, and of [966] bull's and goat's suet and the marrows, and as weak the one containing none of these, but either ingredients all weak in potency, or ingredients stronger than these themselves but intermediate in their temperaments and potencies, or with one or two of the strong ingredients mixed in with the weak ones.

term_table.greek_sentence: δῆλον γὰρ ὅτι τὸ μεταξὺ πλάτος ἐν ἅπασι τοῖς φαρμάκοις οὐκ ὀλίγον ἐστὶ κατὰ τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον, ἐπὶ κοινῇ δυνάμει πάντων αὐτῶν γενικῶς νοουμένῃ, καθ’ ἣν ὁμογενῆ τε καὶ ὁμοειδῆ τὰ φάρμακα λέγεται, καθάπερ γε ἕτερα διαφέροντα γενικαῖς ἢ εἰδικαῖς διαφοραῖς.

Pl. Ti. 84d , cf. 70c , Arist. Resp. 476a9 , LXX 3 Ki. 22.34 : mostly in pl., Archil. 9.5 , Alc. 39.1 , A. Th. 61 , S. Tr. 567 , etc.; διὰ πνευμόνων θερμὸν ἄησιν ὕπνον A. Lys. 367 , Ra. 474 ; πλευμόνων πολὺς πόνος ib. 829 ; as the seat of love, [ Κύπρισ] Διὸς τυραννεῖ πλευμόνων S. Fr. 941.15 . sea-lungs, jelly-fish, Pl. Phlb. 21c , Arist. PA 681a18 , Thphr. Sign. 40 , Pytheas ap. Plb. 34.3.4 ; term of abuse applied by Epicurus to Nausiphanes, Epicur. Frr. 114 , 236 . (Gramm. differ as to the forms. Eust. ( 483.10 , 1436.62 ) and Phot. both recognize πλεύμων as the Homeric and ancient form; this was also the true Att. form, Moer. p.309 P., Sch. Ar. Pax 1069 , Eust. 483.10 ; it is found in the best codd. of A. Th. 61 , S. Tr. 567 , as well as in codd. of Alc. (l.c. ap. Ath. 10.430b ), Hp. ( Art. 41 , Prog. 23 , al., cf. i p.cxx K.), Ar. , Pl. , and Arist. , also in Pap., Phld. Ir. pp.27,28 W., and Inscr., IG 42(1).122.56 (Epid., iv B. C.), and is doubtless the original form, which was altered in accordance with a supposed deriv. from πνεῦμα suggested by Arist. Resp. 476a9 , cf. EM 677.31 . Cf. Lith. plaũčiai 'lungs', cogn. with πλέω, as 'that which floats', cf. Engl. lights, also lungs, cogn. with ἐλαφρός.)

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μέτρον, τό, that by which anything is measured: measure, rule, μέτρ' ἐν χερσὶν ἔχοντες Il. 12.422 ; ἐν μέτροισι ταμὼν δόνακας h.Merc. 47 ; πάντ' ἄνδρα πάντων χρημάτων μ. εἶναι is a measure of all things, Pl. Tht. 183c , cf. Protag. ap. Arist. Metaph. 1053a36 ; μ. αὐτῷ οὐχ ἡ ψυχή, ἀλλ' ὁ νόμος X. Cyr. 1.3.18 . Math., measure, divisor, Eratosth. ap. Nicom. Ar. 1.13 , etc. measure of content, whether solid or liquid, δῶκεν μέθυ, χίλια μ. Il. 7.471 ; εἴκοσι δ' ἔστω μ. . . ἀλφίτου Od. 2.355 ; ὕδατος ἀνὰ εἴκοσι μ. χεῦε 9.209 , cf. Il. 23.268 , 741 , Hes. Op. 350 , 600 , etc.; at Samos, of the μέδιμνος, SIG 976.55 (ii B.C.); in Egypt, of the ἀρτάβη, μ. δοχικόν PTeb. 11.6 (ii B.C.); also of smaller units, as μ. ἑξαχοίνικον ib. 105.40 (ii B.C.); μέτροις καὶ σταθμοῖς by measure and weight, Decr. ap. And. 1.83 ; in the widest sense, either weight or measure, Φείδωνος τοῦ τὰ μ. ποιήσαντος Πελοποννησίοισι Hdt. 6.127 ; μ. οἰνηρά, σιτηρά, Arist. EN 1135a2 ; Κιλικίῳ μ. μετρεῖν OGI 579.2 (Cilicia). any space measured or measurable, length, size, in pl., dimensions, μέτρα κελεύθου the length of the way, Od. 4.389 ; μέτρα θαλάσσης Hes. Op. 648 , Orac. ap. Hdt. 1.47 ; μορφῆς μέτρα bodily dimensions, E. Alc. 1063 ; τὰ μ. τοῦ λίθου its distances from a given point in given directions, its position, Hdt. 2.121 .ά, cf. Pl. Lg. 843e , Plu. Sol. 23 ; ἄστρων μέτρα S. Fr. 432.8 ; ἀπέχει . . θαλάσσης μέτρον ἑξήκοντα σταδίους Th. 8.95 ; τῷ Ἴστρῳ ἐκ τῶν ἴσων μ. ὁρμᾶται [ὁ Νεῖλος] starts from the same distances as (i.e. the position corresponding to the source of) the Ister , Hdt. 2.33 ; εἰδέναι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ χώραν μέτρῳ καὶ τόπῳ X. Cyr. 8.5.3 ; ἐντὸς τῶν μ. τετμημένον μέταλλον Hyp. Eux. 35 ; later of Time, duration, μέτρα βίοιο ἄρκια APl. 4.333 ( Antiphil. ); ἐτέων μέτρα, ὡράων μέτρον, AP 7.334 , 9.481 ; μέτρα ἐνιαυτῶν, νυκτός, Arat. 464.731 ; χρονικὰ μ. Simp. in de An. 299.37 . limit, goal, ὅρμου μ. the goal which is the mooring-place, Od. 13.101 ; ἥβης μ. ἱκέσθαι the term which is puberty, Il. 11.225 , Hes. Op. 132 ; but, ἥβης μ. ἔχειν full measure of youthful vigour, ib. 438 , Thgn. 1119 ; σοφίης, γνωμοσύνης μ. Sol. 13.52 , 16.2 . due measure or limit, proportion, μέτρα φυλάσσεσθαι Hes. Op. 694 ; χρὴ κατ' αὐτὸν παντὸς ὁρᾶν μέτρον Pi. P. 2.34 ; μέτρα μὲν γνώμᾳ διώκων, μέτρα δὲ καὶ κατέχων Id. I. 6(5).71 ; κατὰ μέτρον Hes. Op. 720 ; πίνειν ὑπὲρ μέτρον Thgn. 498 ; προστιθεὶς μ. A. Ch. 797 (lyr.); τί μ. κακότατος ἔφυ; S. El. 236 (lyr.); μ. ἔχει have a moderating power, Pl. Lg. 836a ; πλέον πίνειν τοῦ μέτρου Id. R. 621a ; μ. ἔχειν Id. Lg. 957a ; μέτρῳ, = μετρίως, καταβαίνειν Pi. P. 8.78 ; οὐδεὶς τῷ μ. τὸ πίνειν ἔστεργε Alciphr. 3.32 . τίς ἱππείοις ἐν ἔντεσσιν μέτρα . . ἐπέθηκ' checks, i.e. bits, Pi. O. 13.20 . metre, Ar. term_table.lsj_entry_text: νέος, νέα, Ion. νέη, νέον; Ion. νεῖος (q.v.): [fem. νέας as monosyll., A. Th. 327 (lyr.); contr. fem. νῆ Xenoph. 42 (= Ar. Fr. 9 ), Eugaeon (?) 1 ]: young, youthful (of children, youths, and of men at least as old as 30 , v. X. Mem. 1.2.35 ), ν. πάϊς Od. 4.665 ; κοῦροι ν. Il. 13.95 ; ν. ἀνήρ 23.589 : alone, νέοι youths, 1.463 , Hes. Sc. 281 , etc.: later mostly with Art., οἱ νέοι Ar. Nu. 1059 , etc.: prov., ὁ ν. ἔσται ν. 'boys will be boys', Lib. Ep. 910.3 ; οἱ ν., corporately organized, SIG 831.8 (Pergam., ii A.D.), etc.; opp. ἔφηβοι, παῖδες, ib. 589.38 (Magn.Mae., ii B.C.): opp. γέρων, ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες Il. 2.789 , etc.; ἢ ν. ἠὲ παλαιός 14.108 , cf. Od. 1.395 , etc.; opp. γεραίτερος, 3.24 ; opp. προγενέστερος, 2.29 ; opp. γεραιός, X. Lac. 1.7 ; εὐθὺς ἐκ νέου ἐθίζειν from youth upwards, Pl. Grg. 510d , etc.; ἐκ νέων παίδων Id. Lg. 887d ; ἐκ νέων ἐθίζεσθαι Arist. EN 1103b24 ; ἐκ νέας (sc. ψυχῆς) Pl. R. 409a ; τὸ ν., = νεότης , youth (in the abstract), S. OC 1229 (lyr.), E. Ion 545 : also in concrete sense, τὸ ν. ἅπαν all young creatures, Pl. Lg. 653d ; οὐ δύναται τὸ ν. ἡσυχάζειν Arist. Pol. 1340b29 ; σκιρτητικὸν τὸ ν. Corn. ND 20 ; also, of minors, νέου ὄντος ἔτι Th. 1.107 ; cf. νεώτερος. rarely of animals and plants, ὄρπηκες, ἔρνος, Il. 21.38 , Od. 6.163 ; οἱ ν. τῶν νεβρῶν X. Cyn. 9.8 . suited to a youth, youthful, ἄεθλοι Pi. O. 2.43 ; ν. θράσος A. Pers. 744 (troch.); ν. φροντίς youthful spirits, E. Med. 48 ; νέαις ταῖς διανοίαις χρωμένους Lys. 24.16 ; of persons, ἄφρων νέος τε E. IA 489 , cf. Pl. R. 378a ; ν. τε καὶ ὀξύς Id. Grg. 463e (but διαφέρει οὐδὲν ν. τὴν ἡλικίαν ἢ τὸ ἦθος νεαρός Arist. EN 1095a6 ). new, fresh, ν. θάλαμος Il. 17.36 ; ν. ἄλγος 6.462 ; νέῳ . . κόλλοπι Od. 21.407 (this sense elsewh. in Hom. only in Adv. νέον, v. infr.); λίνον Alc. 15 (dub.); πόνοι . . νέοι παλαιοῖσι συμμιγεῖς κακοῖς A. Th. 740 (lyr.), etc.; οἶνος ν. Ar. Pax 916 ; ἐν τοῖς μουσικοῖς τὰ ν. [μέλη] εὐδοκιμεῖ X. Cyr. 1.6.38 ; ἡ ν. (sc. σελήνη) the new moon, esp. in phrase ἕνη καὶ νέα, v. ἕνος 2 ; but μηνὸς τῇ ν. (sc. ἡμέρᾳ) on the first day of the month, Pl. Lg. 849b ; ν. ἦμαρ A.R. 4.1479 : in this sense rarely of persons, ὁ ν. ταγὸς μακάρων A. Pr. 96 (anap.), cf. Ar. Pl. 960 ; οἱ ν. θεοί A. Eu. 721 ; cf. νεώτερος. of events, etc., new, with collat. notion of unexpected, strange, untoward, evil, τί ν.; Id. Ag. 85 (anap.); προσδοκῶ τι γὰρ ν. E. Supp. 99 ; μῶν τι βουλεύῃ ν.; S. term_table.english_sentence_A: For "to be relaxed" is said as the contrary of "to be tensed." At any rate it has been written somewhere by Hippocrates too as follows: "of hard skin, softening; of tensed skin, relaxation." If, then, one were to use the names in their proper sense, one will say that certain drugs are emollients of hardened bodies, namely those that dissolve their hardness, just as the relaxing ones are curative of tension.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At any rate, it has been written somewhere by Hippocrates as follows: 'of hard skin, softening; of tightened skin, relaxation.' If, then, one were to use the words in their proper sense, one will say that certain drugs are emollient of bodies that have become hardened, namely those that dissolve their hardness, just as certain drugs are relaxing, namely those curative of tension.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Yet the manner of the evacuation is not the same in both; rather, as has been shown in the treatise on the Therapeutic Method, in which the method of cure of all the other affections too has been stated, in the case of inflamed parts the repellent quality of the drugs is beneficial during the first periods, and the discutient quality throughout; whereas in scirrhi the discutient quality alone is beneficial, without the repellent.

term_table.english_sentence_B: Yet the mode of evacuation is not the same in both. Rather, as has been shown in the treatise on the Therapeutic Method, in which the method of cure of all the other affections has also been set out, in inflamed parts the repellent quality of drugs is beneficial in the first stages, and the discutient quality throughout.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀνίατος [ι], Ion. ἀνθωρο-ίητος, ον, incurable, Hp. Aph. 7.87 ; ἕλκος, τραῦμα, Pl. Lg. 877a , 878c : also in moral sense, πράγματα ib. 660c ; ἀ. καὶ ἀνήκεστα κακά Aeschin. 3.156 ; ἀνελευθερία ἀ. ἐστιν Arist. EN 1121b13 . of persons, incurable, incorrigible, Pl. R. 410a , Grg. 526b ; ἀ. κατὰ τὴν μοχθηρίαν Arist. EN 1165b18 , al. Adv. ἀνιάτως, ἔχειν to be incurable, Pl. Phd. 113e , D. 18.324 ; οἱ ἀ. κακοί Arist. EN 1137a29 . Act. , ἀ. μετάνοια unavailing repentance, Antipho 2.4.12 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τὰ μὲν οὖν τελέως σκιῤῥωθέντα τελέως ἐστὶν ἀνίατα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Now those parts that have become completely scirrhous are completely incurable; and one must diagnose them by the fact that no sensation at all remains in the affected parts.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now parts that have become completely scirrhous are completely incurable.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀμυδρ-ός, ά, όν, dim, faint, obscure: of impressions on the eye, ἀ. χοιράς a rock dimly seen through water, Archil. 129 ; ἀ. γράμματα scarce legible letters, Th. 6.54 ; ἀ. φέγγος, χρῶμα, Arist. Mete. 343b13 , 372a2 ; ἀ. τὰ εἴδη τῶν ἰχθύων, σκιὰς μᾶλλον ἢ ἰχθῦς εἰκάσεις (in a painting) Paus. 10.28.1 . Adv. ἀμυδσῶς, βλέπειν, ὁρᾶν, Arist. HA 537b11 , 556b19 ; ἀ. μιμεῖσθαί τι represent its form obscurely, ib. 502b9 ; ἀ. ἔχειν to be ill-defined, PA 668a3 . generally, faint, weak, σφυγμὸς ἀ. τὸν τόνον Aret. CA 2.3 , cf. SD 1.12 ; τυπαί Nic. Th. 358 ( Comp. ). of impressions on the mind, vague, ἀ. εἶδος Pl. Ti. 49a ; ἀ. πρὸς ἀλήθειαν faint in comparison with truth, Id. R. 597a ; δι' ἀμυδρῶν ὀργάνων by imperfect organs, Id. Phdr. 250b , cf. Tht. 195a ; μαντεῖα ἀμυδρότερα τοῦ τι σαφὲς σημαίνειν too obscure . . , Id. Ti. 72b ; ἀ. ἐλπίς Plu. Alc. 38 ; ἀ. λόγος [ Longin. ] Rh. p.195H. ; -ότερα σχήματα Aps. p.327 H.; συναίσθησις Dam. Pr. 81 ( Sup. ), etc. Adv. -ῶς καὶ οὐθὲν σαφῶς Arist. Metaph. 985a13 , cf. 988a23 ; faintly, of one near death, Max.Tyr. 16.2 : Comp. ἀμυδρότερον Pl. Sph. 250e , Plu. 2.1025d .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐφ’ ὧν δ’ ἐστὶ μὲν αἴσθησις, ἀλλ’ ἀμυδρὰ, θεραπεύεται ταῦτα διὰ φαρμάκων διαφορούντων μὲν δηλονότι τὸ παχυνθὲν ὑγρὸν, οὐ μὴν ἰσχυρῶς γε καὶ ἀθρόως [993] τοῦτο ποιούντων, ὡς τὰ διαφορητικὰ ποιοῦσι φάρμακα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Those, however, in which there is sensation, but faint, are treated by means of drugs which do indeed disperse the thickened humour, yet do not do this strongly and all at once, [993] as the discutient drugs do.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But those in which sensation is present, though faint, are treated by means of drugs that do, clearly, disperse the thickened fluid, yet do not do this strongly and all at once [993], as the discutient drugs do.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐπι-σπαστικός, ή, όν, drawing to oneself, drawing in, τοῦ ὑγροῦ Arist. Pr. 966a4 ; ἀτμοὶ ἐ. πρὸς ἑαυτούς Str. 15.1.38 ; αἵματος Gal. Nat. term_table.greek_sentence: καλοῦσι δὲ ἐπισπαστικά τε καὶ ἐξιπωτικὰ τὰ τοιαῦτα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Such drugs they call epispastic (drawing) and expressive (squeezing-out).
term_table.english_sentence_B: Such drugs are called drawing (epispastic) and squeezing-out (exipōtic).

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μετά-πτωσις, εως, ἡ, change, Pl. Lg. 895b , etc.; τῶν πραγμάτων Arist. MM 1207b12 ; τὸ κατὰ μετάπτωσιν ἐνόχλημα Epicur. Fr. 154 ; ὁ βίος ἀδήλους τὰς μ. ἔχει Men. Adv. 181.2 : generally, change, μ. τοῦ ο εἰς τὸ α Tryphoib. 174.4 ; ἐκ -πτώσεως A.D. Synt. 50.20 .
term_table.greek_sentence: θαυμάζειν δ’ οὐ χρὴ τὴν μετάπτωσιν εἰς σκληρότητα γιγνομένην ἐκ τῶν φλεγμαινόντων, ὅταν ἅμα τό τε ἐπιῤῥυὲν ὑγρὸν ᾖ παχύτερόν τε καὶ γλίσχρον, ἥ τε ἴασις διὰ φαρμάκων γένηται ξηραινόντων σφοδρῶς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: One should not wonder at the change into hardness that comes about from inflamed parts, when at the same time the humour that has flowed in is both thicker and viscous, and the cure is effected through drugs that dry violently.
term_table.english_sentence_B: One should not be surprised at the change into hardness that takes place from inflamed parts when, at the same time, the fluid that has flowed in is rather thick and viscous and the cure is effected by drugs that dry vehemently.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: παχύς, εῖα ( Ion. -έα Hp. Superf. 21 ), ύ, thick, stout, χειρὶ παχείῃ Il. 5.309 , etc. ; παχέος παρὰ μηροῦ 16.473 ; παχὺν αὐχένα Od. 9.372 ; π. πούς Hes. term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀρθρῖτις, ιδος , ἡ (acc. -ῖτιν Porph. Abst. 1.53 ), as if fem. of ἀρθρίτης, which does not occur:—of or in the joints, νόσος Hp. Aff. 30 ; ἡ ἀ. gout, Id. Aph. 3.16 (pl.), Aret. SD 2.12 , etc.
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ τούτῳ τῷ τρόπῳ κατά τε τὰς ἀρθρίτιδας οἱ πῶροι γίγνονται καὶ κατὰ τὰς νεφρίτιδας οἱ λίθοι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And it is in this way that in arthritic affections the tophi (poroi) come about, and in nephritic affections the stones.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And it is in this way that the chalk-stones (pōroi) form in arthritic affections and the stones in nephritic affections.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐὰν δέ ποτε τὸ φλεγμονὴν ἐργασόμενον ῥεῦμα λεπτὸν ᾖ κατὰ τὴν σύστασιν, ἥ τε ἴασις αὐτοῦ διὰ τῶν ξηραινόντων καὶ θερμαινόντων γένηται φαρμάκων, οὐδὲν ὑπολείπεται σκιῤῥῶδες.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if ever the flux that is going to produce an inflammation is thin in consistency, and its cure is effected through drying and heating drugs, nothing scirrhous is left behind.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if ever the flux that is going to produce an inflammation is thin in consistency, and its cure is effected by drying and heating drugs, nothing scirrhous is left behind.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ πολλοὺς ἐξ ἐρυσιπελάτων ἀμέτρως παθόντων ταῦτα σκιῤῥώδεις [994] ὄγκους ἔχοντας θεώμεθα διὰ τὴν ἀμαθίαν τῶν θεραπευτάντων αὐτοὺς ἰατρῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And we see many people who, from erysipelas that have suffered these things immoderately, have scirrhous [994] tumours, through the ignorance of the physicians who treated them.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And we see many who, from erysipelases that were immoderately subjected to these [i.e. strongly cooling and astringent applications], have scirrhous [994] swellings, through the ignorance of the physicians who treated them.

term_table.greek_sentence: τοῦτο δ’ ἔπραξεν ὁ Μενεκράτης, ἐπειδὴ πολλάκις οὐ μόνον ἀκόντων ἁμαρτάνεσθαι συμβαίνει κατὰ τὰς γραφὰς, ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ φθόνον ἑκόντων ἐνίων, τὸ μὲν ο γράμμα θ ποιούντων διὰ μέσης τῆς στρογγύλης γραμμῆς ἑλκυσθείσης ἑτέρας ἐγκαρσίας, τὸ δὲ ἰῶτα γράμμα προστεθείσης ἑτέρας ὁμοίως ἐγκαρσίας, ὥσπερ καὶ ἀποξυσθείσης μιᾶς γραμμῆς ἐκ τοῦ γράμμα καὶ ῥῶ τὸν χαρακτῆρα τοῦ ἰῶτα καταλείπεσθαι συμβαίνει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Menecrates did this because it often happens that errors are made in the written texts not only unintentionally, but also deliberately on the part of some out of envy, who make the letter omicron a theta by drawing another, transverse, line through the middle of the round stroke, and the letter iota, likewise, by adding another transverse line, just as also, when one stroke is scraped away from the letter gamma (γράμμα in the text) and from rho, it happens that the shape of iota is left behind.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Menecrates did this because it often happens that errors are made in the writings not only by people acting unintentionally but also by some acting deliberately out of envy: they make the letter ο into θ by drawing another, transverse line through the middle of the round line, and alter the letter iota by adding another, likewise transverse, line; just as, when one line is scraped off from the letter [gamma?] and from rho, the result is that the character of iota is left.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σύν-θεσις, εως, ἡ, putting together, composition, combination, Pl. Phd. 93a , R. 611b ; τῶν λίθων Arist. EN 1174a23 , cf. IG 42(1).103.56 (Epid., iv B.C.), 7.3073.92 (Lebad., ii B.C.); τῶν σπονδύλων Sor. 1.102 ; storage, τῶν μήλων (quinces in a ῥίσκος) Phylarch. 10 J. ; but ἐλαιῶν ς. a preserve of olives, Gp. 9.28.2 . in concrete sense, junction, ὀστῶν Arist. PA 658b19 ; συνθέσεις (λέγω τὰς γωνίας) Id. Pr. 910b14 . in various technical senses: in Grammar, composition, γραμμάτων τε συνθέσεις, i.e. syllables and words, A. Pr. 460 , cf. Arist. Metaph. 1092a26 ; ς. ἔκ τε ῥημάτων γιγνομένη καὶ ὀνομάτων, i.e. sentences, Pl. Sph. 263d , cf. Cra. 431c , Arist. Po. 1458a28 , Gal. 15.487 ; περὶ συνθέσεως ὀνομάτων, title of work by D.H. ; also, the juxtaposition of letters in a word, Arist. Rh.Al. 1434b34 ; of an author's composition, Isoc. 10.11 ; so ἡ τῶν μέτρων ς. metrical composition, Arist. Po. 1449b35 ; ἡ τῶν ἐπῶν ς. D.S. 5.74 ; ἡ τοῦ παίωνος ξ. the way the paeon is made up, Plu. 2.1143d ; the constitution of things, Hp. Virg. 1 . Math., synthesis of a problem (opp. ἀνάλυσις), Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.7 , explained in Papp. 634 ; ἡ κατὰ ς. ἀγωγή synthetic procedure, Id. 412.2 . Math., ς. λόγου transformation of a ratio known as componendo, Euc. 5 Def. 14 ; κατὰ -σιν, = componendo, Archim. Aequil. 2.9 . Math., addition, Ph. 1.11 , Plu. 2.1018c , Dioph. 1 Intr.; καθ' ἁντινοῦν -σιν however many times added, i.e. whatever number of times taken (multiplied), Archim. Spir. 1 :—also as Pythag. name for 2 , Anatol. ap. Theol.Ar. 8 . in Logic, union of noun and verb or of two objects of thought in a statement, Arist. Int. 16a12 , de An. 430a27 ; also ὁ παρὰ τὴν ς. [λόγος] the fallacy of composition, opp. διαίρεσις, Id. SE 177a33 . in Physics, composition of substances, parts of organisms, from their elementary constituents, Id. PA 646a12 , Top. 151a23 ; opp μίξις (combination), Id. GC 328a6 . in Medicine, compounding of essences and drugs, τῶν μύρων Thphr. Od. 14 , al., cf. D.S. 4.45 , Aglaïas 8 . combination of parts so as to form a whole, γενέσεις καὶ ς. Pl. R. 533b ; ἡ τῶν στρωμάτων ς. Id. Plt. 280b , cf. Arist. PA 645a35 , Metaph. 1014b37 ; in plants, Thphr. HP 5.5.2 . in concrete sense, a social or political combination, Arist. Pol. 1276b7 ; a military formation, Ael. Tact. 18.5 . agreement, treaty, Pi. P. 4.168 , Fr. 205 ; πὸς τὰς συνθέσις in accordance with the agreements, IG 5(2).343.41 , 60 (Orchom. Arc. , iv B.C.); ἐκ συνθέσεως by arrangement, D.S. 13.112 , etc.; συνθέσεις περὶ γάμων Plu. Sull. 35 . ς. λόγων making up accounts, Stud.Pal. 4.70.391 (i A.D.); so ς. alone, εἰς σύνθεσιν τῷ βασιλεῖ PTeb. 714.6 (ii B.C.). set, service (most freq. in Lat. synthesis): collection of clothes, wardrobe, Dig. 34.2.38.1 ; also, dress, gown, costume, suit, ς. τελείας λευκὰς δεκατρεῖς, γυναικείας ς. PHamb. 10.13 , 21 (ii A.D.), cf. POxy. 1153.23 (i A.D.), 496.4 (ii A.D.), PSI 10.1117.11 , 13 (ii A.D.), Mart. 2.46.4 , 5.79.2 ; synthesinam indutus, Suet. Ner. 51 . service of plate, ς. πινακίων BGU 781 i 5 (i A.D.), cf. Mart. 4.46.15 , Stat. Silv. 4.9.44 .
term_table.greek_sentence: κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν δὲ τρόπον ἐκ πολλῶν γραμμάτων τῶν μὲν προσθέσει, τῶν δὲ συνθέσει, τῶν δ’ ἀφαιρέσει, [996] συμβαίνει τὴν ἀλλοίωσιν γενέσθαι τῶν δηλούντων αὐτὰ χαρακτήρων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: In the same way, in the case of many letters, by addition in some, by combination in others, by subtraction in others, [996] it comes about that the characters signifying them undergo alteration.
term_table.english_sentence_B: In the same way, in the case of many letters, it comes about that the characters indicating them are altered, by addition in some cases, by combination in others, and by removal in others.

O. 1.29 ; of style, λέξις ποιητικωτέρα καὶ π. Isoc. 15.47 ( Comp. ); σχηματισμοί D.H. Is. 3 . intricate, complex, εἱλιγμοὶ -ώτατοι, of a labyrinth, Hdt. 2.148 ; of an oracle, Id. 7.111 ( Comp. ); ὁ θεὸς ἔφυ τι π. E. Hel. 711 ; π. νόμος, opp. νοῆσαι ῥᾴδιος, Pl. Smp. 182b ; π. μηχάνημα, λόγοι, S. OC 762 , Ar. Th. 438 ; opp. ἁπλούστερος, Arist. Rh. 1416b25 ; οὐδὲν π. οὐδὲ σοφόν D. 9.37 . Adv. -λως, αὐδώμενος speaking in double sense, S. term_table.lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. Herm. 62 . healing remedy, medicine, in Hom. mostly of those applied outwardly, ἐπιθήσει φάρμαχ' ἅ κεν παύσῃσι μελαινάων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.191 ; ἐπ' ἄρ' ἤπια φάρμακα πάσσε ib. 218 ; ὀδυνήφατα φ. πάσσων 5.401 , 900 , cf. 11.515 , 830 , 15.394 ; προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φ. Od. 10.392 ; φ. περιαλείφειν Ar. Eq. 906 ; also of potions, πιὼν φάρμακ' Od. 10.326 ; φ. πεπωκώς Hdt. 4.160 , cf. Pi. l. c.; παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ Pl. R. 406d , cf. Grg. 467c ; φ. χριστόν E. Hipp. 516 ; ἔγχριστον Theoc. 11.1 ; ἐπίχριστον Str. 17.1.10 ; ἐπίπαστον Theoc. l. c.; καταπλαστόν Ar. Pl. 716 ; ποτόν E. Hipp. l.c.; freq. in Medic. writers, Sor. 1.4 , Gal. 6.265 , etc.; of medicines for cattle, PFlor. 222.11 (iii A. D.). c. gen. (v. infr. 11 ), φ. νόσου a medicine for it, remedy against it, A. Pr. 251 , 606 (lyr.); βηχός Phryn.Com. 60 : κεφαλῆς for a head-ache, Pl. Chrm. 155b ; στραγγουρίας Arist. HA 612b16 , cf. 624a16 ; μέθης Amphis 37 ; δίψης AP 6.170 ( Thyill. ); but ὑγιείας φ. a medicine to restore or maintain health, Aristid. Or. 37(2).11 . enchanted potion, philtre: hence, charm, spell, Od. 4.220 sq., Ar. Pl. 302 , Theoc. 2.15 , PSI 1.64.20 (i B. C.); φαρμάκοις τὸν ἄνδρ' ἔμηνεν Ar.
