The dry ingredients are pounded and sifted through a very fine sieve; the rest are dissolved in vinegar and ground smooth; then all are mixed together, and the oil of cypros is added to the ground ingredients; and having taken it up we use it. Another. ℞ Frankincense 8 dr.; myrrh 8 dr.; ammoniac incense 8 dr.; split alum and white pepper, 8 dr. each; nitre 8 dr.; vinegar, a sufficient amount; oil of cypros 2 cotylae; wax, a half-litra. The meltable ingredients are melted and added to the ground ones. Another, that of the Neapolitan, a drug that has proved successful for sciatics, arthritics and podagrics; it frees them from the whole condition. ℞ Frankincense 2 oz.; white pepper 2 oz.; ammoniac incense 2 oz.; myrrh 2 oz.; flower of Assian stone 2 oz.; split alum 2 oz.; nitre 2 oz.; juice of centaury 2 oz.; lees of Italian wine 1 xestes.

of cyprus oil, of bay oil, of myrtle oil, of storax oil, and of wax, [1021] one litra each; of turpentine a half-litra; of galbanum one ounce; of opopanax half an ounce. Pour the meltable ingredients over the ground ones. Another. It was composed for Domitius Nigrinus, and it frees from the whole condition. ℞ Percolated myrrh, 2 ounces; frankincense, 2 ounces; ammoniac incense, 1 ounce; red nitre or dirty salt, 2 ounces; split alum, 2 ounces; flower of Assian stone, 2 ounces; pith of colocynth, 2 ounces; juice of mandrake, 2 ounces; honey, 2 ounces; euphorbium, 2 ounces; saffron unguent, 6 ounces; quince unguent, 6 ounces; storax unguent, 6 ounces; malabathrum unguent, 6 ounces; bay unguent, 6 ounces; must unguent, 6 ounces; hedychroum unguent, 6 ounces; marjoram unguent, 6 ounces; seal fat, 6 ounces (if this is not available, one must use deer marrow, as old as possible); wax, 1 litra; galbanum, 1 ounce; turpentine, a half-litra; opopanax, half an ounce; lees of Italian wine, 1 xestes. Prepare as stated above.

This preparation is to be used with the podarkes prepared for Sabernius Valens, which is entitled [1022] 'the costly one of Pompeius'. The one made with poplar: for sufferers from sciatica, the arthritic, the paralysed, and the tremulous; it also serves for daily use. Take: of poplar shoots, 1 mina; of the root of wild cucumber, 4 pounds; of cassia in pipes, 2 pounds; of saffron unguent, 2 pounds; of saffron, 3 ounces; of fragrant wine, 12 sextarii; of Sabine oil, 300 (?) sextarii; of sampsuchum, 4 pounds; of wax, 4 pounds. Having carefully chopped the poplar shoots, keep them in a double perfumer's vessel, and add to them the sampsuchum and the cucumber root, chopped coarsely; add the wine to these, and let everything steep for 9 days. On the following day, add the oil, beat it up carefully, and boil it, using a gentle fire. Then squeeze out the liquid, add to it wax scraped fine and marrow that has been ground smooth, set it on the fire and boil it; when it has melted, take it off the fire and add the saffron unguent, stirring continuously. Having ground the saffron preparation, take it up with the blood of a land tortoise, so that it has the thickness of old oil. The tortoise is slaughtered at the collarbone with a reed scraped on both sides.

Add the meltable ingredients to the [1023] saffron and, having beaten them up together, take up the mixture and use it. The drug frees the patient from the whole affection. It becomes even better if it takes up a generous quantity of the tortoise's blood. Another: it is effective for the discomforts arising from chilling and for contusions from blows. ℞ Of poplar twigs, 1 mina. Of the root of wild cucumber, 4 litrae. Of cassia in tubes, 2 litrae. Of deer's marrow, 2 litrae. Of saffron, 3 litrae. Of fragrant wine, 12 xestae. Of oil, 10 litrae. Of sampsuchum, 4 litrae. Of wax, 4 litrae. Of the blood of a land tortoise: however much you add, you will improve the drug. Prepare as stated above. Another acopon, the one made with toads. A man of the xystus (an athlete) used this both as an acopon and as a malagma (emollient), and was freed from the whole affection. The particulars of the preparation are as follows. ℞ Of old Sabine oil, 3 litrae. Of the root of wild cucumber, 3 litrae. Of wax, 3 litrae. Of apochyma (pitch scraped from ships), 3 litrae. Of old pig's fat, 3 litrae. Of toad-frogs, the large ones, 3 in number, or failing these, 5 of the small ones. Of deer's marrow, 3 ounces. Of aphronitre, 3 ounces. Of unfired sulphur, 3 ounces. Of laurel oil, 3 ounces. Of iris oil, 3 ounces.

Of malabathrum unguent, [1024] 1 pound; of sampsuchum, 1 pound. Cutting the roots into thick pieces, and putting them together with the sampsuchum into the oil, and setting it over coals, boil; and when the roots have dried out, squeeze out the liquid, and throw away the roots and the sampsuchum. Then, letting the frogs down into a little woven basket, sewing up its lips, and putting it into the squeezed-out oil, set the vessel back on the fire, covered with a lid. When a sufficient interval has passed for the frogs to have melted away, lift out the basket, squeeze out the liquid, and throw the basket away. To the oil that remains add the meltable ingredients, stirring continually. Last of all add the marrow and the galbanum; and when it has dissolved, lift it from the fire and let it cool somewhat, then sprinkle on the dry ingredients, pounded and sifted through a very fine sieve, stirring continually; and having emptied it into a mortar and pounded it, add 1½ pounds of malabathrum unguent. Pound again, take it up into a leaden vessel, and keep it airtight. The drug is to be used sometimes as a malagma (emollient), once the abatement of the disease has set in, and sometimes also as an ointment for rubbing on.

[1025] For taking as much of the drug as suffices, dissolving it in unguent and bringing it to the thickness of a liquid cerate, we use it. Another, that of Halieus, a successful drug, in connection with which Halieus, while spending his time [there] and gripped by the affection to such a degree that his poor body was distorted, used the drug and was freed from the entire condition. The preparation was given to Valerius Paulinus. It is as follows. ℞ Of Sabine oil, 3 litrai. Of poplar shoots, 1 litra. If the shoots are not available, one must use sampsuchum, so that there is a double amount of the sampsuchum. It also contains sampsuchum, 1 litra. Of oil of cypros, 1 litra. Of iris oil, 1 litra. Of mastic, 1 litra. Of percolated myrrh, a half-litra. Of wax, 3 litrai. Of apochyma, 3 litrai. Of rich swine's fat, 3 litrai. Of unfired sulphur, 3 ounces. Of foam of nitron, 3 ounces. Of galbanum, 3 litrai. Of deer marrow, 4 ounces. Of land tortoises, 10: one must add the blood to the drug once it has been prepared and is already being triturated. One must prepare it as has been said. In the use of the drug one must take 1 litra and add to it, for the sake of fragrance, 3 ounces of opobalsamum.

[1026] and of malabathrum unguent 1 ounce. This, for daily uses, is prepared thus. Another, the one of Halieus, modified by Valerius Paulinus. ℞ Of wax 3 litrae; of root of wild cucumber 3 litrae; of apochyma 3 litrae; of rich pig's suet 3 litrae; of Sabine oil 3 litrae; of oil of cypros 1 litra; of lily oil 1 litra; of saffron oil 1 litra; of mastic 1 litra; of stacte a half-litra; of deer's marrow 1½ litrae; of galbanum 1½ litrae; toads 5; of sampsuchum or of poplar twigs 3 litrae; of unfired sulphur 3 ounces; of aphronitrum 3 ounces; the blood of several tortoises. Prepare as stated before. Another, of Flavius Clemens, a successful drug. We know that people whose whole body had been distorted by podagra and cheiragra used this and were restored to such a degree that they walked about unimpaired. ℞ Of Sabine oil 12 litrae; of the root of wild cucumber 12 litrae; of wax 1 litra; of terebinth 1 litra; of deer's marrow 1 litra; of galbanum 1 litra; frogs, 6 in number.

We divide the oil, and in one part we boil the frogs, in the other the roots; then, having strained the [1027] liquid, we use it for the preparation of the drug, and we use the drug as an acopon. This drug [was made] for Valerius Paulinus, with additions made to the recipe in this way: sampsuchum, 1½ litrae; saffron unguent, 1 litra; malabathrum [unguent], 1 litra; opobalsam, 3 ounces; the blood of 10 tortoises; deer marrow, 2 litrae; galbanum, 2 litrae; old pig fat, 3 litrae; apochyma, 1 litra; wax, 3½ litrae; unfired sulphur, 1 ounce; aphronitre, 4 ounces; toads, 3; the blood of 15 tortoises; and instead of the saffron [unguent], Syrian [unguent], 1 litra; sampsuchum, 1½ litrae. Prepare in the proper manner. Another, of Pompeius Sabinus; it is entitled 'the costly'. It was prepared for Aburnius Valens; it is effective for sciatics, arthritics, the gouty, the tremulous, and for every affection of the sinews. The particulars of its preparation are as follows. Take: sampsuchum, 2 litrae; fenugreek, 2 litrae; melilot, 1 litra; libanotis, 1 litra; savin, 1½ litrae; cachrys, 1 litra; cyprinum, 1 litra; southernwood, 1 litra; cardamom, a half-litra; laurel berries, a half-litra; fragrant wine, 24 sextarii.

of iris unguent, 15 litrae [1028]; of oil of cypros, 2 litrae; of laurel oil, of must oil, of malabathrum oil, 2 litrae each; of Syrian unguent, 2 litrae; of wax, 2 litrae; of terebinth resin, 1 litra; of galbanum, 2 ounces; of opopanax, 3 ounces; of purified ammoniac incense, 4 ounces; of long pepper, of red nitron, of flower of Assian stone, of the pith of colocynth, of split alum, 4 ounces each; of frankincense, 4 ounces; of centaury, 4 ounces; of juice of mandrake, of percolated myrrh, of boiled honey, 4 ounces each; toads, large frogs, six in number; of land tortoises, 10: the blood. The drug is prepared in a varied manner. Having pounded the aromatic and dry ingredients into coarse pieces, put them into a double perfumer's vessel and poured wine over them, we leave them to steep for 3 days; and on the 4th

On the fourth day, taking up as much of the wine as is sufficient, we steep in it the ammoniac incense, frankincense, galbanum, opopanax and the remaining juices; when these have dissolved we triturate them; onto these, once triturated, we add, pounded and sifted, the alum, red nitre, colocynth, flower of Assian stone and pepper, and we triturate the rest of the dry ingredients; onto these we add [1029] percolated myrrh and the honey. When these have been prepared in this way, we add all the liquids to the things steeping in the wine, and, setting it on the fire, we boil it, stirring continually. And when most of the wine has been consumed, we squeeze out the liquid, and, putting the frogs into it, as was stated above, we boil it, and then we add the meltable ingredients; and when these have melted, taking it off the fire, we add it to the triturated ingredients, and after pounding it up we take it up and use it. Another acopon, metasyncritic: for sciatics, arthritics, paralytics, those with tremors. Julius Secundus used it. It breaks up chronic conditions; it is effective also for those suffering from headache. ℞ Adarce 2 oz.; percolated myrrh 2 oz.; aphronitre 2 oz.; euphorbium, opobalsam, 2 ounces each; storax unguent 1 litra. Pound and sift the dry ingredients and add to them the percolated myrrh and the opobalsam, and after pounding them up take them up in the storax unguent and use it, sometimes with the drug undiluted, sometimes diluted; it also assists concoction. Another, composed for Orfitus.

Using this, he was freed from the affection of the chest, which had become troublesome and long-standing. [1030] Rx: adarce, 2 oz.; percolated myrrh, 2 oz.; aphronitre, 3 oz.; euphorbium, ½ oz. (otherwise, 6 oz.); unguent of malabathrum, 1 pound; of what is called in Latin foliatum, half a pound; wax, 2 oz.; opobalsam, 2 oz. Prepare in the customary manner. Another, that of the Neapolitan, composed for Agrippa. Rx: adarce, with the reeds removed, 3 ounces; euphorbium, 3 oz. (otherwise, 6); aphronitre, 3 oz.; stacte, 3 ounces; opobalsam, 3 ounces; unguent of malabathrum of the first quality, 1 pound; foliatum of the first quality, half a pound; hedychroum, half a pound; saffron unguent, half a pound; Asian nard of Thyateira, of the first quality, half a pound; wax, 3 oz. Prepare in the customary manner. Another, a royal myracopon, for chronic affections; it also assists digestions. Rx: aromatic calamus, 3 oz.; carpobalsam, 3 oz.; amomum, 3 ounces; cardamom, 3 oz.; flower of schoenus, 3 oz.; rose-scented cassia, 3 ounces; melilot, 3 oz.; sampsuchum, 3 oz.; savin, 3 ounces; fenugreek, 3 oz.; cyperus, 3 oz.; nard, 3 oz.; white pepper, 3 ounces.

of Troglodytic myrrh a half-litra, [1031] of euphorbium, adarce and nitron a half-litra each, of Falernian wine 16 xestai, of malabathrum unguent of the first preparation 2 litrai, of nard of the first composition 1 litra, of foliatum of the first quality 1 litra, of opobalsam 1 litra, of saffron unguent 1 litra, of storax unguent of the first quality 1 litra, of almond unguent 1 litra, of Commagenian 1 litra, of must unguent 1 litra, of iris unguent 1 litra, of hedychroum 2 litrai, of marjoram unguent of the first quality 2 litrai. Boil in the manner of the unguent-makers. The drug is exceedingly good; it was prepared for Celer the primipilarius. It is effective for sufferers from sciatica, for arthritics, for paralytics, for those with tremor, for spasms and ruptures, and for the scirrhous conditions of the viscera, and it assists concoction when anointed on the mouth of the stomach and on the upper back. Another, composed for Aquilia Secundilla. Take: of euphorbium, opobalsam and percolated myrrh 2 ounces each, of foam of nitron 3 ounces, of wax 1 ounce, of malabathrum unguent 1 litra, of foliatum a half-litra, of saffron unguent a half-litra, of nard unguent a half-litra, of hedychroum a half-litra, of marjoram unguent a half-litra. Prepare in the usual way. The foregoing would indeed have sufficed.

For Asclepiades wrote out carefully both their preparations [1032] and their uses, whereas Andromachus did so more carelessly, as is his habit: he did not even indicate what each of them is by nature fitted to do, but left this to us, since he always composed his writings as if for practitioners of the art. But since some of the akopa, though closely similar to one another, differ in their proportions, I have for this reason written these out above as well, since readers are able, from what Asclepiades taught, to reason about these too, as to which of the akopa will best suit which affections. And I too say this, having gone through certain general accounts concerning them, from which those who attend to what is about to be said will arrive more methodically at their uses. [The akopa written by Andromachus.] The green akopon of Halieus. ℞ Wax, terebinth, old oil, of each 1½ litrae; aphronitre 4 ounces; galbanum 3 ounces; scraped verdigris 3 ounces; opopanax 6 ounces; ammoniac incense 3 ounces; manna 3 ounces; vinegar 2 ounces; quince oil 2 ounces; oil of cypros 2 ounces; iris oil 2 ounces; goat's fat 1 ounce. Another good akopon. ℞ Wax 16 litrae; aphronitre 8 drachms.

[1033] laurel berries, eight in number; white pepper, 1 drachm; crocomagma, a sufficient amount; deer marrow, 2 drachms; myrrh, 1 drachm; wax, 1 drachm; Rhodian wine, 1 [unit not given]; vinegar, a little, for the dry ingredients. Another, that of Bassus the Stoic. ℞ root of wild cucumber, 1 litra; castoreum, 2 oz.; deer marrow, 6 oz.; old oil, 2 litrae; wax, 1 litra; aphronitre, 3 oz.; laurel berries, 2 sextarii; green rue, a bundle filling the hand; libanotis, an equal amount; old Sabine oil, 10 litrae. The roots and the herbs are boiled in the oil, then they are squeezed out, then the meltable ingredients are poured in. Another. ℞ opopanax, 1 oz.; resin, 1 oz.; pine resin, 2 litrae; wax, 1 litra; ammoniac incense, 6 oz.; oesypum, 2 oz.; old oil, 1½ sextarii; flower of salt, 2 oz. Another. ℞ wax, 1 litra; deer marrow, 2 oz.; Babylonian unguent, 1 litra; hedychroum, 1 litra; stacte, 1 litra; malabathrum, 1 oz.; nard, 1 oz.; opobalsam, 6 oz. Melt the marrow in sea water or in brine, having treated the meltable ingredients together; the opobalsam last. If the acopon is too liquid, add more wax.

Another acopon [1034] of Quadratus. Take: iris unguent, 1 oz.; wax, 1 oz.; cyprinum, 1 oz.; laurel oil, 1 oz.; old oil, 3 oz.; terebinth resin, 1 ounce; deer marrow, 1 oz.; oesypum, 1 oz.; pepper, 1 oz.; nitre, 4 dr.; unfired sulphur, 4 dr.; pellitory, 4 dr.; honey, 1 oz. The meltable ingredients over the dry ones. Another, the foul-smelling acopon. Take: terebinth resin, 56 dr.; wax, 28 dr.; oesypum, 6 dr.; honey, 6 dr.; deer marrow, 6 dr.; ammoniac incense, 6 dr.; galbanum, 6 dr.; aphronitre, 6 dr.; sometimes opopanax, 6 dr.; bay berries, 6 dr.; old oil, 1 xestes; wine, 2 cotylae. Some add castoreum, 3 dr. Another, the one made with sampsuchum. Take: wax, 1 litra; omphacine oil, 3 xestae; sampsuchum, 1 xestes; fenugreek, 1 xestes; old wine, 4 xestae; a bundle of mallow, a bundle of linozostis, roots of wild cucumber. Another, as Antimachus makes it. Take: fresh sampsuchum, libanotis, aspalathus, brathy (which is herba sabina), fenugreek, of each 2 xestae; wax, 1 litra; old wine, 3 xestae; gleucinum, 3 xestae. Another, from Philocles.

℞ Of oil boiled down for a long time, [with?] roots of wild cucumber, 3 sextarii; of wax 1 mina; of terebinth 1 mina; of deer's marrow 25 drachms; of goose fat 25 drachms; of galbanum 12½ drachms; of sampsuchon 1 sextarius; of libanotis 1 sextarius. These last are ground smooth with fragrant wine and mixed in; and it becomes a malagma if more wax is mixed in. Another acopon that has proved successful, as Aphrodas [makes it]. ℞ Of aphronitrum 3 drachms; of pepper 40 grains, and of long [pepper] the same amount; of frankincense 16 drachms. Having pounded these, pour on 1 cotyle of fragrant Chian or Rhodian wine and 9 drachms of honey. Then melt in a dish 12 drachms of Tyrrhenian wax and 42 drachms of bull's fat. Another, which was Asphalartesios' [?]. ℞ Of crocomagma 4 drachms; of deer's marrow 12 drachms; of oesypum 6 drachms; of goose or pig fat 12 drachms; of terebinth 12 drachms; of iris oil 18 drachms; of oil of cypros and of gleucinum, 18 drachms each. Melt the honey, then mix it with the dry ingredients, and having ground [it] smooth together with the [ingredients] in the mortar, use it. Another acopon, the barbarian one, with euphorbium, for sciatics and for many other things. ℞ Of opopanax 1 ounce; of Tyrrhenian [wax] 1 ounce; of terebinth 2 ounces.

of galbanum [1036] 1 oz.; of ammoniac incense 2 oz.; of euphorbium 2 oz.; of castoreum 2 oz.; of white pepper 2 oz.; of deer marrow 4 oz.; of oesypum 4 oz.; of limnestris ½ oz.; of storax oil, laurel oil and marjoram oil, 3 oz. of each; of old oil 2 sextarii; of hedychroum 6 oz. Prepare and use. It is effective for desperate affections of the nerves, and in particular also for sciatics. Another acopon, by which Aruntius Aquila was cured; effective for sciatica and for every tension of the nerves. ♃ Of opopanax 2 ounces; of galbanum 1 oz.; of turpentine 2 ounces; of white pepper and castoreum, 2 oz. of each; of oesypum 4 oz.; of cassia 4 oz.; of deer marrow 4 oz.; of wax 1 pound; of storax oil 6 ounces; of iris oil 6 ounces; of laurel oil 6 ounces; of old oil 1 pound; of euphorbium 2 ounces; of ammoniac incense 2 ounces. Mix the euphorbium with a little honey. Another acopon, that of Glytus, as Philoxenus the grammarian gives it. ♃ Of wax 2 pounds; of ammoniac incense 1 pound; of galbanum 1½ pounds; of storax 1 pound; of bdellium 1 pound; of myrrh 2 oz.; of frankincense 9 oz.; of Attic oesypum 1 pound.

[1037] of propolis, 1 litra; of terebinth resin, 1 litra; of old oil, 2 litrae; of oil of cypros, of iris unguent, of almond oil, 2 litrae each; of Syrian [unguent], 3 litrae; of opopanax, 1 litra. Prepare. Another akopon, a green one, as Clemens Sertorius [gives it], which I use. ℞ Of scraped verdigris, 6 ounces; of roasted resin, 4 ounces; of myrtle oil, 1 litra; of mastic oil, 1 litra; of old oil, 1 litra; of laurel oil, 2 litrae; of Syrian [unguent], 1 litra; of must oil, 3 litrae; of lamb's suet, 3 ounces; of Pontic wax, 3 litrae; of galbanum, 1 litra; of tender leaves of myrtle, of green leaves of rue, of green libanotis, of tender leaves of bay, 6 ounces each; of the herb sage, a half-litra. Pound the green ingredients and steep them in the oils for a night and a day, then boil them together with the meltable ingredients. When you take it from the fire, put in the verdigris and, having strained it, store it away. It is effective against every pain of the sinews. Another warming akopon, as Castus [gives it], for chronic conditions, spasms. ℞ Of pitch oil, 1 xestes; of Syrian unguent, the same amount; of Illyrian iris, the same amount; of terebinth, 1 litra; of axunge, 1 litra; of ship scrapings, 1 ounce.

[1038] Boil, stirring with fresh rue. Another acopon, the good one of Orion the comber. Take: of wax 6 litrae; of propolis 5 litrae; of Illyrian iris 4 litrae; of turpentine [resin] 4 litrae; of opopanax 3 litrae; of old oil 4 litrae; of galbanum 2 litrae; of mastic oil 3 litrae; of myrtle [oil] 3 litrae; of ammoniac incense 1 litra; of deer marrow 3 litrae; of oesypum 6 litrae; of laurel berries 1 litra; of storax [oil] 3 litrae; of almond [oil] 3 litrae; of calf suet 3 litrae, and of lion [suet] 1½ litrae; of opobalsam 1½ litrae. Prepare carefully. Another good myracopon. Take: of malabathrum, of hedychroum, of nard, of Babylonian saffron [unguent], a half-litra each; of stacte 6 ounces; of opobalsam 6 ounces; of wax 6 ounces; of Commagenum 6 ounces; of aloe 2 ounces; of honey 3 ounces. Prepare. Another myracopon, which I use. Of white wax 2 ounces; of aromatized goose fat 1 ounce; of aromatized bull suet 1 ounce; of aromatized lion fat 2 ounces; of aromatized crocodile [fat] 1 ounce; of deer marrow 1 ounce; of ammoniac salt 2 ounces; of white pepper 2 ounces; of frankincense 1 ounce; of cinnamon 3 ounces.

[1039] of aphronitrum, 1 ounce; of Illyrian iris, 2 sextarii; of nard unguent, 1 sextarius; of Alexandrian malabathrum, 2 sextarii; of stacte, 2 pounds; of Syrian saffron oil, 2 pounds; of honey, 4 pounds; of opobalsam, 1 sextarius; of Commagenian, 2 pounds. Prepare as you know. Another myracopon. ♃ Of Tyrrhenian wax, 6 ounces; of ammoniacum, 4 ounces; of euphorbium, 4 pounds; of white pepper, 4 ounces; of limnestris, 4 ounces; of magma of malabathrum, 6 ounces; of opobalsam, 1 pound; of malabathrum, 1 pound; of stacte, 6 ounces; of foliatum, 6 ounces; of nard, 3 pounds. [Preparations of gleucinum.] Preparation of gleucinum, as Andromachus. Next after the acopa written above, Andromachus wrote a preparation of gleucinum, not inappropriately joining it to the acopon unguents; for it is most anodyne and most effective against fatigue. It is written by him word for word as follows. Preparation of gleucinum which I use. ♃ Of myrrh, 2 pounds; of Indian nard, 2 pounds; of costus, 3 pounds; of storax, 1 pound;

of bdellium, sampsuchon, balsam wood, mastic, cardamom, spathe, [1040] Illyrian iris, misy, asarum, 2 litrai each; of melilot 1 litra; of Celtic nard 1 litra; of aspalathus and calamus a half-litra each; of long aristolochia 1½ litrai; of seed of libanotis 2 xestai; of frankincense 3 litrai; of cassia 3 litrai; of fenugreek 2 xestai; of sphagnos 2 litrai; of amomum 2 litrai; of bark of frankincense 1 litra; of dry roses 2 litrai; of savin 6 ounces; of fennel 2 litrai; of balsam fruit 2 litrai; of saffron 3 ounces; of laurel berries 1 litra; of white pepper 1 litra; of opobalsam 3 ounces; of leaves of malabathrum two litrai; two fresh pine cones; of fresh rue 2 ounces; of ammoniac salt 4 drachmas; of nitron 4 drachmas; of old wine 12 xestai; of good must 2½ keramia; of old oil 5 litrai. Prepare for 40 days. Having written these things, Andromachus did not go on to give the manner of preparation, as Criton did. Moreover, he also did not make clear how many Italian litrai, or how many xestai, he means the keramion to be. Preparation of gleucinum, as Criton gives it in the second book of the Cosmetics. Criton wrote the preparation of gleucinum at the end of the book, in these very words:

[1041] Gleucinum has a warming, relaxing power. It is effective for affections in the uterus and for every sympathetic affection of the sinews; its preparations are many. The one called simple is as follows. ℞ Put a metretes of fresh must of the Maroneian grape into a tin vessel and boil it over coals; when it has boiled up three or four times, pour it off into an earthenware metretes, set it in the sun, and add white omphacine oil, 6 choes; schinus, 6 minas (others, ½ mina); nard, the same amount; calamus, the same amount; aspalathus, the same amount; elate, 1 mina; cyperus, 1 mina; cardamom, 8 minas; amomum, the same amount; melilot, 5 ounces. Let everything be ground smooth; then, after stirring them together for 8 days and clearing off the must, use it. Preparation of gleucinum, as Dioscorides in the first book On Materia Medica. Dioscorides wrote as follows.

The simple gleucinum is prepared from omphacine oil, mastic (schinus), Celtic nard, calamus, spathe, aspalathus, melilot, costus and must, with grape-pomace (stemphyla) placed in the middle being rubbed round together in the vessel that holds the aromatics, the wine and [1042] the oil. It is stirred for thirty days, twice a day; then it is pressed out and stored. It has a warming, emollient, relaxing power, effective against rigors, against all nervous affections, and against those in the uterus. It is of more benefit than any acopon, being emollient. Preparation of gleucinum, according to Heras. Since Heras wrote out the preparation of gleucinum more clearly than they did, at the end of his pharmaceutical book, I shall set out his text too, word for word, as follows. Composition of gleucine oil, effective against chills and above all against nervous affections; it benefits those with opisthotonos and those with emprosthotonos, applied warm by means of clean wool soaked in the oil and laid on the affected places. ♃ Venafran oil, 208 litrae (otherwise, 250); old fragrant Falernian wine, 3 sextarii; Aminaean must, 108 sextarii; helenium, 12 litrae; spathe, 5 litrae; aspalathus, 5 litrae; hedysarum, 2½ litrae; 'mother' artemisia, 2½ litrae; cyperus, 2 litrae; myrrh, 3 litrae (others, 1 litra); white pepper, 2½ litrae; splanchnon, 2½ litrae; xylobalsamum, 2½ litrae.

of long birthwort [1043] 1 pound 3 ounces; of dry myrtle leaves 1 ounce; of dry libanotis 5 ounces; of dry bay leaves 12 ounces; of bdellium 2½ pounds; of Illyrian iris 2½ pounds; of storax 1 pound 3 ounces; of dry cassia 1 pound 3 ounces; of ladanum 1 pound 3 ounces; of cardamom 1 pound 3 ounces; of saffron 1 pound 3½ ounces; of balsam fruit 2½ pounds; of frankincense 5 pounds; of crocomagma 5 pounds; of panax 1 pound 3 ounces; of aromatic reed 5 pounds; of asarum 2½ pounds; of black cassia 2½ pounds; of amomum in the cluster 1 pound 3 ounces; of flower of schoenus 5 pounds; of costus 5 pounds 3 ounces; of Celtic nard 5 pounds; of melilot 1 pound 3 ounces; of sampsuchum 1 pound 3 ounces; of dry roses 1 pound 3 ounces; of fenugreek ½ pound, or 2½ pounds; of opobalsam 5 small vessels; of malabathrum unguent 1 pound. Pound the dry ingredients, sift them through a rather coarse sieve, and steep them in wine. Pound the bdellium as well, even if it is not dry; but if it should be greasy, dissolve it in the wine by pounding it in a mortar.

Put it into a small perfumer's vessel made of tin, cover it [1044] carefully with a lid, and leave it for twelve days and twelve nights. Let the must be made ready at the same time, from grapes cleanly pressed out, so that it contains nothing of dew. Then, putting the must into a large bronze cauldron, so that there is room also for the boiling-up of the must, add all the ingredients that have been soaked in the wine, together with the oil and the wine; and let it be stirred twice a day with a perfumer's spatula for an hour. Let the spatula be wiped carefully, so that what has remained on it and turned sour may not spoil the drug when the spatula is put in again. Let the vessel be fitted with a lid and, above, with several piercings (κεντρῶσι), and let it be tied round carefully. Let a coiled ring be placed under the vessel. When fifteen days have passed, let the ammoniac and the amomum itself be added, pounded rather coarsely. At thirty days one must give it two or three boilings in a double vessel over coals, adding the opobalsam to the unguent as well. Then, taking the vessel off and letting it cool for a while, pour off the unguent.

The remainder, while still hot, is to be pressed out in little baskets, first by hand, then by means of a press. Having done something (?) on account of the perfume, throw it off into [1045] the malabathrum itself, if we put in perfume poured over hot water, and stir it up with the spatula so that it mixes. Then, having left it for one day, store it away in glass vessels, [or] earthenware ones smeared with gum. [The acopa written by Heras.] An acopon for paralytics and in general for every pain. ♃ Green rue, 1 litra; dry pennyroyal, 1 litra; cyperus, 1 litra; natron, 50 drachms; fenugreek, 1 litra; dry linozostis, 1 litra; horehound, 1 litra; libanotis, 1 litra; birthwort, 1 litra; bitter almonds, peeled, half a modius; iris, 2 litrai; terebinth, 2 litrai; laurel berries, 2 litrai; root of wild cucumber, 2 litrai; ammoniac incense, 2 litrai; savin, 2 litrai; white hellebore, 6 litrai; green myrtle, 3 litrai; dry laurel leaves, 3 litrai; wax, 4 litrai; bdellium, 4 litrai; wine, 2 kotylai (in another [copy], 12 choes of the wine); oil, 4 choes.

Having pounded coarsely the ingredients that ought to be pounded, pour on water and, in turn (ἔμπαλιν), the pounded ingredients; pour on in addition both the wine and the oil, [1046] and let it stand overnight. On the following day boil it, until these ingredients, floating in it, are thoroughly boiled down and the oil takes on the quality from the boiled ingredients. All this comes about with time. Then, having taken it off and squeezed out the dregs, add the wax, the resin and the bdellium. Another green akopon, for sciatica and paralyses. I used this in the case of Fortes. ℞ Terebinth resin, 1 litra; manna, 4 ounces; galbanum, 4 ounces; aphronitre, 4 ounces; ammoniac incense, 4 ounces; opopanax, 4 ounces; goat suet, 6 ounces; verdigris, 5 ounces; oil of cypros, 1 kotyle; iris oil, 1½ kotylai; quince oil, 4 ounces; Syrian unguent, 3 ounces; pepper, 3 ounces (some, 4 ounces); old olive oil, 1½ xestai; adarce, 1 ounce; vinegar, as much as is fully sufficient. Triturate the verdigris, the opopanax and the aphronitre with the vinegar; melt the rest and pour it over them. Another akopon, for chronic sciatica, for ankylai and paralyses; it is very effective. ℞ Old olive oil and iris oil, 6 litrai; and laurel oil, 6 litrai; pyrakinon (πυρακείνου), 6 litrai; wax, 6 litrai; terebinth, 2 ounces.

euphorbium [1047] 2 oz.; ammoniac incense 3 ounces; castoreum 2 oz.; opopanax 2 oz.; galbanum 2 ounces; deer marrow 2 oz.; pepper 2 oz. Melt the meltable ingredients, pour them over the dry ones, combine them into one, and use. Another acopon for sciaticas and in general for everything. ℞ myrrh one part, pellitory half a part. Pour gleucinum (must-oil) over them once they have been ground smooth, so that the drug becomes glutinous; and at the time of use, mix in rose-oil and use. [Damocrates' preparations of acopa.] Since there is much talk among those devoted to medicine about the use of all the acopa and myracopa, I shall explain what these are and how they help, and how one must prepare each drug among them individually. All of them, then, are effective against pains of the nerves, and of all the flesh and the muscles, those pains that fatigue or chill has taken hold of, or that have arisen without a manifest cause.

and those who must often bear similar pains and hardships, [1048] those easily seized by chills and fatigues, if one, having used them beforehand, then goes out to the labours required by the necessities of life; and it puts flesh on parts of the body that are wasting (ἀτροφοῦντα), if one anoints the affected parts again after food; and it will suit those who are slow to recover, and old men, if they use them in winter towards evening. What each of the akopa (anti-fatigue remedies) does we shall tell in other verses, either setting it beneath their recipes or else placing the use before the recipe. But now I shall say how the first must be made. Of ammoniac, 10 oz. – whether one wants ounces or some other weight – and the same of frankincense; of galbanum 4; of deer marrow 4, and 4; of Attic oesypum they send (πέμπουσι) the same; and of translucent turpentine 4; of good, fresh honey, again 10.

[1049] and of Pontic wax a weight equal to this; and of fresh, soft goose fat, 10; of Falernian wine 5 cotylae, or a little fewer, or even a little more; and of good old oil, twice 20. Take care that this is not foul-smelling when you put it in, for in this way it will be agreeable to those who use it. Prepare it as follows.

In a rather large mortar, having crushed frankincense into very small grains, and the ammoniac too, pouring wine over them at once and letting these be moderately soaked, grind with the pestle; and when you have made it of the thickness of honey, add the honey and the oesypum and the deer marrow; then, having united these in the mortar, melt in a pot the wax and all the oil and the fat and the galbanum and the turpentine; and having let them all melt, pour them over the contents of the mortar, [1050] and having stirred a little with the pestle so that it may cool somewhat, then rub all these together with the hands until everything is united and takes on the thickness of good liquid honey; and so store it in a tin vessel or else a boxwood one, using it carefully as a most excellent drug. It is also most beneficial for women who have had an inflammation of the uterus bringing on indurations and fear of a scirrhus; in their case order the drug, smeared thus on a pessary, to be applied to the uterus. This also works for pains of the ears that are without ulcer, the violent ones without flux; mix with the drug 4 or 3 parts of Sergetic iris unguent, and having soaked wool in it warm, put it into the passage. Another.

This green acopon too is very efficacious, [1051] which is why it acts more at the onsets of the pains; and it is beneficial for arthritic and podagric patients, when before the baths they are rubbed with the drug, both the feet and the thickened sinews. For in this way I have known some to become healthy. It contains: of good frankincense, 1 litra; of ammoniac incense, 2 litrae; of the whitest aphronitre, 1 litra; and, having cleansed the same [?], of Attic wool-grease, of good myrrh, of galbanum free of wood, and of pure opopanax: of each of these, weighing carefully, twice 4 ounces; of fresh euphorbium, 4 ounces; and equal to these of rough limnesium. Those who sell the ingredients in Italy, and those who buy them, call this adarce. Of very good Pontic wax, 2 litrae; of pure terebinth resin, 2½ litrae.

[1052] Of laurel oil, oil of cypros and must-oil (gleucinum), one litra each; of Sergetic iris oil, of old olive oil, and of fresh mastic-oil, of each of these again two litrai by weight; of vinegar a moderate amount. In this grind the dry ingredients for a sufficient time and carefully reduce them to smoothness; then add them, after melting the unguents, the wax, the galbanum and the terebinth, the juice of panax and the other liquid ingredients, and after pouring these out, hot and still boiling, into the mortar. Rub up the ingredients in it vigorously with the pestle and with the hand, and when you have united everything, store the drug in a box such as I described a little earlier. Use it with confidence in all chronic conditions. Another. This too is an acopon, easily procured and good, especially in winter, able to help those who are easily overcome on journeys.

[1053] It contains: of pure galbanum, 3 ounces; of fresh opopanax, one ounce; of flower of salt, 3; and of oesypum, 4; of fine ammoniac incense, 8 pounds; of wax, 1 pound; of roasted pine resin (pityinē), not ill-smelling, twice 4 ounces; and a pound of Sabine oil, twice 4; and more in winter: put in about a pound; of dark Falernian wine, 10 ounces. Prepare it thus.

In a mortar crush the ammoniac, then, putting in wine, moisten it a little, and when you have ground it carefully, then add the flower of salt and the oesypum. Then, grinding thoroughly and bringing it to the thickness of honey, and having melted the meltable ingredients, afterwards add the galbanum and the opopanax and melt again, and pour this over the ingredients that have previously been made smooth in the mortar and well united; [1054] and having thus mixed the drug with the hands while it is still warm, store it away in a glass vessel. Another myracopon. This myracopon too is among the very fine ones, for it is pleasant and gives effective help against the pains of which I spoke a little before. It contains: of good stacte three ounces, of opobalsam 3, and of Attic honey 3, and of pure Pontic wax 3; of crocinum and of Syrian unguent 4 oz.; of the whitest ammoniac and of ground salt 2 oz.; and one [ounce] and one part of terebinth [resin], white and purified; and of cinnamon and malabathrum add besides one pound and a third part of a pound. And if by chance you have no malabathrum, add the same amount of Gangetic nard.

This unguent is among the moderately good ones, [1055] but it is sufficiently drug-like, as no other is. Or likewise the same amount of Sergetic iris unguent, or of Cyzicene, that is, of marjoram unguent. You will use these, as I said, when the malabathrum is not at hand. For I consider it a moderate myracopon, no less beneficial to those who use it. Prepare it thus: having first ground [the ingredients] up carefully, add the honey, and having ground it fine in due measure and mixed in the stacte and the opobalsam, grind carefully again. Then put pure terebinth resin, wax and the saffron unguent into a double vessel and melt the aforementioned with water, about evening (?) [περὶ δεῖλον], in another pot.

Having melted these, pour malabathrum in alongside, and having united everything in due proportion, so that it does not boil, lift the double vessel out of the pot; and having cooled it carefully and scraped out the drug, and adding it to the things mentioned before, grind it again in the mortar until [1056] the whole is well united and becomes one drug. If you wish to make it more efficacious for the sinews (νεῦρα) and for chronic conditions and the affections and the tensions of the muscles, mix into the whole by weight 2 ounces of good and still fresh euphorbium, having first ground it together with the salts, the honey and the opobalsam for a sufficient time. Having thus united all the aforementioned, store it in a box or in a glass vessel, using it preferably after the baths. But when making a myracopon for a king, an Augustus, prepare this one, most easily and without fire, having of opobalsam a measure of about 3 ounces, and of the finest malabathrum 15 ounces, of good cinnamon the same, and of odourless, very white wax 10 drachms.

[1057] Prepare it thus: a third part of the malabathrum, and the wax cut into the smallest pieces, put into a thin silver bowl. Having melted them over very hot water, cool and scrape; and adding this, ground smooth, to the opobalsam and the cinnamon, grind again, uniting the whole. Then at last, pouring the remaining malabathrum in with them, unite it by grinding with your hands, and so store it in a silver vessel or a thick glass one; for thus you will keep the drug safely. And by adding a third of a litra of Gangetic nard you will make the drug sweeter, and a better liniment for recent conditions. If cinnamon is not at hand, by leaving it out you will have it only very slightly inferior, but truly good, and far better than any other myracopon.

But if you wish to make it more efficacious [1058] for the conditions I mentioned before, add four drachms of Atlantic euphorbium. For in this way it will be pleasant and active, even though it is composed of few ingredients. I have known some, however, who use many fats, and much marrow, and certain aromatics, and juices, and unguents, and certain oils; having in turn made use of these myself, I came, of course, to recognise that such things belong to men lacking in taste, who have not discerned the ingredients and the simple natures of these.
